君子約敷言之訓而深賛其妙焉夫皇極之訓
要之使人會歸於極而已然其理則出於天焉
===
非達天德者其孰能知之箕子衍皇極之疇以
告武王至此若曰人君之建極於天下也敷言
之道雖本於人之身而神道之教實原於天之
命是故其爲訓也豈徒使之諷詠而已哉由是
而示於人曰會其有極蓋極之理涵於心而具
足也玆惟戒其私念之萌而王義王道王路是
遵焉則約情以協中有以萃衆志之渙而凡同
心以向道者有定趨矣又於是而示於人曰歸
其有極蓋極之理見於事而各當也玆惟戒其
punctuated:
是訓，于帝其訓。
樊璽
同考試官教諭易批〔詞理俱到〕
同考試官教諭金批〔鋪敘敷言之蘊，精純溫潤〕〔可以占其人矣〕
考試官教諭何批〔瑩徹可觀〕
考試官教諭錢批〔典雅之作〕
君子約敷言之訓而深賛其妙焉。夫皇極之訓，要之使人會歸於極而已，然其理則出於天焉。非達天德者，其孰能知之？箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王，至此若曰：人君之建極於天下也，敷言之道雖本於人之身，而神道之教實原於天之命。是故其爲訓也，豈徒使之諷詠而已哉？由是而示於人曰：「會其有極。」蓋極之理涵於心而具足也。玆惟戒其私念之萌，而王義、王道、王路是遵焉，則約情以協中，有以萃衆志之渙，而凡同心以向道者有定趨矣。又於是而示於人曰：「歸其有極。」蓋極之理見於事而各當也。玆惟戒其
translation_en:
…these are instructions; they are the instructions of the Lord on High.

Fan Xi 樊璽

Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: 〔Both expression and reasoning are fully realized.〕
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: 〔He unfolds the implications of the proclaimed words with refinement, purity, warmth, and polish.〕〔From this one may judge the man himself.〕
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔Luminous and lucid, well worth reading.〕
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: 〔A work of classical elegance.〕

The gentleman summarizes the instruction conveyed by the proclaimed words and deeply praises its subtle excellence. The instruction of the August Ultimate, in essence, simply leads people to assemble at and return to the Ultimate. Yet its principle issues from Heaven. Who but one who comprehends Heaven’s virtue could understand it? Jizi elaborated the section on the August Ultimate to instruct King Wu. At this point, he seems to say: When the ruler establishes the Ultimate throughout the world, although the way of proclaiming words is rooted in his own person, instruction through the spiritual way truly originates in Heaven’s mandate. Thus, could this instruction be intended merely for people to recite and chant?

Accordingly, he instructs people, saying: “Assemble at the Ultimate.” The principle of the Ultimate is contained in the mind in its fullness. Here he warns them against the first stirrings of selfish thoughts, so that they follow royal righteousness, the royal way, and the royal path. By restraining their feelings to accord with the mean, they can bring together the scattered purposes of the multitude; all who turn with united minds toward the Way then have a fixed direction.

Further, he instructs people, saying: “Return to the Ultimate.” The principle of the Ultimate manifests itself in affairs, giving each its proper measure. Here he warns them against their…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不善之動而蕩蕩平平正直是由焉則視履以
考祥有以止至善之域而凡造道以優入者有
定守矣夫敷言之訓如此是豈一己之私哉吾
知道本固有而播之聲詠者莫非烝民秉彝之
良固天下之常理也理本無外而普之話言者
實皆萬世定保之徵固天下之大訓也然訓雖
君也而言則純乎理焉謂天之訓可也惟皇降
衷若或啓之以左右乎斯民者也天其無言之
君矣乎言雖君也而理則本於天焉謂天之敎
===
可也惟帝佑民若或道之以寵綏乎四方者也
君其有言之天矣乎夫敷言之妙有如此以是
而達之臣民則人心之天隨感而應會極歸極
固有莫知其然者彝倫之叙固其所歟雖然是
豈可以易致者哉蓋人君必有合天之心而後
有同天之化苟非建極之君位在德元而徒以
言語感人者末矣故建極者必求端於天而憲
天者必求端於心此固箕子告武王之意也四
海永清之治其亦有由也夫
punctuated: 不善之動，而蕩蕩、平平、正直是由焉，則視履以考祥，有以止至善之域，而凡造道以優入者有定守矣。夫敷言之訓如此，是豈一己之私哉？吾知道本固有，而播之聲詠者，莫非烝民秉彝之良，固天下之常理也；理本無外，而普之話言者，實皆萬世定保之徵，固天下之大訓也。然訓雖君也，而言則純乎理焉，謂天之訓可也。惟皇降衷，若或啓之以左右乎斯民者也，天其無言之君矣乎？言雖君也，而理則本於天焉，謂天之敎可也。惟帝佑民，若或道之以寵綏乎四方者也，君其有言之天矣乎？夫敷言之妙有如此，以是而達之臣民，則人心之天隨感而應。會極、歸極，固有莫知其然者，彝倫之叙固其所歟？雖然，是豈可以易致者哉？蓋人君必有合天之心，而後有同天之化。苟非建極之君，位在德元，而徒以言語感人者，末矣。故建極者必求端於天，而憲天者必求端於心。此固箕子告武王之意也，四海永清之治，其亦有由也夫！
translation_en:
…the stirring of what is not good, and follow only what is broad, level, and upright. Then, by examining their conduct to judge its auspicious consequences, they can come to rest in the realm of the highest good; all who advance toward the Way and enter deeply into it will have a fixed principle to uphold.

Such is the instruction imparted through the proclamation of words. Could this be merely one person's private concern? I know that the Way is inherently possessed: what is disseminated in recitation and song is nothing other than the goodness of the constant moral nature held by all the people. It is indeed the enduring principle of all under Heaven. Principle, by its nature, excludes nothing: what is made universally known through spoken instruction is truly evidence of lasting stability and preservation through myriad generations. It is indeed the great teaching of all under Heaven.

Yet although the instruction comes from the ruler, its words accord wholly with principle; it may therefore be called Heaven's instruction. August Heaven bestows the moral mean, as though something were giving guidance so as to assist these people. Is Heaven, then, a ruler without speech? Although the words come from the ruler, their principle is rooted in Heaven; they may therefore be called Heaven's teaching. The Lord on High protects the people, as though something were guiding them so as to cherish and bring peace to the four quarters. Is the ruler, then, a Heaven that speaks?

Such is the subtle efficacy of proclaiming words. When these words are conveyed to officials and people, the Heaven within the human heart responds as it is moved. In gathering around the supreme standard and returning to it, people may indeed be unaware of how this comes about. Is not the ordering of the constant human relationships its proper result?

Yet could this be attained easily? The ruler must first possess a heart united with Heaven before he can exercise a transforming influence like Heaven's. Unless he is a ruler who establishes the supreme standard, occupying his position as foremost in virtue, merely seeking to move people through words is a superficial pursuit. Thus, one who establishes the supreme standard must seek its source in Heaven, and one who models himself on Heaven must seek its source in his own heart. This was indeed the meaning of Jizi's counsel to King Wu. Surely the government that brings enduring peace throughout the Four Seas has its foundation here!

===
以致用於天下者才德而已矣諸侯能全備之
則何用而不臧乎此天子美諸侯之詩蓋以答
瞻彼洛矣也若曰王者之使人也固無求備之
心而人臣之用世也貴得泛應之妙今茲會同
洛邑者何如哉彼身之所處不一而有所謂左
有所謂右者萬事萬物之變也道之所應有常
而左必曰宜右必曰有者揆事宰物之權也夫
人才非全才而德非備德則亦一偏之士而無
以周左右之用矣惟我君子也大道不器而所

translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Employ him on the left, on the left: the gentleman is suited to it. Employ him on the right, on the right: the gentleman has what it requires.”

Liao Ruchun

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔Captures the poet’s intent.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor: 〔The wording is rich and elaborate, without a single superfluous phrase; sufficient to … [?]〕〔one who expounds the Odes.〕
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔Rich and ample.〕
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔Full and flowing.〕

The poet praises the talents and virtue of the feudal lords, whose service is adequate to every task. For what enables a gentleman to render service throughout the realm is simply talent and virtue. If the feudal lords possess these in their entirety, what service could they perform that would not be good? This is a poem in which the Son of Heaven praises the feudal lords, offered in response to “Gaze upon That Luo” (Zhan bi Luo yi). It is as though he said: When a king employs men, he certainly does not expect perfection; yet when a minister serves the world, what is prized is his marvelous ability to respond to every circumstance. How, then, do those now assembled at Luoyi measure up?

The situations in which a man finds himself are diverse: what are called “the left” and “the right” represent the changing circumstances of all affairs and things. The Way’s responses have a constant principle: that service on the left is necessarily called “suitable,” and service on the right is necessarily described as “having what it requires,” reflects the capacity to weigh affairs and govern things. If a man’s talents are not comprehensive and his virtue is not complete, he is merely a man of partial attainments, unable to fulfill the tasks of both left and right. title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以辦天下之事者遺之至艱而不撓大德不官
而所以任天下之重者投之至繁而不擾左之
左之以時措之而已矣推行盡利也化裁盡神
也而各協於中正之極右之右之以時出之而
已矣取之不窮也用之不匱也而悉備乎廣大
之全隨在而皆天子之所使則隨在而皆君子
之所宜入而在內則佐王經邦國而予曰有先
後也出而在外則佐王平邦國而予曰有禦侮
也蓋不特宜於文而又宜於武矣其諸咸宜者
===
乎無往而非天子之所命則無往而非君子之
所有以綏太平則順治之猷慰一人求寧之念
也以戡禍亂則威嚴之略協一人先事之圖也
蓋不特有文事而又有武備矣其諸富有者乎
是則由左而觀之故謂之宜耳而復有之於右
未嘗滯於左也則雖曰無所不宜可也由右而
觀之故謂之有耳而復宜之於左未嘗滯於右
也則雖曰無所不有可也東都一會而以作六
師其所以致福祿之如茨保邦家於萬年者誠
punctuated: 以辦天下之事者，遺之至艱而不撓；大德不官，而所以任天下之重者，投之至繁而不擾。左之左之，以時措之而已矣。推行盡利也，化裁盡神也，而各協於中正之極。右之右之，以時出之而已矣。取之不窮也，用之不匱也，而悉備乎廣大之全。隨在而皆天子之所使，則隨在而皆君子之所宜。入而在內，則佐王經邦國，而予曰有先後也；出而在外，則佐王平邦國，而予曰有禦侮也。蓋不特宜於文，而又宜於武矣，其諸咸宜者乎！無往而非天子之所命，則無往而非君子之所有。以綏太平，則順治之猷慰一人求寧之念也；以戡禍亂，則威嚴之略協一人先事之圖也。蓋不特有文事，而又有武備矣，其諸富有者乎！是則由左而觀之，故謂之宜耳，而復有之於右，未嘗滯於左也，則雖曰無所不宜可也；由右而觀之，故謂之有耳，而復宜之於左，未嘗滯於右也，則雖曰無所不有可也。東都一會，而以作六師，其所以致福祿之如茨、保邦家於萬年者，誠
translation_en:
…that by which he manages the affairs of the realm: entrusted with the greatest difficulties, he does not falter. Great virtue is not confined to a single office, and through that by which he bears the weighty responsibilities of the realm, he remains unperturbed even when charged with the most complex tasks. Employ him on the left, employ him on the left: it is simply a matter of putting him to work as the occasion requires. In carrying things out, he realizes every benefit; in adapting and shaping them, he exercises the fullest subtlety. Each accords with the highest standard of centrality and correctness. Employ him on the right, employ him on the right: it is simply a matter of bringing him forward at the proper time. What may be drawn from him is inexhaustible; what may be put to use never runs short. He possesses in full the entire breadth of these capacities.

Wherever the Son of Heaven employs him, there the gentleman proves equal to his task. When he enters and serves at court, he assists the king in ordering the realm, and I say that I have one to guide and assist me. When he goes out and serves beyond the court, he assists the king in pacifying the realm, and I say that I have one to repel aggression. Thus he is suited not only to civil affairs but also to military affairs. Is he not suited to them all? Wherever the Son of Heaven commands him to go, there the gentleman possesses the requisite capacities. In securing lasting peace, his plans for orderly government console the sovereign in his desire for tranquillity. In suppressing calamity and disorder, his imposing strategies accord with the sovereign’s plans to anticipate events. Thus he possesses not only civil accomplishments but also military preparedness. Is he not richly endowed?

Viewed from the left, he is therefore called well suited; yet he also possesses what is needed on the right and has never been confined to the left. Thus one may indeed say that there is nothing to which he is unsuited. Viewed from the right, he is therefore said to possess what is needed; yet he is also suited to service on the left and has never been confined to the right. Thus one may indeed say that there is nothing he does not possess. With a single gathering in the eastern capital, the six armies are roused. As for bringing blessings and emoluments as abundant as thatching reeds, and preserving the realm for ten thousand years, truly…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
於斯人乎有賴矣彼文章車馬云者何足以觀
君子之深哉嘗論才德之難久矣裨諶謀野則
獲而謀邑則否孟公綽優於趙魏老而不可為
滕薛大夫何則局於量也乃裳華所稱用之左
右而無施不可又若是其全且備者豈虛譽乎
哉諸侯來朝則敷奏之明試之而其言其功良
有明徵矣吾於是而知詩人非譽之也蓋試之
也抑亦因以勸戒之也歟
天子萬壽明明天子令聞不已
===

大臣答君必欲其永年而永譽也夫年與譽而
俱永天下之純嘏也大臣既祝之而復進之忠
愛寧有已哉詩人美召虎平淮之功此則述其
banxin: 鄉試錄 四十 姜忻
punctuated:
於斯人乎有賴矣！彼文章車馬云者，何足以觀君子之深哉？嘗論才德之難久矣。裨諶謀野則獲，而謀邑則否；孟公綽優於趙魏老，而不可為滕薛大夫。何則？局於量也。乃裳華所稱，用之左右而無施不可，又若是其全且備者，豈虛譽乎哉？諸侯來朝，則敷奏之，明試之，而其言其功，良有明徵矣。吾於是而知詩人非譽之也，蓋試之也，抑亦因以勸戒之也歟？

translation_en:
…depends upon such men! As for patterned robes, carriages, and horses, how could these suffice to reveal the gentleman’s depth? The difficulty of finding talent joined with virtue has long been discussed. Bi Chen succeeded when devising plans in the countryside, but not when doing so in the city. Meng Gongchuo was more than equal to serving as a household elder for the Zhao or Wei families, but could not serve as a grand master in Teng or Xue. Why? Their capacities had limits. Yet the man praised in “Shang hua” [“Glorious Blossoms,” ?] could be employed on either the left or the right, with no assignment beyond his ability. Could praise of someone so complete and fully accomplished be empty? When the feudal lords came to court, their statements were presented and their abilities clearly tested; there was indeed manifest evidence of both their words and their achievements. From this I know that the poet was not merely praising him, but putting him to the test—and perhaps also thereby encouraging and admonishing him!

“May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years! May the illustrious Son of Heaven’s good repute never cease.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor: 〔The wording is dignified, and loyalty and affection are abundantly evident. One may discuss with this writer the way of serving as a minister.〕
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔Abundant in expression and meaning.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
答稱之意也若曰帝王德至於天而必得其壽
德至於人而必得其名兼此二者故全也虎之
所以對揚王休者豈徒作召公考而已哉彼人
君以一身斂五福之全所不能必之天者壽也
而萬壽則無疆矣今我天子也統華夷之大而
爲中興之主崇高富貴此固其凝命之初耳必
自天祐之而難老永錫裕而爲悠遠之休威福
玉食此固其履端之始耳必自天申之而年所
多歷綿而爲永貞之慶俾爾壽而臧王心有常
寧也俾爾彌爾性君身有常固也蓋萬年此天
地則萬年此天子殆與文之壽考武之眉壽而
同其久矣然則江漢之朝宗固不獨今日爲爾
也而虎之所以承圭瓚土田之錫者不將永賴
於後世也哉人君以一身爲萬國之主所不能
必之人者令聞也而不已則有常矣今我明明
天子也懋脩攘之略而成中興之功以内則順
治而天下稱仁也要必有永保之謨焉而明王
之頌恒歸於知臨之大君以外則威嚴而天下
punctuated: 答稱之意也。若曰：帝王德至於天，而必得其壽；德至於人，而必得其名。兼此二者，故全也。虎之所以對揚王休者，豈徒作召公考而已哉？彼人君以一身斂五福之全，所不能必之天者，壽也；而萬壽則無疆矣。今我天子也，統華夷之大，而爲中興之主。崇高富貴，此固其凝命之初耳；必自天祐之而難老，永錫裕而爲悠遠之休。威福玉食，此固其履端之始耳；必自天申之而年所多歷，綿而爲永貞之慶。俾爾壽而臧，王心有常寧也；俾爾彌爾性，君身有常固也。蓋萬年此天地，則萬年此天子，殆與文之壽考、武之眉壽而同其久矣。然則江漢之朝宗，固不獨今日爲爾也；而虎之所以承圭瓚土田之錫者，不將永賴於後世也哉？人君以一身爲萬國之主，所不能必之人者，令聞也；而不已則有常矣。今我明明天子也，懋脩攘之略，而成中興之功。以内則順治，而天下稱仁也；要必有永保之謨焉，而明王之頌恒歸於知臨之大君。以外則威嚴，而天下
translation_en:
…the meaning of his words in response to the royal commendation. It is as though he said: When an emperor’s virtue reaches Heaven, he must receive longevity; when his virtue reaches the people, he must receive renown. Possessing both, he is therefore complete. In responding to and extolling the king’s favor, was Hu merely completing the work of the Duke of Shao?

The ruler gathers the fullness of the five blessings in his own person. What he cannot be certain of obtaining from Heaven is longevity; yet longevity of ten thousand years knows no bounds. Our present Son of Heaven rules the vast domains of Chinese and non-Chinese peoples and is the sovereign of a dynastic resurgence. Lofty rank, wealth, and honor are merely the beginning of his securing the Mandate. Heaven must bless him so that he scarcely ages, forever granting abundance to constitute lasting favor. The power to punish and reward, and the enjoyment of precious food, are merely the outset of his reign. Heaven must renew its blessings so that he passes through many years, extending them into the blessing of enduring constancy. “May you live long and prosper”: the king’s heart enjoys lasting peace. “May you fulfill your allotted span”: the ruler’s person enjoys lasting security. For if this Heaven and Earth endure ten thousand years, this Son of Heaven will endure ten thousand years, virtually equaling the long life of King Wen and the venerable longevity of King Wu. Thus, the Jiang and Han rivers’ homage to the sea is certainly not confined to this day. And will not Hu’s receipt of the jade tablet, the jade-handled libation ladle, and lands and fields bring enduring benefit to later generations?

The ruler in his single person is lord of the myriad states. What he cannot be certain of obtaining from others is a good reputation; yet if it never ceases, it endures constantly. Our present illustrious Son of Heaven diligently develops strategies for internal cultivation and the repulsion of external threats, thereby accomplishing a dynastic resurgence. Within his realm, government is orderly, and all under Heaven praise his benevolence. There must, however, be plans to preserve this forever, so that praise of the enlightened king continually accrues to the great sovereign who governs with wisdom. Beyond his realm, his authority inspires awe, and all under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
稱義也要必有永終之道焉而聖人之歌常集
於聰明之元后其實愈大而其聲愈弘也其積
愈厚而其光愈遠也盖天子此萬年則令聞亦
此萬年殆與文之聿駿武之顯名而同其美矣
然則江漢之聲靈固不獨今日爲爾也而虎之
效經營疆理之勞者亦將有詞於永世也哉吁
先之以萬壽而得聞以彰之則壽爲有光繼之
以令聞而得壽以承之則聞爲有藉于此見召
公報禮之重而其言亦可繹思矣抑論壽非倖
===
致也必有以爲享壽之原聞非襲取也必有以
爲致聞之實萬壽令聞召公豈徒諛其君者至
篇終則曰矢其文德洽此四國此所謂原所謂
實也亦康公卷阿之遺法歟歆以壽考福祿之
盛而歸於用馮翼孝德之賢頌不忘規有自來
矣詩曰召公是似甚矣虎之似乎奭也

李伯廉
punctuated:
稱義也，要必有永終之道焉，而聖人之歌常集於聰明之元后。其實愈大，而其聲愈弘也；其積愈厚，而其光愈遠也。盖天子此萬年，則令聞亦此萬年，殆與文之聿駿、武之顯名而同其美矣。然則江漢之聲靈，固不獨今日爲爾也；而虎之效經營疆理之勞者，亦將有詞於永世也哉！吁！先之以萬壽，而得聞以彰之，則壽爲有光；繼之以令聞，而得壽以承之，則聞爲有藉。于此見召公報禮之重，而其言亦可繹思矣。抑論壽非倖致也，必有以爲享壽之原；聞非襲取也，必有以爲致聞之實。萬壽令聞，召公豈徒諛其君者？至篇終則曰：「矢其文德，洽此四國。」此所謂原、所謂實也。亦康公《卷阿》之遺法歟？歆以壽考福祿之盛，而歸於用馮翼孝德之賢，頌不忘規，有自來矣。《詩》曰：「召公是似。」甚矣，虎之似乎奭也！

春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕
李伯廉
translation_en:
…acclaimed for righteousness. There must assuredly be a way to sustain this to the very end, so that songs praising the sage will continually converge upon the discerning sovereign. The greater his actual achievements, the more far-reaching his renown; the richer his accumulated virtue, the farther his radiance extends. If the Son of Heaven enjoys these ten thousand years, his good reputation will likewise endure for ten thousand years, matching in glory King Wen’s illustrious greatness and King Wu’s manifest fame. Thus the awe-inspiring prestige celebrated in “The Jiang and Han Rivers” will assuredly not be confined to the present day; and Hu’s labors in ordering the realm and demarcating its territories will also be commemorated in words for all time!

Ah! First comes the wish for boundless longevity: when reputation lends it distinction, longevity acquires splendor. Next comes the wish for a good reputation: when longevity sustains it, reputation gains support. Here we see the weight the Duke of Shao attached to reciprocating the king’s ceremonial favor; his words also deserve thoughtful consideration. Yet longevity does not come by chance: there must be a foundation for enjoying it. Reputation cannot simply be appropriated: there must be substantial achievements that bring it about. In wishing his ruler boundless longevity and a good reputation, could the Duke of Shao have been merely flattering him? At the poem’s end he says: “Set forth your civil virtue, and bring harmony to these four quarters.” This is what is meant by that foundation and that substance. Is this also the method handed down by Duke Kang in “The Winding Mound” (Juan a)? He inspires the ruler with the abundance of longevity, blessings, and emoluments, but ultimately directs him toward employing worthy men who offer support and possess filial virtue. Praise that does not forget admonition has a long history. The Book of Odes says: “The Duke of Shao is whom you resemble.” How closely Hu indeed resembled Shi!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, men of Song, men of Qi, and men of Zhu attacked Ni.” 〔The fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Li Bolian

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭袁批題本平淡而作更豐腴是深於
春秋者
同考試官教授蔣批結着齊桓管仲之意當是如此
考試官教諭何批嚴整中式
考試官教諭錢批雅健
春秋紀兵權之有屬見伯業之未成此伐郳之
役桓雖圖伯而猶未成乎伯也不然何以後于
主兵之宋乎昔管仲相桓肇始伯業北杏之後
會宋伐郳夫伯者之先諸侯例也桓既伯矣何
===
以序于宋下蓋天下有伯則專征之權在伯主
天下無伯則主兵之柄在諸侯茲焉桓也心雖
切于匡世而尊主庇民之業不可以旦夕而成
志雖在于主盟而攘夷安夏之勳未可以歲月
而集伐宋之師甞以威震諸侯矣而威未能遽
伸也威不伸而何以萃天下之渙于鄄之會甞
以信懷諸侯矣而信未能遽洽也信不洽而何
以合天下之離是故伐郳之師主兵者猶屬于
三恪之宋而大邦未見其盡畏也桓豈不欲仗
punctuated:
同考試官教諭袁批：「題本平淡，而作更豐腴，是深於《春秋》者。」
同考試官教授蔣批：「結着齊桓管仲之意，當是如此。」
考試官教諭何批：「嚴整中式。」
考試官教諭錢批：「雅健。」
《春秋》紀兵權之有屬，見伯業之未成。此伐郳之役，桓雖圖伯，而猶未成乎伯也。不然，何以後于主兵之宋乎？昔管仲相桓，肇始伯業，北杏之後，會宋伐郳。夫伯者之先諸侯，例也。桓既伯矣，何以序于宋下？蓋天下有伯，則專征之權在伯主；天下無伯，則主兵之柄在諸侯。茲焉桓也，心雖切于匡世，而尊主庇民之業，不可以旦夕而成；志雖在于主盟，而攘夷安夏之勳，未可以歲月而集。伐宋之師，甞以威震諸侯矣，而威未能遽伸也。威不伸，而何以萃天下之渙？于鄄之會，甞以信懷諸侯矣，而信未能遽洽也。信不洽，而何以合天下之離？是故伐郳之師，主兵者猶屬于三恪之宋，而大邦未見其盡畏也。桓豈不欲仗
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is plain, but the composition gives it greater richness. This is someone deeply versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals.”
Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “The conclusion brings out the intentions of Duke Huan of Qi and Guan Zhong. This is just how it should be.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Rigorous and orderly, conforming to the prescribed form.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records where military authority lay, revealing that the hegemonic enterprise was not yet accomplished. In this campaign against Ni, although Duke Huan sought hegemony, he had not yet become hegemon. Otherwise, why would he be placed after Song, which commanded the troops? Formerly, when Guan Zhong served as Duke Huan’s chief minister and initiated his hegemonic enterprise, after the meeting at Beixing they joined Song in attacking Ni. Now, it is the rule that the hegemon precedes the other feudal lords. If Huan was already hegemon, why was he listed below Song? When the realm has a hegemon, authority to undertake punitive expeditions on his own initiative rests with the hegemonic lord; when the realm has no hegemon, command of troops rests with the feudal lords. At this time, although Huan’s heart was set on putting the world to rights, the work of honoring the sovereign and protecting the people could not be accomplished overnight. Although he aspired to preside over covenants, the achievement of repelling the Yi and securing the Xia could not yet be brought to completion within mere months or years. In the campaign against Song, he had already awed the feudal lords with his might, yet that might could not immediately extend everywhere. Without its extension, how could he gather together the scattered elements of the realm? At the meeting at Juan, he had already won over the feudal lords through his trustworthiness, yet that trust could not immediately permeate everywhere. Without its permeation, how could he unite the divided elements of the realm? Thus, in the campaign against Ni, command of the troops still belonged to Song, one of the Three Honored Lineages, and the great states had not yet shown that they all stood in awe of him. How could Huan not have wished to wield …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
鉞而臨戎哉顧諸侯之不親輿情之未附亦紓
徐以俟其成而已從兵者僅止于附庸之郳而
小邾未見其盡懷也桓豈不欲徵兵以討貳哉
顧衆志之未定專欲之難成亦委曲以求其濟
而已後此而南征北略桓之績固偉也而不知
其有待于陳鄭同盟之後爲宋伐郕此其肇謀
之日耳不然奉揚寔征之命齊將帥宋以從事
矣又安能爲之下乎後此而九合一匡桓之功
固大也而不知其有假于三十年經營之力因
===
人成事特其創業之初耳不然光昭賜履之勳
宋將悉賦以從齊矣又安敢爲之上乎聖人序
齊于宋下雖以著其伯業未成之實亦以望其
有成之意也吁此見春秋之不可無齊桓而聖
人之惓惓于桓者其爲世道慮也夫抑有疑焉
齊宋匹也齊方伐宋而遽從之以兵豈宋眞能
令齊哉無亦以上公之宋人望攸屬從宋則宋
可服宋服而諸侯可坐致矣嗚呼此桓之微意
也抑亦仲之謀也惜也始之以憂勤繼之以矜
punctuated:
鉞而臨戎哉？顧諸侯之不親，輿情之未附，亦紓徐以俟其成而已。從兵者僅止于附庸之郳，而小邾未見其盡懷也。桓豈不欲徵兵以討貳哉？顧衆志之未定，專欲之難成，亦委曲以求其濟而已。後此而南征北略，桓之績固偉也，而不知其有待于陳鄭同盟之後。爲宋伐郕，此其肇謀之日耳。不然，奉揚寔征之命，齊將帥宋以從事矣，又安能爲之下乎？後此而九合一匡，桓之功固大也，而不知其有假于三十年經營之力。因人成事，特其創業之初耳。不然，光昭賜履之勳，宋將悉賦以從齊矣，又安敢爲之上乎？聖人序齊于宋下，雖以著其伯業未成之實，亦以望其有成之意也。吁！此見春秋之不可無齊桓，而聖人之惓惓于桓者，其爲世道慮也夫！

抑有疑焉：齊宋匹也，齊方伐宋，而遽從之以兵，豈宋眞能令齊哉？無亦以上公之宋，人望攸屬，從宋則宋可服，宋服而諸侯可坐致矣。嗚呼！此桓之微意也，抑亦仲之謀也。惜也！始之以憂勤，繼之以矜
translation_en:
…the battle-axe and personally command in war? Yet, considering that the regional lords were not close to him and popular sentiment had not rallied to him, he could only proceed patiently and await success. Those following in the campaign amounted merely to Ni, a dependent state, while Xiao Zhu had not yet shown complete allegiance [?]. Did Duke Huan not wish to levy troops to punish disloyalty? Yet, considering that men’s minds were unsettled and that his wishes alone could hardly secure success, he could only accommodate circumstances and seek to bring his undertaking to fruition.

After this, Huan campaigned south and north, and his achievements were indeed magnificent. Yet people fail to recognize that these had to await his alliance with Chen and Zheng. Attacking Cheng on Song’s behalf belonged merely to the days when he first laid his plans. Otherwise, in carrying out and upholding the royal command to undertake punitive expeditions, Qi would have led Song into action: how could it have stood below Song? After this, Huan nine times assembled the lords and once set the realm aright; his accomplishments were indeed great. Yet people fail to recognize that these depended upon thirty years of sustained effort. Accomplishing things through others belonged merely to the beginning of his enterprise. Otherwise, in gloriously displaying the achievements associated with his royally granted territory, Song would have mobilized all its military resources to follow Qi: how would it have dared stand above Qi?

In placing Qi below Song, the Sage not only made clear that Huan’s enterprise as hegemon was still incomplete, but also expressed his hope that it would succeed. Ah! This shows that the Spring and Autumn period could not have done without Duke Huan of Qi. The Sage’s deep concern for Huan surely arose from his concern for the moral and political order of the age!

Yet a doubt remains. Qi and Song were peers. Qi had just attacked Song, yet suddenly followed it with troops: could Song really command Qi? Was it not rather that Song, possessing the senior ducal rank, was where men’s hopes converged? By following Song, Huan could secure Song’s submission; once Song submitted, the regional lords could be won over without further exertion. Ah! This was Huan’s subtle intention, and also Zhong’s strategy. What a pity! He began with anxious diligence, but followed it with pride…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
伐召陵盟濤塗執而桓之志荒矣噫此齊桓之
業所以止于伯歟
公會晉侯宋公衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚　楚人執鄭行人良霄〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐
子滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子
佐淮夷會于申〔昭公四年〕
方繼懋
===
同考試官教諭袁　批　措詞嚴正命意精深傑作也
同考試官教授蔣　批　以謀駕楚以誠服鄭古字類能言之充暢則惟見此篇
考　試　官教諭何　批　謹嚴
考　試　官教諭錢　批　詞意裕如
伯主得駕外服內之道而成功春秋所以善之
也此見晉悼謀足以屈楚而誠足以服鄭也偉
矣哉復伯之績乎且晉文襄之業中微悼公思
起而振之當是時北嚮與晉爭諸侯者楚也楚
punctuated:
伐，召陵盟，濤塗執，而桓之志荒矣。噫！此齊桓之業所以止于伯歟？

公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。楚人執鄭行人良霄。〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕

方繼懋

同考試官教諭袁批：措詞嚴正，命意精深，傑作也。
同考試官教授蔣批：以謀駕楚，以誠服鄭，古字類能言之，充暢則惟見此篇。
考試官教諭何批：謹嚴。
考試官教諭錢批：詞意裕如。

伯主得駕外服內之道而成功，《春秋》所以善之也。此見晉悼謀足以屈楚，而誠足以服鄭也。偉矣哉，復伯之績乎！且晉文、襄之業中微，悼公思起而振之。當是時，北嚮與晉爭諸侯者，楚也。楚
translation_en:
…boasting; the covenant was concluded at Shaoling and Tao Tu was seized, and Duke Huan’s ambition went astray. Alas! Was this why Duke Huan of Qi’s achievement stopped at hegemony?

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. The men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, Zheng’s envoy. 〔Both entries are from the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquises of Cai and Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscounts of Xu, Teng, Dun, Hu, Shen, and Lesser Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen. 〔The fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Fang Jimao

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The wording is rigorous and upright; the conception is subtle and profound. A masterpiece.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor: “‘To master Chu through strategy and win Zheng’s submission through sincerity’: writings of old could generally express this [?], but only in this essay have I seen it developed so fully and fluently.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “Careful and rigorous.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “Ample command of both expression and ideas.”

A hegemon achieves success by finding the way to master those outside and secure the submission of those within: this is why the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him. Here we see that Duke Dao of Jin possessed strategy sufficient to subdue Chu and sincerity sufficient to win Zheng’s submission. How magnificent was his achievement in restoring the hegemony! The enterprise of Dukes Wen and Xiang of Jin had declined in the intervening years, and Duke Dao sought to rise and revive it. At that time, it was Chu that faced north and contended with Jin for the allegiance of the feudal lords. Chu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不屈伯不可得而復也中立而依違於晉楚之
間者鄭也鄭不從伯亦不可得而復也人皆曰
蠢爾之荆可以力制悼則不任力而任謀焉息
民取之魏絳善陣聽于知罃施舍輸積導利而
民悅矣減牲更幣制度而財節矣三分四軍不
戰而氣自倍矣羣策畢舉而坐得勝算悼之所
以駕楚者豈徒以其力耶人皆曰反覆之鄭可
以威懾悼則不用威而用誠焉許伯駢而不拒
信子展而不疑禮囚歸俘無係累之慘矣納候
===
禁侵無猜暴之患矣遣使脩告咸喻乎諸侯之
志矣推心置腹而攜貳獻誠悼之所以服鄭者
豈徒以其威耶由是楚雖強也悼之謀足以制
之三駕罷兵之後爭鄭之心頓沮雖以良霄之
告絕而僅執使泄忿焉蓋雖欲抗晉而不能抗
晉之謀也使暴骨以逞則楚勝而晉亦病矣況
兩廣爭雄固楚之長技也又豈遽出晉人下哉
由是鄭雖貳也悼之誠足以孚之東門觀兵之
後從晉之念遂堅至于楚虔之會申而始獻禮
punctuated: 不屈，伯不可得而復也。中立而依違於晉楚之間者，鄭也；鄭不從，伯亦不可得而復也。人皆曰：「蠢爾之荆，可以力制。」悼則不任力而任謀焉。息民取之魏絳，善陣聽于知罃，施舍輸積，導利而民悅矣；減牲更幣，制度而財節矣；三分四軍，不戰而氣自倍矣。羣策畢舉而坐得勝算，悼之所以駕楚者，豈徒以其力耶？人皆曰：「反覆之鄭，可以威懾。」悼則不用威而用誠焉。許伯駢而不拒，信子展而不疑，禮囚歸俘，無係累之慘矣；納候禁侵，無猜暴之患矣；遣使脩告，咸喻乎諸侯之志矣。推心置腹而攜貳獻誠，悼之所以服鄭者，豈徒以其威耶？由是楚雖強也，悼之謀足以制之。三駕罷兵之後，爭鄭之心頓沮；雖以良霄之告絕，而僅執使泄忿焉。蓋雖欲抗晉，而不能抗晉之謀也。使暴骨以逞，則楚勝而晉亦病矣。況兩廣爭雄，固楚之長技也，又豈遽出晉人下哉？由是鄭雖貳也，悼之誠足以孚之。東門觀兵之後，從晉之念遂堅，至于楚虔之會申，而始獻禮
translation_en:
…unless Chu were subdued, the hegemony could not be restored. It was Zheng that stood between Jin and Chu, wavering in its allegiance; unless Zheng submitted, the hegemony likewise could not be restored. Everyone said, “That unruly Jing can be controlled by force.” Yet Duke Dao relied on strategy rather than force. For giving the people respite, he adopted Wei Jiang’s counsel; for skillful military dispositions, he listened to Zhi Ying. He distributed relief, granted remissions, and transported accumulated supplies, promoting the people’s welfare and winning their satisfaction. He reduced sacrificial animals and altered ceremonial gifts, regulating expenditure and conserving resources. He divided the four armies into three contingents, and their vigor redoubled without battle. Bringing all these strategies into play, he secured the means of victory at ease. Was force alone how Duke Dao held Chu in check?

Everyone said, “Fickle Zheng can be overawed by might.” Yet Duke Dao employed sincerity rather than intimidation. He granted Bo Pian’s request without rejecting it and trusted Zizhan without suspicion. He treated prisoners courteously and returned captives, sparing them the misery of bondage. He admitted scouts [?] and prohibited incursions, removing the troubles caused by suspicion and violence. He dispatched envoys to renew communications, fully explaining the intentions of the feudal lords. By opening his heart, he induced those wavering in allegiance to offer their loyalty. Was might alone how Duke Dao brought Zheng into submission?

Thus, although Chu was powerful, Duke Dao’s strategy sufficed to control it. After the three campaigns had ended and the armies had withdrawn, Chu’s determination to contest possession of Zheng abruptly faltered. Even when Liang Xiao announced the severance of relations, Chu merely detained the envoy to vent its anger. Although Chu wished to resist Jin, it could not withstand Jin’s strategy. Had Duke Dao sought gratification through warfare that left bones exposed, even if Chu had been overcome, Jin too would have been exhausted. Moreover, vying for supremacy with its two chariot divisions was precisely Chu’s particular strength. How could it readily have proved inferior to Jin?

Thus, although Zheng wavered in allegiance, Duke Dao’s sincerity sufficed to win its trust. After the display of troops at the eastern gate, its resolve to follow Jin became firm. Only when Qian of Chu convened the meeting at Shen did Zheng begin to present ceremonial offerings…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
從事焉蓋雖欲叛晉而不忍叛晉之誠也使强
之以威則鄭服而晉亦勞矣況二境玉帛固鄭
之故智也又豈終在晉宇下哉吁駕楚以謀制
人而不制于人也服鄭以誠信人而人亦信之
也此晉悼伯事之善所以克復文襄之烈而蕭
魚之會春秋特書以美之歟抑蕭魚之功美矣
所以處美者未盡也懿親之鄭撫而有之可也
女樂之賂奚納焉楚既服矣焉用勤諸侯以謀
吳豈其侈心之萌不能自制而魏知諸臣猶有
===
遺策乎雖然晉伯復興楚氛未燄以平昭之庸
猶爲諸侯師則以悼之餘烈在也悼其可少乎
哉
禮記
其功大者其樂備其治辨者其禮具
姚士觀
同考試官教諭李批分別功治俱有條理是宜
究心於制作之原者

punctuated:
從事焉，蓋雖欲叛晉，而不忍叛晉之誠也。使强之以威，則鄭服而晉亦勞矣。況二境玉帛，固鄭之故智也，又豈終在晉宇下哉？吁！駕楚以謀，制人而不制于人也；服鄭以誠，信人而人亦信之也。此晉悼伯事之善，所以克復文襄之烈，而蕭魚之會，《春秋》特書以美之歟！抑蕭魚之功美矣，所以處美者未盡也。懿親之鄭，撫而有之可也，女樂之賂奚納焉？楚既服矣，焉用勤諸侯以謀吳？豈其侈心之萌不能自制，而魏知諸臣猶有遺策乎？雖然，晉伯復興，楚氛未燄，以平昭之庸猶爲諸侯師，則以悼之餘烈在也。悼其可少乎哉！

…and entered their service. Even if Zheng wished to rebel against Jin, it could not bear to betray Jin’s sincerity. Had Jin compelled it through force, Zheng would have submitted, but Jin too would have been wearied. Moreover, offering jade and silk at both borders was Zheng’s familiar stratagem: how could it have remained forever under Jin’s roof? Ah! To master Chu through strategy was to control others without being controlled by them; to win Zheng’s submission through sincerity was to trust others and receive their trust in return. Such was the excellence of Duke Dao of Jin’s conduct as hegemon. It enabled him to restore the achievements of Dukes Wen and Xiang, and surely explains why the Spring and Autumn Annals specially recorded the meeting at Xiaoyu in praise of him!

Yet, admirable as the achievement at Xiaoyu was, his handling of that success was not wholly satisfactory. It was proper to cherish Zheng, a closely related state, and retain its allegiance; why accept its gift of female musicians? Once Chu had submitted, why trouble the feudal lords with plans concerning Wu? Could it be that he could not restrain his budding extravagance, and that the ministers of the Wei and Zhi lineages still left something wanting in their counsels? Nevertheless, Jin’s hegemony revived, and Chu’s threatening influence had yet to blaze up. Even men as mediocre as Dukes Ping and Zhao could still lead the feudal lords because Duke Dao’s achievements continued to exert their force. Can Duke Dao be held in little esteem?

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
〔然而本之天德尤見卓識〕
考試官敎諭錢批〔發揮精到可以爲文矣〕
論治功之盛者必極其制作之隆焉甚矣禮樂
非無因而作也功大治辯而制作其有不隆者
乎記樂記者其意蓋謂帝王之御世也固必有
禮樂以昭一代之制尤必因治功以爲制作之
基是豈可以强爲者哉彼樂作於功成之後則
樂者所以象此功也功有未大斯樂有未備矣
惟夫帝績所凝著地平天成之效王業所建極
===
民和物阜之徵此則無爲而成凡天下之言功
者孰得而尚之可謂大矣由是而播之於樂也
吾見情深文明而諧之八音有以洩其雍容之
象德厚流光而奕之萬舞有以彰其揖遜之風
美善於是乎兼該也情文於是乎具舉也在王
者非有心於樂之備而豐功之洋溢自與天地
而同其和矣樂其有不備乎禮制於治定之餘
則禮者所以飾此治也治有未辯斯禮有未具
矣惟夫黎民敏德妙於變時雍之休四方從欲
punctuated:
〔然而本之天德，尤見卓識。〕
考試官敎諭錢批〔發揮精到，可以爲文矣。〕
論治功之盛者，必極其制作之隆焉。甚矣，禮樂非無因而作也！功大治辯，而制作其有不隆者乎？記樂記者，其意蓋謂帝王之御世也，固必有禮樂以昭一代之制，尤必因治功以爲制作之基，是豈可以强爲者哉？彼樂作於功成之後，則樂者所以象此功也。功有未大，斯樂有未備矣。惟夫帝績所凝著，地平天成之效；王業所建極，民和物阜之徵。此則無爲而成，凡天下之言功者，孰得而尚之？可謂大矣。由是而播之於樂也，吾見情深文明，而諧之八音，有以洩其雍容之象；德厚流光，而奕之萬舞，有以彰其揖遜之風。美善於是乎兼該也，情文於是乎具舉也。在王者，非有心於樂之備，而豐功之洋溢，自與天地而同其和矣。樂其有不備乎？禮制於治定之餘，則禮者所以飾此治也。治有未辯，斯禮有未具矣。惟夫黎民敏德，妙於變時雍之休；四方從欲
translation_en:
〔…Yet in grounding it in heavenly virtue, he displays especially outstanding insight.〕
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔The exposition is perceptive and precise: this may indeed be called accomplished writing.〕
Anyone discussing the flourishing achievements of government must fully explore the magnificence of its ritual and musical institutions. How profound it is that rites and music are never instituted without a basis! When achievements are great and government well ordered, could these institutions fail to flourish? The author of the Record of Music presumably meant that, in governing the world, emperors and kings certainly require rites and music to manifest the institutions of their age; above all, they must take the achievements of government as the foundation for establishing those institutions. How could this be accomplished by force?
Music is created after achievements have been brought to completion; thus music serves to represent those achievements. If the achievements are not yet great, the music will not yet be complete. Consider imperial accomplishments embodied in the results of earth being brought to order and heaven’s work fulfilled, and the royal enterprise establishing the highest standard, evidenced by harmony among the people and abundance in all things. These are accomplished through nonaction. Of all the achievements spoken of throughout the world, what could surpass them? They may indeed be called great.
When these are then expressed in music, I see profound feeling and brilliant cultural expression harmonized through the eight classes of musical instruments, conveying an image of dignified ease; abundant virtue, whose radiance spreads afar, splendidly displayed in the wan dance, manifesting the spirit of courteous deference. Beauty and goodness are thereby both encompassed; inner feeling and outward form are thereby fully expressed. The king does not deliberately seek completeness in music: rather, the overflowing abundance of his achievements naturally shares the harmony of heaven and earth. How could his music fail to be complete?
Rites are instituted after government has been settled; thus rites serve to adorn that government. If government is not yet well ordered, the rites will not yet be fully provided. Consider the common people diligently pursuing virtue, wondrously attaining the blessings of transformation and concord, and the four quarters following the ruler’s wishes…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
丕協和風動之化此則垂拱而定凡天下之言
治者孰得而加之可謂辯矣由是而飾之以禮
也吾見顯設於章程而本末兼體有以昭秩敘
之常敷施於物采而文質適均有以貫亨嘉之
會品節於是乎克全也經制於是乎大備也在
王者非有心於禮之具而至治之敷宣自與天
地而同其節矣禮其有不具乎吁樂備於功之
大則聞其樂而功之崇卑可知也禮具於治之
辯則見其禮而治之隆汙可知也記者以是而
===
論禮樂殆觀其深矣甞觀子夏之告文侯謂大
當而後制禮大定而後作樂則知古之帝王惟
其時位相符治功竝懋見之制作固粹然而無
議矣然有本之於身以妙制作之原而出於治
功之外者中正和樂是也天德也制作不本於
天德而徒曰治功焉抑末矣然則禮樂固因於
治功而天德尤其本也
天子者與天地參
劉良弼
punctuated:
丕協和風動之化，此則垂拱而定，凡天下之言治者，孰得而加之？可謂辯矣。由是而飾之以禮也，吾見顯設於章程，而本末兼體，有以昭秩敘之常；敷施於物采，而文質適均，有以貫亨嘉之會。品節於是乎克全也，經制於是乎大備也。在王者非有心於禮之具，而至治之敷宣，自與天地而同其節矣。禮其有不具乎？吁！樂備於功之大，則聞其樂而功之崇卑可知也；禮具於治之辯，則見其禮而治之隆汙可知也。記者以是而論禮樂，殆觀其深矣。甞觀子夏之告文侯，謂大當而後制禮，大定而後作樂，則知古之帝王，惟其時位相符，治功竝懋，見之制作，固粹然而無議矣。然有本之於身，以妙制作之原，而出於治功之外者，中正和樂是也，天德也。制作不本於天德，而徒曰治功焉，抑末矣。然則禮樂固因於治功，而天德尤其本也。

天子者，與天地參。
劉良弼
translation_en:
…fully accord with the transforming influence that moves like the wind. Thus order is established with the ruler merely folding his hands. Of all under Heaven who speak of good government, who could surpass this? It may indeed be called well ordered. When this is then adorned with ritual, I see it visibly embodied in regulations, with root and branches alike incorporated, thereby making manifest the constant principles of rank and precedence; and extended to objects and ornament, with refinement and substance properly balanced, thereby bringing together all that flourishes and is auspicious. Its gradations and restraints are thus complete, and its enduring institutions fully established. It is not that the true king deliberately seeks completeness in ritual: rather, the diffusion of perfect government naturally shares the measured order of Heaven and Earth. How could ritual fail to be complete?

Ah! Since music becomes fully developed through the greatness of achievements, one can hear the music and know how lofty or low those achievements are. Since ritual becomes complete through the thorough ordering of government, one can observe the ritual and know whether government is flourishing or debased. The author of the Record discusses ritual and music on this basis; surely he has perceived their depths. I have read what Zixia told Marquis Wen: only after things are thoroughly fitting is ritual instituted, and only after order is firmly established is music created. Thus we know that the emperors and kings of antiquity, whose times and positions accorded and whose government and achievements alike flourished, expressed these in institutions that were indeed pure and beyond criticism.

Yet there is something rooted in one's own person that perfects the source of institutional creation and extends beyond government and achievement: centrality, correctness, harmony, and joy. These are the virtue of Heaven. To create institutions without grounding them in the virtue of Heaven, speaking merely of government and achievement, is surely to attend only to the branches. Thus ritual and music certainly arise from government and achievement, but the virtue of Heaven is their still more fundamental root.

“The Son of Heaven Forms a Triad with Heaven and Earth”
Liu Liangbi

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批〔詞典雅而意宏闊十一日善〕
〔發三才之蘊者〕
考試官教諭何批〔只就參字發揮而條理森〕
〔然自著殆非淺學所及可敬可敬〕
考試官教諭錢批〔理明詞暢〕
惟聖人在上而克配乎造化焉蓋法象莫大乎
天地也聖人在天子之位而有以參之其諸合
上下而一之者乎經解載夫子之言及此若曰
天子之與天地自其迹之殊者而擬之若不可
===
以比而爲一自其理之同者而觀之則實可以
參而爲三今夫君天下者曰天子聰明本於天
縱而正位凝命以膺帝眷之隆睿知由於夙成
而宅中圖大以建維皇之極夫固極天下之至
尊矣然何以能與天地參哉蓋以昊天其子端
拱以臨四方雖混然中處也而道萃貞元之會
自合上下以同流百辟其刑中正以觀天下固
巍然莫京也而首出民物之倫自與貞觀而相
準天位乎上以氣運地位乎下以形運天子位
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批〔詞典雅而意宏闊，十一日善〕〔發三才之蘊者。〕
考試官教諭何批〔只就參字發揮，而條理森〕〔然自著，殆非淺學所及，可敬可敬。〕
考試官教諭錢批〔理明詞暢。〕
惟聖人在上，而克配乎造化焉。蓋法象莫大乎天地也，聖人在天子之位而有以參之，其諸合上下而一之者乎？《經解》載夫子之言及此，若曰：天子之與天地，自其迹之殊者而擬之，若不可以比而爲一；自其理之同者而觀之，則實可以參而爲三。今夫君天下者曰天子，聰明本於天縱，而正位凝命，以膺帝眷之隆；睿知由於夙成，而宅中圖大，以建維皇之極。夫固極天下之至尊矣，然何以能與天地參哉？蓋以昊天其子，端拱以臨四方，雖混然中處也，而道萃貞元之會，自合上下以同流；百辟其刑，中正以觀天下，固巍然莫京也，而首出民物之倫，自與貞觀而相準。天位乎上以氣運，地位乎下以形運，天子位
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The diction is classical and elegant, and the conception broad and expansive. ‘Eleven days, good’ [?]; it brings out the hidden significance of the Three Powers.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “It develops only the word ‘participate,’ yet its orderly structure emerges distinctly of itself. This is surely beyond the reach of shallow learning. Admirable, admirable!”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent.”
Only a sage occupying the highest position can match the creative and transforming powers of the cosmos. For among models and exemplars, none is greater than Heaven and Earth. When a sage occupies the position of the Son of Heaven and can participate with them, does he not unite what is above and below into one? The ‘Explanation of the Classics’ records words of the Master concerning this, as though to say: if we compare the Son of Heaven with Heaven and Earth in terms of their differing manifestations, they seem incapable of being equated and treated as one; but if we view them in terms of the principle they share, they can indeed stand together as three.
Now, he who rules all under Heaven is called the Son of Heaven. His perceptiveness and understanding are Heaven-bestowed; he takes his rightful position and secures the Mandate, receiving the abundant favor of the Lord on High. His sagely wisdom matures early; he dwells at the center and plans great undertakings, establishing the sovereign’s supreme standard. He assuredly occupies the utmost position of honor under Heaven. Yet how can he participate with Heaven and Earth?
It is because august Heaven regards him as its son. Sitting upright with hands folded, he presides over the four quarters. Although he occupies the center in undifferentiated unity, his Way gathers within itself the conjunction of completion and renewal, naturally uniting above and below in a common flow. The many lords take him as their model. Through centrality and correctness, he presents himself as an exemplar to all under Heaven. Though loftily without peer, he stands foremost among the ranks of people and things, naturally conforming to the constant pattern displayed by Heaven and Earth. Heaven is positioned above and operates through vital energy; Earth is positioned below and operates through physical form; the Son of Heaven is positioned …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎中而以化運立此參彼有以神夫協一之機
天確然以統元氣地隤然以統元形天子渾然
以統元化合異爲同有以極夫兼兩之妙人見
其撫萬邦而克艱以爲不若天地之無心也而
不知其參和不偏三才昭竝立之體所以爲天
地之宗子者此也人見其運萬幾而無斁以爲
不若天地之無憂也而不知其範圍不過三極
立大中之矩所以爲天下之至人者此也上律
下襲造化其爲徒焉蓋彼非有餘而此非不足
===
者矣兩儀攸分豈不與之異位而同神也哉仰
觀俯察天地其惟肖焉蓋彼非獨隆而此非獨
歉者矣乾坤奠位豈不與之異形而同體也哉
謂之曰與天地參信乎非天子不能同天地之
大而非天地不足以見天子之大矣觀天子者
盍亦求端於天地已乎抑論天子參天地非徒
以形象之合而已也要必有德爲之本焉克明
俊德顧諟明命聖人所以亹亹而不懈亦惟恃
此以求合於天地耳故格天之業至今誦之不
punctuated: 乎中而以化運，立此參彼，有以神夫協一之機。天確然以統元氣，地隤然以統元形，天子渾然以統元化，合異爲同，有以極夫兼兩之妙。人見其撫萬邦而克艱，以爲不若天地之無心也，而不知其參和不偏，三才昭竝立之體，所以爲天地之宗子者此也。人見其運萬幾而無斁，以爲不若天地之無憂也，而不知其範圍不過，三極立大中之矩，所以爲天下之至人者此也。上律下襲，造化其爲徒焉，蓋彼非有餘而此非不足者矣。兩儀攸分，豈不與之異位而同神也哉？仰觀俯察，天地其惟肖焉，蓋彼非獨隆而此非獨歉者矣。乾坤奠位，豈不與之異形而同體也哉？謂之曰「與天地參」，信乎非天子不能同天地之大，而非天地不足以見天子之大矣。觀天子者，盍亦求端於天地已乎？抑論天子參天地，非徒以形象之合而已也，要必有德爲之本焉。克明俊德，顧諟明命，聖人所以亹亹而不懈，亦惟恃此以求合於天地耳。故格天之業，至今誦之不
translation_en:
… in the center and operates through transformative influence. Established here as a third alongside those two, he gives wondrous efficacy to the workings of their unity. Heaven, firm and steadfast, governs the primal vital force; Earth, yielding and compliant, governs primal form; the Son of Heaven, an undivided whole, governs primal transformation. Bringing what differs into unity, he fully realizes the subtle power of embracing both. People see him caring for the myriad states and overcoming difficulties, and suppose that he falls short of Heaven and Earth in their freedom from deliberate intention. Yet they do not understand that he joins them in impartial harmony: the Three Powers manifest their standing together. This is what makes him the principal heir of Heaven and Earth. People see him attending tirelessly to the myriad affairs of government, and suppose that he falls short of Heaven and Earth in their freedom from care. Yet they do not understand that his ordering and encompassing of things never oversteps the bounds: the Three Ultimates establish the standard of the great mean. This is what makes him the consummate person of all under Heaven.

Taking his rule from above and following what lies below, he has the creative processes of nature as his companions. Those two have no surplus, nor does he have any deficiency. Though the Two Modes occupy distinct positions, does he not differ from them in position while sharing their spiritual efficacy? Looking upward and examining below, he takes Heaven and Earth as his likeness. They alone do not possess abundance, nor does he alone suffer want. Though Heaven and Earth have their established positions, does he not differ from them in form while sharing their essential constitution? This is called “forming a triad with Heaven and Earth.” Truly, none but the Son of Heaven can equal the greatness of Heaven and Earth, and nothing but Heaven and Earth suffices to reveal the greatness of the Son of Heaven. Should those who contemplate the Son of Heaven not also seek their starting point in Heaven and Earth?

Yet to speak of the Son of Heaven forming a triad with Heaven and Earth is not merely to speak of a correspondence in outward form. Virtue must necessarily be its foundation. Making illustrious his eminent virtue and keeping the luminous mandate constantly in view: these are what the sage relies upon, in his diligent and unremitting efforts, to seek accord with Heaven and Earth. Thus, his achievement in reaching Heaven is praised to this day without …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
弃不然而以滯諸其形象謂其有所合焉則上
下頓殊可得而參之乎是故有配天之業者必
有憲天之德而後可
第貳場
論
聖人與天地同體
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批滾滾千數百言悉皆根極
理要而無一費詞非眞有所得者不能及此允宜高薦
===

同考試官教諭黃批順理成文自然中度
考試官教諭何批文有氣魄有條理讀之灑
然可以式矣

論曰聖人者天地合德者也是故聖德之徵也
其體一天地而已而初非有心于強合者矣夫
天下之理一誠盡之矣天地也聖人也未始有

punctuated:
弃。不然而以滯諸其形象，謂其有所合焉，則上下頓殊，可得而參之乎？是故有配天之業者，必有憲天之德而後可。

第貳場
論
聖人與天地同體
祝眉壽

同考試官教諭何批：理極精純，詞復雅健。
同考試官教諭黃批：順理成文，自然中度。
考試官教諭何批：文有氣魄，有條理，讀之灑然，可以式矣。
考試官教諭錢批：善發天地聖人之蘊。

論曰：聖人者，天地合德者也。是故聖德之徵也，其體一天地而已，而初非有心于強合者矣。夫天下之理，一誠盡之矣。天地也，聖人也，未始有異也。夫惟其誠也未始有異，是之謂合德者也。
translation_en:
…abandoned. If, instead, one remains fixated on their outward forms and claims that there is some correspondence between them, then, since what is above and what is below are utterly distinct, how could one stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third? Thus, one who achieves deeds worthy of matching Heaven must first possess the virtue of taking Heaven as his model.

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Forms One Substance with Heaven and Earth”
Zhu Meishou

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: These many hundreds of words flow forth in a torrent, all thoroughly grounded in the essentials of principle, without a single wasted expression. Only someone who has truly attained understanding could accomplish this. He certainly deserves recommendation for a high ranking.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: The reasoning is supremely refined and pure; the language is also elegant and vigorous.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: The composition follows principle and naturally accords with the proper standard.

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: The writing has force and spirit, as well as orderly reasoning. Reading it leaves one refreshed; it can serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: It skillfully brings out the profound significance of Heaven, Earth, and the sage.

The discourse reads: The sage is one whose virtue accords with that of Heaven and Earth. Thus, the manifestation of sagely virtue consists simply in forming one substance with Heaven and Earth; there is never any intention of forcing this accord. All the principles under Heaven are encompassed in the single quality of sincerity. In this, Heaven and Earth and the sage have never differed. Precisely because their sincerity has never differed, they are said to accord in virtue.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
曾謂聖人合德于天地而其德之徵于外也顧
可以異言乎哉是故發之高明高明一天也積
之博厚博厚一地也高厚又悠久者一天地之
無疆也其體之在聖人也卽其在天地者也由
是而功化之隆凡所以覆載成物焉者悉于此
乎備焉體用一原上下同流其斯以為天地人
之至妙至妙者乎聖人抑何嘗有所容心也哉
嘗謂天位乎上也地位乎下也聖人混然中處
也殊形而異質其相去甚遠也而何以同其體
===
乎是蓋未知誠耳誠實理也合天地人而一之
者也非有二也茲天地之所以為天地而人之
所以為人者也使或在人者誠有未至斯與天
地不相似矣如是而欲與天地同體也得乎惟
聖人之德眞純無妄通乎天地而聖人又為天
地之所篤厚焉者聖人旣為天地之所篤厚而
聖德之純又通極于天地而無間則自能以一
身而立極于天下而天下之民物咸于是乎屬
望焉聖人亦自知其責之不容諉而天地之篤
punctuated: 曾謂聖人合德于天地，而其德之徵于外也，顧可以異言乎哉？是故發之高明，高明一天也；積之博厚，博厚一地也；高厚又悠久者，一天地之無疆也。其體之在聖人也，卽其在天地者也。由是而功化之隆，凡所以覆載成物焉者，悉于此乎備焉。體用一原，上下同流，其斯以為天地人之至妙至妙者乎？聖人抑何嘗有所容心也哉？嘗謂天位乎上也，地位乎下也，聖人混然中處也，殊形而異質，其相去甚遠也，而何以同其體乎？是蓋未知誠耳。誠，實理也，合天地人而一之者也，非有二也。茲天地之所以為天地，而人之所以為人者也。使或在人者誠有未至，斯與天地不相似矣。如是而欲與天地同體也，得乎？惟聖人之德眞純無妄，通乎天地，而聖人又為天地之所篤厚焉者。聖人旣為天地之所篤厚，而聖德之純又通極于天地而無間，則自能以一身而立極于天下，而天下之民物咸于是乎屬望焉。聖人亦自知其責之不容諉，而天地之篤
translation_en: Could one suppose that the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth, yet speak of the outward manifestations of his virtue as different from theirs? Thus, when expressed in loftiness and brilliance, it is one with Heaven’s loftiness and brilliance; when accumulated in breadth and depth, it is one with Earth’s breadth and depth. Its loftiness and depth, together with its enduring constancy, are one with the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth. The underlying substance present in the sage is precisely that present in Heaven and Earth. Hence the greatness of his achievements and transforming influence: everything by which beings are sheltered, sustained, and brought to completion is fully furnished here. Substance and function have a single source; above and below flow together. Is this not the most profound marvel of Heaven, Earth, and humanity? Yet when has the sage ever introduced any deliberate contrivance into it? It has been said that Heaven occupies the position above, Earth the position below, and the sage dwells harmoniously between them. Distinct in form and different in constitution, they are very far apart; how, then, can they share the same substance? Such a question simply shows a failure to understand sincerity. Sincerity is real principle: it unites Heaven, Earth, and humanity as one, admitting no duality. This is what makes Heaven and Earth Heaven and Earth, and human beings human. If sincerity in a person falls short, that person does not resemble Heaven and Earth. In such circumstances, could one hope to share their substance? Only the sage’s virtue is truly pure and free from falsity, communicating with Heaven and Earth; moreover, the sage receives Heaven and Earth’s abundant favor. Since the sage receives this abundant favor, and the purity of his sagely virtue also communicates fully with Heaven and Earth without any separation, he can naturally, in his own person, establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. All people and things throughout the world look to him with hope. The sage himself also knows that he cannot evade his responsibility, and that Heaven and Earth’s abundant favor …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
厚乎我者非欲使之自有餘而已也而所以發
揮其事業丕闡其經綸以康濟乎天下是皆于
其德之徵者取足焉固非有待于其外而功化
之所由基駿業之所由成者胥此也寧不與天
地而並運而有非形之所可拘質之所能限者
乎先儒推究聖人功用之所自而必于其德之
徵者曰與天地同體信乎其體之同也而形之
殊質之異不與焉何也今夫天司覆者也覆物
其用也而陰陽成象四時以為柄日星以為紀
===
雨露以為澤雷霆以為威必有高明者為之體
也今夫地司載者也載物其用也而剛柔成質
山川之流峙草木之夭喬鳥獸之飛走鱗介之
潜藏必有博厚者為之體也天地以生物為心
而成物其用也至健而不息永貞而有常寒暑
晝夜之變易歲月日時之推行元會運世之循
環而又有悠久者為之體也此造化之妙而莫
非一誠之所為也聖人于此以一人之身參兩
乎天地而為民物之主履之為達德措之為達
punctuated: 厚乎我者，非欲使之自有餘而已也，而所以發揮其事業，丕闡其經綸，以康濟乎天下，是皆于其德之徵者取足焉。固非有待于其外，而功化之所由基、駿業之所由成者，胥此也。寧不與天地而並運，而有非形之所可拘、質之所能限者乎？先儒推究聖人功用之所自，而必于其德之徵者曰：「與天地同體。」信乎其體之同也，而形之殊、質之異不與焉。何也？今夫天，司覆者也，覆物其用也。而陰陽成象，四時以為柄，日星以為紀，雨露以為澤，雷霆以為威，必有高明者為之體也。今夫地，司載者也，載物其用也。而剛柔成質，山川之流峙，草木之夭喬，鳥獸之飛走，鱗介之潜藏，必有博厚者為之體也。天地以生物為心，而成物其用也。至健而不息，永貞而有常，寒暑晝夜之變易，歲月日時之推行，元會運世之循環，而又有悠久者為之體也。此造化之妙，而莫非一誠之所為也。聖人于此，以一人之身參兩乎天地，而為民物之主，履之為達德，措之為達
translation_en:
…the generosity that Heaven and Earth bestow upon me is not intended merely to leave me personally with abundance. Rather, it enables the sage to develop his undertakings, give magnificent expression to his ordering of affairs, and bring peace and succor to all under Heaven. For all this, he finds sufficient resources in the manifestations of his virtue. He certainly need not depend upon anything outside it: the foundation of his achievements and transforming influence, and the accomplishment of his great undertakings, all lie here. How could he fail to operate alongside Heaven and Earth, with something in him that physical form cannot confine and material constitution cannot limit? When earlier Confucian scholars traced the source of the sage’s efficacy, they invariably grounded it in the manifestations of his virtue, saying: “He forms one body with Heaven and Earth.” Truly, their underlying substance is the same; differences in physical form and material constitution have no bearing upon it. Why is this so?

Heaven has charge of covering things; covering them is its function. Yin and yang produce celestial configurations; the four seasons serve as its governing handle, the sun and stars as its ordering framework, rain and dew as its beneficence, and thunder as its might. It must have loftiness and brightness as its underlying substance. Earth has charge of bearing things; bearing them is its function. The hard and soft form material substance: mountains stand and rivers flow, plants grow tender and trees rise tall, birds fly and beasts run, and scaled and shelled creatures hide below. It must have breadth and thickness as its underlying substance. Heaven and Earth take the generation of things as their heart, and bringing things to completion is their function. Utterly vigorous, they never cease; enduringly steadfast, they maintain constancy. Cold and heat, day and night alternate; years, months, days, and hours advance; the cosmic cycles of yuan, hui, yun, and shi revolve. Here, too, enduring permanence constitutes their underlying substance. Such is the wondrous working of creation and transformation, and none of it is other than the operation of a single sincerity.

In this, the sage, in his single person, joins Heaven and Earth to form a triad and becomes the lord of people and things. Embodied in his conduct, this becomes universally applicable virtue; put into practice, it becomes the universal…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
道普之爲九經垂之爲三重散之而爲三千三
百錯之而爲容爲執爲敬爲別形之而爲著爲
明爲動爲變徵諸庶民刑之百辟致中和賛化
育乆道成化而天下之物無不覆焉無不載焉
又無不成焉是亦天地之覆物載物而物被常
覆常載者也人將曰聖人之曲成天下功業如
此其隆也而不知此特用之及于物者耳而要
其所以然是必有體以運行于其間可以配諸
天地之體相與脗合而不悖而後其用爲不窮
===
是故德之徵而爲高也明也高明固聖人所以
覆物之體也而其峻極莫踰掀揭莫掩四時循
其序也日月貞其明也雨風露雷順其化也有
以配天之高明不與天同體乎德之徵而爲博
也厚也博厚固聖人所以載物之體也而其周
遍無遺漸漬無間流峙者奠其位也夭喬者若
其性也飛走生息者順其天也有以配地之博
厚不與地同體乎德之徵而爲悠也乆也悠乆
固聖人所以成物之體也而其高明不可極博
punctuated:
道，普之爲九經，垂之爲三重，散之而爲三千三百，錯之而爲容、爲執、爲敬、爲別，形之而爲著、爲明、爲動、爲變。徵諸庶民，刑之百辟，致中和，賛化育，乆道成化，而天下之物無不覆焉，無不載焉，又無不成焉。是亦天地之覆物載物，而物被常覆常載者也。人將曰：「聖人之曲成天下，功業如此其隆也！」而不知此特用之及于物者耳。而要其所以然，是必有體以運行于其間，可以配諸天地之體，相與脗合而不悖，而後其用爲不窮。
是故德之徵而爲高也、明也，高明固聖人所以覆物之體也。而其峻極莫踰，掀揭莫掩，四時循其序也，日月貞其明也，雨風露雷順其化也，有以配天之高明，不與天同體乎？德之徵而爲博也、厚也，博厚固聖人所以載物之體也。而其周遍無遺，漸漬無間，流峙者奠其位也，夭喬者若其性也，飛走生息者順其天也，有以配地之博厚，不與地同體乎？德之徵而爲悠也、乆也，悠乆固聖人所以成物之體也。而其高明不可極，博
translation_en:
…ways universally followed. Extended broadly, it becomes the nine guiding principles; handed down, it becomes the three weighty matters. Distributed in detail, it becomes the three thousand and three hundred rules of ritual. Applied in their various settings, it becomes proper demeanor, the holding of ceremonial objects, reverence, and distinction; taking manifest form, it becomes conspicuousness, clarity, movement, and transformation. Verified among the common people and made a model for the lords, it brings equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization, assists the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, and, through enduring adherence to the Way, brings transformation to completion. Thus nothing under Heaven goes unsheltered, unsupported, or unfulfilled. This, too, is like Heaven and Earth sheltering and supporting things, with all things receiving their constant shelter and support. People will say: “So great are the sage’s achievements in bringing everything under Heaven to fulfillment according to its particular nature!” Yet they do not know that this is merely his functioning as it reaches things. To grasp why this is so, there must be an underlying substance operating within it, capable of matching the substance of Heaven and Earth, perfectly corresponding with it without contradiction. Only then can its functioning be inexhaustible.
Thus, when virtue manifests itself as loftiness and brightness, these are indeed the substance through which the sage shelters things. Its towering height cannot be surpassed, and its elevated radiance cannot be obscured. The four seasons follow their sequence; the sun and moon remain constant in their brightness; rain, wind, dew, and thunder accord with its transforming work. Since it can match Heaven’s loftiness and brightness, does it not share Heaven’s substance? When virtue manifests itself as breadth and depth, these are indeed the substance through which the sage supports things. It extends everywhere without omission and permeates without interruption. Flowing waters and standing mountains settle into their places; tender plants and tall trees accord with their natures; creatures that fly, run, live, and propagate follow their Heaven-given endowments. Since it can match Earth’s breadth and depth, does it not share Earth’s substance? When virtue manifests itself as continuance and duration, these are indeed the substance through which the sage brings things to fulfillment. Its loftiness and brightness admit of no limit, and its breadth…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
厚不可窮變易者不能間也推行者不能巳也
循環者不能盡也有以同天地之無疆不與天
地同體乎惟其體之同是以用之同而聖人功
業之隆于是卓乎其不可及也巳然豈聖人有
心于臆度而強制以求其必合也哉蓋不同之
以形而同之以理不同之以質而同之以神其
在聖人也非有小于天地而其在天地也非有
加于聖人謂天地爲聖人可也謂聖人爲天地
亦可也夫何形之所可拘而質之所能限耶噫
===
同體之義深乎雖然聖人非特與天地同體而
實有功于天地者也蓋語高明者惟天而非聖
人以參賛之則高明無以成其運語博厚者惟
地而非聖人以參賛之則博厚無以成其功語
悠久者惟天地而非聖人以默成之則悠久無
以成其化是故曆象授時璿璣齊政聖人之所
以經天也莫非成天之體也畫井分州封山濬
川聖人之所以緯地也莫非成地之體也上律
下襲仰觀俯察聖人所以彌綸天地之道也莫
punctuated:
厚不可窮，變易者不能間也，推行者不能巳也，循環者不能盡也，有以同天地之無疆，不與天地同體乎？惟其體之同，是以用之同，而聖人功業之隆，于是卓乎其不可及也巳。然豈聖人有心于臆度而強制，以求其必合也哉？蓋不同之以形，而同之以理；不同之以質，而同之以神。其在聖人也，非有小于天地；而其在天地也，非有加于聖人。謂天地爲聖人可也，謂聖人爲天地亦可也。夫何形之所可拘，而質之所能限耶？噫！同體之義深乎！
雖然，聖人非特與天地同體，而實有功于天地者也。蓋語高明者惟天，而非聖人以參賛之，則高明無以成其運；語博厚者惟地，而非聖人以參賛之，則博厚無以成其功；語悠久者惟天地，而非聖人以默成之，則悠久無以成其化。是故曆象授時，璿璣齊政，聖人之所以經天也，莫非成天之體也；畫井分州，封山濬川，聖人之所以緯地也，莫非成地之體也；上律下襲，仰觀俯察，聖人所以彌綸天地之道也，莫
translation_en:
…its depth cannot be exhausted. Change cannot interrupt it; its onward movement cannot be stopped; its cycles cannot be exhausted. Thus it shares the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth: does it not form one substance with them? Precisely because their substance is the same, their functioning is also the same; hence the greatness of the sage’s achievements stands loftily beyond reach. Yet could the sage deliberately engage in conjecture and force matters in order to secure this correspondence? Their unity lies not in form but in principle, not in material constitution but in spiritual efficacy. What resides in the sage is no less than what resides in Heaven and Earth, and what resides in Heaven and Earth is no greater than what resides in the sage. One may call Heaven and Earth the sage, and one may also call the sage Heaven and Earth. How could form constrain this, or material constitution limit it? Ah, how profound is the meaning of forming one substance!
Nevertheless, the sage not only forms one substance with Heaven and Earth but also makes a real contribution to them. When speaking of height and brilliance, we refer to Heaven alone; yet without the sage’s participation and assistance, that height and brilliance could not fulfill their courses. When speaking of breadth and depth, we refer to Earth alone; yet without the sage’s participation and assistance, that breadth and depth could not accomplish their work. When speaking of enduring constancy, we refer to Heaven and Earth alone; yet without the sage’s silently bringing things to completion, that constancy could not accomplish its transformations. Thus, calculating and observing celestial phenomena to give the people the seasons, and using the jade celestial instrument to bring the celestial regulators into accord, are the means by which the sage orders Heaven: all serve to bring Heaven’s substance to fulfillment. Marking out well-field divisions and dividing the provinces, demarcating the mountains and dredging the rivers, are the means by which the sage orders Earth: all serve to bring Earth’s substance to fulfillment. Taking his rule from above and following what is below, looking upward to observe and downward to examine, are the means by which the sage comprehensively orders the Way of Heaven and Earth: none…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
非成天地之體也天地無心聖人代之言天地
無爲聖人代之工天地聖人其相須以有成而
聖人尤天地之所以代終者乎然則未至于聖
者而脩焉以復其性精之于莫見莫顯約之于
不見不聞而必造于純亦不已之妙則不賞不
怒而天下以勸以威由是而天地位萬物育卿
雲見甘露降河出圖洛出書山出器車麒麟遊
郊藪而四靈畢至以至于篤恭不顯之化又何
以異于天地哉是又聖脩之極也此中庸之所
===
爲作也是爲論
表
擬宋以文彦博富弼同中書門下平章事
謝表〔至和二年〕
廖如春
同考試官教諭胡 批 寫出二賢相翊輔之忱宛
然可讀
同考試官教諭項 批 贍而有體且多用本色而
精渾無迹尤見工緻
punctuated:
非成天地之體也。天地無心，聖人代之言；天地無爲，聖人代之工。天地、聖人，其相須以有成，而聖人尤天地之所以代終者乎？然則未至于聖者，而脩焉以復其性，精之于莫見莫顯，約之于不見不聞，而必造于純亦不已之妙，則不賞不怒，而天下以勸以威。由是而天地位，萬物育，卿雲見，甘露降，河出圖，洛出書，山出器車，麒麟遊郊藪，而四靈畢至。以至于篤恭不顯之化，又何以異于天地哉？是又聖脩之極也。此《中庸》之所爲作也。是爲論。

表

擬宋以文彦博、富弼同中書門下平章事謝表〔至和二年〕
廖如春

同考試官教諭胡批：寫出二賢相翊輔之忱，宛然可讀。

同考試官教諭項批：贍而有體，且多用本色，而精渾無迹，尤見工緻。
translation_en:
…all serve to bring the constitutive reality of Heaven and Earth to fulfillment. Heaven and Earth have no conscious intent; the sage speaks on their behalf. Heaven and Earth undertake no deliberate action; the sage performs their work. Heaven and Earth and the sage depend upon one another to achieve fulfillment; is it not especially through the sage that Heaven and Earth have their work carried through to completion? Thus, those who have not yet attained sagehood cultivate themselves to recover their nature, refining it in what is most subtly manifest and conspicuous, and concentrating it in what is neither seen nor heard. They must attain the wondrous state of purity that never ceases. Then, without their bestowing rewards or displaying anger, all under Heaven are encouraged and held in awe. Consequently, Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and the myriad things flourish. Auspicious clouds appear, sweet dew descends, the Yellow River yields the Diagram, the Luo River yields the Writing, and the mountains yield ritual vessels and carriages. Qilin roam the outskirts and marshes, and all four numinous creatures arrive. When transformation through profound reverence and unobtrusive virtue is attained, how does this differ from Heaven and Earth? This, too, is the ultimate attainment of sagely cultivation. This is why the Doctrine of the Mean was written. Such is this discourse.

Memorial

A memorial of thanks, composed in the voices of Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi upon their appointment under the Song as Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat–Chancellery. 〔Second year of Zhihe [1055]〕
By Liao Ruchun.

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the sincere devotion of the two worthy chief councilors in assisting the ruler, bringing it vividly before the reader.”

Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor, comments: “Ample in substance and proper in form, it also largely employs language natural to its subject. Refined and seamlessly integrated, it leaves no trace of artifice, displaying particularly delicate craftsmanship.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭何批冲腴有味
考試官教諭錢批詞藻蔚然四六之佳者
至和二年某月某日具官臣文彥博臣富
弼伏蒙
聖恩以臣等同中書門下平章事者
紫禁近中台星兩燦麗
天之曜
黃樞分上相德一慶遇
主之榮
===
綸綍同宣拜稽交讓仰
龍光之斯極顧𧖟負以何勝臣彥博臣弼誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊惟中書掌奏漢
庭倣內史之遺門下分曹唐室有左省之
號品秩竝崇宰路政事咸共平章義本虞
書制詳舊史命名肇於貞觀加禮耆勳入
銜始自永淳相因後代於昭
皇宋益簡臣鄰雖中書為右未遑與門下省而
對移然任官維賢則必得讀書人而後用
punctuated:
考試官教諭何批：冲腴有味。
考試官教諭錢批：詞藻蔚然，四六之佳者。
至和二年某月某日，具官臣文彥博、臣富弼伏蒙聖恩，以臣等同中書門下平章事者。
紫禁近中，台星兩燦，麗天之曜；黃樞分上，相德一慶，遇主之榮。綸綍同宣，拜稽交讓。仰龍光之斯極，顧𧖟負以何勝？臣彥博、臣弼誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟中書掌奏，漢庭倣內史之遺；門下分曹，唐室有左省之號。品秩竝崇，宰路政事咸共平章。義本虞書，制詳舊史。命名肇於貞觀，加禮耆勳；入銜始自永淳，相因後代。於昭皇宋，益簡臣鄰。雖中書為右，未遑與門下省而對移；然任官維賢，則必得讀書人而後用。
translation_en:
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Mild and rich, with lasting savor.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “Luxuriant in its literary embellishment: an excellent example of four-and-six parallel prose.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the second year of Zhihe, your servants Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi, holding their respective offices, humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment as Jointly Administrators of Affairs of the Secretariat–Chancellery.
Close to the center of the Purple Forbidden Palace, two ministerial stars shine together, their radiance adorning Heaven; sharing the highest offices at the imperial pivot, we ministers rejoice together in the honor of encountering our sovereign. The imperial commands have been proclaimed to us together; bowing low, each yields precedence to the other. Looking up at this utmost imperial favor, how can we bear the burden of our own shortcomings [?]? Your servants Yanbo and Bi, in profound fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words:
We humbly reflect that the Secretariat’s charge over memorials followed, at the Han court, the surviving practices of the Metropolitan Administrator; the Chancellery, with its separate offices, bore the designation “Left Department” under the Tang. Both were exalted in rank, and the affairs of government within the chief councilors’ purview were jointly deliberated and settled. The meaning derives from the Documents of Yu; the institution is detailed in the histories of earlier dynasties. The designation originated in the Zhenguan reign, conferring additional honor upon aged men of distinguished service. Its incorporation into official titles began in the Yongchun reign and was continued by succeeding dynasties. Under our illustrious imperial Song, still greater care has been taken in selecting ministers close to the throne. Although the Secretariat takes precedence, there has been no opportunity for a reciprocal transfer with the Chancellery [?]. Yet since only the worthy are to be appointed to office, men versed in books must first be found before they are employed.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰普曰質協恭
開寶之隆如李如張並受
咸平之
命遠惟旦準為烈近之韓范可稱必求異能方
堪峻陟
知人由於
堯哲才則甚難
建典法於周官員不必備詎期葑菲濫預鈞
衡茲蓋伏遇
===
○○○○
德協舜華
志恢禹績
問學日就
恭儉天成
無逸書屏儼若羹墻之見
籍田撰記深惟稼穡之艱屏
出通天羊
存中夜
punctuated: 曰普曰質，協恭開寶之隆；如李如張，並受咸平之命。遠惟旦準為烈，近之韓范可稱。必求異能，方堪峻陟。知人由於堯哲，才則甚難；建典法於周官，員不必備。詎期葑菲，濫預鈞衡！茲蓋伏遇○○○○，德協舜華，志恢禹績，問學日就，恭儉天成。無逸書屏，儼若羹墻之見；籍田撰記，深惟稼穡之艱。屏出通天，羊存中夜。
translation_en:
…Men such as Pu and Zhi worked together reverently during the flourishing Kaibao era; men such as Li and Zhang alike received appointments in the Xianping era. Among earlier men, Dan and Zhun achieved distinction; among more recent men, Han and Fan deserve praise. Only those of exceptional ability were sought, for only such men could bear elevation to high office. Even with Yao’s wisdom in discerning men, talent was exceedingly hard to find; in establishing institutions according to the Offices of Zhou, there was no need to fill every post. How could we, worthless as turnip greens, have expected undeservedly to participate in the highest councils of government?
This is because we have humbly encountered ○○○○, whose virtue matches Shun’s splendor, whose ambition extends Yu’s achievements, whose inquiry and learning advance daily, and whose reverence and frugality are innate. You had “Against Idleness” inscribed upon a screen, as though seeing the ancient sages before you in your soup and upon the wall. You composed an account of the imperial plowing field, reflecting deeply upon the hardships of sowing and reaping. You put aside the “Heaven-reaching” ceremonial cap [?], and spared a sheep in the middle of the night [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
經營西北
期清幽夏之塵
頒賜學庸
獨舉聖賢之要
開天章而入對臺諫并用乎四賢
宴祕省而賦詩
喜起重賡於千載數
行錄繫屢
詔蠲租
===
露禱
禁庭
精回雲漢
躬臨孔廟
光賁人文
禮備樂和
仁昭義立財不蓄而
國富兵不試而
威張
punctuated:
經營西北，期清幽夏之塵；頒賜學庸，獨舉聖賢之要。開天章而入對，臺諫并用乎四賢；宴祕省而賦詩，喜起重賡於千載。數行錄繫，屢詔蠲租。
露禱禁庭，精回雲漢；躬臨孔廟，光賁人文。禮備樂和，仁昭義立；財不蓄而國富，兵不試而威張。
translation_en:
…He directed affairs in the northwest, seeking to clear the dust of warfare from You and Xia; he bestowed copies of the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, singling out the essentials of the sages and worthies. He opened the Tianzhang Pavilion to receive advisers in audience, employing four worthy men together as censors and remonstrance officials. He held a banquet in the Palace Library and composed poetry: after a thousand years, the song of ruler and ministers joyfully rising to their duties was continued anew. He repeatedly ordered reviews of prisoners’ cases and frequently decreed remissions of land taxes.
He prayed beneath the open sky within the palace precincts, his sincerity moving Heaven to relieve drought. He personally visited the Temple of Confucius, shedding lustre upon civilized learning. Ritual was complete and music harmonious; benevolence shone forth and righteousness was established. Wealth was not hoarded, yet the state was rich; troops were not put to the test, yet its might spread abroad…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
澤溢窮荒
馨升
玄昊保章奏
舍譽之見義掃攙搶瑞芝産
化成之楹品高連理合肥之稻再實周穎偕
榮異域之象交陳軒麟竝集
光昭
一祖
二宗之
===
統遹成斗米十錢之風
治已垂裳
心猶考相崇資顯秩當求有用之才
盛世
昌辰尤急可觀之效仰荷
陶鈞之竝覆遂使韈線之兼容
渥殊禮於郊迎
賢人情於夢卜
恩超象審誦說命以凜如質匪鷹揚捧
punctuated:
澤溢窮荒，馨升玄昊。保章奏舍譽之見，義掃攙搶。瑞芝産化成之楹，品高連理；合肥之稻再實，周穎偕榮。異域之象交陳，軒麟竝集。光昭一祖二宗之統，遹成斗米十錢之風。
治已垂裳，心猶考相。崇資顯秩，當求有用之才；盛世昌辰，尤急可觀之效。仰荷陶鈞之竝覆，遂使韈線之兼容。渥殊禮於郊迎，賢人情於夢卜。恩超象審，誦說命以凜如；質匪鷹揚，捧
translation_en:
…Your beneficence overflows into the remotest wilderness, and its fragrance rises to the lofty heavens. The Astrologer reports the appearance of “Sheyu” [?], and righteousness sweeps away the baleful stars [?]. Auspicious numinous fungi grow upon the pillars of Huacheng, surpassing even trees with joined branches in excellence; the rice of Hefei bears grain twice, its ears flourishing all around together [?]. Elephants from foreign lands are presented in succession, and qilin gather together. Your radiance illuminates the dynastic succession of the one founding ancestor and the two ancestral sovereigns, carrying forward an age when a dou of rice costs ten cash.
Though your government already achieves order with robes hanging loosely, your mind still attends to selecting ministers. For lofty standing and illustrious rank, one must seek men of useful talent; in a flourishing age and prosperous time, demonstrable results are especially urgent. Reverently receiving the all-encompassing care of your shaping power, we find that even talents as slight as thread for stockings are accommodated. You lavish exceptional ceremony upon welcoming the worthy in the suburbs, and express your regard for worthy men through dreams and divination [?]. Your favor surpasses the search by likeness for Fu Yue; reciting the Charge to Yue, we stand in awe. Though our qualities fall short of the hawk-like prowess of the Grand Duke, we reverently hold up…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
丹書而惕若伏念臣彥博臣弼汾陽布素蚤
叨進士之科洛水章縫偶與茂才之選異
人國士抑聲聞之過情陳力匡時蓋朴忠
而自許具劉平之案仰體
欽恤之
衷却元昊之書爰正
朝廷之體行鐵錢平市價敢云臨事有方糾
僞牒繳詞頭竊慕直言不隱督師河北竟
出軍候之謀奉使契丹徒爭獻納之字薦
===
賢靡知爲
國救荒匪以要名置散投閒終懷犬馬之戀
匿瑕含垢猥蒙
天地之全一朝
召還同日
褒擢喜接夔龍之武共虎對揚勉圖盆稷之
謨咸駿奔走匪石不二斷金與齊屹立
朝端益養折衝之重恪守前志渾忘顧慮之
私則知印押班不徒旅進旅退而
punctuated: 丹書而惕若。伏念臣彥博、臣弼，汾陽布素，蚤叨進士之科；洛水章縫，偶與茂才之選。異人國士，抑聲聞之過情；陳力匡時，蓋朴忠而自許。具劉平之案，仰體欽恤之衷；却元昊之書，爰正朝廷之體。行鐵錢，平市價，敢云臨事有方；糾僞牒，繳詞頭，竊慕直言不隱。督師河北，竟出軍候之謀；奉使契丹，徒爭獻納之字。薦賢靡知爲國，救荒匪以要名。置散投閒，終懷犬馬之戀；匿瑕含垢，猥蒙天地之全。一朝召還，同日褒擢。喜接夔龍之武，共虎對揚；勉圖盆稷之謨，咸駿奔走。匪石不二，斷金與齊。屹立朝端，益養折衝之重；恪守前志，渾忘顧慮之私。則知印押班，不徒旅進旅退而
translation_en: …the Cinnabar Document, and trembled in awe. We, your servants Yanbo and Bi, humbly reflect: one, a commoner of Fenyang, early received the undeserved distinction of becoming a metropolitan graduate; the other, a scholar from the Luo River region, happened to be selected among men of outstanding talent. To call us extraordinary men and outstanding servants of the state is surely to let reputation exceed reality; yet we have presumed to offer our simple loyalty, exerting our abilities to set the age aright. In preparing the case concerning Liu Ping, we reverently embodied Your Majesty’s concern for caution and compassion in punishment; in rejecting Yuanhao’s letter, we upheld the dignity of the court. We introduced iron currency and stabilized market prices, though we dare not claim skill in handling affairs; we exposed fraudulent documents and returned draft directives, privately aspiring to speak frankly and conceal nothing. While supervising the armies in Hebei, one ultimately devised a plan involving military scouts [?]; while serving as envoy to the Khitan, the other merely contested the wording of “offering” and “presenting” tribute. In recommending worthy men, we scarcely knew how to serve the state [?]; in relieving famine, we did not seek fame. Assigned to inactive posts and cast into retirement, we nevertheless retained the devotion of dogs and horses. Concealing our flaws and bearing with our faults, Your Majesty, like Heaven and Earth, graciously preserved us intact. Recalled at a single summons, we were commended and promoted on the same day. Delighted to follow in the footsteps of Kui and Long, we reverently [?] respond to and proclaim your favor; striving to emulate the counsels of Pen [?] and Ji, we all hasten to your service. Our hearts, unlike stones that can be turned, remain undivided; our unity matches that which can cut through metal. Standing firmly at the head of the court, we shall further cultivate the weight of authority that overcomes opposition; faithfully maintaining our former resolve, we shall wholly forget private calculations and concerns. Thus, in handling seals and leading the court ranks, we shall do more than merely advance and withdraw with the others, but …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
獻善宣
美庶能爲德爲民竭此共濟之猷副彼僉諧
之望伏願
人惟求舊
率由慶曆之朋
念不遺遐
誕布至和之化
階平
衡正海晏河清
===
如月如日如南山保萬年之
宗社
多富多壽多男子綿百世之
本支臣彥博臣弼無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated: 獻善宣美，庶能爲德爲民，竭此共濟之猷，副彼僉諧之望。伏願人惟求舊，率由慶曆之朋；念不遺遐，誕布至和之化。階平衡正，海晏河清。如月如日如南山，保萬年之宗社；多富多壽多男子，綿百世之本支。臣彥博、臣弼無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en: …by presenting worthy counsel and proclaiming Your Majesty’s virtues, we may serve virtue and the people, devote ourselves fully to plans for working together, and fulfill the hope that all will act in harmony. We humbly wish that, in seeking men, you will favor those long tried, following the example of the fellowship of the Qingli era; that your care will not overlook those far away, and that you will spread widely the transforming influence of the Zhihe era. May the Three Steps stars be at peace and the Balance stars correctly aligned; may the seas be calm and the Yellow River clear. Like the moon, like the sun, like the Southern Mountain, may the dynastic ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain endure for ten thousand years. With abundant wealth, long life, and many sons, may the main and collateral branches of the imperial line continue for a hundred generations. Your servants Yanbo and Bi, looking up to Heaven and reverently toward Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain our fervent emotion and profound trepidation. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批〔洪範傳心之要至我〕
〔聖祖皇上而以明以行所謂心同道同者子能悉之可謂善觀〕
〔聖人之深者矣敬服敬服〕
同考試官教諭何批〔揄揚鋪敘具有源委宜錄以式〕
===
同考試官教諭黃批〔敷對詳明摛詞溫雅子其〕
〔善鳴者耶〕
考試官教諭何批〔頌述之文典重溫潤可謂得體〕
考試官教諭錢批〔詞潤氣完足占所養〕
帝王有建極之盛德而後能斂天下之福
斂天下之福者克享天心者也帝王有敷
極之宏猷而後能錫天下以福錫天下以
福者善體天心者也何也蓋大君者天地
之宗子也惟德動天惟天眷德故建極而
punctuated:
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
祝眉壽

同考試官教諭王批〔《洪範》傳心之要，至我〕〔聖祖、皇上而以明以行，所謂心同道同者，子能悉之，可謂善觀〕〔聖人之深者矣。敬服！敬服！〕
同考試官教諭何批〔揄揚鋪敘，具有源委，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭黃批〔敷對詳明，摛詞溫雅，子其〕〔善鳴者耶？〕
考試官教諭何批〔頌述之文，典重溫潤，可謂得體。〕
考試官教諭錢批〔詞潤氣完，足占所養。〕

帝王有建極之盛德，而後能斂天下之福。斂天下之福者，克享天心者也。帝王有敷極之宏猷，而後能錫天下以福。錫天下以福者，善體天心者也。何也？蓋大君者，天地之宗子也。惟德動天，惟天眷德，故建極而
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays (five questions)
First Question
Zhu Meishou

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The essentials of the transmission of the mind in the ‘Great Plan’ (Hongfan) have been elucidated and put into practice by our sagely founding emperor and His Majesty. You have fully grasped what is meant by their sharing the same mind and the same Way. You may indeed be said to perceive well the profundities of the sages. My admiration! My admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “The praise and exposition fully set forth both origins and ramifications. This should be recorded to serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Your response is detailed and clear, and your language gentle and elegant. Are you not one who gives fine expression to his thoughts?”

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “As a work of praise and narration, this is dignified and substantial, gentle and polished. It may be called appropriate to its genre.”

Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “The diction is polished and the vital force complete: these suffice to reveal your cultivation.”

Only when emperors and kings possess the abundant virtue needed to establish the supreme standard can they gather to themselves the blessings of all under Heaven. Those who gather these blessings are able to win the favor of Heaven’s heart. Only when emperors and kings possess the grand designs needed to extend the supreme standard can they bestow blessings upon all under Heaven. Those who bestow these blessings are skilled at embodying Heaven’s heart. Why is this? The great ruler is the principal heir of Heaven and Earth. Virtue alone moves Heaven; Heaven cherishes virtue alone. Thus, when he establishes the supreme standard …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之福歸之矣臣民者又大君之子也
惟天生物惟聖成之故敷極而錫天下以
福矣惟建極以斂福也可以觀格天之精
焉惟敷極以錫福也可以觀代天之治焉
此皇極之義所以為萬世君天下之準而
我
聖祖契悟之精
皇上繼述之善豈非超越千古而
紹帝王之盛者哉請敬陳之皇極之名孰昉
===
乎昉於書之洪範也蓋自神禹治水地平
天成而洛書呈其數武王造周諮謨訪道
而箕子叙其疇以其數言之則列于極之
上者有五行五事八政五紀焉列于極之
下者有三德稽疑庶徵福極焉八者固與
皇極而同叙于疇以其義言之則五紀以
上極之所以建也三德以下極之所以行
也八者皆待皇極而各得其理然是極也
非他也即中也中立而四方取正之謂也
punctuated:
天下之福歸之矣。臣民者，又大君之子也。惟天生物，惟聖成之，故敷極而錫天下以福矣。惟建極以斂福也，可以觀格天之精焉；惟敷極以錫福也，可以觀代天之治焉。此皇極之義，所以為萬世君天下之準，而我聖祖契悟之精、皇上繼述之善，豈非超越千古而紹帝王之盛者哉？請敬陳之。
皇極之名孰昉乎？昉於《書》之《洪範》也。蓋自神禹治水，地平天成，而洛書呈其數；武王造周，諮謨訪道，而箕子叙其疇。以其數言之，則列于極之上者，有五行、五事、八政、五紀焉；列于極之下者，有三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極焉。八者固與皇極而同叙于疇。以其義言之，則五紀以上，極之所以建也；三德以下，極之所以行也。八者皆待皇極而各得其理。然是極也，非他也，即中也，中立而四方取正之謂也。
translation_en:
…all the blessings of the realm converge upon him. Ministers and common people, in turn, are children of the great sovereign. Heaven brings things into being; the sage brings them to fulfillment. Thus, by extending the supreme standard, the sovereign bestows blessings upon the realm. In establishing the standard to gather blessings, one may discern the spiritual refinement through which he moves Heaven; in extending the standard to bestow blessings, one may discern his governance on Heaven’s behalf. This is why the meaning of the august standard serves as the measure for those who rule the realm throughout all ages. Do not our Sagely Ancestor’s profound comprehension of it and Your Majesty’s excellence in continuing and carrying forward his work surpass all antiquity and perpetuate the glory of the ancient emperors and kings? Allow me respectfully to explain.
Where did the term “august standard” originate? It originated in the “Great Plan” chapter of the Book of Documents. When the divine Yu brought the waters under control, the earth was put in order and Heaven’s work accomplished, and the Luo Writing revealed its numbers. When King Wu founded the Zhou, he sought counsel and inquired into the Way, and Jizi set forth its categories. In their numerical sequence, the categories preceding the standard are the Five Phases, the Five Activities, the Eight Affairs of Government, and the Five Regulators of Time; those following it are the Three Virtues, the Resolution of Doubts, the Various Signs, and Blessings and Calamities. These eight are indeed enumerated as categories alongside the august standard. In terms of their significance, however, the categories through the Five Regulators of Time are the means by which the standard is established, while those from the Three Virtues onward are the means by which it is put into practice. All eight depend upon the august standard for each to attain its proper order. Yet this standard is nothing other than the center: it means that the center is established and the four quarters take their standard of correctness from it.
