title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯舜之執中湯之建中皆是物也天以皇
極之理賦于人而不能使人之協于極于
是乎以彌綸輔相之道付之君君建其極
而天眷爲之申錫矣有不萃天下之福乎
君以建極之福斂諸躬而必欲臣民之會
歸于極也于是以蕩平正直之理敷于下
人協于極而王道由之宣布矣豈非錫天
下以福乎三代而上治教休明曆祚永久
陰陽調而風雨時羣生和而萬民殖諸福
===
之物可致之祥莫不畢至凡以皇建其極
而敷錫于下也成康而後建極敷極之義
微而斂福錫福之應亦寢以薄矣況于漢
之雜伯唐之雜夷宋之不振又何足以與
于皇極之道哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奮起淮甸汛掃腥羶以
一身爲仁義禮樂之主置天下於衣冠文物
之域
德邁羣倫
punctuated:
堯舜之執中，湯之建中，皆是物也。天以皇極之理賦于人，而不能使人之協于極，于是乎以彌綸輔相之道付之君。君建其極，而天眷爲之申錫矣，有不萃天下之福乎？君以建極之福斂諸躬，而必欲臣民之會歸于極也，于是以蕩平正直之理敷于下。人協于極，而王道由之宣布矣，豈非錫天下以福乎？三代而上，治教休明，曆祚永久，陰陽調而風雨時，羣生和而萬民殖，諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，凡以皇建其極而敷錫于下也。成康而後，建極敷極之義微，而斂福錫福之應亦寢以薄矣。況于漢之雜伯、唐之雜夷、宋之不振，又何足以與于皇極之道哉！
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，奮起淮甸，汛掃腥羶，以一身爲仁義禮樂之主，置天下於衣冠文物之域，德邁羣倫，
translation_en:
Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the Mean and Tang’s establishing the Mean all concerned this same principle. Heaven endows people with the principle of the August Ultimate, yet cannot make them conform to it; thus it entrusts to the ruler the Way of comprehensively ordering and assisting the workings of Heaven. When the ruler establishes this Ultimate, Heaven’s favor bestows its gifts anew. How could all the blessings under Heaven fail to converge upon him? The ruler gathers into his own person the blessings of establishing the Ultimate, yet necessarily desires that his ministers and people should all turn toward it. He therefore spreads among those below the principles of impartiality, equity, rectitude, and uprightness. When people conform to the Ultimate, the Kingly Way is thereby propagated. Is this not to bestow blessings upon all under Heaven? In the Three Dynasties and earlier, government and moral instruction were splendid and enlightened, and dynastic tenure endured. Yin and yang were harmonious, wind and rain came in season, all living things flourished in harmony, and the people multiplied. Every manifestation of blessing and every auspicious sign that could be brought forth arrived in full. All this was because the sovereign established his Ultimate and distributed its gifts to those below. After Kings Cheng and Kang, understanding of establishing and spreading the Ultimate declined, and the corresponding effects of gathering and bestowing blessings likewise gradually diminished. How much less could the Han, with its admixture of hegemonic rule, the Tang, with its admixture of barbarian ways, or the Song, with its failure to revive, qualify as participants in the Way of the August Ultimate!
We reverently consider our Emperor Taizu Gao, who rose in the Huai region and swept away the rank and fetid [alien rulers]. In his own person he became the master of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, and brought all under Heaven into the realm of civilized dress and cultural refinement. His virtue surpassed all others …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
功高萬世其所以
建極者豫矣
敷極者至矣是以
上天眷享諸福萃焉奄有四海不足爲其富也
嚮明而治不足爲其尊也慶雲甘露瑞麥
嘉瓜
太平之祥數數見焉
聖祖豈有心于斂天下之福哉極建而福自歸
之也然而
===
聖祖之心不自已也
禮儀之潤色
律令之詳定凡所以軌衆齊物
訓迪臣民者無所不用其極矣復以洪範蔡
傳有誤
親爲註釋以陰隲下民屬之天以相協厥居屬
之君
睿見神謨闡發皇極精意于千載之下無非欲
天下臣民協于極而同躋于福也蓋眞有
punctuated: 功高萬世。其所以建極者豫矣，敷極者至矣。是以上天眷享，諸福萃焉。奄有四海，不足爲其富也；嚮明而治，不足爲其尊也。慶雲、甘露、瑞麥、嘉瓜，太平之祥數數見焉。聖祖豈有心于斂天下之福哉？極建而福自歸之也。然而聖祖之心不自已也。禮儀之潤色，律令之詳定，凡所以軌衆齊物、訓迪臣民者，無所不用其極矣。復以《洪範》蔡傳有誤，親爲註釋，以「陰隲下民」屬之天，以「相協厥居」屬之君。睿見神謨，闡發皇極精意于千載之下，無非欲天下臣民協于極而同躋于福也。蓋眞有
translation_en:
…his achievements surpassed those of all ages. His preparations for establishing the supreme standard were thorough, and his dissemination of it was complete. Thus Heaven bestowed its favor, and every blessing gathered upon him. Possession of all within the Four Seas was insufficient to express his wealth; facing the light to govern was insufficient to express his dignity. Auspicious clouds, sweet dew, auspicious wheat, and fine melons—signs of Great Peace—appeared again and again. Did the sagely founder deliberately seek to gather all the blessings of the realm to himself? Once the supreme standard was established, blessings naturally accrued to him.

Yet the sagely founder’s concern did not cease. He refined ritual observances and carefully settled the statutes and ordinances. In everything that regulated the multitude, ordered affairs, and instructed and guided his ministers and people, he spared no effort. Moreover, finding errors in Cai’s commentary on the Great Plan, he personally supplied annotations, assigning “silently ordering the people below” to Heaven and “assisting them to live together in harmony” to the ruler. Through his sagely insight and inspired counsels, he elucidated the essential meaning of the sovereign’s supreme standard more than a thousand years after its formulation. All this was intended to bring the ministers and people throughout the realm into accord with that standard, so that they might together attain blessings. For he truly had…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
得於相協厥居之義而無負于代天理物
之責矣豈區區于訓詁之末已哉我
皇上以
上智之資撫
中興之運憲
天法
祖正典明倫宏綱大要無不舉矣
申飭吏治
勤恤民隱
===
===
深仁厚澤無不洽矣
至德馨香休徵協應禾呈三秀之異芝絢五
色之靈白鹿之雙馴玉兎之竝育奇祥上
瑞種種疊出矣我
皇上建極而斂福于
躬所以承
天之庥者何至也
敷極而錫福于下所以代
天之工者何大也質諸
punctuated: 得於相協厥居之義，而無負于代天理物之責矣，豈區區于訓詁之末已哉！我皇上以上智之資，撫中興之運，憲天法祖，正典明倫，宏綱大要無不舉矣；申飭吏治，勤恤民隱，深仁厚澤無不洽矣。至德馨香，休徵協應：禾呈三秀之異，芝絢五色之靈，白鹿之雙馴，玉兎之竝育，奇祥上瑞，種種疊出矣。我皇上建極而斂福于躬，所以承天之庥者何至也！敷極而錫福于下，所以代天之工者何大也！質諸
translation_en:
…grasped the meaning of assisting the people to live together in harmony, and has not failed in the responsibility of ordering all things on Heaven’s behalf. How could this be merely a concern with the minutiae of textual exegesis!

Our Emperor, endowed with the highest wisdom and presiding over an age of dynastic resurgence, takes Heaven as his pattern and his ancestors as his models. He rectifies canonical institutions and clarifies human relationships; every great guiding principle and essential measure has been put into effect. He enjoins stricter standards in the administration of officials and diligently attends to the people’s hidden hardships; his profound benevolence and abundant bounty reach everywhere. His consummate virtue spreads like a fragrance, and favorable signs appear in harmonious response: grain displays the marvel of threefold flowering; numinous fungi gleam in five colors; white deer are tamed in pairs, and jade-white rabbits are reared together. Extraordinary auspicious signs and supreme portents appear in succession in every form.

Our Emperor establishes the Supreme Standard and gathers blessings in his own person: how perfectly he receives Heaven’s favor! He disseminates the Supreme Standard and bestows blessings upon those below: how great is the work he performs on Heaven’s behalf! If this is measured against…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之
建極敷極者夫何異哉然猶慮極道之已敷
而臣民之未協也邇者
鼎新
殿門乃遵
天命述
祖德特取皇極之義名之於
正殿正門也則曰
皇極
===
中極
建極焉於
左右門也則曰會極歸極焉恭覩
詔制有曰人君建中建極乃敘疇錫福之基臣
民會極歸極乃欽若從乂之道大哉
王言不特在廷臣庶接目儆心雖海隅蒼生罔
不欣欣焉知
德意之所嚮我
皇上之所以
punctuated: 聖祖之建極敷極者，夫何異哉？然猶慮極道之已敷，而臣民之未協也。邇者，鼎新殿門，乃遵天命，述祖德，特取皇極之義名之。於正殿正門也，則曰皇極、中極、建極焉；於左右門也，則曰會極、歸極焉。恭覩詔制有曰：「人君建中建極，乃敘疇錫福之基；臣民會極歸極，乃欽若從乂之道。」大哉，王言！不特在廷臣庶接目儆心，雖海隅蒼生，罔不欣欣焉知德意之所嚮。我皇上之所以
translation_en:
…the Sagely Ancestor’s establishment and extension of the supreme standard—how does this differ? Yet His Majesty still feared that, although the Way of the supreme standard had been extended, officials and people had not yet brought themselves into accord with it. Recently, in renovating the halls and gates, he followed Heaven’s Mandate and carried forward his ancestor’s virtue, drawing specifically upon the meaning of the August Ultimate (huangji) to name them. For the principal halls and main gates, the names were Huangji (August Ultimate), Zhongji (Central Ultimate), and Jianji (Establishing the Ultimate); for the gates to the left and right, they were Huiji (Converging upon the Ultimate) and Guiji (Returning to the Ultimate).

We reverently read in the imperial decree: “The ruler’s establishment of the mean and the supreme standard is the foundation for ordering the categories of governance and bestowing blessings; the convergence and return of officials and people to the supreme standard is the way of reverent compliance and submission to good order.” Great indeed are these royal words! Not only do the officials and others at court see them and take admonition to heart; even the common people in the remotest coastal regions all joyfully understand the direction of his virtuous intentions. The means by which our Emperor…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
申其敷錫者尤彰明較著矣
聖祖闡皇極之義以正書傳之誤于先我
皇上揭皇極之要而
命殿門之名于後
聖祖之所闡即
皇上之所名也未遑于昔而有待于
今者也
皇上之所名即
聖祖之所闡也
===
===
善繼其志而
善述其事者也
聖祖發其義以
示天下而皇極之道明
皇上揭其要以
訓天下而皇極之道行神禹之所受武王之
所訪箕子之所敘者至是如日之中天水
之行地矣
世德作求後先輝映猗歟盛哉所以然者由
punctuated:
申其敷錫者尤彰明較著矣。聖祖闡皇極之義，以正書傳之誤于先；我皇上揭皇極之要，而命殿門之名于後。聖祖之所闡，即皇上之所名也，未遑于昔而有待于今者也。皇上之所名，即聖祖之所闡也，善繼其志而善述其事者也。

聖祖發其義以示天下，而皇極之道明；皇上揭其要以訓天下，而皇極之道行。神禹之所受、武王之所訪、箕子之所敘者，至是如日之中天、水之行地矣。世德作求，後先輝映，猗歟盛哉！所以然者，由
translation_en:
…has made all the more manifest his extension of that bestowal of blessings. Earlier, the Sagely Progenitor elucidated the meaning of the Supreme Standard (huangji), correcting errors in the commentary on the Book of Documents; later, our Emperor brought its essentials to the fore by decreeing the names of the palace halls and gates. What the Sagely Progenitor elucidated is precisely what the Emperor has expressed in these names: something for which there had been no opportunity in the past, and which awaited the present. What the Emperor has expressed in these names is precisely what the Sagely Progenitor elucidated. Thus he has ably carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and continued his undertakings.

The Sagely Progenitor expounded its meaning to instruct all under Heaven, making the Way of the Supreme Standard clear. The Emperor has brought its essentials to the fore to teach all under Heaven, putting the Way of the Supreme Standard into practice. What the divine Yu received, what King Wu inquired about, and what Jizi set forth have now become like the sun at the zenith and water flowing across the earth. The virtue of successive generations is carried forward, predecessor and successor illuminating one another. Ah, how magnificent! The reason for this lies in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
我
聖祖
皇上建極之學即古帝王之學故
聖祖
皇上敷極之治即古帝王之治也愚嘗仰窺其
萬一矣以
聖祖之學言之則
存心有錄矣以
格天爲要也
===
精誠有錄矣以
敬天爲首也又嘗伏讀
諭儒臣宋濂之言曰人心虛靈乘氣機出入操
而存之爲難朕罔敢自暇自逸則我
聖祖之學非以一敬爲之主宰乎非堯舜湯武
之學乎以我
皇上之學言之則
敬一有箴矣慮其弗聚弗純也
五箴有註矣謹于操存省察也又嘗伏讀
punctuated:
我聖祖皇上建極之學，即古帝王之學，故聖祖皇上敷極之治，即古帝王之治也。愚嘗仰窺其萬一矣。
以聖祖之學言之，則存心有錄矣，以格天爲要也；精誠有錄矣，以敬天爲首也。又嘗伏讀諭儒臣宋濂之言曰：「人心虛靈，乘氣機出入，操而存之爲難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」則我聖祖之學，非以一敬爲之主宰乎？非堯舜湯武之學乎？
以我皇上之學言之，則敬一有箴矣，慮其弗聚弗純也；五箴有註矣，謹于操存省察也。又嘗伏讀
translation_en:
…the learning by which our Sagely Founder and His Majesty establish the supreme standard is precisely the learning of the ancient sage kings. Thus, the government through which the Sagely Founder and His Majesty extend that standard is precisely the government of the ancient sage kings. In my ignorance, I have ventured to glimpse the smallest part of it.
Regarding the Sagely Founder’s learning, there is a record on preserving the mind, which takes reaching Heaven as its essential aim; there is a record on perfect sincerity, which gives precedence to revering Heaven. I have also reverently read his admonition to the Confucian court scholar Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the movements of vital energy. To grasp and preserve it is difficult. I dare not allow myself leisure or ease.” Was not the Sagely Founder’s learning, then, governed throughout by reverent attentiveness? Was it not the learning of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu?
Regarding His Majesty’s learning, there is the Admonition on Reverent Oneness, expressing concern lest the mind lack concentration and purity; there are annotations to the Five Admonitions, showing care in holding fast to and preserving the mind, and in examining and scrutinizing oneself. I have also reverently read…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
御製重華殿等各置經書備覽詩有曰靈臺虛
而明燭物别垢臧清濁由此分好惡自酌量
好善而惡惡罔非本其良無黨亦無僻平平
而蕩蕩則我
皇上之學又非一敬以為之主宰乎又孰非堯
舜湯武之學乎故以此而
建極則為有本之德而
克享於天眷有德之心矣
斂福于
===
躬者何莫而非
上帝之寵綏也哉以此而
敷極則為有本之治而無負於天佑下民之
意矣
錫福于下者何莫而非
元后之裁成也哉然極建于君矣臣不協焉非
純臣也極敷于上矣民不協焉非良民也
我
皇上既體
punctuated:
御製《重華殿等各置經書備覽》詩有曰：「靈臺虛而明，燭物别垢臧。清濁由此分，好惡自酌量。好善而惡惡，罔非本其良。無黨亦無僻，平平而蕩蕩。」則我皇上之學，又非一敬以為之主宰乎？又孰非堯舜湯武之學乎？故以此而建極，則為有本之德，而克享於天眷有德之心矣。斂福于躬者，何莫而非上帝之寵綏也哉！以此而敷極，則為有本之治，而無負於天佑下民之意矣。錫福于下者，何莫而非元后之裁成也哉！

然極建于君矣，臣不協焉，非純臣也；極敷于上矣，民不協焉，非良民也。我皇上既體
translation_en:
…the imperially composed poem, “Placing the Classics in Chonghua Hall and Other Halls for Consultation,” contains these lines: “The mind is empty and luminous; illuminating things, it distinguishes impurity from goodness [?]. The clear and turbid are thereby divided; likes and dislikes are duly weighed. Loving good and hating evil—all are rooted in its innate goodness. Without faction or partiality, it is even-handed and broad.” Is not reverent attentiveness likewise the governing principle of our Emperor’s learning? And how could any of it be other than the learning of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu? Thus, by establishing the supreme standard through this learning, he possesses virtue with a firm foundation and can receive the favor of Heaven, whose heart cherishes the virtuous. Of the blessings gathered upon his own person, which is not the loving protection of the Lord on High? By extending the supreme standard through this learning, he establishes government with a firm foundation and does not fail Heaven’s intention to protect the common people. Of the blessings bestowed upon those below, which is not brought to fulfillment through the sovereign’s ordering care?

Yet once the ruler has established the supreme standard, ministers who fail to accord with it are not wholly loyal ministers; once the supreme standard has been extended from above, people who fail to accord with it are not good subjects. Our Emperor has already embodied…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
天之心法
祖之意而
敷極
錫福矣凡我臣民又可不仰遵
聖訓而會極歸極乎是必惟臣欽若而凡有能
有爲者皆進其行以昌其邦而務戒夫偏
陂作好作惡之私則舉天下之爲臣者皆
協于極矣有不受福于
朝者乎惟民從乂而凡有猷有爲有守者皆
===
勵其行以迪其德而胥勸於遵義遵道遵
路之歸則舉天下之爲民者皆協于極矣
有不獲福于身者乎此又我臣民之所當
自盡以隆我
皇上敷極之大化以副我
皇上錫福之盛心者也抑
皇極之斂福固矣然疇之敘福必以壽先之則
壽又福之首而天之所以眷
德者尤莫重於此也我
punctuated:
天之心，法祖之意，而敷極錫福矣。凡我臣民，又可不仰遵聖訓而會極歸極乎？是必惟臣欽若，而凡有能有爲者，皆進其行以昌其邦，而務戒夫偏陂、作好、作惡之私，則舉天下之爲臣者皆協于極矣。有不受福于朝者乎？惟民從乂，而凡有猷有爲有守者，皆勵其行以迪其德，而胥勸於遵義、遵道、遵路之歸，則舉天下之爲民者皆協于極矣。有不獲福于身者乎？此又我臣民之所當自盡，以隆我皇上敷極之大化，以副我皇上錫福之盛心者也。
抑皇極之斂福固矣，然疇之敘福必以壽先之，則壽又福之首，而天之所以眷德者，尤莫重於此也。我
translation_en:
…the heart of Heaven and followed the intentions of his ancestors, thereby extending the supreme standard and bestowing blessings. Can all of us, his subjects, fail to reverently follow the sacred instructions and gather at and return to that standard? His ministers must therefore comply respectfully. All who possess ability and accomplishment must advance their conduct to bring prosperity to their country, taking care to guard against the selfishness of partiality and personal likes and dislikes. Then all ministers throughout the realm will accord with the supreme standard. Will any fail to receive blessings from the court? The people must submit to good governance. All who possess plans, accomplishments, and steadfast principles must diligently improve their conduct to advance their virtue, encouraging one another toward the common end of following righteousness, the Way, and the proper path. Then all the people throughout the realm will accord with the supreme standard. Will any fail to obtain blessings for themselves? Here, too, we subjects must exert ourselves to the utmost, magnifying the great transforming influence through which our Emperor extends the supreme standard and fulfilling his abundant desire to bestow blessings.
Moreover, it is certain that the sovereign’s supreme standard gathers blessings. Yet the category that enumerates the blessings necessarily places longevity first. Thus longevity is foremost among blessings, and among the ways in which Heaven cherishes virtue, none carries greater weight than this. Our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇上仁恩汪濊淪膚浹髓
御極愈久則
建極愈隆
敷極愈遠而
斂福愈大所謂
天壽平格
壽考作人將與
天地同其悠久而受天之祐以
永錫我臣民
===
仁壽之福者蓋有
億萬年無疆之慶矣愚敢以是爲
今日頌
第二問
姚士觀
同考試官教諭李批以仁義和敬立説庶幾知
本之學
考試官教諭何批文義深厚有漢人尺度
考試官教諭錢批有根據有斷制非苟作者
punctuated:
皇上仁恩汪濊，淪膚浹髓。御極愈久，則建極愈隆，敷極愈遠，而斂福愈大。所謂「天壽平格」、「壽考作人」，將與天地同其悠久，而受天之祐，以永錫我臣民仁壽之福者，蓋有億萬年無疆之慶矣。愚敢以是爲今日頌。

第二問
姚士觀

同考試官教諭李批：以仁義和敬立説，庶幾知本之學。
考試官教諭何批：文義深厚，有漢人尺度。
考試官教諭錢批：有根據，有斷制，非苟作者。
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s benevolent grace is vast and abundant, penetrating the skin and suffusing the marrow. The longer he occupies the throne, the more exalted becomes his establishment of the supreme standard, the farther its influence extends, and the greater the blessings he gathers. As the sayings go, “Heaven’s gift of longevity arrives in peace” [?] and “In longevity, he nurtures men.” He will endure as long as Heaven and Earth and receive Heaven’s protection, forever bestowing upon us, his subjects, the blessings of benevolence and longevity. There will surely be boundless joy for countless millions of years. I humbly venture to offer this as today’s encomium.

Second Question
Yao Shiguan

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “He grounds his argument in benevolence, righteousness, harmony, and reverence, approaching a learning that understands the fundamentals.”

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “The writing and its meaning are profound and substantial, possessing the measure of Han writers.”

Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “It has solid foundations and decisive judgments; this is no carelessly composed work.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖王以仁育天下然必其心和而後其仁
溥聖王以義正天下然必其心敬而後其
義行是故心和則氣和氣和而天地之和
咸應焉以格神人以和上下無不得其理
是謂大順心敬則事愼事愼而萬民之情
咸若焉以詰姦慝以一法守無不得其宜
是謂大化大順大化四達不悖此古聖帝
明王端冕而治天下之極也甞考漢司馬
氏敘著樂律推本性情之理至謂刑罰不
===
可捐於國誅伐不可偃於天下此其明於
大較矣乃稱說孝文德厚休寧北陲且無
議軍是時天下殷富雞犬萬里可謂和樂
謂爲樂所由興嗟乎此孔子所謂有德君
子之治儻亦執事發問意耶昔者魯兩生
之言曰禮樂積德百年而後興言和氣之
致難也漢志有之曰郡國被刑之衆此和
氣之未洽也故君子因心致愛因愛致敬
不忍斷一草一木以傷天地之和此致一
punctuated: 聖王以仁育天下，然必其心和而後其仁溥；聖王以義正天下，然必其心敬而後其義行。是故心和則氣和，氣和而天地之和咸應焉，以格神人，以和上下，無不得其理，是謂大順。心敬則事愼，事愼而萬民之情咸若焉，以詰姦慝，以一法守，無不得其宜，是謂大化。大順大化，四達不悖，此古聖帝明王端冕而治天下之極也。甞考漢司馬氏敘著樂律，推本性情之理，至謂刑罰不可捐於國，誅伐不可偃於天下，此其明於大較矣。乃稱說孝文德厚，休寧北陲，且無議軍，是時天下殷富，雞犬萬里，可謂和樂，謂爲樂所由興。嗟乎！此孔子所謂有德君子之治，儻亦執事發問意耶？昔者魯兩生之言曰：「禮樂積德百年而後興。」言和氣之致難也。漢志有之曰：「郡國被刑之衆。」此和氣之未洽也。故君子因心致愛，因愛致敬，不忍斷一草一木以傷天地之和，此致一
translation_en:
The sage king nurtures all under Heaven through benevolence, yet only when his heart is harmonious does his benevolence extend everywhere. The sage king sets all under Heaven right through righteousness, yet only when his heart is reverent does his righteousness take effect. Thus, when the heart is harmonious, the vital energies are harmonious; when the vital energies are harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds in full. Spirits and human beings are thereby reached, and those above and below brought into harmony, with everything attaining its proper order. This is called great accord. When the heart is reverent, affairs are handled carefully; when affairs are handled carefully, the feelings of all the people are fully accommodated. Wickedness and wrongdoing are thereby investigated, and observance of the laws made uniform, with everything attaining what is fitting. This is called great transformation. Great accord and great transformation extend in all four directions without conflict: this is the highest achievement of the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity, who governed all under Heaven in ceremonial robes and caps.

I have examined how the Han historian Sima, in his accounts of music and pitch standards, traced their foundations to the principles of human nature and feelings. He went so far as to say that punishments cannot be discarded within the state, nor punitive campaigns brought to an end throughout the world. In this he understood the broad essentials. Yet he praised Emperor Xiaowen’s abundant virtue, the peace of the northern frontier, and the absence even of discussion of military action. At that time, all under Heaven was prosperous, with chickens and dogs throughout ten thousand li—a condition that could indeed be called harmonious and joyful. He described this as the foundation from which music arises. Ah! This is what Confucius called government by a gentleman possessed of virtue. Might this also be what you intended in posing your question?

Long ago, the two scholars of Lu said: “Rites and music arise only after virtue has accumulated for a hundred years.” This speaks of the difficulty of bringing about harmonious vital energies. A treatise in the History of Han says: “The multitude subjected to punishment in the commanderies and kingdoms.” This shows that harmonious vital energies had not yet spread everywhere. Thus the gentleman develops love from his heart, and reverence from love. He cannot bear to cut a single blade of grass or a single tree and thereby injure the harmony of Heaven and Earth. This bringing to unity …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之謂也樂以和民德仁之通也刑以教民
中義之達也明於制置協於化理洋洋乎
大道也哉嘗考之易豫之象曰先王作樂
崇德殷薦上帝以配祖考此言樂之始也
和之至也自虞廷命后夔典樂而詩歌聲
律八音克諧以和神人乃萬世和樂之原
也厥至戛擊搏拊以詠以間簫韶九成鳳
儀獸舞真如天地覆載舜之樂所以爲盡
善後有作者弗可及矣迨於成周其制大
===
備今載之大司樂所掌樂德樂語樂舞致
神悅人以作動物無非虞廷之義也乃率
屬隸肄有大師小師磬鐘笙韎籥章鞮靺
各有司存此因器備官以陳其殷者文也
夫子所謂武未盡善固自其樂之情求之
季札所謂聖人之難也此古樂之盛也元
儒吳澄氏乃謂大司樂宜隸地官是以禮
樂爲邦教而不知宗伯所以和神人而極
感通之大典也豈非更定之鑿耶然太和
punctuated: 之謂也。樂以和民德，仁之通也；刑以教民中，義之達也。明於制置，協於化理，洋洋乎大道也哉！嘗考之《易》，《豫》之象曰：「先王作樂崇德，殷薦上帝，以配祖考。」此言樂之始也，和之至也。自虞廷命后夔典樂，而詩歌聲律，八音克諧，以和神人，乃萬世和樂之原也。厥至戛擊搏拊，以詠以間，簫韶九成，鳳儀獸舞，真如天地覆載，舜之樂所以爲盡善，後有作者弗可及矣。迨於成周，其制大備。今載之《大司樂》，所掌樂德、樂語、樂舞，致神悅人，以作動物，無非虞廷之義也。乃率屬隸肄，有大師、小師、磬、鐘、笙、韎、籥章、鞮靺，各有司存。此因器備官，以陳其殷者，文也。夫子所謂《武》未盡善，固自其樂之情求之。季札所謂「聖人之難也」，此古樂之盛也。元儒吳澄氏乃謂大司樂宜隸地官，是以禮樂爲邦教，而不知宗伯所以和神人而極感通之大典也。豈非更定之鑿耶？然太和
translation_en:
…that is what is meant. Music harmonizes the people's virtue: it is the pervasive working of benevolence. Punishments teach the people the mean: they are the extension of righteousness. Clear in its institutions and arrangements, consonant with transformative governance—how vast is this Great Way! I have examined the Book of Changes, where the Image commentary on Yu, Enthusiasm, says: “The former kings made music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Supreme Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in sacrifice.” This speaks of the origin of music and the utmost attainment of harmony. When the court of Yu appointed Hou Kui to direct music, poetry, song, tones, and pitch standards brought the eight classes of musical instruments into harmony, thereby harmonizing spirits and human beings. This was the source of harmonious music for all ages. When the instruments were scraped, struck, tapped, and beaten, accompanying the singing and filling its intervals, and the Shao music on the pipes completed its nine movements, phoenixes appeared in stately array and beasts danced. Truly, it was like Heaven covering and Earth bearing all things. Thus Shun's music was perfectly good; no later creator could equal it.

By the time of the Zhou dynasty, the institutions of music were fully developed. As now recorded in the “Grand Director of Music” section of the Rites of Zhou, the musical virtues, musical forms of speech, and musical dances under his charge summoned spirits, delighted people, and stirred living creatures. All embodied the principles of the court of Yu. He led his subordinate personnel in rehearsals; there were the Music Master and Assistant Music Master, and officials responsible for stone chimes, bells, mouth organs, mei music, flute songs, and music of foreign peoples, each with an established charge. Providing officials according to the instruments and displaying this abundance constituted music's outward refinement. When the Master said that the Wu music was not perfectly good, he was surely judging it by its underlying sentiment. As Jizha said, “Even a sage would find it difficult!” Such was the flourishing of ancient music.

Yet the Yuan scholar Wu Cheng maintained that the Grand Director of Music ought to be subordinate to the Ministry of Education. This treats ritual and music as instruments of instruction for the state, without recognizing that the Minister of Rites employed them as the great institutions for harmonizing spirits and human beings and bringing their mutual responsiveness and communion to its utmost extent. Was this not a forced attempt to revise the established arrangement? Yet the supreme harmony…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之在成周宇宙間自唐虞而後一再見也
又嘗考之易旅之象曰君子以明慎用刑
而不留獄此言刑之始也敬之至也自虞
書命皐陶爲士而象有典刑流宥五刑鞭
扑之敎惟刑之恤是萬世明刑之則也厥
至五刑有服五流有宅惟明克允刑期無
刑真如天地之栽培傾覆舜之德所以爲
好生後有作者不可及矣至於有周其法
益詳今載之大司寇所掌三典以刑邦國
===
五刑以糾萬民若兩造兩劑嘉石肺石無
非舜典之遺也然而設參置輔若小司寇
之五聲求民情八辟麗邦法三刺斷訟獄
以施上服下服固因時通變以多其法者
制也然布象魏而浹日始斂又慮民之僞
而防之後世所謂俗薄於唐虞者也此先
王之慎刑也乃大司徒又有八刑糾萬民
是以鄉三物之敎而厲禁以弼成之亦制
刑中而敎祗德也豈非協一之政耶然成
punctuated:
之在成周宇宙間，自唐虞而後一再見也。
又嘗考之《易》，旅之象曰：「君子以明慎用刑，而不留獄。」此言刑之始也，敬之至也。自《虞書》命皐陶爲士，而象有典刑，流宥五刑，鞭扑之敎，惟刑之恤，是萬世明刑之則也。厥至五刑有服，五流有宅，惟明克允，刑期無刑，真如天地之栽培傾覆，舜之德所以爲好生，後有作者不可及矣。至於有周，其法益詳。今載之大司寇所掌，三典以刑邦國，五刑以糾萬民，若兩造、兩劑、嘉石、肺石，無非《舜典》之遺也。然而設參置輔，若小司寇之五聲求民情、八辟麗邦法、三刺斷訟獄，以施上服下服，固因時通變以多其法者，制也。然布象魏而浹日始斂，又慮民之僞而防之，後世所謂俗薄於唐虞者也。此先王之慎刑也。乃大司徒又有八刑糾萬民，是以鄉三物之敎而厲禁以弼成之，亦制刑中而敎祗德也，豈非協一之政耶？然成
translation_en:
…such supreme harmony prevailing throughout the world under the Zhou was something seen only once or twice since the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun.
I have also examined this in the Book of Changes. The Image commentary on the hexagram Lü, “The Wanderer,” says: “The gentleman accordingly applies punishments with discernment and caution, and does not leave cases pending.” This speaks of the initial application of punishment and of the utmost reverence. In the Documents of Yu, Gao Yao was appointed Director of Justice. The prescribed punishments were made manifest; banishment mitigated the five punishments; whipping and beating served as correction; and compassion governed punishment. This is the model for enlightened punishment for all ages. When the five punishments each had their proper application and the five forms of banishment their designated places, discernment alone could ensure fairness, and punishment aimed at eliminating the need for punishment. This truly resembled Heaven and Earth nurturing what stands firm and overturning what leans toward collapse. Thus Shun’s virtue lay in his love of life; no later ruler who undertook such work could equal him.
Under the Zhou, the laws became still more detailed. As now recorded among the responsibilities of the Minister of Justice, three penal codes were used to punish the states and five punishments to correct the myriad people. Such provisions as requiring both parties to appear, the paired written submissions, the Good Stone, and the Lung Stone were all legacies of the “Canon of Shun.” Yet additional officers and assistants were appointed. For example, the Vice Minister of Justice used five modes of examining speech and demeanor to ascertain the true circumstances of the people, eight grounds for special consideration in applying the laws of the realm, and three consultations to decide lawsuits and criminal cases, thereby imposing the higher and lower grades of punishment. These were indeed institutions that adapted to changing times by multiplying legal provisions. Yet the laws were displayed on the palace gate towers and taken down only after ten days; further precautions were taken against possible deceit among the people. This is what later generations meant when they said that customs had deteriorated since the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Such was the former kings’ caution in punishment.
The Minister of Education, moreover, had eight punishments for correcting the myriad people. Thus the teaching of the three categories of instruction in the districts was brought to completion with the aid of strict prohibitions. This too meant establishing punishments in due measure and teaching reverence for virtue. Was this not a coordinated and unified administration? Yet under Cheng…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
康之世刑措不用又自唐虞以來一再見
也三代而下雅樂旣隱新聲代變耀祥於
寶鼎較度於律尺無平心宣化之道而惟
以導欲長怨焉陵夷至於勝國胡部雜進
先王之樂亡矣德教旣弛禁罔寖密緩深
故之罪急縱出之誅雖以隋唐之律疏稍
備而繁苛失當先王用刑之義湮矣洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝挺生南服驅除胡虜
===
統一華夏
功成作樂悉屏前代諠譊之習
命尚書詹同陶凱製宴享九奏樂章曰本太初
曰仰大明曰民初生曰品物亨曰御六龍
曰泰階平曰君德成曰聖道成曰樂清寧
洋洋乎得和平廣大之義後以大成樂器
頒降學校又甞
謂侍臣曰禮以道敬樂以宣和不和不敬何以
爲治大哉
punctuated:
康之世，刑措不用，又自唐虞以來一再見也。三代而下，雅樂旣隱，新聲代變，耀祥於寶鼎，較度於律尺，無平心宣化之道，而惟以導欲長怨焉。陵夷至於勝國，胡部雜進，先王之樂亡矣。德教旣弛，禁罔寖密，緩深故之罪，急縱出之誅。雖以隋唐之律疏稍備，而繁苛失當，先王用刑之義湮矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝挺生南服，驅除胡虜，統一華夏，功成作樂，悉屏前代諠譊之習。命尚書詹同、陶凱製宴享九奏樂章：曰本太初，曰仰大明，曰民初生，曰品物亨，曰御六龍，曰泰階平，曰君德成，曰聖道成，曰樂清寧。洋洋乎，得和平廣大之義。後以大成樂器頒降學校，又甞謂侍臣曰：「禮以道敬，樂以宣和。不和不敬，何以爲治？」大哉，
translation_en:
…and Kang, punishments were laid aside and went unused: here was another occurrence of what had been seen in the days of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. After the Three Dynasties, classical music fell into obscurity, and new sounds changed from age to age. Auspicious signs were displayed in precious tripods, and measurements compared on pitch-standard rulers; yet there was no means of calming hearts and spreading moral transformation, only of encouraging desires and fostering resentment. Decline continued until the preceding dynasty, when foreign musical ensembles were indiscriminately introduced, and the music of the ancient kings disappeared. Moral instruction slackened, while the net of prohibitions grew ever tighter. Deliberately aggravating a defendant’s guilt was punished leniently, while knowingly letting offenders escape punishment was punished severely. Although the statutes and commentaries of the Sui and Tang were somewhat comprehensive, their complexity and severity were inappropriate, and the ancient kings’ principles for applying punishments were lost.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao arose preeminently in the southern lands, expelled the foreign invaders, and unified China. His achievements complete, he instituted music, entirely banishing the clamorous practices of previous dynasties. He ordered the ministers Zhan Tong and Tao Kai to compose nine musical movements for banquets and ceremonial feasts: “Rooted in the Primordial Beginning,” “Looking Up to the Great Brightness,” “The People’s First Beginnings,” “The Myriad Things Flourish,” “Driving the Six Dragons,” “The Three Steps Are at Peace,” “The Ruler’s Virtue Is Perfected,” “The Sagely Way Is Perfected,” and “Rejoicing in Clarity and Tranquillity.” How magnificent they were, embodying harmony, peace, breadth, and grandeur! Later, he distributed instruments for the Music of Great Completion to the schools. He also once told his attendant officials: “Ritual guides people toward reverence; music gives expression to harmony. Without harmony or reverence, how can there be good government?” Great indeed…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
王言所以道中和而崇治體之極
垂裕萬世無疆之烈也又
慎重民命鑒胡元條格之謬
勅尚書劉惟謙重會衆律
親自裁定曰名例曰衛禁曰職制曰戶婚曰廐
庫曰擅興曰盜賊曰鬭訟曰詐偽曰雜律
曰捕亡曰斷獄秩秩乎皆
慈愛仁厚之意先是又有
大明令以
===
曉諭臣民嘗
謂都御史陳瑛等曰人命至重既絕不可復續
理刑必務明慎一哉
王心所以昭損益而適輕重之宜萬世遵守不
易之
典也恭惟
皇上中興履泰禮樂刑政煥然明備
上繼
高皇之
punctuated:
王言，所以道中和而崇治體之極，垂裕萬世無疆之烈也。又慎重民命，鑒胡元條格之謬，勅尚書劉惟謙重會衆律，親自裁定：曰名例，曰衛禁，曰職制，曰戶婚，曰廐庫，曰擅興，曰盜賊，曰鬭訟，曰詐偽，曰雜律，曰捕亡，曰斷獄。秩秩乎，皆慈愛仁厚之意。先是，又有《大明令》，以曉諭臣民。嘗謂都御史陳瑛等曰：「人命至重，既絕不可復續，理刑必務明慎。」一哉，王心！所以昭損益而適輕重之宜，萬世遵守不易之典也。
恭惟皇上中興履泰，禮樂刑政煥然明備，上繼高皇之
translation_en:
…these royal words! They guide people toward equilibrium and harmony and elevate the principles of government to their highest realization—a boundless achievement bequeathing abundance to ten thousand generations. Furthermore, taking the lives of the people most seriously and recognizing the errors in the statutes of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, he commanded Minister Liu Weiqian to compile the laws anew and personally adjudicated and settled them. Their divisions were General Principles; Palace Guards and Prohibitions; Official Regulations; Households and Marriage; Stables and Storehouses; Unauthorized Mobilization; Robbery and Theft; Fighting and Litigation; Fraud and Forgery; Miscellaneous Laws; Apprehension of Fugitives; and Adjudication of Cases. In their orderly arrangement, all expressed his loving kindness, benevolence, and generosity. Before this, there had also been the Ordinances of the Great Ming, issued to instruct officials and commoners. He once told Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying and others: “Human life is of the utmost importance. Once extinguished, it cannot be restored. In administering criminal justice, one must strive for discernment and caution.” How undivided was the royal heart! These provisions made clear what should be removed or added and appropriately calibrated the severity of punishments: an enduring code for ten thousand generations to observe.
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty has brought about a restoration and entered an era of peace and prosperity. Rites, music, punishments, and government shine forth, clearly established and fully provided for. You carry forward Emperor Gao’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
洪猷
遠紹虞周之懿典光天之下巍乎
成功凡厥
典禮悉爲
釐正
定孔廟樂舞之
制又嘗
令太常討論元聲
期復古樂
===
超出千古之見
憫念民獄邇歲申
諭諸司
寛恤刑讞又因廷臣疏
請重修條例以輔律所不及又大舜罪疑惟輕
之仁萬代如見也是宜
和氣薰蒸充塞宇宙
湛恩濊澤覃被海隅不戢之萌旋就底定五
帝之
punctuated: 洪猷，遠紹虞周之懿典，光天之下，巍乎成功！凡厥典禮，悉爲釐正。定孔廟樂舞之制，又嘗令太常討論元聲，期復古樂，超出千古之見。憫念民獄，邇歲申諭諸司，寛恤刑讞。又因廷臣疏請，重修條例，以輔律所不及。又大舜罪疑惟輕之仁，萬代如見也。是宜和氣薰蒸，充塞宇宙；湛恩濊澤，覃被海隅。不戢之萌，旋就底定。五帝之
translation_en: …grand designs, carrying forward the admirable institutions of Yu and Zhou from the distant past. Throughout all beneath shining Heaven, how lofty are his accomplishments! All ceremonial institutions have been corrected. He established the regulations for music and dance at the Confucian temples and also once ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to investigate the fundamental tones, intending to restore ancient music—an insight surpassing the ages. Mindful with compassion of the people’s criminal cases, in recent years he has reiterated instructions to the various offices to exercise leniency and compassion in reviewing criminal judgments. Moreover, following a memorialized request from court officials, he revised the supplementary ordinances to cover matters beyond the statutes’ reach. Here again is the benevolence of the Great Shun, who favored lighter punishment when guilt was doubtful, as though visible across ten thousand generations. It is fitting, then, that the breath of harmony should spread and fill the universe, and that profound favor and abundant beneficence should reach even the remotest shores. Those among the people who would not restrain themselves were soon brought to order. The Five Emperors’ …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
德三王之
治千載一時矣愚生何幸躬逢其
盛
第三問
李伯廉
同考試官教諭易批命意鑄詞雅有源流氣象
是能以文鳴天下者
同考試官教諭金批上下數千載文字之評略
具是篇
===
考試官教諭何批論文而有志於道可謂知本
考試官教諭錢批深厚爾雅是真文矣
夫文辭之興也其因時而為之者乎然以
志闡以道章者也夫文非徒為也觀於時
則教化因之矣求之志則人品因之矣體
之道則情理因之矣是故文以載道而輪
轅是飾則虛車也言以觀人而論篤是與
則色莊也辭以敷化而實不中聲則畫象
也嗚呼文者心之精而道之寄也君子於
punctuated:
德、三王之治，千載一時矣！愚生何幸，躬逢其盛！
第三問
李伯廉
同考試官教諭易批：命意鑄詞，雅有源流氣象，是能以文鳴天下者。
同考試官教諭金批：上下數千載文字之評，略具是篇。
考試官教諭何批：論文而有志於道，可謂知本。
考試官教諭錢批：深厚爾雅，是真文矣。
夫文辭之興也，其因時而為之者乎？然以志闡，以道章者也。夫文非徒為也，觀於時，則教化因之矣；求之志，則人品因之矣；體之道，則情理因之矣。是故文以載道，而輪轅是飾，則虛車也；言以觀人，而論篤是與，則色莊也；辭以敷化，而實不中聲，則畫象也。嗚呼！文者，心之精而道之寄也。君子於
translation_en:
…virtue and the governance of the Three Kings: such a conjunction comes but once in a thousand years! How fortunate I, an unworthy student, am to witness this flourishing age in person!
Third Question
Li Bolian
Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: In conceiving its ideas and fashioning its language, this essay has the cultivated bearing of writing rooted in an established tradition. Here is someone capable of making his name throughout the realm through literature.
Comment by Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor: Assessments of writing across several thousand years are presented in outline in this essay.
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: To discuss literature while aspiring to the Way may be called understanding the root.
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: Profound, substantial, and refined: this is true literature.
As literary expression arises, is it perhaps composed in response to its times? Yet it is through intent that it unfolds, and through the Way that it becomes manifest. Writing is not produced to no purpose. Consider it in relation to its times, and moral instruction proceeds through it; examine it for its intent, and the writer’s character finds expression through it; embody the Way in it, and human feelings and principles find expression through it. Thus, writing serves to carry the Way, but if one merely embellishes the wheels and shafts, it is an empty carriage. Speech serves to reveal a person, but if one approves someone merely for earnest discourse, this is only an appearance of solemnity. Literary expression serves to spread moral transformation, but if its substance does not accord with its sound, it is merely a painted image. Ah! Literature is the essence of the heart and the dwelling place of the Way. In it the gentleman…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
是乎考德而徵教焉是豈可以易言哉嘗
聞之太上立德其次立功其次立言言也
者君子不得已而為之然由之不朽者固
道化之極也說者謂文章與時高下以易
詩書春秋屬之皇帝王伯焉是故虞夏之
書渾渾爾商書灝灝爾周書噩噩爾此時
代之變也泥焉者為之則犧尊而青黃之
以簿書而效羲軒之畫舛矣夫子之教曰
有德者必有言是故吉人之辭寡躁人之
===
辭多中心疑者其辭枝誣善之人其辭游
此志氣之別也矯焉者為之則繡其鼙帨
羊質而虎皮鑿矣或者謂文者貫道之器
無係於道非其至者也是故說天莫辨乎
易說事莫辨於書說志莫辨於詩說體莫
辨於禮說理莫辨於春秋此理道之殊致
也昧焉者為之則孤峰絕壁施之廊廟而
駭矣嗟夫文若是也與哉粵自天地儲精
因文以示日月星辰之爛曜山川草木人
punctuated: 是乎考德而徵教焉，是豈可以易言哉？嘗聞之：太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。言也者，君子不得已而為之，然由之不朽者，固道化之極也。說者謂文章與時高下，以《易》《詩》《書》《春秋》屬之皇帝王伯焉。是故虞夏之書渾渾爾，商書灝灝爾，周書噩噩爾，此時代之變也。泥焉者為之，則犧尊而青黃之，以簿書而效羲軒之畫，舛矣。夫子之教曰：「有德者必有言。」是故吉人之辭寡，躁人之辭多，中心疑者其辭枝，誣善之人其辭游，此志氣之別也。矯焉者為之，則繡其鼙帨，羊質而虎皮，鑿矣。或者謂文者貫道之器，無係於道，非其至者也。是故說天莫辨乎《易》，說事莫辨於《書》，說志莫辨於《詩》，說體莫辨於《禮》，說理莫辨於《春秋》，此理道之殊致也。昧焉者為之，則孤峰絕壁施之廊廟，而駭矣。嗟夫！文若是也與哉？粵自天地儲精，因文以示，日月星辰之爛曜，山川草木人
translation_en:
…in this, he examines virtue and seeks evidence of moral instruction. How could this be spoken of lightly? I have heard it said: highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievements; next is establishing words. The gentleman commits himself to words only when he cannot do otherwise. Yet to attain immortality through them is indeed the highest realization of the Way’s transforming power. Commentators say that literary writing rises and falls with its age, assigning the Changes, Odes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals to the august sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons. Thus the documents of Yu and Xia are deep and ample; those of Shang, vast and flowing; those of Zhou, grave and austere. These are changes between historical ages. Those who write while clinging rigidly to these examples paint a sacrificial vessel green and yellow; to imitate the diagrams of Fuxi and Xuanyuan through clerical records is a misapplication.

The Master taught: “Those who possess virtue necessarily have something to say.” Thus the words of an auspicious person are few; those of an impetuous person are many. Those who harbor doubts speak in branching digressions; those who slander the good speak evasively. These are distinctions of intent and disposition. Those who write by artificially forcing such qualities embroider their drums and handcloths [?]: with the substance of a sheep beneath a tiger’s skin, they are contrived.

Some say that writing is a vessel through which the Way runs. Writing unconnected with the Way is not its highest realization. Thus nothing explains Heaven more clearly than the Changes; nothing explains affairs more clearly than the Documents; nothing explains aspirations more clearly than the Odes; nothing explains proper forms more clearly than the Rites; and nothing explains principles more clearly than the Spring and Autumn Annals. These are the distinct ways in which principle and the Way find expression. Those who write without understanding this place a solitary peak or sheer cliff within the halls of government, producing something alarming. Alas! Is this what writing should be?

From the time Heaven and Earth amassed their vital essence, they have revealed it through patterned forms: the brilliant radiance of sun, moon, and stars; mountains, rivers, grasses, trees, and human…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
物之森錯此天地之至文也及夫河洛肇
祥圖書著象而天地之文寄之人矣聖人
者因象以闡數因數以明理彌綸天下之
事著古昔之𠾱𠾱傳千里之忞忞莫非發
揮精蘊經緯人物無意於為文而文莫尚
焉墳典以降六經繼作帝王之道可得而
睹矣秦漢而下言文者率稱漢魏之際多
文人才士焉今觀魏文典論其言七子之
失得詳矣然謂四科不同人有偏能引氣
===
不齊巧拙有素斯文林之孜鏡而達旨之
真諦也陸機文賦備極敷陳妙解情理至
稱謝朝華之已披啓夕秀於未振固百代
之上所獨得者又謂立片辭以居要乃一
篇之警策彬彬乎文質之致矣所謂弘博
君子者耶唐獨孤郁之為文辨有言彩飾
其字慎所為體斯易春秋之一畫一字極
而與天地準者乃所謂其心卓然而絕於
俗不求文而自至者故達論也李文饒忠
punctuated: 物之森錯，此天地之至文也。及夫河洛肇祥，圖書著象，而天地之文寄之人矣。聖人者，因象以闡數，因數以明理，彌綸天下之事，著古昔之𠾱𠾱，傳千里之忞忞，莫非發揮精蘊，經緯人物。無意於為文，而文莫尚焉。墳典以降，六經繼作，帝王之道可得而睹矣。秦漢而下，言文者率稱漢魏之際，多文人才士焉。今觀魏文《典論》，其言七子之失得詳矣。然謂四科不同，人有偏能，引氣不齊，巧拙有素，斯文林之孜鏡，而達旨之真諦也。陸機《文賦》，備極敷陳，妙解情理，至稱「謝朝華之已披，啓夕秀於未振」，固百代之上所獨得者。又謂「立片辭以居要，乃一篇之警策」，彬彬乎文質之致矣，所謂弘博君子者耶？唐獨孤郁之《為文辨》有言：「彩飾其字，慎所為體。」斯《易》《春秋》之一畫一字，極而與天地準者，乃所謂「其心卓然而絕於俗，不求文而自至」者，故達論也。李文饒忠
translation_en:
…the dense array of beings: this is the supreme patterned expression of Heaven and Earth. When auspicious signs first appeared in the Yellow and Luo Rivers, and the River Chart and Luo Writing displayed their images, the patterned expression of Heaven and Earth was entrusted to human beings. The sages elucidated numbers through images and clarified principles through numbers. They comprehensively ordered the affairs of the world, made manifest the distant matters of antiquity [?], and conveyed thoughts from a thousand li away [?]. All of this brought forth profound meanings and ordered human beings and things. They had no intention of producing literary ornament, yet no writing surpassed theirs. From the Ancient Records and Canons onward, the Six Classics arose in succession, making the Way of emperors and kings visible.

From the Qin and Han onward, those who discuss literature generally praise the abundance of accomplished writers and talented men during the transition from Han to Wei. Looking now at Emperor Wen of Wei’s Authoritative Discourses (Dianlun), we find a detailed account of the strengths and weaknesses of the Seven Masters. Yet his statements that the four categories of writing differ, that individuals possess particular talents, that vital energy is unequal [?], and that skill and clumsiness have an inherent basis constitute a discerning mirror for the literary world [?] and the true essence of comprehending literary purpose.

Lu Ji’s Rhapsody on Literature (Wenfu) offers the fullest exposition and a subtle understanding of feeling and principle. His words, “Bid farewell to morning blossoms already unfolded; open the evening flowers that have yet to bloom,” express an insight uniquely attained across a hundred generations. He also says, “Set a brief phrase in a crucial position: it becomes the arresting admonition of the entire piece.” How finely this realizes the harmonious union of ornament and substance! Was he what is called a gentleman of broad learning?

Dugu Yu of the Tang says in his Disquisition on Literary Composition (Weiwen bian): “Embellish its words; take care over the form you employ.” Thus, a single line in the Book of Changes or a single word in the Spring and Autumn Annals, carried to its utmost significance, accords with Heaven and Earth. This is what is meant by “his mind stands loftily apart from convention; without seeking literary excellence, he attains it naturally.” It is therefore a penetrating judgment. Li Wenrao’s loyalty…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
貞世篤丹扆諸箴油然正君之大雅古之
遠不忘君者也然其文論謂氣不可不貫
故曹氏之遺旨也至於文箴謂文之爲物
自然靈氣信乎迫於促節者音律之爲病
矣知言哉由是以推代有述作然莫備於
有唐之朝史稱唐文三變故一代之極則
也攷之劉禹錫序柳子之集曰三代之文
至戰國而病涉秦漢復起漢之文至列國
而病唐興復起治亂之致文辭因之言時
===
代之變者莫當於此矣而非其至也尚衡
序文道元龜有曰君子之文其德全志士
之文其義全詞士之文其思全此自其人
三等之義也然辭士徇辭無取頹靡志士
氣高調苦有感激之道焉誠介然自立者
衡且自道也若夫飾行表德道天人之際
達性命之元非君子之行爲之質焉曷以
文成而見情著事耶故言人品之差者莫
辨於此矣而非其宜也吕溫秀含五行光
punctuated:
貞世篤，《丹扆》諸箴，油然正君之大雅，古之遠不忘君者也。然其《文論》謂氣不可不貫，故曹氏之遺旨也。至於《文箴》，謂文之爲物，自然靈氣，信乎迫於促節者，音律之爲病矣。知言哉！由是以推，代有述作，然莫備於有唐之朝。史稱唐文三變，故一代之極則也。攷之劉禹錫序柳子之集曰：「三代之文，至戰國而病，涉秦漢復起；漢之文，至列國而病，唐興復起。治亂之致，文辭因之。」言時代之變者，莫當於此矣，而非其至也。
尚衡序《文道元龜》有曰：「君子之文，其德全；志士之文，其義全；詞士之文，其思全。」此自其人三等之義也。然辭士徇辭，無取頹靡；志士氣高調苦，有感激之道焉，誠介然自立者，衡且自道也。若夫飾行表德，道天人之際，達性命之元，非君子之行爲之質焉，曷以文成而見情著事耶？故言人品之差者，莫辨於此矣，而非其宜也。吕溫秀含五行，光
translation_en:
…steadfast in loyalty through successive generations. His Admonitions of the Vermilion Screen and other admonitions naturally possess the grand refinement of writing that rectifies the ruler: he was like those men of antiquity who, though far away, never forgot their sovereign. Yet his Discourse on Writing says that vital energy must run throughout a composition, thus preserving the purport of Master Cao’s teaching. As for his Admonition on Writing, it says that writing, as a thing, is a naturally arising spiritual energy. Indeed, when it is constrained by hurried rhythms, the rules of sound and meter become a malady. How well he understood these words! Extending this inquiry, every age has had its writings, but none has been more fully endowed than the Tang dynasty. The histories speak of three transformations in Tang writing; these constituted the highest standards of that age. Examining Liu Yuxi’s preface to Master Liu’s collected works, we find: “The writing of the Three Dynasties fell into decline in the Warring States period, then revived through the Qin and Han. Han writing fell into decline in the period of the divided states, then revived with the rise of the Tang. Literary expression follows the conditions brought about by order and disorder.” No account of changes across the ages is more apt than this, yet it does not reach the ultimate point.
In his preface to the Primal Mirror of the Way of Writing, Shang Heng says: “In the writing of the gentleman, virtue is complete; in the writing of the man of resolve, righteousness is complete; in the writing of the literary craftsman, thought is complete.” This establishes three grades according to the character of the writers themselves. Yet literary craftsmen pursue verbal expression, and there is nothing to commend in decadent weakness. Men of resolve have lofty spirits and anguished tones; their writing gives expression to deeply stirred feelings. They are indeed men who stand firmly on their own, and Heng was also describing himself. But when it comes to refining conduct and manifesting virtue, speaking of the relationship between Heaven and humanity, and comprehending the origins of human nature and destiny, unless the gentleman’s conduct provides the substance, how can completed writing reveal feelings and make affairs manifest? Thus no account distinguishes differences in human character more clearly than this, yet it does not establish the appropriate standard. Lü Wen’s excellence embraced the Five Phases, and his radiance…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
掩一代其著人文化成論所稱夫以剛克
妻以柔立父慈而教子孝而箴爲室家之
文君以仁使臣以義事違弼獻替爲朝廷
之文三公論道六卿分職百揆同歸爲官
司之文寬猛相濟爲刑政之文禮樂變通
爲教化之文其意質而幾於理矣劉夢得
稱其以致君及物爲大欲考要帝王富疆
之際循理合心揭日月而行之偉矣其如
行不掩焉何哉雖然是數子之論文詳矣
===
然魏文父子狙詐相承情投七子而慙德
於七步之吟千載有餘慨焉係蹤張蔡才
如積玉士衡亦一代之絕矣不免太息於
黑幔之夢劉吕之詞贍而豔矣乃身陷叔
文之黨此昔人重有感於言行相顧之難
也自唐而後宋德隆盛厥有歐曾蘇王稱
其名家而上擬唐漢不無濫觴餘波之訛
焉甚矣文之難言也故惟周子太極圖說
張子西銘程子易春秋傳序號著有宋四
punctuated:
掩一代。其著《人文化成論》，所稱「夫以剛克，妻以柔立，父慈而教，子孝而箴，爲室家之文；君以仁使，臣以義事，違弼獻替，爲朝廷之文；三公論道，六卿分職，百揆同歸，爲官司之文；寬猛相濟，爲刑政之文；禮樂變通，爲教化之文」，其意質而幾於理矣。劉夢得稱其以致君及物爲大欲，考要帝王富疆之際，循理合心，揭日月而行之，偉矣！其如行不掩焉何哉？雖然，是數子之論文詳矣。
然魏文父子，狙詐相承，情投七子，而慙德於七步之吟，千載有餘慨焉。係蹤張蔡，才如積玉，士衡亦一代之絕矣，不免太息於黑幔之夢。劉吕之詞贍而豔矣，乃身陷叔文之黨。此昔人重有感於言行相顧之難也。自唐而後，宋德隆盛，厥有歐曾蘇王，稱其名家，而上擬唐漢，不無濫觴餘波之訛焉。甚矣，文之難言也！故惟周子《太極圖說》、張子《西銘》、程子《易》《春秋》傳序，號著有宋四
translation_en:
…overshadowed an entire age. In his Discourse on Transformation through Human Culture, he writes: “The husband governs through firmness, and the wife establishes herself through gentleness; the father teaches with affection, and the son offers admonition with filial devotion: these constitute the patterned order of the household. The ruler employs his ministers with benevolence, and ministers serve him with righteousness; they correct his errors, present what is good, and remove what is harmful: these constitute the patterned order of the court. The Three Dukes discuss the Way, the Six Ministers divide their duties, and the hundred offices converge upon a common end: these constitute the patterned order of official administration. Leniency and severity temper one another: this constitutes the patterned order of punishment and government. Ritual and music adapt to changing circumstances: this constitutes the patterned order of moral transformation.” His meaning is substantial and approaches principle. Liu Mengde praised him for making service to the ruler and benefit to all things his great aspiration, examining the essentials of how emperors and kings attained wealth and strength [?], following principle and according with the heart, and putting these into practice with the sun and moon held aloft. Magnificent indeed! Yet what can be done about his conduct failing to match this? Nevertheless, these men's discussions of writing were comprehensive.
Yet Emperor Wen of Wei and his father perpetuated cunning and deceit. Though he felt an affinity with the Seven Masters, the poem composed in seven paces exposed his shameful conduct, leaving cause for lament more than a thousand years later. Following in the footsteps of Zhang and Cai, with talent like a heap of jade, Shiheng too was an unrivalled figure of his age; yet one cannot help sighing deeply over his dream of the black curtain [?]. The writings of Liu and Lü were abundant and brilliant, yet they themselves became entangled in Shuwen's faction. This is why men of former times felt so deeply the difficulty of making words and conduct accord with one another. After the Tang, the virtue of the Song flourished greatly. Ouyang, Zeng, Su, and Wang were acclaimed as eminent masters and compared with those of the Tang and Han; yet errors arising from literary currents, from their beginnings to their later offshoots, were not absent. How very difficult it is to speak of writing! Thus only Master Zhou's Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Master Zhang's Western Inscription, and Master Cheng's prefaces to the commentaries on the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals were renowned as the Song dynasty's four …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
大作乃載道以爲文斯百世不可易也繼
往聖之絕學開後儒之道統斯爲聖賢之
徒而何以世代論哉然言文之體要者莫
過於宋真德秀氏其爲文章正宗自六經
以下斷自左氏下及有唐而止分屬辭命
議論敘事詩賦四體擇取古文辭之雅馴
類輯標示來學總略旨要犂然當理足令
三代而下仰見古人之奧信乎修辭者之
規矩百世可施行者也後之爲文者有體
===
道之心若周程張子尤以六經爲楨幹而
復參酌於真氏焉則於文道思過半矣
第四問
吳思學
同考試官教諭胡批〔意氣激昂議論切實殆非空言者〕
同考試官教諭項批〔評品曲當詞采溢目可敬可敬〕
考試官教諭何批〔知言之士取之〕
考試官教諭錢批〔是真有志尚友者〕
punctuated:
大作，乃載道以爲文，斯百世不可易也。繼往聖之絕學，開後儒之道統，斯爲聖賢之徒，而何以世代論哉？然言文之體要者，莫過於宋真德秀氏。其爲《文章正宗》，自六經以下，斷自左氏，下及有唐而止，分屬辭命、議論、敘事、詩賦四體，擇取古文辭之雅馴，類輯標示來學，總略旨要，犂然當理，足令三代而下仰見古人之奧。信乎修辭者之規矩，百世可施行者也。後之爲文者，有體道之心，若周程張子，尤以六經爲楨幹，而復參酌於真氏焉，則於文道思過半矣。

第四問
吳思學
同考試官教諭胡批〔意氣激昂，議論切實，殆非空言者。〕
同考試官教諭項批〔評品曲當，詞采溢目，可敬，可敬。〕
考試官教諭何批〔知言之士，取之。〕
考試官教諭錢批〔是真有志尚友者。〕
translation_en:
…great works: they make writing a vehicle for the Way, and thus remain unalterable for a hundred generations. They carry on the lost learning of the sages of old and open the orthodox succession of the Way to later Confucians. Such men belong among the sages and worthies; how could they be judged by the age in which they lived? Yet among those who have discussed the essential forms and principles of writing, none surpasses Zhen Dexiu of the Song. His Orthodox Tradition of Literature (Wenzhang zhengzong), taking literature subsequent to the Six Classics, begins with Master Zuo and extends through the Tang. He divides it into four forms: diplomatic pronouncements, argumentation, narrative, and poetry and rhapsodies. Selecting ancient writings of elegance and propriety, he groups them by kind and presents them as guides to later students. His summaries of their essential purport are lucid and accord with principle, enabling those living after the Three Dynasties to look up to and perceive the profundity of the ancients. Truly, this is a standard for those who cultivate literary expression, applicable for a hundred generations. If later writers possess a resolve to embody the Way, as did Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang, and above all take the Six Classics as their framework while also consulting and weighing Master Zhen’s work, they will have advanced more than halfway toward understanding the Way of writing.

Fourth Question
Wu Sixue
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔His spirit is ardent and elevated, and his arguments are practical and pertinent. These are surely no empty words.〕
Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor, comments: 〔His assessments are apt in every detail, and his literary brilliance fills the eye. Admirable, admirable!〕
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔A scholar who understands words. Select him.〕
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: 〔Here is someone truly resolved to seek fellowship with the worthies of antiquity.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
君子之多識以畜德也而通於今者尤為
博古之助君子之論世以尚友也而求諸
近者尤為遠覽之資何則遠近一心也古
今一理也得其心與理則近猶遠也近篤
而遠益可舉矣今猶古也今準而古益可
酌矣不然卽高極卷由逖窮綺里祗開喪
志之隙耳舍負郭而田甫田不以勞乎生
乎今之世反乎古之道不以倍乎故流水
之為物也不盈科不行君子之志於道也
===
不成章不達君子而欲斐然成章則吾黨
先進不可不論其世而尚友多識其前言
往行而畜德矣執事以江右雋傑言行表
見於我
朝者為問蓋以志尹學顏之業望諸生也愚
不敏往讀王子安滕王閣序其流連光景
模寫情狀吾無取焉獨於江藩形勢之盛
則攬結殆盡其曰星分翼軫翼軫鳥宿也
得文明之位矣曰地接衡廬衡岳宗廬名
punctuated:
君子之多識以畜德也，而通於今者尤為博古之助；君子之論世以尚友也，而求諸近者尤為遠覽之資。何則？遠近一心也，古今一理也。得其心與理，則近猶遠也，近篤而遠益可舉矣；今猶古也，今準而古益可酌矣。不然，卽高極卷由，逖窮綺里，祗開喪志之隙耳。舍負郭而田甫田，不以勞乎？生乎今之世，反乎古之道，不以倍乎？故流水之為物也，不盈科不行；君子之志於道也，不成章不達。君子而欲斐然成章，則吾黨先進不可不論其世而尚友，多識其前言往行而畜德矣。
執事以江右雋傑言行表見於我朝者為問，蓋以志尹學顏之業望諸生也。愚不敏，往讀王子安《滕王閣序》，其流連光景、模寫情狀，吾無取焉；獨於江藩形勢之盛，則攬結殆盡。其曰「星分翼軫」，翼軫鳥宿也，得文明之位矣。曰「地接衡廬」，衡岳宗，廬名
translation_en:
The gentleman acquires wide knowledge to cultivate virtue, and understanding the present is especially helpful in gaining broad knowledge of antiquity. The gentleman considers the ages in which others lived in order to befriend worthy predecessors, and seeking among those nearer at hand is especially useful for surveying the distant past. Why is this? Those near and far share one human heart; antiquity and the present share one principle. Once one grasps this heart and principle, the near is like the distant: a firm grounding in the near makes the distant all the more accessible. The present is like antiquity: taking the present as a standard makes antiquity all the more open to judicious consideration. Otherwise, even if one reaches upward as far as Juan and You [?], and searches the distant past as far as Qili, one merely creates an opening for losing one’s resolve. To abandon fields beside the city walls and cultivate vast distant fields—is this not toil? To live in the present age yet revert to the ways of antiquity—is this not perverse? Thus flowing water does not advance until it has filled each hollow; the gentleman intent upon the Way does not attain understanding until his learning has taken coherent form. If a gentleman wishes his learning to take splendid, coherent form, he must consider the times of the predecessors in our own community and befriend them, acquiring extensive knowledge of their words and deeds in order to cultivate virtue.
You, honored examiners, have asked about outstanding men of Jiangyou whose words and deeds have won distinction under our dynasty. Surely you expect us students to undertake the work of aspiring to be like Yi Yin and learning from Yan Hui. Though I am dull-witted, I once read Wang Zi’an’s Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng. I find nothing to adopt in its lingering over scenery or its depictions of appearances and circumstances; yet it captures almost completely the grandeur of Jiangxi’s geographical setting. It says, “Its stellar divisions are Yi and Zhen.” Yi and Zhen are lunar lodges of the Vermilion Bird: thus this region occupies a position of cultured brilliance. It says, “Its lands adjoin Heng and Lu.” Mount Heng is a patriarch among the sacred peaks, and Mount Lu a renowned …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
鎮也神明和氣在焉曰襟三江而帶五湖
則馮夷陽侯所居實鍾靈秀曰控荆蠻而
引甌越則又見川原延袤寰宇寥廓而人
之生於其間者必皆疏暢洞達而非膚淺
狹小者矣故在晉則有若陶潜𡗝漢則有
若徐穉在唐則有若李覯在宋元則有若
文天祥揭傒斯之數子者或以節義稱或
以文采著或以功業顯雖歷代之英不止
於此而此其最彰明者矣我
===
朝肇宇實汛胡元去穢德之氛復華夏之氣
文明之象也以
太祖之聖開混一之統煕洽之幾也則應五百
之運際風雲之會如元凱之於堯舜俊宅
之於文武寜無人耶矧吾江藩地靈人傑
素甲天下者耶甞取列郡邑乘讀之每得
一人輒踊躍思奮恨未得與之遊而挹其
光霽又恨未得與之竝立于朝而同寅協
恭也舉以語人則黨中一二長老猶歷歷
punctuated: 鎮也，神明和氣在焉。曰「襟三江而帶五湖」，則馮夷、陽侯所居，實鍾靈秀。曰「控荆蠻而引甌越」，則又見川原延袤，寰宇寥廓，而人之生於其間者，必皆疏暢洞達，而非膚淺狹小者矣。故在晉則有若陶潜，𡗝漢則有若徐穉，在唐則有若李覯，在宋元則有若文天祥、揭傒斯之數子者，或以節義稱，或以文采著，或以功業顯。雖歷代之英不止於此，而此其最彰明者矣。我朝肇宇，實汛胡元，去穢德之氛，復華夏之氣，文明之象也。以太祖之聖，開混一之統，煕洽之幾也。則應五百之運，際風雲之會，如元凱之於堯舜、俊宅之於文武，寜無人耶？矧吾江藩，地靈人傑，素甲天下者耶？甞取列郡邑乘讀之，每得一人，輒踊躍思奮，恨未得與之遊而挹其光霽，又恨未得與之竝立于朝而同寅協恭也。舉以語人，則黨中一二長老猶歷歷
translation_en:
…a guardian peak; divine powers and harmonious energies reside there. When he says, “With the Three Rivers as its lapels and the Five Lakes as its girdle,” these are the abodes of Feng Yi and Yang Hou, the water deities, where spiritual potency and beauty truly gather. When he says, “Commanding Jingman and drawing in Ou and Yue,” we see, moreover, rivers and plains stretching far and wide, and the vast expanse of the world. Those born amid such surroundings must surely be open-minded and perceptive, rather than shallow and narrow. Thus, under the Jin there was Tao Qian; under the Han [?] there was Xu Zhi; under the Tang there was Li Gou [?, who lived under the Song]; and under the Song and Yuan there were men such as Wen Tianxiang and Jie Xisi. Some were acclaimed for integrity and righteousness, some renowned for literary accomplishment, and some distinguished by their achievements in public service. Although the outstanding men of successive ages were not limited to these, these were the most illustrious.

When our dynasty established its dominion, it swept away [?] the alien Yuan, dispelled the miasma of corrupt virtue, and restored the vital spirit of the Chinese realm: this was a manifestation of flourishing civilization. Through Taizu’s sagely wisdom, it inaugurated a unified succession of rule: this was the beginning of prosperity and harmony. Could there have been no men who answered the five-hundred-year cycle and encountered that convergence of auspicious circumstances, as the Eight Worthies and Eight Talents did under Yao and Shun, and the eminent men [?] under Kings Wen and Wu? How much more must this be true of our province of Jiangxi, whose spiritually potent land and outstanding people have long ranked foremost in the realm!

I once took up and read the gazetteers of the various prefectures and counties. Whenever I came upon such a man, I would leap with excitement and feel stirred to exert myself. I regretted that I had never been able to associate with him and imbibe his radiant, serene bearing; I also regretted that I had never stood beside him at court, joined in reverence and working together respectfully. When I brought these men up in conversation, one or two elders of the locality still vividly…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
道其事若目擊然無他居相近世不相遠
也故於泰和而得楊文貞士奇王文端直
焉於吉水而得周文襄忱於永新而得劉
文安定之焉於安福而得李文毅時勉劉
忠愍球劉南雄實焉於永豐而得鍾恭愍
同羅修撰倫焉於豐城於南昌於靖安崇
仁而得朱學士善胡祭酒儼況蘇州鍾吳
徵君與弼焉往秩宗楊文恪倣宋朝朱子
名臣言行錄為
===
皇明名臣言行錄自中山武寧王而下凡五十
有四人而文貞等十有三人與焉視彭司
寇所論賛更為詳悉今其書固在不可以
稽心術之微而驗行事之迹耶周禮大司
徒以建邦五典教萬民不啻足矣然必有
鄉師以掌其鄉之治教又有鄉大夫以攷
德行察道藝至於比閭族黨咸有師長胥
正焉無非欲其相觀而善相摩而成也故
曰吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易也張□之
punctuated:
道其事，若目擊然。無他，居相近，世不相遠也。故於泰和而得楊文貞士奇、王文端直焉；於吉水而得周文襄忱，於永新而得劉文安定之焉；於安福而得李文毅時勉、劉忠愍球、劉南雄實焉；於永豐而得鍾恭愍同、羅修撰倫焉；於豐城、於南昌、於靖安、崇仁而得朱學士善、胡祭酒儼、況蘇州鍾、吳徵君與弼焉。往秩宗楊文恪倣宋朝朱子《名臣言行錄》，為《皇明名臣言行錄》，自中山武寧王而下，凡五十有四人，而文貞等十有三人與焉。視彭司寇所論賛，更為詳悉。今其書固在，不可以稽心術之微，而驗行事之迹耶？

《周禮》大司徒以建邦五典教萬民，不啻足矣。然必有鄉師以掌其鄉之治教，又有鄉大夫以攷德行、察道藝。至於比、閭、族、黨，咸有師、長、胥、正焉，無非欲其相觀而善，相摩而成也。故曰：「吾觀於鄉，而知王道之易易也。」張□之
translation_en:
…recounted their deeds as though they had witnessed them themselves. There was no other reason for this: they lived nearby, and their generations were not far apart. Thus, in Taihe we find Yang Shiqi, posthumously titled Wenzhen, and Wang Zhi, posthumously titled Wenduan; in Jishui, Zhou Chen, posthumously titled Wenxiang; and in Yongxin, Liu Dingzhi, posthumously titled Wen’an. In Anfu we find Li Shimian, posthumously titled Wenyi, Liu Qiu, posthumously titled Zhongmin, and Liu Shi, Prefect of Nanxiong. In Yongfeng we find Zhong Tong, posthumously titled Gongmin, and Hanlin Compiler Luo Lun. In Fengcheng, Nanchang, Jing’an, and Chongren we find Academician Zhu Shan, Director of Education Hu Yan, Kuang Zhong, Prefect of Suzhou, and Wu Yubi, the gentleman summoned to serve at court.

Formerly, the Minister of Rites Yang, posthumously titled Wenke, modeled his Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers of the August Ming on Master Zhu’s Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers from the Song dynasty. Beginning with the Prince of Zhongshan, posthumously titled Wuning, it included fifty-four men in all, among whom were Wenzhen and the other twelve men just named. It was more detailed and comprehensive than the appraisals written by Peng, the Minister of Justice. That book is still extant today. Can we not use it to investigate the subtleties of their moral intentions and examine the traces of their conduct?

In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education taught all the people through the five norms by which the state was established. This should have been more than sufficient. Yet there also had to be District Preceptors to oversee administration and instruction in their districts, and District Grand Masters to assess virtuous conduct and examine attainments in the Way and the arts. Even the neighborhood units—the bi, lü, zu, and dang—each had their preceptors, chiefs, assistants, and headmen. All this was intended to enable people to become better by observing one another and to perfect themselves through mutual influence. Thus it is said: “From observing the village, I know how very easy the kingly Way is to practice.” Zhang □’s [name partly illegible]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
窮河源也自豐水始未有不渡豐水而能
窮河源者也夸父之隨日而步也自嵎夷
始未有不由嵎夷而能隨日者也故遠有
所慕者必近有所遺明珠在懷而索之途
則亦左矣故凡鄉之賢士大夫不可不考
而知之則而象之也自今言之歷事
四朝卓然而弘輔相之業者文貞也巡撫三吳
淵然而裕
國計之大者文襄也以拜祭酒者胡則身率
===
諸生成均翕然以從化李則教倣安定胄
子勃然而興起非辟雍之良範耶以居翰
林者朱則掌制校文不負乃祖令器之許
劉則三疏百首無忝八面受敵之才非瀛
洲之妙選耶文端首正奔競之習鳴朝陽
之鳳也彝正抗論起復之非埋都亭之輪
也恭愍作柱史而議揭三綱忠肝義膽貫
日月矣忠愍為侍講而條陳十事奇氣疎
節凌漢霄矣守蘇州而剛毅正直有張詠
punctuated:
窮河源也，自豐水始，未有不渡豐水而能窮河源者也。夸父之隨日而步也，自嵎夷始，未有不由嵎夷而能隨日者也。故遠有所慕者，必近有所遺。明珠在懷而索之途，則亦左矣。故凡鄉之賢士大夫，不可不考而知之，則而象之也。
自今言之，歷事四朝，卓然而弘輔相之業者，文貞也；巡撫三吳，淵然而裕國計之大者，文襄也。以拜祭酒者，胡則身率諸生，成均翕然以從化；李則教倣安定，胄子勃然而興起，非辟雍之良範耶？以居翰林者，朱則掌制校文，不負乃祖令器之許；劉則三疏百首，無忝八面受敵之才，非瀛洲之妙選耶？文端首正奔競之習，鳴朝陽之鳳也；彝正抗論起復之非，埋都亭之輪也。恭愍作柱史而議揭三綱，忠肝義膽貫日月矣；忠愍為侍講而條陳十事，奇氣疎節凌漢霄矣。守蘇州而剛毅正直，有張詠
translation_en:
…in tracing the river to its source, he began at the Feng River: no one could reach the river’s source without crossing the Feng River. When Kuafu pursued the sun on foot, he began at Yuyi: no one could pursue the sun without passing through Yuyi. Thus those who admire something distant inevitably overlook something close at hand. To carry a bright pearl within one’s robe yet search for it along the road is surely misguided. Therefore, we must investigate and come to know the worthy gentlemen and scholar-officials of our own region, taking them as standards and emulating them.
Speaking from our present vantage point, it was Wenzhen who served through four reigns and eminently advanced the work of the chief minister; it was Wenxiang who, as Grand Coordinator of the Three Wu region, brought profound resources to the great task of strengthening state finances. Among those appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Hu personally led the students, and the entire institution followed his transforming influence with one accord; Li modeled his teaching on Anding, and the sons of the state rose vigorously to the challenge. Were these not fine exemplars for the imperial academy? Among those who served in the Hanlin Academy, Zhu handled imperial pronouncements and evaluated compositions, living up to his grandfather’s appraisal of him as a man of exceptional promise; Liu, with his three memorials and hundred poems, did justice to his talent for meeting challenges from all eight directions. Were these not outstanding selections for Yingzhou, the isle of immortals? Wenduan took the lead in correcting the habit of scrambling for advancement: he was a phoenix calling toward the morning sun. Yizheng argued forthrightly against the impropriety of recalling an official to service during mourning: his was the carriage wheel buried at the capital’s posthouse. Gongmin served as an Investigating Censor and, in his arguments, upheld the Three Bonds; his loyal heart and righteous courage shone through sun and moon. Zhongmin served as an Expositor-in-waiting and submitted ten proposals in detail; his extraordinary spirit and untrammeled integrity soared beyond the Milky Way into the heavens. The man who governed Suzhou, resolute, upright, and possessed of Zhang Yong’s …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之遺風非況伯律耶知南雄而耿介清貧
如范丹之寒素非劉嘉秀耶乃若厭舉子
之業鄙箋註之繁聘之以幣帛則應授之
以官職則辭則又吳子傅也玆惟十有三
人或嘉猷茂績足以尊主而庇民或行修
言道足以垂世而立教或危辭崇論足以
正君而善俗或清風高誼足以起懦而廉
頑譬之瑤琨璆琳為體不同均為和氏之
需矣楩楠杞梓為材不同均為大匠之用
===
矣抑聞心者身之本也家者國之本也未
有幼不學而壯能行者也未有不修之于
家而能達之於天子之庭者也夷攷文貞
諸君子美質性成茂才夙禀蓋湖山江岳
之靈有以助天施地生之秀故迥然出類
磊落不羣有年方髫齔即通舉業而為子
弟師者有聰穎不弄十歲通經銳然自任
聖賢之學者有博極羣書旁通醫卜間居
講求性命之理者有少年登科自陳願學
punctuated:
之遺風，非況伯律耶？知南雄而耿介清貧，如范丹之寒素，非劉嘉秀耶？乃若厭舉子之業，鄙箋註之繁，聘之以幣帛則應，授之以官職則辭，則又吳子傅也。玆惟十有三人，或嘉猷茂績，足以尊主而庇民；或行修言道，足以垂世而立教；或危辭崇論，足以正君而善俗；或清風高誼，足以起懦而廉頑。譬之瑤琨璆琳，為體不同，均為和氏之需矣；楩楠杞梓，為材不同，均為大匠之用矣。

抑聞心者身之本也，家者國之本也。未有幼不學而壯能行者也，未有不修之于家而能達之於天子之庭者也。夷攷文貞諸君子，美質性成，茂才夙禀，蓋湖山江岳之靈，有以助天施地生之秀，故迥然出類，磊落不羣。有年方髫齔，即通舉業而為子弟師者；有聰穎不弄，十歲通經，銳然自任聖賢之學者；有博極羣書，旁通醫卜，間居講求性命之理者；有少年登科，自陳願學
translation_en:
…the legacy of Zhang Yong—was this not Kuang Bolü? As prefect of Nanxiong, upright and incorruptible, living in poverty as austere as Fan Dan’s—was this not Liu Jiaxiu? Then there was one who tired of examination studies and disdained the profusion of explanatory annotations: invited with gifts of silk, he accepted; offered official appointment, he declined. This was Wu Zifu. These thirteen men possessed, variously, excellent counsel and outstanding achievements sufficient to honor their ruler and protect the people; cultivated conduct and words expressing the Way sufficient to leave a legacy to posterity and establish moral teaching; forthright speech and lofty arguments sufficient to set the ruler right and improve popular customs; or pure character and elevated principles sufficient to rouse the timid and make the unscrupulous honest. They may be compared to the precious jades yao, kun, qiu, and lin: though differing in substance, all were sought by Master He, the discerning judge of jade. Or they resemble the timbers pian, nan, qi, and zi: though differing in their qualities, all serve the master carpenter’s purposes.

I have also heard that the heart is the foundation of the person, and the family the foundation of the state. Never has anyone failed to learn in youth yet proved capable of putting learning into practice in maturity; never has anyone failed to cultivate himself within the family yet been able to extend that cultivation to the Son of Heaven’s court. Examining Wenzhen and these other gentlemen, we find that their fine qualities were innate and their abundant talents endowed from early life. Surely the numinous powers of lakes, mountains, rivers, and peaks helped bring forth the excellence bestowed by Heaven and nurtured by Earth; thus they stood far above their peers, openhearted and extraordinary. Some, still at the age of childhood topknots and changing teeth, already mastered examination studies and became teachers of the younger generation. Some were intelligent and shunned frivolity, understood the classics at ten, and resolutely took upon themselves the learning of sages and worthies. Some ranged widely through the whole body of books, also understood medicine and divination, and in retirement investigated the principles of human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Some passed the examinations while young and themselves declared their wish to study…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而來有志之許者有少負大志書無不讀
而窮道德之奥者有奉親盡懽居喪盡禮
而昆仲同居無間言者有自幼端重異於
常兒而家貧力薄苦好學者有起家從事
而無異儒流者有計偕京師而不見達官
者有年方十九而一見聖學心竊慨慕者
有天資絶倫而過目輒誦不違父教者有
飽庭訓踐孝友而忠義有根基者有性慷
慨面斥人而遇事無回避者惟其幼而學
===
也心行足以自立故其壯而行也德業足
以成名修之于家也有隱居求志之功故
施之于國也有行義達道之效在當時為
一時之人望在後世為百世之師模雖不
敢謂夔龍臯益伊呂周召之復生而視蕭
曹丙魏房杜姚宋諸人則遠過矣今夫莫
為之前無以彰其美莫為之後無以續其
傳使楊劉諸君子而無足法焉諸君子之
罪也諸君子足法而人莫之法焉咎孰執
punctuated: 而來有志之許者，有少負大志，書無不讀，而窮道德之奥者，有奉親盡懽，居喪盡禮，而昆仲同居無間言者，有自幼端重，異於常兒，而家貧力薄，苦好學者，有起家從事，而無異儒流者，有計偕京師，而不見達官者，有年方十九，而一見聖學，心竊慨慕者，有天資絶倫，而過目輒誦，不違父教者，有飽庭訓，踐孝友，而忠義有根基者，有性慷慨，面斥人，而遇事無回避者。惟其幼而學也，心行足以自立，故其壯而行也，德業足以成名。修之于家也，有隱居求志之功，故施之于國也，有行義達道之效。在當時，為一時之人望；在後世，為百世之師模。雖不敢謂夔龍臯益伊呂周召之復生，而視蕭曹丙魏房杜姚宋諸人，則遠過矣。今夫莫為之前，無以彰其美；莫為之後，無以續其傳。使楊劉諸君子而無足法焉，諸君子之罪也；諸君子足法，而人莫之法焉，咎孰執
translation_en:
…and earned recognition as a man of aspiration [?]. Some harbored great ambitions from youth, read every book they could, and plumbed the profundities of the Way and virtue. Some served their parents with the utmost devotion to their happiness, observed mourning with complete ritual propriety, and lived together with their brothers without a word of discord. Some were dignified and serious from childhood, unlike ordinary children, and, though their families were poor and their means meager, pursued learning with painstaking devotion. Some entered official service and were no different from members of the scholarly community. Some traveled to the capital for the examinations yet declined to visit high officials. Some, at just nineteen, first encountered the learning of the sages and inwardly felt a profound admiration for it. Some possessed unequaled natural gifts, could recite whatever they had read at a glance, and never departed from their fathers’ teachings. Some were thoroughly nurtured by paternal instruction and practiced filial piety and brotherly affection, giving their loyalty and righteousness firm foundations. Some were forthright and spirited by nature, rebuked others to their faces, and never shirked when confronted with an affair.
Precisely because they learned in youth, their dispositions and conduct sufficed to establish them independently; thus, when they acted in maturity, their virtue and accomplishments sufficed to make their names. In cultivating themselves within the family, they achieved the work of dwelling in retirement and pursuing their aspirations; thus, when they put this into practice in service to the state, they realized the effects of practicing righteousness and giving effect to the Way. In their own day, they were men to whom their contemporaries looked up; for later ages, they became teachers and models for a hundred generations. Though we dare not call them reincarnations of Kui, Long, Gao, Yi, Yi Yin, Lü Shang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao, they far surpassed such men as Xiao He, Cao Shen, Bing Ji, Wei Xiang, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yao Chong, and Song Jing.
Now, without predecessors, there is no means to make their excellence manifest; without successors, there is no means to continue their tradition. If gentlemen such as Yang and Liu had nothing worthy of emulation, the fault would be theirs. But if these gentlemen were worthy of emulation and no one emulated them, who would bear the blame…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
哉或曰周公思兼三王仲尼祖述堯舜拘
方徇俗者曲士之見也博諮遠訪者達人
之觀也故一鄉一國不足以盡友古人之
道必欲其與稽以宇宙内事莫非分内事
也愚則以為不然子賤之成德由魯國之
多賢孟子之學孔以鄒魯之甚近彼誠見
古今一理遠近一心學孔子即所以學堯
舜而師魯國之多賢即所以師文王惟其
人不惟其古今則師今者法古之漸也惟
===
其賢不惟其遠近則自邇者行遠之漸也
故愚於備萬而取其孝於若思而取其勤
於文貞而取其達於恂如而取其量於文
毅而取其正於求樂而取其直於行儉而
取其剛於蘇州而取其明於南雄而取其
廉於徵士而取其恬於主靜而取其敏於
世京而取其忠於彛正則又取其有仁者
之勇焉然方有志進取乃所願則學彛正
矣學彛正而文貞諸君子可學也學文貞
punctuated:
哉？或曰：「周公思兼三王，仲尼祖述堯舜。拘方徇俗者，曲士之見也；博諮遠訪者，達人之觀也。故一鄉一國不足以盡友古人之道，必欲其與稽，以宇宙内事莫非分内事也。」愚則以為不然。子賤之成德，由魯國之多賢；孟子之學孔，以鄒魯之甚近。彼誠見古今一理，遠近一心，學孔子即所以學堯舜，而師魯國之多賢即所以師文王。惟其人，不惟其古今，則師今者法古之漸也；惟其賢，不惟其遠近，則自邇者行遠之漸也。
故愚於備萬而取其孝，於若思而取其勤，於文貞而取其達，於恂如而取其量，於文毅而取其正，於求樂而取其直，於行儉而取其剛，於蘇州而取其明，於南雄而取其廉，於徵士而取其恬，於主靜而取其敏，於世京而取其忠，於彛正則又取其有仁者之勇焉。然方有志進取，乃所願則學彛正矣。學彛正而文貞諸君子可學也，學文貞
translation_en:
…indeed? Someone may say: “The Duke of Zhou aspired to unite the achievements of the Three Kings, and Zhongni transmitted the ways of Yao and Shun. To be confined by locality and follow prevailing customs is the outlook of a narrow scholar; to consult widely and seek afar is the perspective of a man of broad understanding. Thus, a single district or state cannot exhaust the way of befriending the ancients. One must seek to investigate them [?], for nothing within the universe lies outside one’s own responsibilities.” I, however, think otherwise. Zijian perfected his virtue because the state of Lu had so many worthy men; Mengzi studied Kongzi because Zou and Lu were so close to one another. They truly understood that antiquity and the present share one principle, and those far and near share one mind. To learn from Kongzi is precisely to learn from Yao and Shun; to take the many worthy men of Lu as teachers is precisely to take King Wen as one’s teacher. If what matters is the person, rather than whether he lived in antiquity or the present, then taking contemporaries as teachers is a gradual approach to emulating the ancients. If what matters is his worthiness, rather than whether he is far or near, then starting nearby is a gradual approach to traveling far.
Thus, from Beiwan I take filial devotion; from Ruosi, diligence; from Wenzhen, breadth of understanding; from Xunru, magnanimity; from Wenyi, uprightness; from Qiule, candor; from Xingjian, firmness; from Suzhou, discernment; from Nanxiong, integrity; from the Recruited Scholar, serenity; from Zhujing, keen responsiveness; and from Shijing, loyalty. From Yizheng I take, moreover, the courage of a benevolent man. Yet, as I now aspire to advancement, my wish is to learn from Yizheng. By learning from Yizheng, I can learn from Wenzhen and the other gentlemen; by learning from Wenzhen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸君子而靖節孺子盱江文山可學也學
靖節孺子盱江文山而夔龍皐益伊傅周
孔可學也執事以爲然否
第五問
廖如春
同考試官教諭袁批兵食爲足方急務策盡之
同考試官教授蔣批識時務者俊傑非子耶
考試官教諭何批自是不易之論
考試官教諭錢批指畫切然佳士也
===
用兵無一定之法制馭者貴乎妙通變之
宜養兵有一定之規經略者貴乎得推行
之利何則兵有行於一時之權者不能以
無利也而非其所可恃也食有出於經常
之計者不容以易盈也而非其所可緩也
苟當其有事而不征調則無以備倉卒之
虞及其無事而不撙節則無以應供億之
費故善用兵者隨時以通其變使緩急有
賴不失夫先事之防善理財者酌古以準
punctuated:
諸君子，而靖節、孺子、盱江、文山可學也；學靖節、孺子、盱江、文山，而夔、龍、皐、益、伊、傅、周、孔可學也。執事以爲然否？

第五問
廖如春
同考試官教諭袁批：「兵食爲足方急務，策盡之。」
同考試官教授蔣批：「識時務者俊傑，非子耶？」
考試官教諭何批：「自是不易之論。」
考試官教諭錢批：「指畫切然，佳士也。」

用兵無一定之法，制馭者貴乎妙通變之宜；養兵有一定之規，經略者貴乎得推行之利。何則？兵有行於一時之權者，不能以無利也，而非其所可恃也；食有出於經常之計者，不容以易盈也，而非其所可緩也。苟當其有事而不征調，則無以備倉卒之虞；及其無事而不撙節，則無以應供億之費。故善用兵者，隨時以通其變，使緩急有賴，不失夫先事之防；善理財者，酌古以準
translation_en:
…these gentlemen, and one may learn to emulate Jingjie, Ruzi, Xujiang, and Wenshan; by learning to emulate Jingjie, Ruzi, Xujiang, and Wenshan, one may learn to emulate Kui, Long, Gao, Yi, Yi, Fu, Zhou, and Kong. Do you, sir, consider this so?

Fifth Question
Liao Ruchun
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “Troops and provisions are an urgent concern [?]; this policy essay treats the subject exhaustively.”
Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “One who understands the needs of the times is an outstanding talent—is that not you?”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “This is indeed an incontrovertible argument.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “His proposals are precise and pertinent. A worthy scholar indeed.”

There is no fixed method for employing troops: those who command them must above all master the appropriate responses to changing circumstances. There are fixed rules for maintaining troops: those who plan and administer military affairs must above all secure the benefits of putting those rules into practice. Why is this? Military operations involve expedients suited to a particular moment. These cannot be said to offer no advantage, yet they are not something on which one can depend. Provisions derive from regular, continuing arrangements. One must not suppose that abundance is easily attained [?], nor is this a matter that can be deferred.

If, when trouble arises, troops are not levied and mobilized, there will be no means of guarding against sudden emergencies. If, when there is no trouble, expenditure is not restrained, there will be no means of meeting the costs of supplies. Thus, those skilled in employing troops adapt to changing circumstances as the occasion demands, ensuring that there is something to rely upon in ordinary times and emergencies alike, and never neglecting precautions taken before events arise. Those skilled in managing finances weigh the practices of antiquity to establish a standard for…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
夫今使上下相安適得夫恒足之道知乎
此可與言兵食矣執事發策而以是下問
為地方慮至深切也敢不悉心以對昔者
聖人之作易也觀象於坤上坎下之卦而
名之曰師孔子因而傳之曰地中有水師
君子以容民畜衆蓋古者寓兵於農伏至
險於大順藏不測於至靜之中民以養兵
兵以衛民斯二者相有而不可以相無相
資而非所以相病也考之周禮以鄉遂出
===
兵以九法治兵則兵出於賦而先王治兵
之法莫有善於此矣貢民以九式斂民以
九賦則賦出於田而先王理財之法莫有
要於此矣自夫兵甲之制作而期門羽林
府兵彍騎之名日益以多天下始困於兵
稅畝之法立而榷茶榷鹽筭緡筭車之數
日益以煩天下始困於食法之不競而治
之不古有由然也我
祖宗創制立法軍雖分隸於衛所復立萬戶府
punctuated:
夫今，使上下相安，適得夫恒足之道。知乎此，可與言兵食矣。執事發策，而以是下問，為地方慮至深切也，敢不悉心以對？昔者聖人之作《易》也，觀象於坤上坎下之卦，而名之曰師。孔子因而傳之曰：「地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。」蓋古者寓兵於農，伏至險於大順，藏不測於至靜之中。民以養兵，兵以衛民，斯二者相有而不可以相無，相資而非所以相病也。考之《周禮》，以鄉遂出兵，以九法治兵，則兵出於賦，而先王治兵之法莫有善於此矣。貢民以九式，斂民以九賦，則賦出於田，而先王理財之法莫有要於此矣。自夫兵甲之制作，而期門、羽林、府兵、彍騎之名日益以多，天下始困於兵；稅畝之法立，而榷茶、榷鹽、筭緡、筭車之數日益以煩，天下始困於食。法之不競而治之不古，有由然也。
我祖宗創制立法，軍雖分隸於衛所，復立萬戶府。
translation_en:
…the present, enabling those above and below to live in mutual harmony and thereby attaining the way to lasting sufficiency. Those who understand this may be engaged in discussion of troops and provisions. In setting this policy question and asking us about these matters, you have shown the deepest concern for this region. How could I fail to devote my whole mind to answering?
When the sage composed the Book of Changes, he contemplated the image of the hexagram with Kun above and Kan below and named it Shi, “The Army.” Confucius subsequently commented upon it: “Within the earth there is water: The Army. Thus the gentleman embraces the people and nurtures the multitude.” In antiquity, soldiers were embedded among the farmers: utmost danger lay within utmost compliance, and unfathomable power was concealed within perfect stillness. The people supported the soldiers, and the soldiers protected the people. These two depended on one another and could not do without one another; they sustained rather than afflicted one another.
Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that troops were raised from the inner and outer suburban districts and governed through the nine methods [?]. Thus troops came from the levy, and none of the former kings’ methods of military administration surpassed this. Contributions were exacted from the people according to the nine expenditure norms [?], and revenue was collected from them through the nine levies. Thus revenue came from the fields, and none of the former kings’ methods of financial administration was more essential than this.
Once military institutions were established and units bearing such names as the Qimen Guards, Yulin Guards, militia forces, and expanded cavalry became ever more numerous, the realm began to suffer under the burden of supporting troops. Once taxation by the mu was instituted and the exactions from tea and salt monopolies, taxes on merchants’ capital, and vehicle taxes became increasingly complicated, the realm began to suffer under the burden of providing supplies. There are reasons why the institutions lack efficacy and government fails to match that of antiquity.
Our dynastic ancestors established institutions and laws. Although the troops were assigned separately to guards and battalions, they also established Myriad Household Offices…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以簡民兵田因則壤以起科復立丁田法
以徵工食以其所徵之食養其所簡之兵
隨操於無事之時效用於有事之日其法
十年一編悉取民間少壯以充其選是卽
寓兵於農之意也夫何法久弊滋民兵之
制猶昔也而審編不愼則老弱者得以參
雜其間况團操之法久矣不行聞金鼓則
心悸見旌旗則目眩矣安在其爲足兵工
食之徵猶昔也而催科不嚴則攬泊者得
===
以漁獵其利况豪猾之徒閔不知畏追呼
之則卽逋拘係之則待斃矣安在其爲足
食惟民兵之不可恃故盜賊之起不免於
募兵惟軍餉之不易足故征調之際不免
於借辦此兵食之所以俱困也江右承平
日久民不知兵邇者吳楚閩粤之間山箐
溪峒之頑乘間竊發流突臨吉諸郡賴我
皇上軫念東南
特命撫臣出師勦滅
punctuated:
以簡民兵。田因則壤以起科，復立丁田法以徵工食，以其所徵之食養其所簡之兵，隨操於無事之時，效用於有事之日。其法十年一編，悉取民間少壯以充其選，是卽寓兵於農之意也。夫何法久弊滋？民兵之制猶昔也，而審編不愼，則老弱者得以參雜其間。况團操之法久矣不行，聞金鼓則心悸，見旌旗則目眩矣，安在其爲足兵？工食之徵猶昔也，而催科不嚴，則攬泊者得以漁獵其利。况豪猾之徒閔不知畏，追呼之則卽逋，拘係之則待斃矣，安在其爲足食？惟民兵之不可恃，故盜賊之起不免於募兵；惟軍餉之不易足，故征調之際不免於借辦。此兵食之所以俱困也。
江右承平日久，民不知兵。邇者吳楚閩粤之間，山箐溪峒之頑乘間竊發，流突臨吉諸郡。賴我皇上軫念東南，特命撫臣出師勦滅。
translation_en:
…to select militiamen. Land was assessed for taxation according to the quality of its soil, and a system of levies on adult males and land was also established to collect funds for pay and provisions. The provisions collected supported the men selected as soldiers, who attended drills in peaceful times and rendered service when trouble arose. Under this system, enrollment took place once every ten years, drawing young, able-bodied men from among the populace to fill the ranks. This embodied the principle of lodging military service within agriculture. How, then, did abuses proliferate as the system grew old? The militia system remains as before, but enrollment is not carefully scrutinized, allowing old and weak men to mingle in the ranks. Moreover, organized drills have long fallen into disuse: the men’s hearts quake at the sound of gongs and drums, and their eyes reel at the sight of banners. How can this provide adequate troops? The levies for pay and provisions remain as before, but collection is not rigorously enforced, allowing tax-payment intermediaries [?] to prey upon the proceeds. Moreover, powerful and crafty men know no fear [?]: when pursued for payment, they flee; when detained, they simply await death. How can this provide adequate supplies?
