title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
蕩蕩乎民無能名焉
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批語意渾融而名實自見
同考試官教諭何批善形容聖人氣象
同考試官教諭黃批得旨
考試官教諭何批雋永有味
考試官教諭錢批渾厚典雅
===
聖人賛帝德之難名以見君道之極也盖堯之
德天德也天則不可知矣而民孰能名之此夫
子所以獨賛其大也若曰人君有合天之德而
後天下有忘言之化是故語大者惟天而語則
天者惟堯堯一天而已矣即是而徵諸民也殆
蕩蕩而無能名焉者乎吾知與天而同其高大
則亦與天而同其流行俊德之明被於四表蕩
蕩乎廣矣而不可限也而意象自為之俱泯帝
德之運格於上下蕩蕩乎遠矣而不可禦也而
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「蕩蕩乎，民無能名焉。」
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批：語意渾融，而名實自見。
同考試官教諭何批：善形容聖人氣象。
同考試官教諭黃批：得旨。
考試官教諭何批：雋永有味。
考試官教諭錢批：渾厚典雅。

聖人賛帝德之難名，以見君道之極也。盖堯之德，天德也。天則不可知矣，而民孰能名之？此夫子所以獨賛其大也。若曰：人君有合天之德，而後天下有忘言之化。是故語大者惟天，而語則天者惟堯。堯，一天而已矣。即是而徵諸民也，殆蕩蕩而無能名焉者乎！吾知與天而同其高大，則亦與天而同其流行。俊德之明，被於四表，蕩蕩乎廣矣，而不可限也，而意象自為之俱泯。帝德之運，格於上下，蕩蕩乎遠矣，而不可禦也，而
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“How vast! The people could find no words to name it.”
Zhu Meishou

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The language and meaning are seamlessly integrated, while name and substance emerge of themselves.”
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “Skillfully portrays the sage’s bearing.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Grasps the essential meaning.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “Rich in lasting savor.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “Full and substantial, classically elegant.”

The sage praises the difficulty of naming the emperor’s virtue, thereby revealing the utmost perfection of the ruler’s Way. For Yao’s virtue was the virtue of Heaven. Heaven cannot be comprehended; who among the people, then, could name his virtue? This is why the Master singled out his greatness for praise. It is as though he were saying: only when a ruler possesses virtue consonant with Heaven can there be a transforming influence throughout the world that makes words forgotten. Thus, in speaking of greatness, there is only Heaven; in speaking of taking Heaven as one’s model, there is only Yao. Yao was simply one with Heaven. If we test this against the people’s experience, was his virtue not so vast that they could find no words to name it? I know that, since he shared Heaven’s height and greatness, he also shared its ceaseless operation. The radiance of his eminent virtue spread to the four outer bounds: how vast in its breadth, impossible to delimit! All conceptions and images of it thereby dissolved of themselves. The operation of the emperor’s virtue reached above and below: how vast in its reach, impossible to impede! And …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
名言自爲之兩忘其存之神也神天德也磅礴
無外而辭不足以盡其神其過之化也化天道
也渾淪無迹而辭不足以體其化觀於朝而百
僚師師但見其讓德而已矣自都俞吁咈之外
又何以擬諸形容也觀於野而百姓皞皞但見
其敏德而已矣自出入耕鑿之外將何所容其
揄揚也雖曰欽明文思紀之帝典矣然此特叙
其德性之美而終無能名其配天之精其猶萬
物日囿於高明焉而莫知其所以爲高者乎雖
===
曰聖神文武載之禹謨矣然此特言其變化之
用而終無能名其如天之妙其猶萬物咸熈於
覆幬焉而莫知其所以爲大者乎吁民無能名
而堯之民亦遊於堯之天矣故曰大哉堯之爲
君也後有作者其弗可及也哉雖然天之道大
矣而一言以盡之曰爲物不貳堯之德大矣而
一言以盡之曰允執厥中至於欽之爲言則又
執中之要而合於天之不貳所以爲民無能名
之本者也君子知堯之欽則可以希聖希天而
punctuated: 名言自爲之兩忘。其存之神也，神，天德也，磅礴無外，而辭不足以盡其神；其過之化也，化，天道也，渾淪無迹，而辭不足以體其化。觀於朝而百僚師師，但見其讓德而已矣。自都俞吁咈之外，又何以擬諸形容也？觀於野而百姓皞皞，但見其敏德而已矣。自出入耕鑿之外，將何所容其揄揚也？雖曰「欽明文思」，紀之《帝典》矣，然此特叙其德性之美，而終無能名其配天之精。其猶萬物日囿於高明焉，而莫知其所以爲高者乎？雖曰「聖神文武」，載之《禹謨》矣，然此特言其變化之用，而終無能名其如天之妙。其猶萬物咸熈於覆幬焉，而莫知其所以爲大者乎？吁！民無能名，而堯之民亦遊於堯之天矣。故曰：「大哉，堯之爲君也！」後有作者，其弗可及也哉！雖然，天之道大矣，而一言以盡之，曰：「爲物不貳。」堯之德大矣，而一言以盡之，曰：「允執厥中。」至於欽之爲言，則又執中之要，而合於天之不貳，所以爲民無能名之本者也。君子知堯之欽，則可以希聖希天而
translation_en: …names and words alike are naturally forgotten before it. His presence is numinous: this numinosity is Heaven’s virtue, vast and all-embracing, and words cannot exhaust it. His passing transforms: this transformation is Heaven’s Way, an undivided whole leaving no trace, and words cannot give it adequate expression. Look at his court, where the hundred officials learn from one another: one sees only his virtue of deference. Beyond their exclamations of approval and dissent, how could one find words to describe it? Look at the countryside, where the common people are content and carefree: one sees only his active virtue. Beyond their going out and coming home, ploughing fields and digging wells, what occasion would there be for them to voice his praises? Although the words “reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful” are recorded in the Canon of the Emperor, they merely describe the beauty of his moral nature; ultimately, they cannot name the refined essence by which he matches Heaven. Is this not like the myriad things dwelling daily within Heaven’s lofty brightness, yet none knowing what makes it lofty? Although the words “sage, numinous, civil, and martial” are recorded in the Counsels of Yu, they merely describe the operation of his transforming powers; ultimately, they cannot name the marvel by which he resembles Heaven. Is this not like the myriad things all flourishing beneath Heaven’s canopy, yet none knowing what makes it great? Ah! The people could find no name for it, yet Yao’s people lived at ease within Yao’s heaven. Thus it is said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler!” Should another arise after him, could he ever equal him? Nevertheless, great as Heaven’s Way is, a single expression exhausts it: “In bringing things into being, it is without duplicity.” Great as Yao’s virtue is, a single expression exhausts it: “Truly hold fast to the Mean.” As for the meaning of reverence, it is the essential means of holding fast to the Mean and accords with Heaven’s freedom from duplicity. It is therefore the foundation of that which the people could find no name for. If the gentleman understands Yao’s reverence, he can aspire to sagehood and to Heaven, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
巍巍蕩蕩會於吾心矣是故則天者莫如堯而
則堯者莫如敬
誠者非自成已而已也所以成物也
黃榜
同考試官教諭易批善發體用一原之理
同考試官教諭金批析理明而措詞潤有養之
士也
考試官教諭何批莊重可誦
考試官教諭錢批理到之文自別
===
中庸著能誠之妙合物我而成之者也夫誠者
萬物之一原也既有以自成矣則自然及物而
豈待於外哉中庸勉人之思誠也意謂誠原於
天本為同具之理而理備於已自有相通之機
人惟誠之未至則已不能成而欲有以成物也
難矣君子知誠之為貴由思誠而至於能誠焉
則存主無偽既以一心而會性命之精實理兼
該自以一身而立人物之極已於是乎成矣夫
豈自成已而已乎吾知無妄流行合人已於一
punctuated:
巍巍蕩蕩，會於吾心矣。是故則天者莫如堯，而則堯者莫如敬。

誠者，非自成已而已也，所以成物也。

黃榜

同考試官教諭易批：善發體用一原之理。
同考試官教諭金批：析理明而措詞潤，有養之士也。
考試官教諭何批：莊重可誦。
考試官教諭錢批：理到之文自別。

《中庸》著能誠之妙，合物我而成之者也。夫誠者，萬物之一原也。既有以自成矣，則自然及物，而豈待於外哉？《中庸》勉人之思誠也，意謂誠原於天，本為同具之理，而理備於已，自有相通之機。人惟誠之未至，則已不能成，而欲有以成物也，難矣。君子知誠之為貴，由思誠而至於能誠焉，則存主無偽，既以一心而會性命之精；實理兼該，自以一身而立人物之極，已於是乎成矣。夫豈自成已而已乎？吾知無妄流行，合人已於一
translation_en:
…the lofty grandeur and boundless breadth will come together within my heart. Thus, none equals Yao in taking Heaven as his model, and nothing equals reverent attentiveness as the means of taking Yao as one’s model.

“Sincerity does not merely complete oneself; it is that by which one completes other things.”

Huang Bang

Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “Skillfully elucidates the principle that substance and function have a single source.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: “His analysis of principle is clear and his wording polished. He is a scholar of cultivated character.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Grave and dignified, worthy of recitation.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “Writing that reaches the heart of principle distinguishes itself.”

The Doctrine of the Mean reveals the subtle efficacy of attaining sincerity: it unites things and the self and brings them to completion. Sincerity is the single source of the myriad things. Once one has the means to complete oneself, its effects naturally extend to other things. How could this depend on anything external? In urging people to reflect upon sincerity, the Doctrine of the Mean means that sincerity originates in Heaven and is fundamentally a principle shared by all. Since this principle is fully present within oneself, there is inherently a capacity for mutual connection. Only because a person’s sincerity has not reached its utmost can the self not be completed; to seek then to complete other things is indeed difficult. The gentleman knows the value of sincerity and, through reflecting upon it, reaches the ability to be sincere. What he preserves within and takes as his guiding purpose is then free of falsity: with his single mind he comprehends the essence of human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Real principle embraces everything: through his own person he establishes the ultimate standard for people and things. The self is thereby completed. Yet how could this amount merely to completing oneself? I know that, as freedom from falsity flows forth, it unites others and oneself in a single…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
致而立此達彼有以妙錫類之神真機貫徹融
物我於無間而體立用行有以普合同之化其
盡人之性也即其盡己之性者推之也成身成
性之中凡所以以人治人者固即此而在焉其
應物之感也即其正己之盡者達之也誠立誠
通之內凡所以因物賦物者要不外於是焉曲
成萬物固自昭明德之能事雖充之以臻位育
之效亦皆吾性之固有耳蓋天之賦於我者理
本至足而功用所成必如是而後始爲無虧也
===
己道濟天下固踐形惟肖之優爲雖擴之以極
參贊之盛無非至誠之全功耳蓋我之得於天
者性本各具而分量所及必如是而後始爲克
盡也已是則惟能成己也而有以立成物之體
惟能成物也而可以驗成己之用物我合一誠
之所以爲貴也而與至誠同其歸矣噫此聖人
體信達順之道也脩己以敬而以安人安百姓
堯舜之盛亦不過本其成己者以運之而已然
亦有不盡然者如吾夫子之在春秋己無不成
punctuated: 致，而立此達彼，有以妙錫類之神；真機貫徹，融物我於無間，而體立用行，有以普合同之化。其盡人之性也，即其盡己之性者推之也。成身成性之中，凡所以以人治人者，固即此而在焉。其應物之感也，即其正己之盡者達之也。誠立誠通之內，凡所以因物賦物者，要不外於是焉。曲成萬物，固自昭明德之能事；雖充之以臻位育之效，亦皆吾性之固有耳。蓋天之賦於我者，理本至足，而功用所成，必如是而後始爲無虧也。己道濟天下，固踐形惟肖之優爲；雖擴之以極參贊之盛，無非至誠之全功耳。蓋我之得於天者，性本各具，而分量所及，必如是而後始爲克盡也已。是則惟能成己也，而有以立成物之體；惟能成物也，而可以驗成己之用。物我合一，誠之所以爲貴也，而與至誠同其歸矣。噫！此聖人體信達順之道也。脩己以敬，而以安人、安百姓，堯舜之盛，亦不過本其成己者以運之而已。然亦有不盡然者，如吾夫子之在春秋，己無不成
translation_en:
…unity: establishing oneself here and bringing fulfillment to others there, one wondrously exercises the spiritual efficacy of extending blessings to one's kind. The true animating impulse penetrates throughout, merging things and oneself without any separation; substance is established and its activity proceeds, universally extending the transforming influence that brings all into harmony. Fully realizing the nature of others is simply an extension of fully realizing one's own nature. Within the fulfillment of one's person and nature already lie all the means of governing people through their own humanity. Responding to things as they move one is simply the outward extension of thoroughly rectifying oneself. Within sincerity's establishment and its pervasive reach, all the means of endowing things according to their particular character are necessarily contained.

Bringing the myriad things to fulfillment in all their particularities is indeed an accomplishment of making bright one's luminous virtue. Even when extended to achieve the proper positioning of Heaven and Earth and the nurturing of all things, it remains entirely inherent in our nature. For the principle Heaven has endowed in us is inherently complete; only when its efficacy achieves this scope can it first be considered unimpaired. Bringing aid to all under Heaven through one's own Way [?] is indeed the ample achievement of fully embodying one's Heaven-given form and faithfully resembling its source. Even when expanded to the utmost flourishing of participation in and assistance to Heaven and Earth's transforming and nurturing work, it is nothing other than the complete achievement of utmost sincerity. For the nature each of us receives from Heaven is inherently complete; only when its full capacity reaches this scope can it first be considered fully realized.

Thus, only by fulfilling oneself can one establish the substance underlying the fulfillment of things; only by fulfilling things can one verify the practical operation of self-fulfillment. Things and oneself become one: this is what makes sincerity precious, and it leads to the same consummation as utmost sincerity. Ah! This is the sages' Way of embodying trustworthiness and extending harmonious accord. Cultivating oneself with reverence so as to bring peace to others and to all the people—even the greatness of Yao and Shun consisted simply in putting their self-fulfillment into operation. Yet there are cases in which this is not entirely so: our Master, for example, lived in the Spring and Autumn period, and there was nothing in himself that he had not fulfilled…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而何以不能大行其道要之誠者全其在我者
也而所遇不可必者時也故曰如有用我者朞
月而已可也然則堯舜也夫子也一誠而已矣
詩云雨我公田遂及我私惟助爲有公田
由此觀之雖周亦助也設爲庠序學校
以教之
陳文燦
同考試官教諭胡批思致縝密詞藻豐蔚佳作
也
===
同考試官教諭項批詞不費而意自足
考試官教諭何批明暢可錄
考試官教諭錢批純正之作
大賢迪君徵以助之可因而及夫教之當舉也
夫政莫大於教養也助法之善詩固有足徵者
而復設學以興教焉其斯爲王道之全乎孟子
告滕君之意蓋曰人君之爲國苟可以厚下不
嫌於立法之同欲有以化民莫先於酌古之制
何則助法與世祿相資所當兼舉者也滕知以
punctuated:
而何以不能大行其道？要之，誠者，全其在我者也；而所遇不可必者，時也。故曰：「如有用我者，朞月而已可也。」然則堯舜也，夫子也，一誠而已矣。
「詩云：『雨我公田，遂及我私。』惟助爲有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設爲庠序學校，以教之。」
陳文燦
同考試官教諭胡批：「思致縝密，詞藻豐蔚，佳作也。」
同考試官教諭項批：「詞不費而意自足。」
考試官教諭何批：「明暢可錄。」
考試官教諭錢批：「純正之作。」
大賢迪君，徵以助之可因，而及夫教之當舉也。夫政莫大於教養也。助法之善，詩固有足徵者，而復設學以興教焉，其斯爲王道之全乎？孟子告滕君之意，蓋曰：人君之爲國，苟可以厚下，不嫌於立法之同；欲有以化民，莫先於酌古之制。何則？助法與世祿相資，所當兼舉者也。滕知以
translation_en:
…yet why was he unable to put his Way broadly into practice? In essence, sincerity means bringing to perfection what lies within oneself; what one encounters and cannot make certain depends on the times. Thus he said: “If someone would employ me, in just a full year something could be accomplished.” Thus Yao and Shun, and the Master, shared nothing other than this one sincerity.
“The Book of Odes says: ‘Let rain fall on our public fields, and then reach our private fields.’ Only under the labor-assistance system are there public fields. Viewed in this light, even the Zhou employed the labor-assistance system. Establish village schools, local schools, and other institutions of learning to instruct the people.”
Chen Wencan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “The thinking is meticulous and closely reasoned; the language is rich and splendid. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor: “The wording is economical, yet the meaning is complete.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “Clear and fluent; worthy of selection.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “A work of purity and correctness.”
In guiding the ruler, the great worthy adduces evidence that the labor-assistance system may be continued, and proceeds to explain that education ought to be instituted. In government, nothing is greater than educating and nourishing the people. The Book of Odes certainly provides sufficient evidence of the merits of the labor-assistance system; if schools are also established to promote education, would this not constitute the completeness of the Kingly Way? The import of Mengzi’s advice to the ruler of Teng was this: when governing a state, a ruler need not object to adopting the same laws as others, provided they can enrich those below him. If he wishes to transform the people, nothing takes precedence over drawing judiciously upon ancient institutions. Why is this? The labor-assistance system and hereditary emoluments support one another and ought to be instituted together. Teng knows to employ…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
祿以待士矣則助之行也豈容已乎是故甞徵
之詩矣詩曰雨我公田遂及我私蓋公田本爲
助法之制而周人乃有公田之詠觀此則治地
以助商固創之而周亦因之也中公外私周亦
行之而民固詠之也合二代以相承俟異世而
可用畫野分田制莫善於此矣而政惟由舊滕
可不知所以從事乎此則養道以厚生所以啓
立敎之端者在是矣至若井田與學校相須不
可偏廢者也誠能用助以養民矣則敎之典也
===
豈容緩乎是故當酌之古矣夫庠序學校稱名
雖殊然建學爲崇善之基而立敎實倡化之本
故必隨在以弘其規而使責成之有地也因性
以牖夫民而俾曲成之有方也敎固由學而立
民必待敎而善化民易俗法莫詳於此矣而因
時立制滕可不知所以自勉乎此則修敎以正
德所以終養民之功者在是矣吁助法行而民
有恒産學校設而民有恒心此王道之全功也
滕君有志於爲國舍是其奚以哉抑是道也帝
punctuated: 祿以待士矣，則助之行也，豈容已乎？是故甞徵之詩矣。詩曰：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」蓋公田本爲助法之制，而周人乃有公田之詠。觀此，則治地以助，商固創之，而周亦因之也；中公外私，周亦行之，而民固詠之也。合二代以相承，俟異世而可用，畫野分田，制莫善於此矣。而政惟由舊，滕可不知所以從事乎？此則養道以厚生，所以啓立敎之端者在是矣。至若井田與學校相須，不可偏廢者也。誠能用助以養民矣，則敎之典也，豈容緩乎？是故當酌之古矣。夫庠序學校，稱名雖殊，然建學爲崇善之基，而立敎實倡化之本。故必隨在以弘其規，而使責成之有地也；因性以牖夫民，而俾曲成之有方也。敎固由學而立，民必待敎而善。化民易俗，法莫詳於此矣。而因時立制，滕可不知所以自勉乎？此則修敎以正德，所以終養民之功者在是矣。吁！助法行而民有恒産，學校設而民有恒心，此王道之全功也。滕君有志於爲國，舍是其奚以哉？抑是道也，帝
translation_en:
…stipends to provide for its gentlemen; how, then, could implementation of the labor-assistance system be dispensed with? Hence an appeal has already been made to the Book of Odes as evidence. The Odes says: “Let rain fall on our public fields, and then reach our private fields.” Public fields were originally an institution of the labor-assistance system, yet the people of Zhou sang of public fields. From this we see that Shang originated cultivation under the labor-assistance system, and Zhou continued it. Zhou likewise practiced the arrangement of public land in the center and private plots around it, and the people sang of it. Transmitted in succession through two dynasties, it remained usable in later ages: no institution was better for marking out the countryside and allocating fields. Since government should follow established precedents, could Teng fail to know how to put this into practice? Herein lies the way of nourishing the people and enriching their livelihood, which lays the groundwork for establishing instruction.

As for the well-field system and schools, they depend upon one another, and neither may be neglected. If the labor-assistance system can indeed be used to nourish the people, how could the institutions of instruction be delayed? Thus one must take ancient practice into consideration. Although the institutions called xiang, xu, xue, and xiao bore different names, establishing schools provides the foundation for honoring goodness, while instituting instruction is the root of promoting moral transformation. Their arrangements must therefore be extended everywhere, so that there are institutions to hold responsible for achieving results. The people must be enlightened in accordance with their nature, with methods that bring each to fulfillment according to individual circumstances. Instruction is established through schools, and the people must receive instruction to become good. No method is more comprehensive for transforming the people and changing customs. Since institutions must be established to suit the times, could Teng fail to know how to exert itself? Herein lies the cultivation of instruction to rectify virtue, which completes the work of nourishing the people.

Ah! When the labor-assistance system operates, the people have a constant livelihood; when schools are established, the people have constant hearts. This is the full achievement of the Kingly Way. If the ruler of Teng aspires to govern his state, what could he employ if he abandoned this? Moreover, this Way—the emperors…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
王相傳之心法也何孟子於滕而言之易耶蓋
堯舜不外乎一性文公聞性善之論似有可爲
之資矣故於井田學校而勉之以力行夫亦嘉
其志而冀吾道之行耳惜乎分田之制未定而
許行倡竝耕之說雖豪傑之士亦棄其學而學
焉故有治法無治人滕之所以不得爲善國也
亦何尤哉
易
中正以觀天下
===
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批中正二字發揮殆盡
同考試官教諭何批明瑩可誦
同考試官教諭黃批措詞精潔是深於易者
考試官教諭何批精確

觀卦體具建極之道而觀之名義可知矣蓋道
莫善於中正也以此而建維皇之極所以爲觀
於天下者不其至哉彖傳釋觀之名義也若曰
punctuated:
王相傳之心法也。何孟子於滕而言之易耶？蓋堯舜不外乎一性，文公聞性善之論，似有可爲之資矣，故於井田學校而勉之以力行，夫亦嘉其志而冀吾道之行耳。惜乎分田之制未定，而許行倡竝耕之說，雖豪傑之士亦棄其學而學焉。故有治法，無治人，滕之所以不得爲善國也，亦何尤哉？

易

中正以觀天下

祝眉壽

觀卦體具建極之道，而觀之名義可知矣。蓋道莫善於中正也，以此而建維皇之極，所以爲觀於天下者，不其至哉？彖傳釋觀之名義也，若曰：
translation_en:
…and kings transmitted to one another as the essential teaching of the mind. Why, then, did Mencius speak of it so readily in Teng? The way of Yao and Shun lay entirely within our common human nature. Having heard the teaching that human nature is good, Duke Wen seemed to possess the capacity to accomplish something. Thus Mencius urged him to put the well-field system and schools into practice. He was simply commending the duke’s aspirations and hoping that our Way might be implemented. Regrettably, before the system of allocating fields had been settled, Xu Xing advocated his doctrine that rulers should till the fields alongside their people. Even men of outstanding ability abandoned their own learning to study his teachings. Thus there were methods of good government, but no men to carry them out: this was why Teng failed to become a well-governed state. What further cause is there for blame?

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
王者以一人而繫天下之望則必以一身而示
天下之準聖人以觀名卦固取夫位與德矣又
九五居上卦之中而得陽位之正則是其爲君
也立天下之大位而出乎身以加乎民者罔非
大中之矩有天下之盛德而發乎邇以見乎遠
者莫非至正之猷惟精惟一執厥中而已矣然
立極於上而有以錫極於下蓋無假於聲色之
大而模範之立已自我而運其機無黨無偏守
其正而已矣然體信於己而足以彰信於民蓋
===
無俟於制作之煩而化導之原已自我而敦其
體近之而觀於朝廷之上百辟之儀刑皆於是
乎取足焉遠之而觀於邦國之間萬民之視效
咸於此乎承式焉道本諸身固未必其咸化於
中也而樹之表儀者行中以端天下之則皇極
其懋建矣不其肅然而可仰也哉中心無爲雖
未必其盡協於正也而彰之軌物者表正以一
天下之趨王度其丕昭矣不其顯然而可觀也
哉夫惟以中正觀天下則其在上也居天位以
punctuated: 王者以一人而繫天下之望，則必以一身而示天下之準。聖人以觀名卦，固取夫位與德矣。又九五居上卦之中，而得陽位之正，則是其爲君也，立天下之大位，而出乎身以加乎民者，罔非大中之矩；有天下之盛德，而發乎邇以見乎遠者，莫非至正之猷。惟精惟一，執厥中而已矣。然立極於上，而有以錫極於下，蓋無假於聲色之大，而模範之立，已自我而運其機。無黨無偏，守其正而已矣。然體信於己，而足以彰信於民，蓋無俟於制作之煩，而化導之原，已自我而敦其體。近之而觀於朝廷之上，百辟之儀刑，皆於是乎取足焉；遠之而觀於邦國之間，萬民之視效，咸於此乎承式焉。道本諸身，固未必其咸化於中也，而樹之表儀者，行中以端天下之則，皇極其懋建矣，不其肅然而可仰也哉？中心無爲，雖未必其盡協於正也，而彰之軌物者，表正以一天下之趨，王度其丕昭矣，不其顯然而可觀也哉？夫惟以中正觀天下，則其在上也，居天位以
translation_en:
… The king, as one man, bears the hopes of all under Heaven; he must therefore make his own person the standard for all under Heaven. In naming the hexagram Guan, “Contemplation,” the sage surely took both position and virtue into account. Moreover, the nine in the fifth place occupies the center of the upper trigram and holds the correct position for a yang line. Thus, as ruler, he occupies the highest position under Heaven, and everything that proceeds from his person to affect the people conforms to the measure of perfect centrality. He possesses the fullest virtue under Heaven, and everything that issues from what is near to become manifest afar follows the course of utmost correctness. He need only be discerning and single-minded, holding fast to the mean. Yet by establishing the supreme standard above, he has the means to bestow that standard upon those below. Without resorting to imposing displays of voice and countenance, he sets the workings of the exemplary standard in motion through his own person. He need only remain impartial and unbiased, preserving his correctness. Yet by embodying trustworthiness himself, he is fully able to make it manifest to the people. Without awaiting elaborate institutions and regulations, he gives substance, through his own person, to the source of moral transformation and guidance.

Viewed close at hand, within the court, he supplies all that the many lords require as a model for their conduct. Viewed from afar, among the states, he provides the pattern that the myriad people all receive and emulate. The Way is rooted in his own person. Although the people may not yet all have been transformed toward centrality, the exemplar he establishes practices centrality to rectify the standards of all under Heaven. The sovereign's supreme standard is thereby firmly established: is it not awe-inspiring and worthy of reverence? Within his heart there is no contrived action. Although the people may not yet all accord with correctness, the norms he makes manifest set forth correctness to unite the aspirations of all under Heaven. The kingly standards are thereby splendidly displayed: are they not illustrious and worthy of contemplation? It is precisely because he displays centrality and correctness to all under Heaven that, in his place above, he occupies Heaven's seat in order to …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
行天道而位益尊其順巽也本天德以行王道
而德愈顯卦之所以名為觀者不可以盡其蘊
乎雖然中正之道天道也而其本則原於一心
帝王奉若天道而天下順治者非徒求諸民也
求端於天以立萬化之原而已故夫子推極天
之神道而以聖人之設教者繼之豈無意乎然
則為觀於天下者中正其道□而道不可以偽
為誠心之學其至要矣乎
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉夫
===
坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉廣
大配天地
宋良佐
同考試官教諭王批〔得潔靜精微之旨〕
同考試官教諭何批〔善發乾坤之蘊〕
同考試官教諭黃批〔廣大就易說最是〕
考試官教諭何批〔文有理趣〕
考試官教諭錢批〔純粹〕
大傳原易書廣大之由而推其合於造化也夫
punctuated:
行天道，而位益尊；其順巽也，本天德以行王道，而德愈顯。卦之所以名為觀者，不可以盡其蘊乎？雖然，中正之道，天道也，而其本則原於一心。帝王奉若天道而天下順治者，非徒求諸民也，求端於天以立萬化之原而已。故夫子推極天之神道，而以聖人之設教者繼之，豈無意乎？然則為觀於天下者，中正其道□，而道不可以偽為，誠心之學其至要矣乎！
夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉；夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。
宋良佐

考試官教諭錢批〔純粹〕
大傳原《易》書廣大之由，而推其合於造化也。夫
translation_en:
…to carry out the Way of Heaven, and his position becomes ever more exalted; in his compliant humility, he takes Heaven’s virtue as his foundation in carrying out the kingly Way, and his virtue becomes ever more manifest. Does this not fully reveal the meaning of the hexagram’s being named Guan (Contemplation)? Yet the way of centrality and correctness is the Way of Heaven, and its foundation originates in the single heart. When emperors and kings reverently follow the Way of Heaven and all under Heaven is obedient and well governed, they do not seek this merely among the people. They seek its beginning in Heaven, thereby establishing the source of all transformation. Thus the Master fully explored Heaven’s spirit-like Way and followed this with the sages’ establishment of instruction. Could this have been without intent? Accordingly, for one who serves as an exemplar for all under Heaven, centrality and correctness are his way [?]; and the Way cannot be counterfeited. Is not the learning that makes the heart sincere supremely essential?
Qian (the Creative), in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus it generates greatness. Kun (the Receptive), in stillness, is gathered in; in movement, it opens out. Thus it generates breadth. In breadth and greatness they match Heaven and Earth.
Song Liangzuo
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔It captures the purport of purity, stillness, refinement, and subtlety.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: 〔It skillfully brings out the inner meaning of Qian and Kun.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔Explaining breadth and greatness in terms of the Changes is exactly right.〕
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔The composition has the savor of principle.〕
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔Pure and unalloyed.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
分動靜而相生造化之廣大也而易書原於是
焉有不與之克配而無間哉夫子傳易之意如
此且夫天地之間不過一陰一陽以為通復而
已造化立其原而易書洩其秘無或二也欲知
易之廣大盍於乾坤乎觀之今夫乾統元化以
為職者也而有動靜之分焉靜之專也有以凝
化育之真機動之直也有以達流行之妙用蓋
乾一之氣推行於坤兩之中無一物而非其所
知始此乾之大也聖人仰觀乎天而體其撰則
===
大之在乾者咸備於易矣大不由此而生乎夫
坤統元形以為職者也而有動靜之別焉翕聚
於靜無之內而資生之體具開闢於動有之際
而時行之化光蓋坤二之量順承乎乾一之施
無一物而非其所作成此坤之廣也聖人俯察
乎地而闡其精則廣之在坤者悉具於易矣廣
不由此而生乎夫一動一靜乾坤異運而同功
廣生大生易書異象而同理究其實寧不有以
配乎天地哉吾知高明不可及者天之所以為
punctuated: 分動靜而相生，造化之廣大也，而易書原於是焉，有不與之克配而無間哉？夫子傳易之意如此。且夫天地之間，不過一陰一陽以為通復而已。造化立其原，而易書洩其秘，無或二也。欲知易之廣大，盍於乾坤乎觀之？今夫乾，統元化以為職者也，而有動靜之分焉。靜之專也，有以凝化育之真機；動之直也，有以達流行之妙用。蓋乾一之氣，推行於坤兩之中，無一物而非其所知始，此乾之大也。聖人仰觀乎天而體其撰，則大之在乾者咸備於易矣。大不由此而生乎？夫坤，統元形以為職者也，而有動靜之別焉。翕聚於靜無之內，而資生之體具；開闢於動有之際，而時行之化光。蓋坤二之量，順承乎乾一之施，無一物而非其所作成，此坤之廣也。聖人俯察乎地而闡其精，則廣之在坤者悉具於易矣。廣不由此而生乎？夫一動一靜，乾坤異運而同功；廣生大生，易書異象而同理。究其實，寧不有以配乎天地哉？吾知高明不可及者，天之所以為
translation_en:
…differentiated into activity and stillness, yet generating one another: this is the breadth and greatness of the creative transformations. Since the Book of Changes has its source in these, could it fail to match them fully, without any gap? Such was the Master's intent in composing his commentary on the Changes. Between Heaven and Earth, there are simply yin and yang, passing through their cycles and returning. The creative transformations establish the source, and the Book of Changes discloses its mysteries: they are in no way two separate things. To understand the breadth and greatness of the Changes, why not examine Qian and Kun?

Now Qian has the charge of governing primordial transformation, and within it there is a distinction between activity and stillness. Through its concentration in stillness, it gathers the true generative impulse of transformation and nurture; through its directness in activity, it realizes the wondrous workings of circulation. The single vital force of Qian moves through the duality of Kun, and there is not a single thing whose inception it does not direct. This is Qian's greatness. The sage looks upward to observe Heaven and embodies its workings; thus all the greatness residing in Qian is fully present in the Changes. Does its greatness not arise from this?

Kun has the charge of governing primordial form, and within it too there is a distinction between activity and stillness. It draws together within the stillness of nonbeing, and the substance on which generation depends is complete; it opens out at the juncture of activity and being, and its transformations, proceeding with the seasons, shine forth. The twofold capacity of Kun compliantly receives the bestowal of the unity of Qian, and there is not a single thing that it does not bring to completion. This is Kun's breadth. The sage looks downward to examine Earth and elucidates its essence; thus all the breadth residing in Kun is fully present in the Changes. Does its breadth not arise from this?

In activity and stillness, Qian and Kun operate differently yet accomplish the same work. In generating breadth and generating greatness, the Book of Changes presents different images yet expresses the same principle. If we investigate its substance, how could it fail to match Heaven and Earth? I know that its unattainable loftiness and brightness are what make Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
天也而易之大自有與天合德之神博厚不可
窮者地之所以爲地也而易之廣自有應地無
疆之妙擴之而無外即其體之丕冒也蘊之而
富有即其量之含弘也造化易理相爲通貫是
易與天地準也而豈可以差殊觀哉咸備乎萬
理即其徧覆乎萬象也兼體乎衆善即其兼載
乎衆形也道器精麤相爲脗合是易與造化參
也而豈可以彼此論哉是可見天地爲易理之
原而易書爲造化之奥所以通達乎遠邇而充
===
塞於兩間也有由然哉大抵人受天地之中以
生而萬物皆備於我吾心固廣大也惟不以私
牿之則靜虚動直而吾心之廣大與天地同位
育參贊皆能事矣故學易者莫先於善事其心
以求廣大之實否則天地法象也易書麤迹也
與吾心若不相關矣故曰天下之理得而成位
乎其中此聖人心易之極功也
書
九功惟叙九叙惟歌
punctuated:
天也，而易之大自有與天合德之神；博厚不可窮者，地之所以爲地也，而易之廣自有應地無疆之妙。擴之而無外，即其體之丕冒也；蘊之而富有，即其量之含弘也。造化易理相爲通貫，是易與天地準也，而豈可以差殊觀哉？咸備乎萬理，即其徧覆乎萬象也；兼體乎衆善，即其兼載乎衆形也。道器精麤相爲脗合，是易與造化參也，而豈可以彼此論哉？是可見天地爲易理之原，而易書爲造化之奥，所以通達乎遠邇而充塞於兩間也，有由然哉！大抵人受天地之中以生，而萬物皆備於我，吾心固廣大也。惟不以私牿之，則靜虚動直，而吾心之廣大與天地同，位育參贊皆能事矣。故學易者莫先於善事其心，以求廣大之實；否則天地法象也，易書麤迹也，與吾心若不相關矣。故曰：「天下之理得而成位乎其中。」此聖人心易之極功也。

書

九功惟叙，九叙惟歌。
translation_en:
…Heaven; and the greatness of the Changes possesses a spiritual efficacy that accords with Heaven’s virtue. Inexhaustible breadth and depth are what make Earth Earth; and the breadth of the Changes possesses a wondrous efficacy that responds to Earth without limit. Expanded, it leaves nothing outside: this is the all-encompassing reach of its substance. Stored within, it possesses abundant riches: this is the capacious inclusiveness of its scope. The workings of creation and the principles of the Changes interpenetrate: thus the Changes accords with Heaven and Earth. How could one regard them as divergent? Its full possession of all principles is precisely its universal embrace of all phenomena; its embodiment of every good is precisely its bearing of all forms. The Way and concrete things, the refined and the coarse, fit together: thus the Changes participates in the workings of creation. How could one discuss them as separate things? From this we can see that Heaven and Earth are the source of the principles of the Changes, while the book of Changes is the inner mystery of creation. There is indeed a reason why it reaches both far and near and fills the space between Heaven and Earth!

In general, human beings are born receiving the balanced endowment of Heaven and Earth, and all things are complete within us; our minds are inherently broad and great. Provided we do not constrain them with selfishness, they are empty in stillness and upright in activity. The breadth and greatness of our minds then equal those of Heaven and Earth, and establishing their proper positions, nurturing all things, and participating in and assisting their transforming work all lie within our capacity. Thus, for those studying the Changes, nothing takes precedence over properly tending their minds, so as to attain the reality of breadth and greatness. Otherwise, Heaven and Earth are merely patterns and images, and the book of Changes merely coarse traces, seemingly unrelated to our minds. Hence it says: “The principles of all under Heaven are grasped, and one takes one’s place in their midst.” This is the supreme achievement of the sage’s Changes within the mind.

Book of Documents

“The nine accomplishments are duly ordered; the nine duly ordered accomplishments are celebrated in song.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
矢思學
同考試官教諭易批深得陳謨之㫖而文足以
發之佳士也取之
同考試官教諭金批平正條達
考試官教諭何批說理之文
考試官教諭錢批精當
政得其理而民樂其生此聖治之徵也夫民情
利於有養也九功敘而養道備矣其樂而形之
歌也惡容已哉大禹述世道之泰欲帝念而保
===
之也蓋曰王政莫大於養民而民風可驗乎治
理今玆治功可見者何如哉彼六府三事曰九
功人君所以立民命也一有未舉難乎其克敘
矣玆惟其脩而和焉則陰陽之運於化工者裁
成以盡其利各循其軌而不紊倫制之陳於藝
極者神化以通其變各當其理而無乖五氣順
而百穀成本於天者適得其化醇之妙民彛正
而庶事舉順乎人者自安於率性之常夫然則
功無不敘而德之所推溥矣政其有弗善耶至
punctuated:
矢思學

同考試官教諭易批：深得陳謨之㫖，而文足以發之，佳士也，取之。
同考試官教諭金批：平正條達。
考試官教諭何批：說理之文。
考試官教諭錢批：精當。

政得其理，而民樂其生，此聖治之徵也。夫民情利於有養也，九功敘而養道備矣，其樂而形之歌也，惡容已哉？大禹述世道之泰，欲帝念而保之也。蓋曰：王政莫大於養民，而民風可驗乎治理。今玆治功可見者何如哉？彼六府三事曰九功，人君所以立民命也。一有未舉，難乎其克敘矣。玆惟其脩而和焉，則陰陽之運於化工者，裁成以盡其利，各循其軌而不紊；倫制之陳於藝極者，神化以通其變，各當其理而無乖。五氣順而百穀成，本於天者適得其化醇之妙；民彛正而庶事舉，順乎人者自安於率性之常。夫然則功無不敘，而德之所推溥矣，政其有弗善耶？至

Shi Sixue 矢思學

Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: “An essay that expounds principle.”
Examiner Qian, an Instructor, comments: “Precise and apt.”

When government accords with proper principle and the people delight in their lives, this is evidence of sagely rule. By their nature, the people benefit from being sustained. When the nine achievements are ordered, the means of sustaining them are complete. How could they refrain from expressing their joy in song? The Great Yu described the peace and prosperity of the age, wishing the emperor to keep it in mind and preserve it.

His meaning was this: nothing in kingly government is greater than sustaining the people, and the customs of the people attest to the orderliness of government. What, then, are the achievements of government now visible? The six resources and three undertakings are called the nine achievements; through them the ruler establishes the people's livelihood. If even one remains unfulfilled, it is difficult for them all to be brought into order. Now, however, they have been cultivated and harmonized. Thus, the operations of yin and yang in the work of creation are regulated and perfected so that their benefits are fully realized, each following its course without disorder. The ethical institutions set forth in the standards of accomplishment [?] are transformed with spirit-like efficacy to accommodate change, each fitting its proper principle without deviation. The five vital forces flow harmoniously and the many grains ripen: what is rooted in Heaven duly attains the marvel of its richly generative transformation. The people's constant moral relationships are set right and the many affairs are accomplished: what accords with human beings rests naturally in the constant norm of following their nature. Thus no achievement remains unordered, and virtue extends its influence far and wide. Could there be anything amiss in such government? As for…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
若府事脩和曰九敘人君所以和民心也一有
未理難乎其感民矣玆惟其備而敘焉則享樂
利之休者慶分願之各足而歡欣自溢於名言
沐膏澤之化者幸生養之有賴而歌聲無間於
遠邇仰觀於天成而樂心生焉其叶之唱和以
鳴造化之盛者翕然擊壤之餘音也俯察於事
治而喜心感焉其比之聲文以宣豫悅之情者
藹然康衢之遺詠也夫然則敘無不歌而功之
所格者深矣民其有弗養耶要之九功之敘君
===
也而利則及於民九敘之歌民也而德則歸於
君有虞致治之盛蔑以加矣然禹欲帝念而保
之其忠愛之心何如哉大抵聲音之道與政通
故古之觀政者惟於民俗之歌致意焉其戒休
董威以保治功於有永亦卽以其歌而勸相之
其所以感天下於和平者至矣成周命太史陳
詩以觀民風其亦有見於此歟是故善政者其
道同
會其有極歸其有極曰皇極之敷言是彝
punctuated:
若府事脩和，曰九敘，人君所以和民心也。一有未理，難乎其感民矣。玆惟其備而敘焉，則享樂利之休者，慶分願之各足，而歡欣自溢於名言；沐膏澤之化者，幸生養之有賴，而歌聲無間於遠邇。仰觀於天成，而樂心生焉，其叶之唱和以鳴造化之盛者，翕然擊壤之餘音也；俯察於事治，而喜心感焉，其比之聲文以宣豫悅之情者，藹然康衢之遺詠也。夫然則敘無不歌，而功之所格者深矣，民其有弗養耶？要之，九功之敘，君也，而利則及於民；九敘之歌，民也，而德則歸於君。有虞致治之盛，蔑以加矣。然禹欲帝念而保之，其忠愛之心何如哉！大抵聲音之道與政通，故古之觀政者，惟於民俗之歌致意焉。其戒休董威，以保治功於有永，亦卽以其歌而勸相之。其所以感天下於和平者至矣。成周命太史陳詩以觀民風，其亦有見於此歟？是故善政者，其道同。

會其有極，歸其有極，曰皇極之敷言，是彝
translation_en:
…as for the cultivation and harmonization of the resources and undertakings, this is called the ninefold ordering: it is how the ruler brings harmony to the people’s hearts. If even one matter remains unregulated, it will be difficult for him to move the people. Only when these are fully provided for and put in order do those enjoying the blessings of ease and benefit rejoice that their respective portions and wishes are satisfied, their delight spontaneously overflowing into words. Those bathed in his beneficent influence count themselves fortunate to have support for their lives and sustenance, and their singing resounds alike near and far. Looking upward, they behold Heaven’s work accomplished, and joy arises in their hearts. Their harmonious singing and responses proclaim the abundance of creation: together they echo the ancient song of Beating the Ground. Looking downward, they observe affairs well governed, and their hearts are stirred with gladness. Their patterned melodies express their pleasure and delight: warmly they continue the ancient song of the Broad Thoroughfare. Thus no aspect of this ordering goes unsung, and the achievements of government reach deep indeed. Could any of the people then fail to be nurtured?

In sum, it is the ruler who orders the nine achievements, but their benefits extend to the people; it is the people who sing of the ninefold ordering, but the credit for virtue returns to the ruler. Nothing could surpass the flourishing government of Youyu, the age of Shun. Yet Yu wished the emperor to remain mindful of it and preserve it. How profound was his loyal devotion! In general, the workings of sound are connected with government. Thus those in antiquity who examined government paid particular attention to the songs current among the people. In admonishing through commendation and supervising through awe, so as to preserve the achievements of government forever, they likewise used these songs to encourage and assist. Their means of moving all under Heaven toward peace and harmony were consummate. When the Zhou court commanded the Grand Astrologer to present poems in order to observe the people’s customs, did it not likewise perceive this principle? Thus those who govern well follow the same Way.

Gather toward the standard; return to the standard. These are the words that set forth the sovereign’s supreme standard; this is the constant rule …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
是訓于帝其訓
書三篇樊璽
同考試官教諭易批詞理俱到
同考試官教諭金批鋪叙敷言之旨精純溫潤可以官其人矣
考試官教諭何批明徹可觀
考試官教諭錢批典雅之作
君子約敷言之訓而深賛其妙焉夫皇極之訓
要之使人會歸於極而已然其理則出於天焉
===
非達天德者其孰能知之箕子衍皇極之疇以
告武王至此若曰人君之建極於天下也敷言
之道雖本於人之身而神道之教實原於天之
命是故其爲訓也豈徒使之諷詠而已哉由是
而示於人曰會其有極蓋極之理涵於心而具
足也玆惟戒其私念之萌而王義王道王路是
遵焉則約情以協中有以萃衆志之渙而凡同
心以向道者有定趨矣又於是而示於人曰歸
有極蓋極之理見於事而各當也玆惟戒其
punctuated:
是訓，于帝其訓。
書三篇，樊璽。
同考試官教諭易批：詞理俱到。
同考試官教諭金批：鋪叙敷言之旨，精純溫潤，可以官其人矣。
考試官教諭何批：明徹可觀。
考試官教諭錢批：典雅之作。
君子約敷言之訓而深賛其妙焉。夫皇極之訓，要之使人會歸於極而已，然其理則出於天焉。非達天德者，其孰能知之？箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王，至此若曰：人君之建極於天下也，敷言之道雖本於人之身，而神道之教實原於天之命。是故其爲訓也，豈徒使之諷詠而已哉？由是而示於人曰：「會其有極。」蓋極之理涵於心而具足也，玆惟戒其私念之萌，而王義、王道、王路是遵焉。則約情以協中，有以萃衆志之渙，而凡同心以向道者有定趨矣。又於是而示於人曰：「歸有極。」蓋極之理見於事而各當也，玆惟戒其
translation_en:
…these are instructions; they accord with the teachings of the Sovereign on High.
Book of Documents: three essays. Fan Xi.
Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: “His exposition of the meaning of the promulgated words is refined, pure, gentle, and polished. This man may be appointed to office.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Clear and penetrating; worthy of attention.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “A work of classical elegance.”
The gentleman sums up the instruction conveyed by the promulgated words and deeply praises its subtle excellence. The instruction of the August Ultimate is, in essence, simply to make people converge upon and return to the Ultimate. Yet its principle comes from Heaven. Who could understand it without comprehending Heaven’s virtue?
Jizi elaborated the category of the August Ultimate to instruct King Wu. At this point, it is as though he said: When the ruler establishes the Ultimate throughout the world, the way of promulgating words is rooted in his own person, but instruction through the numinous Way truly originates in Heaven’s mandate. Thus, can such instruction be intended merely for people to recite and chant?
Accordingly, he declares to the people: “Converge upon the Ultimate.” The principle of the Ultimate is contained in the heart in its fullness. Here he cautions them against the emergence of selfish thoughts, so that they follow the king’s righteousness, the king’s Way, and the king’s path. By restraining their feelings to accord with the mean, they can gather together the scattered purposes of the multitude; all who turn with one heart toward the Way thus have a fixed direction.
Further, he declares to the people: “Return to the Ultimate.” The principle of the Ultimate manifests itself in affairs, giving each its proper measure. Here he cautions them against their…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不善之動而蕩蕩平平正直是由焉則視履以
考祥有以止至善之域而凡造道以優入者有
定守矣夫敷言之訓如此是豈一已之私哉吾
知道本固有而播之聲詠者莫非烝民秉彝之
良固天下之常理也理本無外而普之話言者
實皆萬世定保之徴固天下之大訓也然訓雖
君也而言則純乎理焉謂天之訓可也惟皇降
衷若或啓之以左右乎斯民者也天其無言之
君矣乎言雖君也而理則本於天焉謂天之教
===
可也惟帝佑民若或道之以寵綏乎四方者也
君其有言之天矣乎夫敷言之妙有如此以是
而達之臣民則人心之天隨感而應會極歸極
固有莫知其然者彜倫之叙固其所歟雖然是
豈可以易致者哉蓋人君必有合天之心而後
有同天之化苟非建極之君位在德元而徒以
言語感人者末矣故建極者必求端於天而憲
天者必求端於心此固箕子告武王之意也四
海永清之治其亦有由也夫
punctuated: 不善之動，而蕩蕩、平平、正直是由焉，則視履以考祥，有以止至善之域，而凡造道以優入者有定守矣。夫敷言之訓如此，是豈一已之私哉？吾知道本固有，而播之聲詠者，莫非烝民秉彝之良，固天下之常理也；理本無外，而普之話言者，實皆萬世定保之徴，固天下之大訓也。然訓雖君也，而言則純乎理焉，謂天之訓可也。惟皇降衷，若或啓之，以左右乎斯民者也，天其無言之君矣乎？言雖君也，而理則本於天焉，謂天之教可也。惟帝佑民，若或道之，以寵綏乎四方者也，君其有言之天矣乎？夫敷言之妙有如此，以是而達之臣民，則人心之天隨感而應，會極、歸極，固有莫知其然者。彜倫之叙，固其所歟？雖然，是豈可以易致者哉？蓋人君必有合天之心，而後有同天之化。苟非建極之君，位在德元，而徒以言語感人者，末矣。故建極者必求端於天，而憲天者必求端於心。此固箕子告武王之意也。四海永清之治，其亦有由也夫！
translation_en:
…the stirring of evil, and follows what is broad, even, and upright; then, by examining conduct to assess its auspicious consequences, one can come to rest in the realm of the highest good, and all who advance toward the Way and enter deeply into it will have something fixed to uphold. Such is the instruction conveyed by promulgating words. Could this possibly be one person's private concern? I know that the Way is inherently possessed: what is disseminated through recitation and song is invariably the goodness of the constant moral nature held by the multitude. This is indeed the enduring principle of all under Heaven. Principle excludes nothing: what is spread universally through spoken instruction is truly evidence of what secures lasting stability for myriad generations. This is indeed the great instruction of all under Heaven.

Although the instruction comes from the ruler, its words accord wholly with principle; it may therefore be called Heaven's instruction. The August One bestows the moral mean, as though someone were opening people's understanding and thus assisting them. Is Heaven, then, a ruler without speech? Although the words come from the ruler, their principle is rooted in Heaven; they may therefore be called Heaven's teaching. The Lord on High protects the people, as though someone were guiding them and thereby cherishing and bringing peace to the four quarters. Is the ruler, then, Heaven endowed with speech?

Such is the subtle efficacy of promulgating words. When these are conveyed to officials and people, the Heaven within the human heart responds as it is moved. People gather at the Supreme Standard and return to it, without necessarily knowing how this comes about. Surely the ordering of the constant human relationships is its proper outcome? Yet how could this be easily achieved? A ruler must first possess a heart united with Heaven before he can exercise a transforming influence like Heaven's. Unless he is a ruler who establishes the Supreme Standard and stands foremost in virtue, merely seeking to move people through words is a superficial undertaking. Thus, one who establishes the Supreme Standard must seek its source in Heaven, while one who takes Heaven as his model must seek the source within his own heart. This indeed was the meaning of Jizi's admonition to King Wu. A reign of enduring peace throughout the Four Seas surely has its foundation in this!

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
詩
左之左之君子宜之右之右之君子有之
同考試官教諭胡批〔得詩人之旨〕
同考試官教諭項批〔措詞豐辨而無一字剩語是善說詩者〕
廖如春
考試官教諭何批〔豐贍〕
考試官教諭錢批〔充暢〕
詩人美諸侯之才德而用無不周焉蓋君子所
===
以致用於天下者才德而已矣諸侯能全備之
則何用而不臧乎此天子美諸侯之詩蓋以答
瞻彼洛矣也若曰王者之使人也固無求備之
心而人臣之用世也貴得泛應之妙今茲會同
洛邑者何如哉彼身之所處不一而有所謂左
有所謂右者萬事萬物之變也道之所應有常
而左必曰宜右必曰有者揆事宰物之權也夫
人才非全才而德非備德則亦一偏之士而無
以周左右之用矣惟我君子也大道不器而所
punctuated:
詩

左之左之，君子宜之；右之右之，君子有之。

同考試官教諭胡批〔得詩人之旨〕
同考試官教諭項批〔措詞豐辨，而無一字剩語，是善說詩者〕
廖如春
考試官教諭何批〔豐贍〕

詩人美諸侯之才德，而用無不周焉。蓋君子所以致用於天下者，才德而已矣。諸侯能全備之，則何用而不臧乎？此天子美諸侯之詩，蓋以答《瞻彼洛矣》也。若曰：王者之使人也，固無求備之心；而人臣之用世也，貴得泛應之妙。今茲會同洛邑者何如哉？彼身之所處不一，而有所謂左、有所謂右者，萬事萬物之變也；道之所應有常，而左必曰宜、右必曰有者，揆事宰物之權也。夫人才非全才，而德非備德，則亦一偏之士，而無以周左右之用矣。惟我君子也，大道不器，而所
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“Place him on the left, on the left: the gentleman is suited to it. Place him on the right, on the right: the gentleman has what is needed.”

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the poet’s intent.〕
Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is rich and discriminating, yet contains not a single superfluous word. This is someone skilled at explaining the Odes.〕

Liao Ruchun

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔Rich and ample.〕
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: 〔Full and fluent.〕

The poet praises the talents and virtue of the feudal lords, whose service is comprehensive in every respect. For what enables a gentleman to render service throughout the realm is simply talent and virtue. If the feudal lords possess these in their fullness, in what employment could they fail to excel? This is an ode in which the Son of Heaven praises the feudal lords, apparently in response to “Gaze upon That Luo” (Zhan bi Luo yi). It is as though he were saying: When a king employs men, he certainly does not demand perfection; yet when a minister serves the world, what is valued is his mastery of responding to every circumstance. How, then, do those now assembled at Luoyi measure up? The positions they occupy differ: what are called “left” and “right” represent the changing circumstances of all affairs and things. The Way’s responses follow a constant principle: that the left is invariably called “suited” and the right invariably described as “having what is needed” expresses the discretionary judgment by which affairs are assessed and things governed. If a man’s talents are not comprehensive and his virtue is not complete, he is merely a man of partial abilities, unable to fulfill all the functions of left and right. Our gentleman alone embodies the great Way, which is not confined to the function of a particular vessel, and that by which …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以辦天下之事者遺之至艱而不撓大德不官
而所以任天下之重者投之至繁而不亂左之
左之以時措之而已矣推行盡利也化裁盡神
也而各協於中正之極右之右之以時出之而
已矣取之不窮也用之不匱也而悉備乎廣大
之全隨在而皆天子之所使則隨在而皆君子
之所宜入而在內則佐王經邦國而予曰有先
後也出而在外則佐王平邦國而予曰有禦侮
也蓋不特宜於文而又宜於武矣其諸咸宜者
===
乎無往而非天子之所命則無往而非君子之
所有以綏太平則順治之猷慰一人求寧之念
也以勘禍亂則威嚴之略協一人先事之圖也
蓋不特有文事而又有武備矣其諸富有者乎
是則由左而觀之故謂之宜耳而復有之於右
未嘗滯於左也則雖曰無所不宜可也由右而
觀之故謂之有耳而復宜之於左未嘗滯於右
也則雖曰無所不有可也東都一會而以作六
師其所以致福祿之如茨保邦家於萬年者誠
punctuated: 以辦天下之事者，遺之至艱而不撓；大德不官，而所以任天下之重者，投之至繁而不亂。左之左之，以時措之而已矣。推行盡利也，化裁盡神也，而各協於中正之極。右之右之，以時出之而已矣。取之不窮也，用之不匱也，而悉備乎廣大之全。隨在而皆天子之所使，則隨在而皆君子之所宜。入而在內，則佐王經邦國，而予曰有先後也；出而在外，則佐王平邦國，而予曰有禦侮也。蓋不特宜於文，而又宜於武矣，其諸咸宜者乎！無往而非天子之所命，則無往而非君子之所有。以綏太平，則順治之猷，慰一人求寧之念也；以勘禍亂，則威嚴之略，協一人先事之圖也。蓋不特有文事，而又有武備矣，其諸富有者乎！是則由左而觀之，故謂之宜耳，而復有之於右，未嘗滯於左也，則雖曰無所不宜可也；由右而觀之，故謂之有耳，而復宜之於左，未嘗滯於右也，則雖曰無所不有可也。東都一會，而以作六師，其所以致福祿之如茨、保邦家於萬年者，誠
translation_en:
…that by which he manages the affairs of the world enables him to remain unbowed when entrusted with the greatest difficulties. Great virtue is not confined to a single office, and that by which he bears the weighty responsibilities of the world enables him to remain unconfused when cast into the utmost complexity. Employ him on the left, employ him on the left: it is simply a matter of placing him as the occasion requires. In putting things into practice, he realizes every benefit; in adapting and determining them, he displays consummate subtlety. Each accords with the highest standard of balance and correctness. Employ him on the right, employ him on the right: it is simply a matter of bringing him forth as the occasion requires. What may be drawn from him is inexhaustible; what may be put to use never runs short. He possesses in full a breadth and greatness that embrace everything.

Wherever the Son of Heaven employs him, the noble man proves equal to the task. When he enters and serves within the court, he assists the king in ordering the realm, and I say that I have one who aids me. When he goes out and serves beyond the court, he assists the king in pacifying the realm, and I say that I have one who wards off aggression. Thus he is suited not only to civil affairs but also to military affairs. Is he not one suited to every task? Wherever the Son of Heaven commands him to go, the noble man possesses what is needed. In maintaining peace, his plans for orderly government console the sovereign in his desire for tranquility. In suppressing calamity and disorder, his strategies of awe-inspiring authority accord with the sovereign’s plans to anticipate events. Thus he possesses not only civil accomplishments but also military preparedness. Is he not one richly endowed?

Viewed from the left, he is therefore called suited to the task; yet he also possesses what is needed on the right and has never been confined to the left. Thus one may indeed say that there is no task to which he is unsuited. Viewed from the right, he is therefore said to possess what is needed; yet he is also suited to tasks on the left and has never been confined to the right. Thus one may indeed say that there is nothing he lacks. At a single assembly in the eastern capital, the six armies are roused. As for bringing blessings and emoluments thick as thatch and preserving the realm for ten thousand years, truly…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
於斯人乎有賴矣彼文章車馬云者何足以觀
君子之深哉甞論才德之難久矣裨諶謀野則
獲而謀邑則否孟公綽優於趙魏老而不可爲
滕薛大夫何則局於量也乃裳華所稱用之左
右而無施不可又若是其全且備者豈虛譽乎
哉諸侯來朝則敷奏之明試之而其言其功良
有明徵矣吾於是而知詩人非譽之也蓋試之
也抑亦因以勸戒之也歟
天子萬壽明明天子令聞不已
===
姜忻
同考試官教諭胡批〔善寫詩人祝願之意〕
同考試官教諭項批〔措詞莊重而忠愛藹然可與從政矣〕
考試官教諭何批〔詞義沛然〕
考試官教諭錢批〔是大樣文字〕
大臣答君必欲其永年而永譽也夫年與譽而
俱永天下之純嘏也大臣旣祝之而復進之忠
愛寧有已哉詩人美召虎平淮之功此則述其
punctuated:
於斯人乎有賴矣。彼文章車馬云者，何足以觀君子之深哉？甞論才德之難久矣。裨諶謀野則獲，而謀邑則否；孟公綽優於趙魏老，而不可爲滕薛大夫。何則？局於量也。乃裳華所稱，用之左右而無施不可，又若是其全且備者，豈虛譽乎哉？諸侯來朝，則敷奏之，明試之，而其言其功，良有明徵矣。吾於是而知詩人非譽之也，蓋試之也，抑亦因以勸戒之也歟？

天子萬壽，明明天子，令聞不已。

姜忻

同考試官教諭胡批〔善寫詩人祝願之意〕
同考試官教諭項批〔措詞莊重而忠愛藹然可與從政矣〕
考試官教諭何批〔詞義沛然〕
考試官教諭錢批〔是大樣文字〕

大臣答君，必欲其永年而永譽也。夫年與譽而俱永，天下之純嘏也。大臣旣祝之，而復進之，忠愛寧有已哉？詩人美召虎平淮之功，此則述其
translation_en:
…it is upon such men that reliance must indeed be placed. How could those things spoken of—patterned robes, carriages, and horses—suffice to reveal the gentleman’s depth? I have long pondered the difficulty of attaining both ability and virtue. Bi Chen’s planning succeeded when undertaken in the countryside, but not in the city. Meng Gongchuo was more than qualified to serve as chief steward to the Zhao or Wei family, yet could not serve as a grand master in Teng or Xue. Why? Their capacities had limits. Yet the man praised in Blossoming Flowers (Shang hua), employed on either the left or the right, proved equal to every application. Could praise of someone so complete and fully accomplished be empty? When the regional lords came to court, their reports were presented and their performance clearly tested; there was sound, manifest evidence of both their words and their achievements. From this I know that the poet was not merely praising them: he was assessing them. Or was he also thereby encouraging and admonishing them?

“May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years! May the illustrious Son of Heaven’s good repute never cease.”

Jiang Xin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔Skillfully conveys the poet’s wishes and blessings.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor: 〔The wording is dignified, and loyalty and affection abound. Such a man may be entrusted with government.〕
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔Abundant in expression and meaning.〕
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔This is writing on a grand scale.〕

When a great minister responds to his sovereign, he assuredly desires that the sovereign enjoy both enduring life and enduring renown. For life and renown alike to endure is an unalloyed blessing for all under Heaven. Having offered his wishes, the great minister further urges his sovereign onward: can his loyalty and affection ever cease? The poet praises Shao Hu’s achievement in pacifying the Huai region; this passage recounts his…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
答稱之意也若曰帝王德至於天而必得其壽
德至於人而必得其名兼此二者故全也虎之
所以對揚王休者豈徒作召公考而已哉彼人
君以一身斂五福之全所不能必之天者壽也
而萬壽則無疆矣今我天子也統華夷之大而
爲中興之主崇高冨貴此固其凝命之初耳必
自天祐之而難老永錫裕而爲悠遠之休威福
玉食此固其履端之始耳必自天申之而年所
多歷綿而爲永貞之慶俾爾壽而臧王心有當
===
寧也俾爾彌爾性君身有常固也蓋萬年此天
地則萬年此天子殆與文之壽考武之眉壽而
同其久矣然則江漢之朝宗固不獨今日爲爾
也而虎之所以承圭瓉土田之錫者不將永賴
於後世也哉人君以一身爲萬國之主所不能
必之人者令聞也而不已則有常矣今我明明
天子也懋脩攘之略而成中興之功以內則順
治而天下稱仁也要必有永保之謨焉而明王
之頌恒歸於知臨之大君以外則威嚴而天下
punctuated: 答稱之意也。若曰：帝王德至於天，而必得其壽；德至於人，而必得其名。兼此二者，故全也。虎之所以對揚王休者，豈徒作召公考而已哉？彼人君以一身斂五福之全，所不能必之天者壽也，而萬壽則無疆矣。今我天子也，統華夷之大而爲中興之主，崇高冨貴，此固其凝命之初耳；必自天祐之，而難老永錫，裕而爲悠遠之休。威福玉食，此固其履端之始耳；必自天申之，而年所多歷，綿而爲永貞之慶。俾爾壽而臧，王心有當寧也；俾爾彌爾性，君身有常固也。蓋萬年此天地，則萬年此天子，殆與文之壽考、武之眉壽而同其久矣。然則江漢之朝宗，固不獨今日爲爾也；而虎之所以承圭瓉土田之錫者，不將永賴於後世也哉？人君以一身爲萬國之主，所不能必之人者令聞也，而不已則有常矣。今我明明天子也，懋脩攘之略而成中興之功。以內則順治而天下稱仁也，要必有永保之謨焉，而明王之頌恒歸於知臨之大君；以外則威嚴而天下
translation_en:
…the meaning of his words of acknowledgment and praise. It is as though he said: when an emperor’s virtue reaches Heaven, he must obtain longevity; when his virtue reaches the people, he must obtain renown. Possessing both, he is complete. Was Hu’s response in extolling the king’s favor merely to build a shrine to the Duke of Shao?

The ruler gathers in his own person all five blessings. What he cannot assuredly obtain from Heaven is longevity; yet a life of ten thousand years would know no bounds. Now our Son of Heaven rules the vast realm of Chinese and non-Chinese peoples and is the lord of dynastic restoration. His exalted station, wealth, and honor are merely the beginning of his consolidation of the Mandate. Heaven must itself protect him, forever granting freedom from the infirmities of age, with blessings abundant enough to endure into the distant future. His power to punish and reward, and his precious fare, are merely the beginning of his reign. Heaven must itself renew its blessings upon him, so that he passes through many years, their continuity becoming the good fortune of enduring steadfastness. “May you live long and prosper”: the king’s heart is set upon presiding at court. “May you fulfill your allotted span”: the ruler’s person enjoys lasting strength. If this Heaven and Earth endure ten thousand years, then may this Son of Heaven endure ten thousand years, matching the long life of King Wen and the venerable longevity of King Wu. Thus the Jiang and Han rivers’ homage to the sea is surely not confined to this day alone. And will not Hu, who received the gifts of a jade tablet, a jade libation ladle, and lands, continue to enjoy their benefits through later generations?

The ruler in his own person is lord of the myriad states. What he cannot assuredly obtain from others is a fine reputation; yet if it never ceases, it will endure. Now our illustrious Son of Heaven diligently pursues strategies for internal cultivation and the repulsion of external threats, accomplishing a dynastic restoration. Within the realm, government is orderly and all under Heaven praise his benevolence. Yet he must have plans to preserve this forever, so that praise of the enlightened king continually accrues to the great ruler who governs with wisdom. Beyond the realm, his authority inspires awe, and all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
稱義也要必有永終之道焉而聖人之歌常集
於聰明之元后其實愈大而其聲愈弘也其積
愈厚而其光愈遠也蓋天子此萬年則令聞亦
此萬年殆與文之聿駿武之顯名而同其美矣
然則江漢之聲靈固不獨今日爲爾也而虎之
效經營疆理之勞者亦將有詞於永世也哉吁
先之以萬壽而得聞以彰之則壽爲有光繼之
以令聞而得壽以承之則聞爲有藉于此見召
公報禮之重而其言亦可繹思矣抑論壽非倖
===
致也必有以爲享壽之原聞非襲取也必有以
爲致聞之實萬壽令聞召公豈徒諛其君者至
篇終則曰矢其文德洽此四國此所謂原所謂
實也亦康公卷阿之遺法歟歆以壽考福祿之
盛而歸於用馮翼孝德之賢頌不忘規有自來
矣詩曰召公是似甚矣虎之似乎奭也
春秋
秋宋人齊人邾人伐郳〔莊公十有五年〕
李伯廉
punctuated:
稱義也，要必有永終之道焉，而聖人之歌常集於聰明之元后。其實愈大，而其聲愈弘也；其積愈厚，而其光愈遠也。蓋天子此萬年，則令聞亦此萬年，殆與文之聿駿、武之顯名而同其美矣。然則江漢之聲靈，固不獨今日爲爾也，而虎之效經營疆理之勞者，亦將有詞於永世也哉！吁！先之以萬壽，而得聞以彰之，則壽爲有光；繼之以令聞，而得壽以承之，則聞爲有藉。于此見召公報禮之重，而其言亦可繹思矣。抑論壽非倖致也，必有以爲享壽之原；聞非襲取也，必有以爲致聞之實。萬壽令聞，召公豈徒諛其君者？至篇終則曰：「矢其文德，洽此四國。」此所謂原、所謂實也。亦康公《卷阿》之遺法歟？歆以壽考福祿之盛，而歸於用馮翼孝德之賢，頌不忘規，有自來矣。《詩》曰：「召公是似。」甚矣，虎之似乎奭也！
春秋
秋，宋人、齊人、邾人伐郳。〔莊公十有五年〕
李伯廉
translation_en:
…praise his righteousness. There must assuredly be a way to preserve it to the very end, so that songs celebrating the sage continually converge upon the discerning sovereign. The greater his actual achievements, the more widely his renown resounds; the richer his accumulated merit, the farther his radiance reaches. If the Son of Heaven thus enjoys ten thousand years, his fine reputation will likewise endure for ten thousand years, matching in its glory King Wen’s ever-growing greatness and King Wu’s illustrious name. Thus the awe-inspiring prestige celebrated in “The Jiang and Han” is surely not confined to today; and Hu’s labors in planning and administering the territories will also be celebrated in words for all ages!
Ah! First comes the wish for myriad years of life, with renown to make them illustrious: longevity thereby gains luster. Next comes the wish for a fine reputation, with longevity to sustain it: reputation thereby gains a foundation. Here we see the weight the Duke of Shao attached to reciprocating the ruler’s ceremonial favors; his words also merit careful reflection. Yet longevity is not attained by mere good fortune: there must be a source from which its enjoyment springs. Nor can reputation simply be appropriated: there must be substantive achievements that bring it about. In wishing his ruler long life and a fine reputation, was the Duke of Shao merely flattering him? At the poem’s close he says: “Display your civil virtue, and bring harmony to these four quarters.” This is what is meant by that source and that substance. Is this not also the method handed down by Duke Kang in “The Winding Hill” (Juan a)? He inspires the ruler with the prospect of abundant longevity, blessings, and emoluments, but ultimately directs him toward employing worthy men who offer support and assistance and possess filial piety and virtue. Praise that does not forget admonition has a long history. The Book of Odes says: “Take the Duke of Shao as your model.” How closely Hu resembles Shi!
Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, men of Song, Qi, and Zhu attacked Ni. 〔The fifteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Li Bolian.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭袁批題本平淡而作更馳騁是
深於春秋者
同考試官教授蔣批結着折服管仲處常是如此
考試官教諭何批嚴整中式
考試官教諭錢批雅健
春秋紀兵權之有屬見伯業之未成此伐郳之
役桓雖圖伯而猶未成乎伯也不然何以後于
主兵之宋乎昔管仲相桓肇始伯業北杏之後
會宋伐郳夫伯者之先諸侯例也桓既伯矣何
===
以序于宋下蓋天下有伯則專征之權在伯主
天下無伯則主兵之柄在諸侯兹焉桓也心雖
切于匡世而尊主庇民之業不可以旦夕而成
志雖在于主盟而攘夷安夏之勳未可以歲月
而集伐宋之師甞以威震諸侯矣而威未能遽
伸也威不伸而何以萃天下之渙于鄄之會甞
以信懷諸侯矣而信未能遽洽也信不洽而何
以合天下之離是故伐郳之師主兵者猶屬于
三恪之宋而大邦未見其盡畏也桓豈不欲使
punctuated:
同考試官教諭袁批：題本平淡，而作更馳騁，是深於《春秋》者。
同考試官教授蔣批：結着折服管仲處，常是如此。
考試官教諭何批：嚴整中式。
考試官教諭錢批：雅健。
《春秋》紀兵權之有屬，見伯業之未成。此伐郳之役，桓雖圖伯，而猶未成乎伯也。不然，何以後于主兵之宋乎？昔管仲相桓，肇始伯業，北杏之後，會宋伐郳。夫伯者之先諸侯，例也。桓既伯矣，何以序于宋下？蓋天下有伯，則專征之權在伯主；天下無伯，則主兵之柄在諸侯。兹焉桓也，心雖切于匡世，而尊主庇民之業，不可以旦夕而成；志雖在于主盟，而攘夷安夏之勳，未可以歲月而集。伐宋之師，甞以威震諸侯矣，而威未能遽伸也。威不伸，而何以萃天下之渙？于鄄之會，甞以信懷諸侯矣，而信未能遽洽也。信不洽，而何以合天下之離？是故伐郳之師，主兵者猶屬于三恪之宋，而大邦未見其盡畏也。桓豈不欲使
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is plain, yet the composition ranges freely. This is someone with a profound understanding of the Spring and Autumn Annals.”
Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “The conclusion turns on a point that confounds Guan Zhong; it is always like this [?].”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Rigorous and orderly, meeting the prescribed standard.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records where military authority lay, revealing that the enterprise of hegemony was not yet complete. In this campaign against Ni, although Duke Huan sought hegemony, he had not yet become hegemon. Otherwise, why would he be placed after Song, which commanded the forces? Formerly, Guan Zhong served as Duke Huan’s chief minister and initiated his pursuit of hegemony. After Beixing, they joined Song in attacking Ni. Now, it is the rule that the hegemon takes precedence over the other feudal lords. If Huan was already hegemon, why was he listed below Song? When the realm has a hegemon, authority to undertake punitive expeditions on his own initiative rests with that hegemon; when it has no hegemon, command of armies rests with the feudal lords. At this point, although Huan earnestly desired to set the world right, the work of honoring the sovereign and protecting the people could not be accomplished overnight. Although his ambition was to preside over covenants, the achievement of repelling the non-Chinese peoples and securing the Chinese states could not be amassed within a few months or years. In the campaign against Song, he had indeed awed the feudal lords with his might, but that might could not immediately extend its reach. If his might did not extend, how could he gather together the scattered elements of the realm? At the meeting at Juan, he had indeed sought to win the feudal lords over through his trustworthiness, but that trust could not immediately become pervasive. If trust was not pervasive, how could he unite the divided elements of the realm? Thus, in the campaign against Ni, command of the forces still rested with Song, one of the Three Honored Houses descended from earlier dynasties, and the great states had yet to show that they all stood in awe of Huan. Did Huan not wish to wield …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
鉞而臨戎哉顧諸侯之不親輿情之未附亦紆
徐以俟其成而已從兵者僅止于附庸之郳而
小邦未見其盡懷也桓豈不欲徵兵以討貳哉
顧衆志之未定專欲之難成亦委曲以求其濟
而已後此而南征北略桓之績固偉也而不知
其有待于陳鄭同盟之後爲宋伐郼此其肇謀
之日耳不然奉揚東征之命齊將帥宋以從事
矣又安能爲之下乎後此而九合一匡桓之功
固大也而不知其有假于三十年經營之力因
===
人成事特其創業之初耳不然光昭賜履之勳
宋將悉賦以從齊矣又安敢爲之上乎聖人序
齊于宋下雖以著其伯業未成之實亦以望其
有成之意也吁此見春秋之不可無齊桓而聖
人之惓惓於桓者其爲世道慮也夫抑有疑焉
齊宋匹也齊方伐宋而遽從之以兵豈宋眞能
令齊哉無亦以上公之宋人望攸屬從宋則宋
可服宋服而諸侯可坐致矣嗚呼此桓之微意
也抑亦仲之謀也惜也始之以憂勤繼之以矜
punctuated: 鉞而臨戎哉？顧諸侯之不親，輿情之未附，亦紆徐以俟其成而已。從兵者僅止于附庸之郳，而小邦未見其盡懷也。桓豈不欲徵兵以討貳哉？顧衆志之未定，專欲之難成，亦委曲以求其濟而已。後此而南征北略，桓之績固偉也，而不知其有待于陳鄭同盟之後。爲宋伐郼，此其肇謀之日耳。不然，奉揚東征之命，齊將帥宋以從事矣，又安能爲之下乎？後此而九合一匡，桓之功固大也，而不知其有假于三十年經營之力。因人成事，特其創業之初耳。不然，光昭賜履之勳，宋將悉賦以從齊矣，又安敢爲之上乎？聖人序齊于宋下，雖以著其伯業未成之實，亦以望其有成之意也。吁！此見春秋之不可無齊桓，而聖人之惓惓於桓者，其爲世道慮也夫！抑有疑焉：齊宋匹也，齊方伐宋，而遽從之以兵，豈宋眞能令齊哉？無亦以上公之宋，人望攸屬，從宋則宋可服，宋服而諸侯可坐致矣。嗚呼！此桓之微意也，抑亦仲之謀也。惜也！始之以憂勤，繼之以矜
translation_en:
…the battle-axe and take command in war? Yet, seeing that the regional lords were not closely attached to him and public sentiment had not rallied to him, Duke Huan could only proceed slowly and await success. Those against whom the troops marched extended only to the dependent state of Ni; the small states had not yet all been won over. How could Huan not have wished to levy troops to punish those of divided allegiance? Yet, seeing that the multitude’s resolve was unsettled and that his wishes alone could hardly bring success, he could only seek accomplishment through accommodation.

After this he campaigned south and north, and Huan’s achievements were indeed magnificent. Yet people fail to recognize that these had to await the alliance with Chen and Zheng. Attacking Yi [?] on Song’s behalf marked only the beginning of his designs. Otherwise, in carrying out and proclaiming the command to campaign eastward, Qi would have led Song into action: how could it have taken a place below Song? After this he assembled the regional lords nine times and brought order to the realm, and Huan’s accomplishments were indeed great. Yet people fail to recognize that these depended on thirty years of sustained effort. Depending on others to accomplish his purposes belonged only to the beginning of his undertaking. Otherwise, in gloriously displaying achievements within the bounds granted him, Song would have mobilized all its forces to follow Qi: how would it have dared take a place above Qi?

In placing Qi below Song, the Sage not only made clear that Huan’s enterprise of hegemony was still incomplete, but also expressed his hope that it would succeed. Ah! This shows that the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals could not have done without Duke Huan of Qi. Surely the Sage’s earnest concern for Huan arose from his concern for the moral order of the world!

Yet a doubt remains. Qi and Song were peers. Qi had only just attacked Song, yet suddenly followed it with troops. Could Song truly have commanded Qi? Was it not rather that Song, as a state whose ruler held the highest ducal rank, commanded general esteem? By following Song, Huan could win its submission; once Song submitted, the regional lords could be brought over without further exertion. Ah! This was Huan’s subtle intention, and also Zhong’s strategy. What a pity! He began with anxious diligence, but followed it with pride…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
伐召陵盟濤塗執而桓之志荒矣噫此齊之君
臣所以止于伯歟
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚　楚人執鄭行人良霄〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐
子滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子
佐淮夷會于申〔昭公四年〕
方繼懋
===
同考試官教諭袁　批　措詞嚴正命意精深傑作也
同考試官教授蔣　批　以謀駕夷以誠服鄭手
類能言之充暢典雅僅見此篇
考試官教諭何　批　謹嚴
考試官教諭錢　批　詞意裕如
伯主得駕外服內之道而成功春秋所以善之
也此見晉悼謀足以屈楚而誠足以服鄭也偉
矣哉復伯之績乎且晉文襄之業中微悼公思
起而振之當是時北嚮與晉爭諸侯者楚也楚
punctuated:
伐，召陵盟，濤塗執，而桓之志荒矣。噫！此齊之君臣所以止于伯歟？

公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。楚人執鄭行人良霄。〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕

方繼懋

同考試官教諭袁批：措詞嚴正，命意精深，傑作也。
同考試官教授蔣批：以謀駕夷，以誠服鄭，手類能言之，充暢典雅，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭何批：謹嚴。
考試官教諭錢批：詞意裕如。

伯主得駕外服內之道而成功，春秋所以善之也。此見晉悼謀足以屈楚，而誠足以服鄭也。偉矣哉，復伯之績乎！且晉文襄之業中微，悼公思起而振之。當是時，北嚮與晉爭諸侯者，楚也。楚
translation_en:
…boasting. The covenant was concluded at Shaoling, and Taotu was seized; Duke Huan’s resolve had fallen into neglect. Alas! Was this why the ruler and ministers of Qi advanced no further than hegemony?

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. The men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the envoy of Zheng. 〔Both entries are from the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi assembled at Shen. 〔Fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕
Fang Jimao

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The wording is rigorous and upright; the conception is refined and profound. A masterpiece.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor: “Controlling the barbarians through strategy and bringing Zheng into submission through sincerity: [others?] can speak of this [?], but only this essay expresses it with such fullness, fluency, classical refinement, and elegance.”
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “Careful and rigorous.”
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “Ample ease in both expression and thought.”

A hegemonic lord achieves success by finding the way to control those outside and secure the submission of those within: this is why the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him. Here we see that Duke Dao of Jin possessed strategy sufficient to subdue Chu and sincerity sufficient to secure Zheng’s submission. Great indeed was his achievement in restoring the hegemony! The enterprise of Dukes Wen and Xiang of Jin had declined in the intervening years, and Duke Dao sought to rise and revive it. At that time, it was Chu that faced north and contested with Jin for the allegiance of the feudal lords. Chu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不屈伯不可得而復也中立而依違於晉楚之
間者鄭也鄭不從伯亦不可得而復也人皆曰
蠢爾之荆可以力制悼則不任力而任謀焉息
民取之魏絳善陣聽于知罃施舍輸積導利而
民悅矣减牲更幣制度而財節矣三分四軍不
戰而氣自倍矣羣策畢舉而坐得勝筭悼之所
以駕楚者豈徒以其力耶人皆曰反覆之鄭可
以威懾悼則不用威而用誠焉許伯騽而不拒
信子展而不疑禮囚歸俘無係累之慘矣納候
===
禁侵無猜暴之患矣遣使脩告咸喻乎諸侯之
志矣推心置腹而携貳獻誠悼之所以服鄭者
豈徒以其威耶由是楚雖強也悼之謀足以制
之三駕罷兵之後爭鄭之心頓沮雖以良霄之
告絕而僅執使泄忿焉蓋雖欲抗晉而不能抗
晉之謀也使暴骨以逞則楚勝而晉亦病矣况
兩廣爭雄固楚之長技也又豈遽出晉人下哉
由是鄭雖貳也悼之誠足以孚之東門觀兵之
後從晉之念遂堅至于楚虔之會申而始獻禮
punctuated: 不屈，伯不可得而復也。中立而依違於晉楚之間者，鄭也；鄭不從，伯亦不可得而復也。人皆曰：「蠢爾之荆，可以力制。」悼則不任力而任謀焉。息民取之魏絳，善陣聽于知罃，施舍輸積，導利而民悅矣；减牲更幣，制度而財節矣；三分四軍，不戰而氣自倍矣。羣策畢舉，而坐得勝筭。悼之所以駕楚者，豈徒以其力耶？人皆曰：「反覆之鄭，可以威懾。」悼則不用威而用誠焉。許伯騽而不拒，信子展而不疑，禮囚歸俘，無係累之慘矣；納候禁侵，無猜暴之患矣；遣使脩告，咸喻乎諸侯之志矣。推心置腹，而携貳獻誠。悼之所以服鄭者，豈徒以其威耶？由是楚雖強也，悼之謀足以制之。三駕罷兵之後，爭鄭之心頓沮，雖以良霄之告絕，而僅執使泄忿焉。蓋雖欲抗晉，而不能抗晉之謀也。使暴骨以逞，則楚勝而晉亦病矣。况兩廣爭雄，固楚之長技也，又豈遽出晉人下哉？由是鄭雖貳也，悼之誠足以孚之。東門觀兵之後，從晉之念遂堅，至于楚虔之會申，而始獻禮
translation_en:
…unless it was subdued, hegemony could not be restored. The state that stood between Jin and Chu, wavering in its allegiance, was Zheng; unless Zheng submitted, hegemony likewise could not be restored. Everyone said, “That unruly Jing can be controlled by force.” Duke Dao, however, relied on strategy rather than force. For giving the people respite, he adopted Wei Jiang’s advice; for skillful military dispositions, he listened to Zhi Ying. He dispensed relief and transported accumulated stores, promoting the people’s welfare so that they were content. He reduced sacrificial animals and revised ceremonial gifts, regulating expenditure so that resources were conserved. He divided the four armies into three contingents, doubling their vigor without battle. With all these plans put into effect, he secured the means of victory with ease. Was it merely through force that Duke Dao mastered Chu?

Everyone said, “Fickle Zheng can be overawed by might.” Duke Dao, however, used sincerity rather than intimidation. He assented to Bo Xi’s request [?] without rejecting it and trusted Zizhan without suspicion. He treated prisoners courteously and returned captives, ending the misery of confinement and bonds. He admitted scouts [?] and prohibited incursions, removing the troubles of suspicion and violence. He dispatched envoys to convey formal communications, making the intentions of the feudal lords fully understood. He opened his heart to others, and those whose allegiance had wavered offered their sincere loyalty. Was it merely through intimidation that Duke Dao won Zheng’s submission?

Thus, although Chu was strong, Duke Dao’s strategy sufficed to control it. After the three campaigns ended and the troops stood down, Chu’s resolve to contest possession of Zheng abruptly collapsed. Even when Liang Xiao announced the severance of relations, Chu merely detained the envoy to vent its anger. For although it wished to resist Jin, it could not counter Jin’s strategy. Had Duke Dao sought satisfaction through warfare that left soldiers’ bones exposed, even if Chu had been defeated, Jin too would have been exhausted. Moreover, contending for supremacy with its two chariot divisions was precisely Chu’s particular strength: how could it readily have proved inferior to Jin?

Thus, although Zheng wavered in its allegiance, Duke Dao’s sincerity sufficed to win its trust. After the display of troops at the eastern gate, its resolve to follow Jin became firm. Only when Qian of Chu convened the assembly at Shen did Zheng begin to present ceremonial gifts…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
從事焉蓋雖欲叛晉而不忍叛晉之誠也使強
之以威則鄭服而晉亦勞矣況二境玉帛固鄭
之故智也又豈終在晉宇下哉吁駕楚以謀制
人而不制于人也服鄭以誠信人而人亦信之
也此晉悼伯事之善所以克復文襄之烈而蕭
魚之會春秋特書以美之歟抑蕭魚之功美矣
所以處美者未盡也懿親之鄭撫而有之可也
女樂之賂奚納焉楚旣服矣焉用勤諸侯以謀
吳豈其侈心之萌不能自制而魏知諸臣猶有
===
遺策乎雖然晉伯復興楚氛未燄以平昭之庸
猶為諸侯師則以悼之餘烈在也悼其可少乎
哉
禮記
其功大者其樂備其治辯者其禮具
姚士觀
同考試官教諭李批分別功治俱有條理是嘗
究心於制作之原者
考試官教諭何批體貼象成飾治處詞理蔚
punctuated:
從事焉，蓋雖欲叛晉，而不忍叛晉之誠也。使強之以威，則鄭服而晉亦勞矣。況二境玉帛，固鄭之故智也，又豈終在晉宇下哉？吁！駕楚以謀，制人而不制于人也；服鄭以誠，信人而人亦信之也。此晉悼伯事之善，所以克復文襄之烈，而蕭魚之會，《春秋》特書以美之歟？抑蕭魚之功美矣，所以處美者未盡也。懿親之鄭，撫而有之可也，女樂之賂奚納焉？楚旣服矣，焉用勤諸侯以謀吳？豈其侈心之萌不能自制，而魏知諸臣猶有遺策乎？雖然，晉伯復興，楚氛未燄，以平昭之庸，猶為諸侯師，則以悼之餘烈在也。悼其可少乎哉！
禮記
其功大者，其樂備；其治辯者，其禮具。
姚士觀
同考試官教諭李批：分別功治，俱有條理，是嘗究心於制作之原者。
考試官教諭何批：體貼象成飾治處，詞理蔚
translation_en:
…and took part in its affairs. Even if Zheng wished to rebel against Jin, it could not bear to betray Jin’s sincerity. Had Jin compelled it through force, Zheng would have submitted, but Jin too would have exhausted itself. Moreover, presenting jade and silk to both neighboring powers was Zheng’s familiar stratagem: how could it have remained forever under Jin’s dominion? Ah! By mastering Chu through strategy, Duke Dao of Jin controlled others without being controlled by them; by winning Zheng through sincerity, he trusted others and was trusted in return. Such was Duke Dao’s excellence in the conduct of the hegemony. Was this not why he could restore the achievements of Dukes Wen and Xiang, and why the Spring and Autumn Annals specially recorded the meeting at Xiaoyu to praise it?
Yet, admirable as the achievement at Xiaoyu was, his handling of that success was not wholly satisfactory. It was proper to cherish Zheng, a closely related state, and retain its allegiance; why accept its gift of female musicians? Once Chu had submitted, why trouble the feudal lords with plans concerning Wu? Could it be that he could not restrain his burgeoning extravagance, and that ministers such as Wei and Zhi still left some counsels unoffered? Nevertheless, Jin’s hegemony revived, and Chu’s threatening influence did not blaze up. Even with the mediocrity of Dukes Ping and Zhao, Jin still led the feudal lords, because Duke Dao’s enduring achievements remained. Could Duke Dao’s contribution possibly be slighted?
Record of Rites
“He whose achievements are great has music complete in all its forms; he whose government is well ordered has rites fully provided.”
Yao Shiguan
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “He distinguishes achievements from government, treating both in an orderly manner. This is someone who has carefully investigated the origins of the establishment of rites and music.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “He closely grasps the points concerning representing accomplished achievements through music and embellishing government through rites; his language and reasoning are rich…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭錢〔終篇本之天德尤見卓識〕批〔發揮精到可以為文矣〕
論治功之盛者必極其制作之隆焉甚矣禮樂
非無因而作也功大治辯而制作其有不隆者
乎記樂記者其意蓋謂帝王之御世也固必有
禮樂以昭一代之制尤必因治功以為制作之
基是豈可以强為者哉彼樂作於功成之後則
樂者所以象此功也功有未大斯樂有未備矣
惟夫帝績所凝著地平天成之效王業所建極
===
===
民和物阜之徵此則無為而成凡天下之言功
者孰得而尚之可謂大矣由是而播之於樂也
吾見情深文明而諧之八音有以洩其雍容之
象德厚流光而奕之萬舞有以彰其揖遜之風
美善於是乎兼該也情文於是乎具舉也在王
者非有心於樂之備而豐功之洋溢自與天地
而同其和矣樂其有不備乎禮制於治定之餘
則禮者所以飾此治也治有未辯斯禮有未具
矣惟夫黎民敏德妙於變時雍之休四方從欲
punctuated:
考試官教諭錢〔終篇本之天德，尤見卓識〕批〔發揮精到，可以為文矣〕。

論治功之盛者，必極其制作之隆焉。甚矣，禮樂非無因而作也！功大治辯，而制作其有不隆者乎？記《樂記》者，其意蓋謂帝王之御世也，固必有禮樂以昭一代之制，尤必因治功以為制作之基，是豈可以强為者哉？彼樂作於功成之後，則樂者所以象此功也。功有未大，斯樂有未備矣。惟夫帝績所凝著，地平天成之效；王業所建極，民和物阜之徵。此則無為而成，凡天下之言功者，孰得而尚之？可謂大矣。由是而播之於樂也，吾見情深文明，而諧之八音，有以洩其雍容之象；德厚流光，而奕之萬舞，有以彰其揖遜之風。美善於是乎兼該也，情文於是乎具舉也。在王者，非有心於樂之備，而豐功之洋溢，自與天地而同其和矣。樂其有不備乎？禮制於治定之餘，則禮者所以飾此治也。治有未辯，斯禮有未具矣。惟夫黎民敏德，妙於變時雍之休；四方從欲
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔By grounding the conclusion in Heaven’s virtue, the essay displays particularly outstanding discernment.〕 〔Its exposition is incisive and thorough: this may indeed be called accomplished writing.〕

Whoever discusses the greatness of orderly government and achievement must fully explore the magnificence of the institutions they produce. How profoundly true it is that rites and music do not arise without a basis! When achievements are great and government well ordered, could the resulting institutions fail to flourish? The compiler of the Record of Music presumably meant that emperors and kings, in governing the world, certainly require rites and music to manifest the institutions of their age, but must above all take orderly government and achievement as the foundation for establishing those institutions. How could this be accomplished by force?

Music arises after achievements have been completed; thus music gives representational form to those achievements. If the achievements are not yet great, the music will not yet be complete. Consider imperial accomplishments crystallized in the effects of an earth brought to order and Heaven’s work fulfilled, and kingly undertakings brought to their highest point in the signs of a harmonious people and abundant things. These are accomplishments attained without contrived action. Of all the achievements spoken of under Heaven, what could surpass them? They may indeed be called great.

When these achievements are then expressed through music, I see profound feeling and radiant form harmonized through the eight classes of instruments, conveying an image of serene dignity; abundant virtue whose influence spreads far, splendidly displayed in the wan dance, manifesting a spirit of deference and yielding. Beauty and goodness are thus both embraced; inner feeling and outward form are thus both fully expressed. The king has no deliberate intention of making his music complete; rather, his abundant achievements overflow, naturally sharing in the harmony of Heaven and Earth. How could his music fail to be complete?

Rites are instituted after government has become settled; thus rites embellish that government. If government is not yet well ordered, rites will not yet be fully established. Consider the common people earnestly pursuing virtue, wondrously attaining the blessing of transformation and concord, and the people of the four quarters following their desires…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
丕協和熈皡之化此則垂拱而定凡天下之言
治者孰得而加之可謂辯矣由是而飾之以禮
也吾見緣情以作則而本末兼體有以昭秩敘
之常殊事以合敬而文質適均有以貫亨嘉之
會章程於是乎式全也經制於是乎大備也在
王者非有心於禮之具而至治之敷宣自與天
地而同其節矣禮其有不具乎吁樂備於功之
大則聞其樂而功之崇卑可知也禮具於治之
辯則見其禮而治之隆汙可知也記者以是而
===
論禮樂殆觀其深矣甞觀子夏之告文侯謂大
當而後制禮大定而後作樂則知古之帝王惟
其時位相符治功竝懋見之制作固粹然而無
議矣然有本之於身以妙制作之原而出於治
功之外者中正和樂是也天德也制作不本於
天德而徒曰治功焉抑末矣然則禮樂固因於
治功而天德尤其本也
天子者與天地參 劉良弼
punctuated:
丕協和熈皡之化，此則垂拱而定，凡天下之言治者，孰得而加之？可謂辯矣。由是而飾之以禮也，吾見緣情以作則，而本末兼體，有以昭秩敘之常；殊事以合敬，而文質適均，有以貫亨嘉之會。章程於是乎式全也，經制於是乎大備也。在王者非有心於禮之具，而至治之敷宣，自與天地而同其節矣。禮其有不具乎？吁！樂備於功之大，則聞其樂而功之崇卑可知也；禮具於治之辯，則見其禮而治之隆汙可知也。記者以是而論禮樂，殆觀其深矣。甞觀子夏之告文侯，謂大當而後制禮，大定而後作樂，則知古之帝王惟其時位相符，治功竝懋，見之制作，固粹然而無議矣。然有本之於身，以妙制作之原，而出於治功之外者，中正和樂是也，天德也。制作不本於天德，而徒曰治功焉，抑末矣。然則禮樂固因於治功，而天德尤其本也。

天子者與天地參。劉良弼。
translation_en:
…fully accord with the harmonizing, radiant transformation. This is order established with folded hands, without exertion. Of all those under Heaven who speak of governance, who could surpass it? It may indeed be called fully ordered. When this order is then adorned with ritual, I see standards fashioned in accordance with human feelings, embodying both root and ramifications, thereby manifesting the enduring principles of rank and precedence; distinct observances united in reverence, with refinement and substance aptly balanced, thereby bringing together all that is excellent in their harmonious convergence. Regulations are thus made complete, and institutions fully furnished. The king does not deliberately seek completeness in ritual; rather, the diffusion of perfect government naturally shares the measured order of Heaven and Earth. How could ritual fail to be complete?

Ah! Music reaches completeness through the greatness of achievement: hearing the music, one can judge whether the achievement is high or low. Ritual becomes fully furnished through the thorough ordering of government: seeing the ritual, one can judge whether government flourishes or declines. In discussing ritual and music on this basis, the author of the Record surely perceived their depths. I have read Zixia’s statement to Marquis Wen that ritual is instituted only after great propriety has been attained, and music composed only after great stability has been secured. Thus we know that the emperors and kings of antiquity, their times and positions corresponding and their government and achievements alike flourishing, manifested these in their institutions and compositions, which were indeed wholly pure and beyond reproach.

Yet there is something rooted in one’s own person that brings subtle perfection to the source of institutions and compositions, something beyond government and achievement: centrality, correctness, harmony, and joy. These are the virtues of Heaven. To establish institutions and compose music without grounding them in the virtues of Heaven, speaking merely of government and achievement, is surely to concern oneself with the secondary. Thus ritual and music certainly depend upon government and achievement, but the virtues of Heaven are their still more fundamental root.

“The Son of Heaven Forms a Triad with Heaven and Earth” — Liu Liangbi.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批詞典雅而意宏闊子之直善
發三才之蘊者
考試官教諭何批只就參字發揮而條理森
然自著殆非淺學所及可敬可敬
考試官教諭錢批理明詞暢
惟聖人在上而克配乎造化焉蓋法象莫大乎
天地也聖人在天子之位而有以參之其諸合
上下而一之者乎經解載夫子之言及此若曰
天子之與天地自其迹之殊者而擬之若不可
以比而爲一自其理之同者而觀之則實可以
參而爲三今夫君天下者曰天子聰明本於天
縱而正位凝命以膺帝眷之隆睿知由於夙成
而宅中圖大以建維皇之極夫固極天下之至
尊矣然何以能與天地參哉蓋以昊天其子端
拱以臨四方雖混然中處也而道萃貞元之會
自合上下以同流百辟其刑中正以觀天下固
巍然莫京也而首出民物之倫自與貞觀而相
準天位乎上以氣運地位乎下以形運天子位
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批：詞典雅而意宏闊，子之直善發三才之蘊者。
考試官教諭何批：只就參字發揮，而條理森然自著，殆非淺學所及，可敬，可敬！
考試官教諭錢批：理明詞暢。
惟聖人在上，而克配乎造化焉。蓋法象莫大乎天地也，聖人在天子之位而有以參之，其諸合上下而一之者乎？《經解》載夫子之言及此，若曰：天子之與天地，自其迹之殊者而擬之，若不可以比而爲一；自其理之同者而觀之，則實可以參而爲三。今夫君天下者曰天子，聰明本於天縱，而正位凝命，以膺帝眷之隆；睿知由於夙成，而宅中圖大，以建維皇之極。夫固極天下之至尊矣，然何以能與天地參哉？蓋以昊天其子，端拱以臨四方，雖混然中處也，而道萃貞元之會，自合上下以同流；百辟其刑，中正以觀天下，固巍然莫京也，而首出民物之倫，自與貞觀而相準。天位乎上，以氣運；地位乎下，以形運；天子位
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The diction is refined and the conception expansive. You truly excel at bringing out the profound significance of the Three Powers [?].”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The exposition concentrates solely on the word ‘participate,’ yet its orderly structure stands out clearly of itself. This is surely beyond the reach of shallow learning. Admirable, admirable!”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language flows freely.”
Only when a sage occupies the highest position can he match the creative workings of Heaven and Earth. For among the patterns to be emulated, none is greater than Heaven and Earth. When a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven and can participate alongside them, is he not one who joins what is above and below into a single whole? The “Explanation of the Classics” chapter records the Master's words on this subject, as if to say: if we compare the Son of Heaven with Heaven and Earth in terms of their differing manifestations, they seem incapable of being equated and made one; but if we consider the principles they share, they can indeed stand together as three.
