Now, he who rules all under Heaven is called the Son of Heaven. His perceptiveness originates in Heaven's endowment; he takes his rightful position and secures the Mandate, thereby receiving the abundant favor of the Supreme Sovereign. His sagely wisdom matures early; he dwells at the center and plans great undertakings, thereby establishing the august sovereign's supreme standard. He assuredly occupies the most exalted position in all the world. Yet how can he stand alongside Heaven and Earth?
It is because August Heaven regards him as its son. With hands folded in dignified repose, he presides over the four quarters. Although he rests at the center in undivided wholeness, the Way gathers in him at the conjunction of consummation and renewal, naturally uniting above and below in a common flow. The many lords take him as their model. Upright and balanced, he presents himself for all under Heaven to behold. He towers without equal, standing foremost among the ranks of people and things, and naturally accords with the constant pattern displayed by Heaven and Earth. Heaven occupies the position above and operates through vital force; Earth occupies the position below and operates through physical form; the Son of Heaven occupies the position…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎中而以化運立此參彼有以神夫協一之機
天確然以統元氣地隤然以統元形天子渾然
以統元化合異爲同有以極夫兼兩之妙人見
其撫萬邦而克艱以爲不若天地之無心也而
不知其參和不偏三才昭竝立之體所以爲天
地之宗子者此也人見其運萬幾而無斁以爲
不若天地之無憂也而不知其範圍不過三極
立大中之矩所以爲天下之至人者此也上律
下襲造化其爲徒焉蓋彼非有餘而此非不足
===
者矣兩儀攸分豈不與之異位而同神也哉仰
觀俯察天地其惟肖焉蓋彼非獨隆而此非獨
歉者矣乾坤奠位豈不與之異形而同體也哉
謂之曰與天地參信乎非天子不能同天地之
大而非天地不足以見天子之大矣觀天子者
盍亦求端於天地已乎抑論天子參天地非徒
以形象之合而已也要必有德爲之本焉克明
俊德顧諟明命聖人所以亹亹而不懈亦惟恃
此以求合於天地耳故格天之業至今誦之不
punctuated: 乎中而以化運，立此參彼，有以神夫協一之機。天確然以統元氣，地隤然以統元形，天子渾然以統元化，合異爲同，有以極夫兼兩之妙。人見其撫萬邦而克艱，以爲不若天地之無心也，而不知其參和不偏，三才昭竝立之體，所以爲天地之宗子者此也。人見其運萬幾而無斁，以爲不若天地之無憂也，而不知其範圍不過，三極立大中之矩，所以爲天下之至人者此也。上律下襲，造化其爲徒焉，蓋彼非有餘而此非不足者矣。兩儀攸分，豈不與之異位而同神也哉？仰觀俯察，天地其惟肖焉，蓋彼非獨隆而此非獨歉者矣。乾坤奠位，豈不與之異形而同體也哉？謂之曰與天地參，信乎非天子不能同天地之大，而非天地不足以見天子之大矣。觀天子者，盍亦求端於天地已乎？抑論天子參天地，非徒以形象之合而已也，要必有德爲之本焉。克明俊德，顧諟明命，聖人所以亹亹而不懈，亦惟恃此以求合於天地耳。故格天之業，至今誦之不
translation_en:
…in the center and operates through transforming influence. Established here as a third alongside those two, he gives wondrous efficacy to the workings of their harmonious unity. Heaven, firm and strong, governs primal vital energy; Earth, yielding and receptive, governs primal form; the Son of Heaven, in undivided wholeness, governs primal transformation. Bringing what differs into unity, he fully realizes the marvel of embracing both. People see him tending the myriad states and mastering difficulties, and think he falls short of Heaven and Earth in their freedom from deliberate intent. They do not understand that his participation in their harmony is impartial: the Three Powers display their standing together. This is what makes him the principal heir of Heaven and Earth. People see him managing the myriad affairs without weariness, and think he falls short of Heaven and Earth in their freedom from care. They do not understand that his all-embracing ordering never oversteps its bounds: the Three Ultimates establish the standard of the great mean. This is what makes him the consummate person of all under Heaven. Taking his rule from above and following what is below, he becomes a companion of the creative transformation of things. Those two have no surplus, nor does he have any deficiency. Though the Two Powers are divided, does he not occupy a different position while sharing their spiritual efficacy? Looking upward and examining below, he resembles Heaven and Earth. They alone are not exalted, nor is he alone deficient. With Heaven and Earth established in their places, does he not differ from them in form while sharing their essential constitution? Thus he is said to stand as a third alongside Heaven and Earth. Truly, none but the Son of Heaven can equal their greatness, and nothing short of Heaven and Earth can reveal his greatness. Should those who contemplate the Son of Heaven not also seek their starting point in Heaven and Earth?

Yet to speak of the Son of Heaven standing as a third alongside Heaven and Earth is not merely to speak of a correspondence in outward forms. Virtue must necessarily be its foundation. Making illustrious his outstanding virtue and keeping the luminous Mandate constantly in view: these alone sustain the sage in his unremitting diligence as he seeks accord with Heaven and Earth. Thus his achievements in reaching Heaven are praised to this day without…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
今不然而以滯諸其形象謂其有所合焉則上
下頓殊可得而參之乎是故有配天之業者必
有憲天之德而後可
第貳場
論
聖人與天地同體
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批洋洋千數言筆有根極
理要而無費詞非真有所得者不能及此允宜高薦
===
同考試官教諭何批理極精純詞復雅健
同考試官教諭黃批順理成文自然中度
考試官教諭何批文有氣魄有條理論之體
然可以式矣
考試官教諭錢批盡發天地聖人之蘊
論曰聖人者天地合德者也是故聖德之徵也
其體一天地而已而初非有心乎強合者矣夫
天下之理一誠盡之矣天地也聖人也未始有
異也夫惟其誠也未始有異是之謂合德者也
punctuated:
今不然，而以滯諸其形象，謂其有所合焉，則上下頓殊，可得而參之乎？是故有配天之業者，必有憲天之德而後可。

第貳場
論
聖人與天地同體
祝眉壽

同考試官教諭王批：洋洋千數言，筆有根極，理要而無費詞。非真有所得者不能及此，允宜高薦。
同考試官教諭何批：理極精純，詞復雅健。
同考試官教諭黃批：順理成文，自然中度。
考試官教諭何批：文有氣魄，有條理，論之體然，可以式矣。
考試官教諭錢批：盡發天地聖人之蘊。

論曰：聖人者，天地合德者也。是故聖德之徵也，其體一天地而已，而初非有心乎強合者矣。夫天下之理，一誠盡之矣。天地也，聖人也，未始有異也。夫惟其誠也未始有異，是之謂合德者也。
translation_en:
…Now, if instead one remains confined to their outward forms and claims that they coincide in some respect, then what is above and what is below are utterly distinct: how could one stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third? Thus, anyone whose achievements match Heaven must first possess the virtue of taking Heaven as his model.

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Forms One Body with Heaven and Earth”
Zhu Meishou

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “An expansive composition of more than a thousand words, with writing firmly rooted in fundamental principles. Its reasoning is essential and its wording free of waste. Only someone who has truly attained understanding could achieve this. It certainly merits recommendation for a high place.”

Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is exceptionally refined and pure; the language is also elegant and vigorous.”

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The composition follows the principles of its subject and naturally meets the proper standard.”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The writing has force and coherent organization. Such is the proper form of a discourse [?]; it can serve as a model.”

Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “It fully brings out the profound significance of Heaven, Earth, and the sage.”

The discourse reads: The sage is one whose virtue accords with that of Heaven and Earth. Thus, the manifestation of sagely virtue consists simply in forming one body with Heaven and Earth; from the outset, there is no deliberate attempt to force such an accord. The principles of all under Heaven are fully encompassed by sincerity alone. In this, Heaven and Earth and the sage have never differed. Precisely because their sincerity has never differed, they are said to accord in virtue.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
可謂聖人合德于天地而其德之徵于外也胡
可以異言乎哉是故發之高明高明一天也積
之博厚博厚一地也高厚又悠久者一天地之
無疆也其體之在聖人也即其在天地者也由
是而功化之隆凡所以覆載成物焉者悉于此
乎備焉體用一原上下同流其斯以為天地人
之至妙至妙者乎聖人抑何嘗有所容心也哉
嘗謂天位乎上也地位乎下也聖人混然中處
也殊形而異質其相去甚遠也而何以同其體
===
乎是蓋未知誠耳誠實理也合天地人而一之
者也非有二也玆天地之所以為天地而人之
所以為人者也使或在人者誠有未至斯與天
地不相似矣如是而欲與天地同體也得乎惟
聖人之德眞純無妄通乎天地而聖人又為天
地之所篤厚焉者聖人旣為天地之所篤厚而
聖德之純又通極于天地而無間則自能以一
身而立極于天下而天下之民物咸于是乎屬
望焉聖人亦自知其責之不容諉而天地之篤
punctuated: 可謂聖人合德于天地，而其德之徵于外也，胡可以異言乎哉？是故發之高明，高明一天也；積之博厚，博厚一地也；高厚又悠久者，一天地之無疆也。其體之在聖人也，即其在天地者也。由是而功化之隆，凡所以覆載成物焉者，悉于此乎備焉。體用一原，上下同流，其斯以為天地人之至妙至妙者乎？聖人抑何嘗有所容心也哉？嘗謂天位乎上也，地位乎下也，聖人混然中處也，殊形而異質，其相去甚遠也，而何以同其體乎？是蓋未知誠耳。誠，實理也，合天地人而一之者也，非有二也。玆天地之所以為天地，而人之所以為人者也。使或在人者誠有未至，斯與天地不相似矣。如是而欲與天地同體也，得乎？惟聖人之德眞純無妄，通乎天地，而聖人又為天地之所篤厚焉者。聖人旣為天地之所篤厚，而聖德之純又通極于天地而無間，則自能以一身而立極于天下，而天下之民物咸于是乎屬望焉。聖人亦自知其責之不容諉，而天地之篤
translation_en:
…It may be said that the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth. How, then, could the outward manifestations of his virtue be spoken of as different from theirs? Thus, when expressed in loftiness and brightness, it is one with Heaven; when accumulated in breadth and depth, it is one with Earth. Its loftiness and depth, together with its enduring constancy, are one with the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth. Its substance in the sage is precisely what it is in Heaven and Earth. Hence the greatness of his achievements and transforming influence: all that shelters, sustains, and brings things to completion is fully present here. Substance and function have one source; above and below share one flow. Is this not the most wondrous, most wondrous aspect of Heaven, Earth, and humanity? Yet when has the sage ever introduced any deliberate contrivance into it?

It has been said that Heaven occupies the place above, Earth the place below, and the sage dwells integrally between them. Distinct in form and different in constitution, they are very far apart. How, then, can they share the same substance? Such a question merely shows that sincerity has not yet been understood. Sincerity is real principle: it unites Heaven, Earth, and humanity as one, without duality. This is what makes Heaven and Earth Heaven and Earth, and human beings human. If sincerity in a person should fall short, that person would not resemble Heaven and Earth. Could one in such a condition wish to share their substance?

Only the sage’s virtue is truly pure and free of falsity, pervading Heaven and Earth; and the sage, in turn, receives Heaven and Earth’s abundant favor. Since he receives their abundant favor, and the purity of his sagely virtue reaches throughout Heaven and Earth without interruption, he can naturally, in his own person, establish the supreme standard for all under Heaven. The people and things of the world all look to him with expectation. The sage himself also knows that his responsibility cannot be evaded, and that Heaven and Earth’s abundant…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
厚乎我者非欲使之自有餘而已也而所以發
揮其事業丕闡其經綸以康濟乎天下是皆于
其德之徵者取足焉固非有待于其外而功化
之所由基駿業之所由成者胥此也寧不與天
地而並運而有非形之所可拘質之所能限者
乎先儒推究聖人功用之所自而必于其德之
徵者曰與天地同體信乎其體之同也而形之
殊質之異不與焉何也今夫天司覆者也覆物
其用也而陰陽成象四時以為柄日星以為紀
===
雨露以為澤雷霆以為威必有高明者為之體
也今夫地司載者也載物其用也而剛柔成質
山川之流峙草木之夭喬鳥獸之飛走鱗介之
潛藏必有博厚者為之體也天地以生物為心
而成物其用也至健而不息永貞而有常寒暑
晝夜之變易歲月日時之推行元會運世之循
環而又有悠久者為之體也此造化之妙而莫
非一誠之所為也聖人于此以一人之身參兩
于天地而為民物之主履之為達德措之為達
punctuated: 厚乎我者，非欲使之自有餘而已也。而所以發揮其事業，丕闡其經綸，以康濟乎天下，是皆于其德之徵者取足焉，固非有待于其外。而功化之所由基、駿業之所由成者，胥此也。寧不與天地而並運，而有非形之所可拘、質之所能限者乎？先儒推究聖人功用之所自，而必于其德之徵者曰：「與天地同體。」信乎其體之同也，而形之殊、質之異不與焉。何也？今夫天，司覆者也；覆物，其用也。而陰陽成象，四時以為柄，日星以為紀，雨露以為澤，雷霆以為威，必有高明者為之體也。今夫地，司載者也；載物，其用也。而剛柔成質，山川之流峙，草木之夭喬，鳥獸之飛走，鱗介之潛藏，必有博厚者為之體也。天地以生物為心，而成物其用也。至健而不息，永貞而有常，寒暑晝夜之變易，歲月日時之推行，元會運世之循環，而又有悠久者為之體也。此造化之妙，而莫非一誠之所為也。聖人于此，以一人之身，參兩于天地，而為民物之主。履之為達德，措之為達
translation_en:
…the generous favor that Heaven and Earth bestow upon me is not intended merely to leave me personally with an abundance. Rather, everything by which the sage develops his undertakings, greatly unfolds his ordering of affairs, and brings peace and succor to all under Heaven finds sufficient resources in the manifestations of his virtue. He certainly need not look outside it. The foundations of his achievements and transforming influence, and the accomplishment of his great undertakings, all derive from this. How could he fail to operate together with Heaven and Earth, possessing something that physical form cannot confine and material constitution cannot limit? Earlier Confucian scholars investigated the source of the sage’s efficacy and, grounding their judgment in the manifestations of his virtue, said: “He shares one substance with Heaven and Earth.” Truly, their substance is the same; differences of physical form and material constitution have no bearing on this. Why is that?

Heaven is responsible for covering things; covering things is its function. Yin and yang produce celestial configurations; the four seasons serve as its means of governance, the sun and stars as its ordering markers, rain and dew as its beneficence, and thunder as its awe-inspiring power. There must be height and brightness to constitute its substance. Earth is responsible for supporting things; supporting things is its function. The hard and the soft form material substance; mountains rise and rivers flow, grasses and trees grow tender or tall, birds fly and beasts run, and scaled and shelled creatures conceal themselves below. There must be breadth and depth to constitute its substance.

Heaven and Earth take the generation of things as their heart, and bringing things to completion is their function. Supremely vigorous, they never cease; enduringly steadfast, they maintain constancy. Cold and heat, day and night alternate; years, months, days, and hours advance; the cosmic periods of yuan, hui, yun, and shi revolve in cycles. There must also be enduring continuity to constitute their substance. Such is the subtle working of creation and transformation, and none of it is other than the work of a single sincerity. Here the sage, in his individual person, joins Heaven and Earth as a third and becomes the ruler of people and things. Practiced in his conduct, this becomes universally applicable virtue; put into effect, it becomes the universally applicable…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
道普之爲九經垂之爲三重散之而爲三千三
百錯之而爲容爲執爲敬爲别形之而爲著爲
明爲動爲變徵諸庶民刑之百辟致中和贊化
育久道成化而天下之物無不覆焉無不載焉
又無不成焉是亦天地之覆物載物而物被常
覆常載者也人將曰聖人之曲成天下功業如
此其隆也而不知此特用之及于物者耳而要
其所以然是必有體以運行于其間可以配諸
天地之體相與脗合而不悖而後其用爲不窮
===
是故德之徵而爲高也明也高明固聖人所以
覆物之體也而其峻極莫踰掀揭莫掩四時循
其序也日月貞其明也雨風露雷順其化也有
以配天之高明不與天同體乎德之徵而爲博
也厚也博厚固聖人所以載物之體也而其周
遍無遺漸漬無間流峙者奠其位也夭喬者若
其性也飛走生息者順其天也有以配地之博
厚不與地同體乎德之徵而爲悠也久也悠久
固聖人所以成物之體也而其高明不可極這
punctuated:
道，普之爲九經，垂之爲三重，散之而爲三千三百，錯之而爲容、爲執、爲敬、爲别，形之而爲著、爲明、爲動、爲變。徵諸庶民，刑之百辟，致中和，贊化育，久道成化，而天下之物無不覆焉，無不載焉，又無不成焉。是亦天地之覆物載物，而物被常覆常載者也。人將曰：「聖人之曲成天下，功業如此其隆也！」而不知此特用之及于物者耳。而要其所以然，是必有體以運行于其間，可以配諸天地之體，相與脗合而不悖，而後其用爲不窮。

是故德之徵而爲高也、明也，高明固聖人所以覆物之體也。而其峻極莫踰，掀揭莫掩，四時循其序也，日月貞其明也，雨風露雷順其化也，有以配天之高明，不與天同體乎？德之徵而爲博也、厚也，博厚固聖人所以載物之體也。而其周遍無遺，漸漬無間，流峙者奠其位也，夭喬者若其性也，飛走生息者順其天也，有以配地之博厚，不與地同體乎？德之徵而爲悠也、久也，悠久固聖人所以成物之體也。而其高明不可極，這
translation_en:
…ways universally followed. Extended broadly, it becomes the nine guiding principles; handed down, it becomes the three weighty institutions. Elaborated in detail, it becomes the three thousand and three hundred rules of ritual. Applied in their various settings, these become proper bearing, the holding of objects, reverence, and distinctions; manifested outwardly, it becomes conspicuous, becomes clear, moves others, and transforms them. Verified among the common people and taken as a model by the many lords, it brings equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization and assists the transforming and nurturing processes of Heaven and Earth. By enduring in its Way, it accomplishes transformation: nothing under Heaven is left unsheltered, unsupported, or unfulfilled. This too is like Heaven and Earth sheltering and supporting things, which receive their constant shelter and support. People will say, “How exalted are the sage’s achievements in bringing everything under Heaven to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances!” Yet they do not understand that this is merely his functioning as it reaches things. To grasp why it is so, there must be an underlying substance operating within it, capable of matching the substance of Heaven and Earth, agreeing with it without contradiction. Only then can its functioning be inexhaustible.

Thus, when virtue manifests itself as loftiness and brightness, this loftiness and brightness are precisely the substance through which the sage shelters things. Its towering height cannot be surpassed; its brilliance cannot be obscured. The four seasons follow their sequence, the sun and moon remain constant in their light, and rain, wind, dew, and thunder accord with its transforming influence. Since it can match Heaven’s loftiness and brightness, does it not share Heaven’s substance? When virtue manifests itself as breadth and depth, this breadth and depth are precisely the substance through which the sage supports things. It extends everywhere without omission and permeates everything without interruption. Flowing waters and standing mountains settle into their places; tender plants and tall trees accord with their natures; creatures that fly, run, live, and propagate follow their Heaven-given dispositions. Since it can match Earth’s breadth and depth, does it not share Earth’s substance? When virtue manifests itself as enduring continuity, this enduring continuity is precisely the substance through which the sage brings things to fulfillment. Its loftiness and brightness cannot be fathomed, [the following character, 這, is doubtful: ?]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
厚不可窮變易者不能間也推行者不能已也
循環者不能盡也有以同天地之無疆不與天
地同體乎惟其體之同是以用之同而聖人功
業之隆于是卓乎其不可及也已然豈聖人有
心于臆度而強制以求其必合也哉蓋不同之
以形而同之以理不同之以質而同之以神其
在聖人也非有小于天地而其在天地也非有
加于聖人謂天地爲聖人可也謂聖人爲天地
亦可也夫何形之所可拘而質之所能限耶噫
===
同體之義深乎雖然聖人非特與天地同體而
實有功于天地者也蓋語高明者惟天而非聖
人以參賛之則高明無以成其運語博厚者惟
地而非聖人以參賛之則博厚無以成其功語
悠久者惟天地而非聖人以默成之則悠久無
以成其化是故曆象授時璿璣齊政聖人之所
以經天也莫非成天之體也畫井分州封山濬
川聖人之所以緯地也莫非成地之體也上律
下襲仰觀俯察聖人所以彌綸天地之道也莫
punctuated:
厚不可窮，變易者不能間也，推行者不能已也，循環者不能盡也。有以同天地之無疆，不與天地同體乎？惟其體之同，是以用之同，而聖人功業之隆，于是卓乎其不可及也已。然豈聖人有心于臆度而強制，以求其必合也哉？蓋不同之以形，而同之以理；不同之以質，而同之以神。其在聖人也，非有小于天地；而其在天地也，非有加于聖人。謂天地爲聖人可也，謂聖人爲天地亦可也。夫何形之所可拘，而質之所能限耶？噫！同體之義深乎！
雖然，聖人非特與天地同體，而實有功于天地者也。蓋語高明者惟天，而非聖人以參賛之，則高明無以成其運；語博厚者惟地，而非聖人以參賛之，則博厚無以成其功；語悠久者惟天地，而非聖人以默成之，則悠久無以成其化。是故曆象授時，璿璣齊政，聖人之所以經天也，莫非成天之體也；畫井分州，封山濬川，聖人之所以緯地也，莫非成地之體也；上律下襲，仰觀俯察，聖人所以彌綸天地之道也，莫
translation_en:
…its depth cannot be exhausted. Change cannot interrupt it; its onward movement cannot cease; its cycles cannot be exhausted. Thus it shares the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth: does it not form one body with them? Precisely because they are one in substance, they are one in function, and so the grandeur of the sage’s achievements stands beyond all reach. Yet could the sage deliberately conjecture and impose constraints to compel this correspondence? Their unity lies not in physical form but in principle, not in material constitution but in spiritual efficacy. In the sage there is nothing less than Heaven and Earth; in Heaven and Earth there is nothing exceeding the sage. One may call Heaven and Earth the sage, and one may also call the sage Heaven and Earth. How could physical form constrain this, or material constitution limit it? Ah, how profound is the meaning of forming one body!
Nevertheless, the sage not only forms one body with Heaven and Earth but also contributes to their accomplishment. When we speak of height and brightness, these belong to Heaven alone; yet without the sage’s participation and assistance, this height and brightness could not accomplish their course. When we speak of breadth and depth, these belong to Earth alone; yet without the sage’s participation and assistance, this breadth and depth could not accomplish their work. When we speak of enduring constancy, this belongs to Heaven and Earth alone; yet without the sage silently bringing it to fulfillment, this enduring constancy could not accomplish its transforming work. Thus, calculating and observing celestial phenomena to impart the seasons, and using the jade celestial instrument to bring the celestial governors into accord, are the means by which the sage orders Heaven: all fulfill Heaven’s substance. Laying out well-fields and dividing the provinces, marking off mountains and dredging rivers are the means by which the sage orders Earth: all fulfill Earth’s substance. Taking what is above as the standard and following what is below, observing above and examining below, are the means by which the sage comprehensively encompasses the Way of Heaven and Earth: none…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
非成天地之體也天地無心聖人代之言天地
無爲聖人代之工天地聖人其相須以有成而
聖人尤天地之所以代終者乎然則未至于聖
者而脩焉以復其性精之于莫見莫顯約之于
不見不聞而必造于純亦不已之妙則不賞不
怒而天下以勸以威由是而天地位萬物育卿
雲見甘露降河出圖洛出書山出器車麒麟遊
郊藪而四靈畢至以至于篤恭不顯之化又何
以異于天地哉是又聖脩之極也此中庸之所
===
爲作也是爲論
表
擬宋以文彦博富弼同中書門下平章事
謝表〔至和二年〕
廖如春
同考試官教諭胡 批 寫出二賢相翊輔之忱悃
然可讀
同考試官教諭項 批 贍而有體善用本色而
精渾無迹尤見工緻
punctuated:
非成天地之體也。天地無心，聖人代之言；天地無爲，聖人代之工。天地聖人，其相須以有成，而聖人尤天地之所以代終者乎？然則未至于聖者，而脩焉以復其性，精之于莫見莫顯，約之于不見不聞，而必造于純亦不已之妙，則不賞不怒，而天下以勸以威。由是而天地位，萬物育，卿雲見，甘露降，河出圖，洛出書，山出器車，麒麟遊郊藪，而四靈畢至。以至于篤恭不顯之化，又何以異于天地哉？是又聖脩之極也。此《中庸》之所爲作也。是爲論。

表

擬宋以文彦博、富弼同中書門下平章事謝表〔至和二年〕

廖如春

同考試官教諭胡批：寫出二賢相翊輔之忱，悃然可讀。

同考試官教諭項批：贍而有體，善用本色，而精渾無迹，尤見工緻。
translation_en:
…of completing the essential constitution of Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind; the sage speaks on their behalf. Heaven and Earth take no deliberate action; the sage performs their work. Heaven and Earth and the sage depend upon one another to bring things to completion. Is the sage not, above all, the means by which Heaven and Earth have their work carried through to its end?

Thus, those who have not yet attained sagehood cultivate themselves to recover their nature. They refine their cultivation in what is unseen and unmanifest, and concentrate it upon what is neither seen nor heard, necessarily reaching the wondrous state of purity that never ceases. Then, without rewards or anger, they inspire and awe all under Heaven. Through this, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things flourish. Auspicious clouds appear, sweet dew descends, the Yellow River brings forth the Chart, the Luo River brings forth the Writing, and mountains yield precious vessels and carriages. Qilin roam the outskirts and marshes, and all four numinous creatures arrive. When their transforming influence reaches the point of profound reverence without outward display, how does it differ from that of Heaven and Earth? This, too, is the ultimate attainment of sagely cultivation. This is why the Doctrine of the Mean was written. Thus concludes this discourse.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi as Grand Councilors (tong zhongshu menxia pingzhang shi). 〔Second year of Zhihe [1055]〕

By Liao Ruchun.

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the heartfelt devotion of the two worthy chief ministers in supporting their sovereign. Sincere and engaging to read.”

Associate Examiner Xiang, Instructor, comments: “Ample in expression and proper in form. It handles the natural style of the genre well, with refinement and wholeness that leave no trace of artifice; its craftsmanship and delicacy are especially evident.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭何批沖腴有味
考試官教諭錢批詞語蔚然四六之佳者
至和二年某月某日具官臣文彥博臣富
弼伏蒙
聖恩以臣等同中書門下平章事者
紫禁近中台星兩燦麗
天之曜
黃樞分上相德一慶遇
主之榮
===
綸綍同宣拜稽交讓仰
龍光之斯極顧蚊負以何勝臣彥博臣弼誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊惟中書掌奏漢
庭倣內史之遺門下分曹唐室有左省之
號品秩竝崇宰路政事咸共平章義本虞
書制詳舊史命名肇於貞觀加禮耆勳入
銜始自永淳相因後代於昭
皇宋益簡臣鄰雖中書爲右未遑與門下省而
對移然任官維賢則必得讀書人而後用
punctuated:
考試官教諭何批：沖腴有味。
考試官教諭錢批：詞語蔚然，四六之佳者。
至和二年某月某日，具官臣文彥博、臣富弼伏蒙聖恩，以臣等同中書門下平章事者。
紫禁近中，台星兩燦，麗天之曜；黃樞分上，相德一慶，遇主之榮。綸綍同宣，拜稽交讓。仰龍光之斯極，顧蚊負以何勝！臣彥博、臣弼誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟中書掌奏，漢庭倣內史之遺；門下分曹，唐室有左省之號。品秩竝崇宰路，政事咸共平章。義本虞書，制詳舊史。命名肇於貞觀，加禮耆勳；入銜始自永淳，相因後代。於昭皇宋，益簡臣鄰。雖中書爲右，未遑與門下省而對移；然任官維賢，則必得讀書人而後用。
translation_en:
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Subtle and rich, with lingering savor.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “The language is luxuriant—a fine example of four-and-six parallel prose.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the second year of Zhihe, your servants Wen Yanbo and Fu Bi, holding their respective official titles, have reverently received your sagely favor appointing us Joint Managers of Affairs with the Secretariat–Chancellery.
Close to the center of the Purple Forbidden Precinct, two ministerial stars shine brightly, adorning the heavens with their radiance; sharing the highest ministerial station at the imperial pivot, we rejoice together in the virtue expected of chief councillors [?] and in the honor of finding a sovereign who appreciates us. The imperial commands have been proclaimed to us together; bowing and prostrating ourselves, each yields precedence to the other. We look up to this utmost imperial glory, yet wonder how our strength, like that of a mosquito bearing a burden, could sustain it! Your servants Yanbo and Bi, in profound fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit:
We humbly consider that the Secretariat, responsible for memorials, followed at the Han court the legacy of the Metropolitan Governor; the Chancellery, with its separate offices, bore in the Tang the designation “Left Department.” Both enjoyed exalted rank among the chief councillors, jointly deliberating upon affairs of government. The meaning of “equitable deliberation” derives from the Documents of Yu; the institutional arrangements are detailed in the old histories. The designation originated in the Zhenguan reign, bestowing additional honor upon aged, meritorious officials; its incorporation into official titles began in the Yongchun reign and was followed by later dynasties. Under our illustrious imperial Song, still greater care is taken in selecting the sovereign’s close ministers. Although the Secretariat holds precedence and there has been no occasion for a reciprocal exchange of position with the Chancellery [?], appointment to office rests upon worthiness: men of learning must be found before they are employed…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰普曰質協恭
開寶之隆如李如張並受
咸平之命遠惟旦準爲烈近之韓范可稱必
求異能方堪峻陟知人由於
堯哲才則甚難建典法於周官員不必備詎期
葑菲濫預鈞衡玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
德協舜華
志恢禹績
===
問學日就
恭儉天成
無逸書屛儼若羹墻之見
籍田撰記深惟稼穡之艱犀
出通天羊
存中夜
經營西北期清幽夏之塵
頒賜學庸獨舉聖賢之要
開天章而入對臺諫并用乎四賢
punctuated: 曰普曰質，協恭開寶之隆；如李如張，並受咸平之命。遠惟旦準爲烈，近之韓范可稱。必求異能，方堪峻陟。知人由於堯哲，才則甚難；建典法於周官，員不必備。詎期葑菲，濫預鈞衡。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，德協舜華，志恢禹績，問學日就，恭儉天成。無逸書屛，儼若羹墻之見；籍田撰記，深惟稼穡之艱。犀出通天，羊存中夜。經營西北，期清幽夏之塵；頒賜學庸，獨舉聖賢之要。開天章而入對，臺諫并用乎四賢；
translation_en:
…Those called Pu and Zhi served together with reverent accord during the flourishing Kaibao reign; men such as Li and Zhang alike received appointments in the Xianping reign. Among earlier men, Dan and Zhun had distinguished achievements; among more recent men, Han and Fan deserve praise. Only exceptional ability warrants elevation to high office. Recognizing men requires Yao’s wisdom, yet talent is exceedingly hard to find; the Offices of Zhou established the institutional rule that offices need not all be filled. How could we, worthless as turnip and radish greens, have expected to be admitted undeservedly to the highest councils?

This is surely because we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇: your virtue matches Shun’s brilliance, and your ambition extends Yu’s achievements. Your inquiry and learning advance daily; your reverence and frugality are innate. With “Against Luxurious Ease” inscribed upon a screen, you seem to behold the ancient sages in your soup and upon your walls. In composing a record of the imperial ploughing field, you reflected deeply upon the hardships of sowing and reaping. The “Heaven-reaching” rhinoceros horn was brought forth [?]; sheep were spared at midnight [?]. You direct affairs in the northwest, hoping to clear away the dust of conflict in You and Xia. By bestowing the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, you single out the essentials of the sages and worthies. You opened the Tianzhang Pavilion to receive answers in audience, employing the four worthies together in the censorial and remonstrance offices; …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
宴秘省而賦詩喜起重賡於千載
數行錄繫
屢詔蠲租
露禱禁庭精回雲漢
躬臨孔廟光賁人文
禮備樂和
仁昭義立財不蓄而
國富兵不試而威張
澤溢窮荒
===
馨升
玄昊保章奏
含譽之見義掃攙搶瑞芝産
化成之楹品高連理合肥之稻再實周潁偕
榮異域之象交陳軒麟竝集
光昭
一祖
二宗之統釀成斗米十錢之休
治巳垂裳
punctuated: 宴秘省而賦詩，喜起重賡於千載。數行錄繫，屢詔蠲租。露禱禁庭，精回雲漢；躬臨孔廟，光賁人文。禮備樂和，仁昭義立，財不蓄而國富，兵不試而威張。澤溢窮荒，馨升玄昊。保章奏含譽之見，義掃攙搶；瑞芝産化成之楹，品高連理。合肥之稻再實，周潁偕榮；異域之象交陳，軒麟竝集。光昭一祖二宗之統，釀成斗米十錢之休。治巳垂裳。
translation_en:
…At banquets in the Palace Library, he composed poems, renewing after a thousand years the responsive songs of ruler and ministers rejoicing and rising to their tasks. He repeatedly ordered reviews of prisoners’ cases and frequently decreed remission of land taxes. Praying beneath the open sky within the palace precincts, his sincerity turned back the drought. Visiting the temple of Confucius in person, he shed lustre upon civilized learning. Ritual was complete and music harmonious; benevolence shone forth and righteousness was established. Wealth was not hoarded, yet the state prospered; arms were not put to the test, yet its might spread. His beneficence overflowed to the remotest wilds, and its fragrance rose to high Heaven.

The Astronomer reported the appearance of the Hanyu auspicious star; righteousness swept away the baleful comet [?]. Auspicious fungi grew on the pillars of Huacheng, ranking above trees with intertwined branches. Rice at Hefei ripened twice, while Zhou and Ying flourished together [?]. Elephants from foreign lands were presented in succession, and qilin gathered together. He gloriously illuminated the succession of the one founding ancestor and the two ancestral sovereigns, bringing about the blessing of rice costing ten cash a peck. His government had already attained the ease of ruling with robes hanging down…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
心猶考相崇資顯秩當求有用之才
盛世昌辰尤急可觀之效仰荷
陶鈞之竝覆遂使韈線之兼容
渥殊禮於郊迎
賢人情於夢卜
恩超象審誦說命以凜如質匪鷹揚捧丹書而
惕若伏念臣彥博臣弼汾陽布素蚤叨進
士之科洛水章縫偶與茂才之選異人國
士抑聲聞之過情陳力匡時蓋朴忠而自
===
許具劉平之案仰體
欽恤之衷却元昊之書爰正
朝廷之體行鐵錢平市價敢云臨事有方糾
僞牒繳詞頭竊慕直言不隱督師河北竟
出軍候之謀奉使契丹徒爭獻納之字薦
賢麤知爲
國救荒匪以要名置散投閒終懷犬馬之戀
匿瑕舍垢猥蒙
天地之全一朝
punctuated: 心猶考相。崇資顯秩，當求有用之才；盛世昌辰，尤急可觀之效。仰荷陶鈞之竝覆，遂使韈線之兼容。渥殊禮於郊迎，賢人情於夢卜。恩超象審，誦《說命》以凜如；質匪鷹揚，捧《丹書》而惕若。伏念臣彥博、臣弼，汾陽布素，蚤叨進士之科；洛水章縫，偶與茂才之選。異人國士，抑聲聞之過情；陳力匡時，蓋朴忠而自許。具劉平之案，仰體欽恤之衷；却元昊之書，爰正朝廷之體。行鐵錢，平市價，敢云臨事有方；糾僞牒，繳詞頭，竊慕直言不隱。督師河北，竟出軍候之謀；奉使契丹，徒爭獻納之字。薦賢麤知爲國，救荒匪以要名。置散投閒，終懷犬馬之戀；匿瑕舍垢，猥蒙天地之全。一朝
translation_en:
…Your mind still attends to choosing chief councillors. For lofty rank and illustrious office, men of practical ability must be sought; in a flourishing age and prosperous times, demonstrable achievements are especially urgent. We reverently receive the encompassing care of Your Majesty’s shaping power, which makes room even for contributions as slight as thread for stockings. You lavish exceptional courtesies upon those welcomed in the suburbs, and show your feeling for worthy men through dreams and divination [?]. Your favor surpasses the search by a likeness: we recite the Charge to Yue with awe. Though we lack the mettle of the eagle soaring aloft, we hold the Cinnabar Book with trembling reverence.
We humbly reflect that your servants Yanbo and Bi were, respectively, a commoner of Fenyang who early received the unmerited distinction of attaining the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) degree, and a scholar in Confucian dress from the Luo River who happened to be selected in the examination for outstanding talent. To call us extraordinary men or outstanding servants of the state is surely to let reputation exceed reality; yet we have presumed to possess an honest loyalty with which to devote our abilities to setting the age right.
In setting out the case of Liu Ping, we reverently embodied Your Majesty’s concern for care and compassion in punishment; in rejecting Yuanhao’s letter, we upheld the dignity of the court. In putting iron currency into circulation and stabilizing market prices, how could we claim to have handled affairs with skill? In exposing fraudulent documents and returning draft instructions for imperial pronouncements, we privately aspired to speak frankly and conceal nothing. While supervising the army in Hebei, we ultimately devised a plan involving military scouts [?]; while serving as envoy to the Khitan, we merely disputed the wording of “presenting” and “delivering.” In recommending worthy men, we had some rough understanding of serving the state; in relieving famine, we did not seek fame. Assigned to inactive posts and cast into idleness, we nevertheless retained the devotion of dogs and horses. Your Majesty concealed our faults and overlooked our blemishes, graciously granting us the preservation afforded by Heaven and Earth. Then one day…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
召還同目
褒擢喜接夔龍之武共虎對揚勉圖益稷之
謨咸駿奔走匪石不二斷金與齊屹立
朝端益養折衝之重恪守前志渾忘顧慮之
私則知印押班不徒旅進旅退而獻善宣
美庶能爲德爲民竭此共濟之猷副彼僉
諧之望伏願
人惟求舊率由慶曆之朋
念不遺遐誕布至和之化
===
階平衡正海晏河清
如月如日如南山保萬年之家室
多富多壽多男子綿百世之本支臣彥博臣
弼無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated:
召還，同目褒擢，喜接夔龍之武；共虎對揚，勉圖益稷之謨，咸駿奔走。匪石不二，斷金與齊。屹立朝端，益養折衝之重；恪守前志，渾忘顧慮之私。則知印押班，不徒旅進旅退；而獻善宣美，庶能爲德爲民。竭此共濟之猷，副彼僉諧之望。
伏願人惟求舊，率由慶曆之朋；念不遺遐，誕布至和之化。階平衡正，海晏河清。如月如日，如南山，保萬年之家室；多富多壽多男子，綿百世之本支。臣彥博、臣弼無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…recalled to court and together accorded commendation and promotion [?], we rejoice to follow in the footsteps of Kui and Long. Together we reverently respond to and proclaim your commands [?], striving to devise plans like those of Yi and Ji, all hastening diligently to serve. Our hearts, unlike stones that can be turned, remain undivided; our concord equals that which can cut through metal. Standing firm at the head of the court, we shall further cultivate the authority that repels aggression; steadfastly observing our former resolve, we shall wholly forget private misgivings. Thus, in overseeing seals and directing court ranks [?], we shall do more than merely advance and retire with the assembled officials. By presenting worthy counsel and proclaiming your excellence, we hope to serve virtue and the people. We shall exhaust our plans for working together to meet the hopes expressed in the unanimous agreement upon our appointment.
We humbly pray that, in seeking men, you will favor those long tried, following the example of the fellowship of the Qingli era; and that your care will overlook none, however distant, spreading far and wide the transforming influence of the Zhihe era. May the celestial Steps be level and the Balance upright; may the seas be calm and the Yellow River clear. Like the moon, like the sun, like the Southern Mountain, may your imperial house endure for ten thousand years. With abundant wealth, long life, and many sons, may its main line and collateral branches continue for a hundred generations. Your servants Yanbo and Bi, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain our intense emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to convey our thanks to your hearing.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策五道
第一問
祝眉壽
同考試官教諭王批洪範傳心之要至我
聖祖
皇上而以明以行所謂心同道同者子能悉之可謂善觀
聖人之深者矣敬服敬服
同考試官教諭何批輪換鋪叙具有源委足錄以式
同考試官教諭黃批敷對詳明摛詞溫雅千兵
善鳴者耶
考試官教諭何批頌述文典重溫潤可謂得體
考試官教諭錢批淵博懇亮足占所養
===
帝王有建極之盛德而後能斂天下之福
斂天下之福者克享天心者也帝王有敷
極之宏猷而後能錫天下以福錫天下以
福者善體天心者也何也蓋大君者天地
之宗子也惟德動天惟天眷德故建極而
punctuated:
第叄場
策五道
第一問
祝眉壽

同考試官教諭王批：洪範傳心之要，至我聖祖皇上而以明以行。所謂心同道同者，子能悉之，可謂善觀聖人之深者矣。敬服！敬服！
同考試官教諭何批：輪換鋪叙，具有源委，足錄以式。
同考試官教諭黃批：敷對詳明，摛詞溫雅，千兵善鳴者耶？
考試官教諭何批：頌述文典重溫潤，可謂得體。
考試官教諭錢批：淵博懇亮，足占所養。

帝王有建極之盛德，而後能斂天下之福。斂天下之福者，克享天心者也。帝王有敷極之宏猷，而後能錫天下以福。錫天下以福者，善體天心者也。何也？蓋大君者，天地之宗子也。惟德動天，惟天眷德，故建極而
translation_en:
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Zhu Meishou

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The essentials of transmitting the mind in the Great Plan were illuminated and put into practice by our Sagely Founder and His Majesty. You fully comprehend what is meant by their sharing the same mind and the same Way; you may indeed be said to discern well the profundity of the sages. I admire this most respectfully! Most respectfully!”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “The exposition proceeds through successive turns, fully setting out origins and ramifications. It deserves to be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The response is detailed and clear, its language gentle and elegant. Is this one who sounds forth well among a thousand soldiers [?]?”

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: “The writing in praise and narration is classical, dignified, warm, and polished. It may be said to suit the occasion.”

Comment by Examiner Qian, Instructor: “Erudite, earnest, and sincere: it sufficiently reveals the author’s cultivation.”

Only when emperors and kings possess the abundant virtue needed to establish the supreme standard can they gather to themselves the blessings of all under Heaven. Those who gather the blessings of all under Heaven are those capable of enjoying Heaven’s favor. Only when emperors and kings possess the grand designs needed to extend the supreme standard can they bestow blessings upon all under Heaven. Those who bestow blessings upon all under Heaven are those who fittingly embody Heaven’s intentions. Why is this? The sovereign is the principal heir of Heaven and Earth. Virtue alone moves Heaven; Heaven cherishes virtue alone. Thus, when he establishes the supreme standard …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之福歸之矣臣民者又大君之子也
惟天生物惟聖成之故敷極而錫天下以
福矣惟建極以斂福也可以觀格天之精
焉惟敷極以錫福也可以觀代天之治焉
此皇極之義所以為萬世君天下之準而
我
聖祖契悟之精
皇上繼述之善豈非超越千古而紹帝王之盛
者哉請因明問而敬陳之皇極之名孰昉
===
乎昉於書之洪範也蓋自神禹治水地平
天成而洛書呈其數武王造周諮謨訪道
而箕子叙其疇以其數言之則列于極之
上者有五行五事八政五紀焉列于極之
下者有三德稽疑庶徵福極焉八者固與
皇極而同叙于疇以其義言之則五紀以
上極之所以建也三德以下極之所以行
也八者皆待皇極而各得其理然是極也
非他也即中之立而四方取正之謂也
punctuated:
天下之福歸之矣。臣民者，又大君之子也。惟天生物，惟聖成之，故敷極而錫天下以福矣。惟建極以斂福也，可以觀格天之精焉；惟敷極以錫福也，可以觀代天之治焉。此皇極之義，所以為萬世君天下之準，而我聖祖契悟之精、皇上繼述之善，豈非超越千古而紹帝王之盛者哉？請因明問而敬陳之。

皇極之名孰昉乎？昉於《書》之《洪範》也。蓋自神禹治水，地平天成，而洛書呈其數；武王造周，諮謨訪道，而箕子叙其疇。以其數言之，則列于極之上者，有五行、五事、八政、五紀焉；列于極之下者，有三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極焉。八者固與皇極而同叙于疇。以其義言之，則五紀以上，極之所以建也；三德以下，極之所以行也。八者皆待皇極而各得其理。然是極也，非他也，即中之立而四方取正之謂也。
translation_en:
…the blessings of All under Heaven accrue to him. Ministers and subjects, in turn, are children of the great ruler. Heaven brings things into being, and the sage brings them to completion; thus, by extending the standard, the ruler bestows blessings upon All under Heaven. In establishing the standard to gather blessings, we may observe the utmost refinement of his power to move Heaven; in extending the standard to bestow blessings, we may observe his governance on Heaven’s behalf. This is why the meaning of the August Standard (huangji) serves as the norm for those who rule All under Heaven throughout the ages. Do not our Sagely Ancestor’s profound comprehension of it and His Majesty’s excellence in continuing and carrying forward his work surpass all antiquity and perpetuate the grandeur of the ancient emperors and kings? Permit me respectfully to set this forth in response to your discerning question.

Where did the term “August Standard” originate? It originated in the “Great Plan” chapter of the Book of Documents. When the divine Yu brought the waters under control, the earth was set in order and Heaven’s work accomplished, and the Luo Writing revealed its numbers. When King Wu founded the Zhou, he sought counsel and inquired into the Way, and Jizi set out its categories. In terms of their numerical arrangement, the categories placed before the Standard are the Five Elements, the Five Personal Activities, the Eight Affairs of Government, and the Five Measures of Time; those placed after it are the Three Virtues, the Examination of Doubts, the Various Signs, and Blessings and Extremities. These eight are indeed set out as categories alongside the August Standard. In terms of their meaning, the Five Measures of Time and the categories preceding them provide the means by which the Standard is established; the Three Virtues and the categories following them provide the means by which the Standard is put into practice. All eight depend upon the August Standard for each to attain its proper ordering. Yet this Standard is nothing other than the establishment of the center, from which the four quarters take their rule of correctness.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯舜之執中湯之建中皆是物也天以皇
極之理賦于人而不能使人之協于極于
是乎以彌綸輔相之道付之君君建其極
而天眷篤之申錫矣有不萃天下之福乎
君以建極之福斂諸躬而必欲臣民之會
歸于極也于是以蕩平正直之理敷于下
人協于極而王道由之宣布矣豈非錫天
下以福乎三代而上治教休明曆祚永久
陰陽調而風雨時羣生和而萬民殖諸福
===
之物可致之祥莫不畢至凡以皇建其極
而敷錫于下也成康而後建極敷極之義
微而斂福錫福之應亦寖以薄矣況于漢
之雜伯唐之雜夷宋之不振又何足以與
于皇極之道哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奮起淮甸汛掃腥羶以一身爲仁
義禮樂之主置天下於衣冠文物之域德
邁羣倫功高萬世其所以建極者豫矣敷
極者至矣是以
punctuated:
堯舜之執中，湯之建中，皆是物也。天以皇極之理賦于人，而不能使人之協于極，于是乎以彌綸輔相之道付之君。君建其極，而天眷篤之，申錫矣，有不萃天下之福乎？君以建極之福斂諸躬，而必欲臣民之會歸于極也，于是以蕩平正直之理敷于下。人協于極，而王道由之宣布矣，豈非錫天下以福乎？三代而上，治教休明，曆祚永久，陰陽調而風雨時，羣生和而萬民殖，諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，凡以皇建其極而敷錫于下也。成康而後，建極敷極之義微，而斂福錫福之應亦寖以薄矣。況于漢之雜伯、唐之雜夷、宋之不振，又何足以與于皇極之道哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，奮起淮甸，汛掃腥羶，以一身爲仁義禮樂之主，置天下於衣冠文物之域。德邁羣倫，功高萬世，其所以建極者豫矣，敷極者至矣，是以
translation_en:
Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the mean and Tang’s establishing the mean were all this same thing. Heaven endows human beings with the principle of the august standard, yet cannot make them conform to it. It therefore entrusts to the ruler the Way of bringing all things into order and assisting their development. When the ruler establishes this standard, Heaven bestows its deep favor upon him and renews its gifts. Could he then fail to gather all the blessings under Heaven? The ruler gathers into his own person the blessings of establishing the standard, yet necessarily wishes his officials and people to converge upon it. He therefore spreads among those below the principles of impartiality and uprightness. The people conform to the standard, and through this the Kingly Way is promulgated. Is this not bestowing blessings upon all under Heaven? During the Three Dynasties and earlier, government and moral instruction were splendid and enlightened, and dynastic mandates endured long. Yin and yang were harmonious, winds and rains timely; living beings flourished in harmony, and the people multiplied. Every manifestation of blessing and every auspicious sign that could be brought forth arrived in full. All this was because the sovereign established his standard and spread its blessings among those below. After Kings Cheng and Kang, the meaning of establishing and spreading the standard grew obscure, and the corresponding effects of gathering and bestowing blessings likewise gradually diminished. How much less could the Han, which mixed in hegemonic rule, the Tang, which mixed in foreign ways, or the Song, which failed to regain its strength, qualify as participants in the Way of the august standard?
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who rose in the Huai region and swept away the rank and foul-smelling [alien rulers]. In his own person he became the master of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, and brought all under Heaven into the realm of civilized dress and cultural refinement. His virtue surpassed all others, and his achievements towered over ten thousand generations. His means of establishing the standard were fully prepared, and his spreading of it reached the utmost extent. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
上天眷享諸福萃焉奄有四海不足爲其富也
嚮明而治不足爲其尊也慶雲甘露瑞麥
嘉瓜太平之祥數數見焉
聖祖豈有心于斂天下之福哉極建而福自歸
之也然而
聖祖之心不自已也禮儀之潤色律令之詳定
凡所以軌衆齊物訓迪臣民者無所不用
其極矣復以洪範蔡傳有誤
親爲註釋以陰隲下民屬之天以相協厥居屬
===
之君
睿見神謨闡發皇極精意于千載之下無非欲
天下臣民協于極而同躋于福也蓋真有
得於相協厥居之義而無負于代天理物
之責矣豈區區于訓詁之末已哉我
皇上以上智之資撫
中興之運憲
天法
祖正典明倫宏綱大要無不舉矣
punctuated:
上天眷享，諸福萃焉。奄有四海，不足爲其富也；嚮明而治，不足爲其尊也。慶雲、甘露、瑞麥、嘉瓜，太平之祥數數見焉。聖祖豈有心于斂天下之福哉？極建而福自歸之也。
然而聖祖之心不自已也。禮儀之潤色，律令之詳定，凡所以軌衆齊物、訓迪臣民者，無所不用其極矣。復以《洪範》蔡傳有誤，親爲註釋，以「陰隲下民」屬之天，以「相協厥居」屬之君。睿見神謨，闡發皇極精意于千載之下，無非欲天下臣民協于極而同躋于福也。蓋真有得於相協厥居之義，而無負于代天理物之責矣，豈區區于訓詁之末已哉？
我皇上以上智之資，撫中興之運，憲天法祖，正典明倫，宏綱大要無不舉矣。
translation_en:
…Heaven bestowed its favor and accepted his offerings, and every blessing gathered upon him. Possession of all within the Four Seas was insufficient to express his wealth; governing while facing the light was insufficient to express his dignity. Auspicious clouds, sweet dew, auspicious wheat, and excellent melons—portents of peace—appeared again and again. Did the sagely founder deliberately seek to gather the blessings of the world to himself? Once the august standard was established, blessings came to him of their own accord.
Yet the sagely founder did not allow himself to rest. He refined ceremonial forms and settled the statutes and ordinances in detail. In everything that regulated the multitude, brought affairs into order, and instructed and guided his officials and people, he exerted himself to the utmost. Moreover, finding errors in Cai’s commentary on the “Great Plan” (Hongfan), he personally composed annotations, assigning “quietly ordering the people below” to Heaven and “assisting them to live together in harmony” to the ruler. His penetrating insight and inspired counsels elucidated the essential meaning of the august standard more than a thousand years later. His sole desire was that officials and people throughout the realm should conform to that standard and together attain blessings. He truly grasped the meaning of assisting the people to live together in harmony and fulfilled his responsibility to govern all things on Heaven’s behalf. Could his concern have been confined merely to the minor details of textual exegesis?
Our Emperor, endowed with the highest wisdom and presiding over an age of resurgence, takes Heaven as his pattern and his ancestors as his models, rectifies the established institutions, and clarifies human relationships. He has put into effect every great principle and essential measure.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
申飭吏治勤恤民隱深仁厚澤無不洽矣
至德馨香休徵協應禾呈三秀之異芝絢五
色之靈白鹿之雙馴玉兎之竝育奇祥上
瑞種種疊出矣我
皇上建極而斂福于躬所以承天之休者何至
也敷極而錫福于下所以代天之工者何
大也質諸
聖祖之建極敷極者夫何異哉然猶慮極道之
已敷而臣民之未協也邇者
===
鼎新
殿門乃遵
天命述
祖德特取皇極之義名之於
正殿正門也則曰
皇極
中極
建極焉於
左右門也則曰會極歸極焉恭覩
punctuated:
申飭吏治，勤恤民隱，深仁厚澤，無不洽矣。至德馨香，休徵協應，禾呈三秀之異，芝絢五色之靈，白鹿之雙馴，玉兎之竝育，奇祥上瑞，種種疊出矣。我皇上建極而斂福于躬，所以承天之休者何至也！敷極而錫福于下，所以代天之工者何大也！質諸聖祖之建極敷極者，夫何異哉？然猶慮極道之已敷，而臣民之未協也。
邇者，鼎新殿門，乃遵天命，述祖德，特取皇極之義，名之於正殿正門也，則曰皇極、中極、建極焉；於左右門也，則曰會極、歸極焉。恭覩
translation_en:
…He has admonished and disciplined the officialdom and diligently attended to the people's hidden sufferings; his profound benevolence and abundant beneficence have reached everywhere. His consummate virtue spreads its fragrance, and auspicious signs respond in harmony: grain displays the marvel of three ears on a stalk; numinous fungi shine in five colors; white deer appear as a tame pair, and white rabbits are reared together. Extraordinary auspices and supreme portents have appeared repeatedly in every variety. Our Emperor establishes the august standard and gathers blessings into his own person—how consummately he receives Heaven's favor! He promulgates that standard and bestows blessings upon those below—how great is his work on Heaven's behalf! Measured against the sagely progenitor's establishment and promulgation of the standard, how does this differ? Yet he still worries that, although the Way of the standard has been promulgated, his officials and people have not brought themselves into harmony with it.
Recently, in renovating the halls and gates, he followed Heaven's mandate and carried forward his ancestor's virtue, drawing specifically upon the meaning of the “august standard” to name them. For the principal halls and gates, the names were Huangji (“August Standard”), Zhongji (“Central Standard”), and Jianji (“Establishing the Standard”); for the gates to the left and right, they were Huiji (“Converging upon the Standard”) and Guiji (“Returning to the Standard”). We have reverently read…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
詔制有曰人君建中建極乃敘疇錫福之基臣
民會極歸極乃欽若從乂之道大哉
王言不特在廷臣庶接目儆心雖海隅蒼生罔
不欣欣焉知德意之所嚮我
皇上之訓以申其敷錫者尤彰明較著矣
聖祖闡皇極之義以正書傳之誤于先我
皇上揭皇極之要而命
殿門之名于後
聖祖之所闡即
===
皇上之所名也未遑于昔而有待于今者也
皇上之所名即
聖祖之所闡也善繼其志而善述其事者也
聖祖發其義以示天下而皇極之道明
皇上揭其要以訓天下而皇極之道行神禹之
所受武王之所訪箕子之所敘者至是如
日之中天水之行地矣
世德作求後先輝映猗歟盛哉所以然者由
我
punctuated:
詔制有曰：「人君建中建極，乃敘疇錫福之基；臣民會極歸極，乃欽若從乂之道。」大哉，王言！不特在廷臣庶接目儆心，雖海隅蒼生，罔不欣欣焉，知德意之所嚮。我皇上之訓，以申其敷錫者，尤彰明較著矣。
聖祖闡皇極之義，以正書傳之誤于先；我皇上揭皇極之要，而命殿門之名于後。聖祖之所闡，即皇上之所名也，未遑于昔而有待于今者也。皇上之所名，即聖祖之所闡也，善繼其志而善述其事者也。
聖祖發其義以示天下，而皇極之道明；皇上揭其要以訓天下，而皇極之道行。神禹之所受、武王之所訪、箕子之所敘者，至是如日之中天、水之行地矣。世德作求，後先輝映，猗歟盛哉！所以然者，由我
translation_en:
…the imperial edict states: “For the ruler to establish the Mean and the Ultimate Standard is the foundation for ordering the categories and bestowing blessings; for subjects to converge upon and return to the Ultimate Standard is the way of reverent compliance and submission to governance.” How great are these royal words! Not only do officials and commoners at court see them and take warning to heart: even the people in the remotest coastal regions rejoice without exception, understanding the intent of his benevolence. Our Emperor’s instruction, reaffirming his universal bestowal of blessings, is especially clear and manifest.
The Sagely Progenitor first elucidated the meaning of the August Ultimate Standard (huangji), correcting errors in the commentary on the Book of Documents; our Emperor subsequently brought its essentials to the fore by naming the halls and gates. What the Sagely Progenitor elucidated is precisely what the Emperor has embodied in these names: what there was no time to accomplish in the past awaited the present. What the Emperor has embodied in these names is precisely what the Sagely Progenitor elucidated: he has admirably carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and continued his undertakings.
The Sagely Progenitor expounded its meaning to instruct all under Heaven, and the Way of the August Ultimate Standard became clear. The Emperor brought its essentials to the fore to admonish all under Heaven, and that Way was put into practice. What the divine Yu received, what King Wu inquired into, and what Jizi set forth has now become like the sun at the zenith and water flowing over the earth. Carrying forward ancestral virtue, predecessor and successor illuminate one another. Ah, how magnificent! The reason for this lies in our …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖
皇上建極之學即古帝王之學故
聖祖
皇上敷極之治即古帝王之治也愚甞仰窺其
萬一矣以
聖祖之學言之則
存心有錄矣以格天為要也
精誠有錄矣以敬天為首也又甞伏讀
諭儒臣宋濂之言曰人心虛靈乗氣機出入操
===
而存之為難朕罔敢自暇自逸則我
聖祖之學非以一敬為之主宰乎非堯舜湯武
之學乎以我
皇上之學言之則
敬一有箴矣慮其弗聚弗純也
四箴有註矣謹于視聽言動也又甞伏讀
御製重華殿等各置經書備覽詩有曰靈臺虛
而明燭物別垢臧清濁由此分好惡自酌量
好善而惡惡罔非本其良無黨亦無偏平平
punctuated:
聖祖、皇上建極之學，即古帝王之學，故聖祖、皇上敷極之治，即古帝王之治也。愚甞仰窺其萬一矣。以聖祖之學言之，則存心有錄矣，以格天為要也；精誠有錄矣，以敬天為首也。又甞伏讀諭儒臣宋濂之言曰：「人心虛靈，乗氣機出入，操而存之為難。朕罔敢自暇自逸。」則我聖祖之學，非以一敬為之主宰乎？非堯舜湯武之學乎？

以我皇上之學言之，則敬一有箴矣，慮其弗聚弗純也；四箴有註矣，謹于視聽言動也。又甞伏讀御製《重華殿等各置經書備覽》詩，有曰：「靈臺虛而明，燭物別垢臧。清濁由此分，好惡自酌量。好善而惡惡，罔非本其良。無黨亦無偏，平平
translation_en:
…the learning by which our Sagely Founder and His Majesty establish the Supreme Standard is precisely the learning of the ancient sage-kings. Thus the governance by which our Sagely Founder and His Majesty extend the Supreme Standard is precisely the governance of the ancient sage-kings. I, in my ignorance, have ventured to glimpse a ten-thousandth part of it. Speaking of the Sagely Founder’s learning, there are records on preserving the mind, which take reaching Heaven as their essential purpose; there are records on perfect sincerity, which give foremost place to revering Heaven. I have also reverently read his instruction to the Confucian minister Song Lian: “The human mind is empty and numinous; it comes and goes with the workings of vital energy. Holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult. I dare not indulge in leisure or ease.” Was not the learning of our Sagely Founder governed throughout by reverent attentiveness alone? Was it not the learning of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu?

Speaking of His Majesty’s learning, there is the Admonition on Reverent Oneness, expressing concern lest the mind lack concentration and purity; there are annotations to the Four Admonitions, enjoining care in looking, listening, speaking, and acting. I have also reverently read the imperially composed poem, “Placing Classical Books in Chonghua Hall and Other Locations for Consultation,” which includes these lines: “The mind’s numinous terrace is empty and bright; / It illuminates things and distinguishes the foul from the good. / Through it the clear and turbid are distinguished; / Likes and dislikes are duly weighed. / Loving goodness and hating evil, / All arise from its innate goodness. / Without faction and without partiality, / Even and impartial…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而蕩蕩則我
皇上之學又非一敬以為之主宰乎又孰非堯
舜湯武之學乎故以此而建極則為有本
之德而克享於天眷有德之心矣斂福于
躬者何莫而非上帝之寵綏也哉以此而
敷極則為有本之治而無負於天佑下民
之意矣錫福于下者何莫而非元后之裁
成也哉然極建于君矣臣不協焉非純臣
也極敷于上矣民不協焉非良民也我
===
皇上既體天之心法
祖之意而敷極錫福矣凡我臣民又可不仰遵
聖訓而會極歸極乎是必惟臣欽若而凡有能
有為者皆進其行以昌其邦而務戒夫偏
陂作好作惡之私則舉天下之為臣者皆
協于極矣有不受福于朝者乎惟民從乂
而凡有猷有為有守者皆勵其行以迪其
德而胥勸於遵義遵道遵路之歸則舉天
下之為民者皆協于極矣有不獲福于身
punctuated:
而蕩蕩。則我皇上之學，又非一敬以為之主宰乎？又孰非堯舜湯武之學乎？故以此而建極，則為有本之德，而克享於天眷有德之心矣。斂福于躬者，何莫而非上帝之寵綏也哉？以此而敷極，則為有本之治，而無負於天佑下民之意矣。錫福于下者，何莫而非元后之裁成也哉？然極建于君矣，臣不協焉，非純臣也；極敷于上矣，民不協焉，非良民也。

我皇上既體天之心、法祖之意，而敷極錫福矣，凡我臣民，又可不仰遵聖訓而會極歸極乎？是必惟臣欽若，而凡有能有為者，皆進其行以昌其邦，而務戒夫偏陂、作好作惡之私，則舉天下之為臣者皆協于極矣，有不受福于朝者乎？惟民從乂，而凡有猷有為有守者，皆勵其行以迪其德，而胥勸於遵義、遵道、遵路之歸，則舉天下之為民者皆協于極矣，有不獲福于身
translation_en:
…and broad and open. Is not reverent attentiveness likewise the governing principle of our Emperor’s learning? And how could any of it fail to be the learning of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu? Thus, when he establishes the supreme standard through this learning, his virtue has a firm foundation, and he can enjoy Heaven’s favor, accorded from its regard for those who possess virtue. Of the blessings gathered upon his person, which does not come from the Lord on High’s gracious care? When he extends the supreme standard through this learning, his government has a firm foundation, and he fulfills Heaven’s intention to protect the people below. Of the blessings bestowed upon those below, which does not result from the sovereign’s ordering and perfecting of things? Yet once the ruler has established the supreme standard, ministers who do not conform to it are not wholly loyal ministers; once the supreme standard has been extended from above, people who do not conform to it are not good subjects.

Our Emperor has already embodied Heaven’s purpose and followed the intentions of his ancestors, extending the supreme standard and bestowing blessings. Can all of us, his ministers and people, then fail reverently to obey his sagely instructions and gather at and return to the supreme standard? Ministers must therefore reverently comply: all who have ability and capacity for action must advance their conduct so as to make their state flourish, taking care to guard against the selfishness of partiality and bias, and of arbitrary likes and dislikes. Then all ministers throughout the realm will conform to the supreme standard. Will any fail to receive blessings from the court? The people must submit to good government: all who possess plans, capacity for action, and steadfast principles must strive in their conduct to advance their virtue, encouraging one another toward the common end of following righteousness, following the Way, and following the proper path. Then all the people throughout the realm will conform to the supreme standard. Will any fail to obtain blessings for themselves…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
者乎此又我臣民之所當自盡以隆我
皇上敷極之大化以副我
皇上錫福之盛心者也抑皇極之斂福固矣然
疇之敘福必以壽先之則壽又福之首而
天之所以眷德者尤莫重於此也我
皇上仁恩汪濊淪膚浹髓
御極愈久則建極愈隆敷極愈遠而斂福愈大
所謂天壽平格壽考作人將與天地同其
悠久而受天之祐以永錫我臣民仁壽之
===
福者蓋有億萬年無疆之休矣愚敢以是
爲
今日頌
第二問
同考試官教諭李批以仁義禮樂立說庶幾知
本之學姚士觀
考試官教諭何批文義深厚有漢人尺度
考試官教諭錢批有根據有斷制非苟作者
punctuated:
者乎？此又我臣民之所當自盡，以隆我皇上敷極之大化，以副我皇上錫福之盛心者也。抑皇極之斂福固矣，然疇之敘福，必以壽先之，則壽又福之首，而天之所以眷德者，尤莫重於此也。我皇上仁恩汪濊，淪膚浹髓，御極愈久，則建極愈隆，敷極愈遠，而斂福愈大。所謂天壽平格，壽考作人，將與天地同其悠久，而受天之祐，以永錫我臣民仁壽之福者，蓋有億萬年無疆之休矣。愚敢以是爲今日頌。

第二問

同考試官教諭李批：以仁義禮樂立說，庶幾知本之學。姚士觀。

考試官教諭何批：文義深厚，有漢人尺度。

考試官教諭錢批：有根據，有斷制，非苟作者。
translation_en:
…could there be such a person? This, too, is something in which we, his subjects, must exert ourselves fully, to enhance the great transforming influence of His Majesty’s dissemination of the August Standard and to fulfill his generous intention of bestowing blessings. Now, that the August Standard gathers blessings is certain. Yet, when the category of blessings in the Great Plan enumerates them, it invariably places longevity first. Longevity is thus foremost among blessings, and among Heaven’s ways of favoring virtue, none is more weighty than this. His Majesty’s benevolence and gracious bounty are vast, penetrating the skin and permeating the marrow. The longer he occupies the throne, the more exalted his establishment of the Standard, the farther its dissemination, and the greater his gathering of blessings. This is what is meant by “Heaven-granted longevity attaining its full measure” and “nurturing men through venerable longevity.” He will endure as long as Heaven and Earth and receive Heaven’s protection, forever bestowing upon us, his subjects, the blessings of benevolence and longevity: boundless felicity for hundreds of millions of years. I venture to offer this as a eulogy for the present day.

Second Question

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “He grounds his argument in benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music, approaching a learning that understands the fundamentals.” Yao Shiguan 姚士觀.

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The writing and its meaning are profound and substantial, possessing the standards of Han writers.”

Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “It has a sound basis and decisive judgments; this is no careless composition.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之謂也樂以和民德仁之通也刑以教民
中義之達也明於制置協於化理洋洋乎
大道也哉嘗考之易豫之象曰先王作樂
崇德殷薦上帝以配祖考此言樂之始也
和之至也自虞廷命后夔典樂而詩歌聲
律八音克諧以和神人乃萬世和樂之原
也厥至戛擊搏拊以詠以間簫韶九成鳳
儀獸舞眞如天地覆載舜之樂所以爲盡
善後有作者弗可及矣迨於成周其制大
===
備今載之大司樂所掌樂德樂語樂舞致
神悅人以作動物無非虞廷之義也乃率
屬隸肄有大師小師磬鐘笙鎛籥章鞮屨
各有司存此因器備官以陳其殷者文也
夫子所謂武未盡善固自其樂之情求之
季札所謂聖人之難也此古樂之盛也元
儒吳澄氏乃謂大司樂宜隸地官是以禮
樂爲邦教而不知宗伯所以和神人而極
感通之大典也豈非更定之鑿耶然太和
punctuated: 之謂也。樂以和民德，仁之通也；刑以教民中，義之達也。明於制置，協於化理，洋洋乎大道也哉！嘗考之《易》，《豫》之象曰：「先王作樂崇德，殷薦上帝，以配祖考。」此言樂之始也，和之至也。自虞廷命后夔典樂，而詩歌聲律，八音克諧，以和神人，乃萬世和樂之原也。厥至戛擊搏拊，以詠以間，簫韶九成，鳳儀獸舞，眞如天地覆載，舜之樂所以爲盡善，後有作者弗可及矣。迨於成周，其制大備。今載之《大司樂》，所掌樂德、樂語、樂舞，致神悅人，以作動物，無非虞廷之義也。乃率屬隸肄，有大師、小師、磬、鐘、笙、鎛、籥章、鞮屨，各有司存。此因器備官，以陳其殷者，文也。夫子所謂《武》未盡善，固自其樂之情求之；季札所謂「聖人之難也」，此古樂之盛也。元儒吳澄氏乃謂大司樂宜隸地官，是以禮樂爲邦教，而不知宗伯所以和神人而極感通之大典也，豈非更定之鑿耶？然太和
translation_en:
…is what is meant. Music harmonizes the people’s virtue: it is the pervading influence of benevolence. Punishments teach the people to keep to the mean: they are the extension of righteousness. Clear in their institutional arrangements and consonant with moral transformation and good order—how vast is this great Way!

I have examined the Book of Changes. The Image commentary on the hexagram Yu (Enthusiasm) says: “The former kings made music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in sacrifice.” This speaks of the beginnings of music and the utmost attainment of harmony. From the time when the court of Yu appointed Hou Kui to oversee music, poetry and song, tones and pitch standards, and the eight classes of instruments were brought into harmony, thereby harmonizing spirits and humans. This was the source of harmonious music for all subsequent ages. When the instruments were struck and tapped, with singing and instrumental interludes, and the Xiao Shao music completed its nine movements, phoenixes appeared in stately bearing and beasts danced. Truly, this resembled Heaven’s covering and Earth’s bearing of all things. This is why Shun’s music was perfectly good: no subsequent composer could equal it.

By the time of the established Zhou dynasty, the institutions of music were fully developed. What is now recorded in the “Grand Director of Music” section—the musical virtues, musical expressions, and musical dances under his charge, which summoned spirits, delighted people, and stirred living creatures—all embodied the principles of the court of Yu. He led his subordinates in rehearsal; there were the grand and lesser music masters, officials for stone chimes, bells, mouth organs, large bells, flute music, and the Di Lü musicians, each with assigned responsibilities. Establishing a full complement of offices according to the instruments, thereby displaying music’s abundance, constituted its outward refinement. When the Master said that the Wu music was not perfectly good, he was assuredly judging it by the sentiments it expressed. What Ji Zha called “a difficult attainment even for a sage” exemplified the flourishing of ancient music.

Yet the Yuan scholar Wu Cheng maintained that the Grand Director of Music should be subordinate to the Ministry of Education. This treats rites and music as instruments of instruction for the realm, without understanding that they are the great ceremonial means by which the Minister of Rites harmonizes spirits and humans and brings their mutual responsiveness and communion to their fullest extent. Is this not a forced revision of the institutional order? Yet the supreme harmony…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之在成周宇宙間自唐虞而後一再見也
又嘗考之易旅之象曰君子以明慎用刑
而不留獄此言刑之始也敬之至也自虞
書命皐陶為士而象有典刑流宥五刑鞭
扑之敎惟刑之恤是萬世明刑之則也厥
至五刑有服五流有宅惟明克允刑期無
刑眞如天地之栽培傾覆舜之德所以為
好生後有作者不可及矣至於有周其法
益詳今載之大司寇所掌三典以刑邦國
===
五刑以糾萬民若兩造兩劑嘉石肺石無
非舜典之遺也然而設參置輔若小司寇
之五聲求民情八辟麗邦法三刺斷訟獄
以施上服下服固因時通變以多其法者
制也然布象魏而浹日始斂又慮民之偽
而防之後世所謂俗薄於唐虞者也此先
王之慎刑也乃大司徒又有八刑糾萬民
是以鄕三物之敎而厲禁以弼成之亦制
刑中而敎祇德也豈非協一之政耶然成
punctuated:
之在成周宇宙間，自唐虞而後一再見也。
又嘗考之《易》，旅之象曰：「君子以明慎用刑，而不留獄。」此言刑之始也，敬之至也。自《虞書》命皐陶為士，而象有典刑，流宥五刑，鞭扑之敎，惟刑之恤，是萬世明刑之則也。厥至五刑有服，五流有宅，惟明克允，刑期無刑，眞如天地之栽培傾覆。舜之德所以為好生，後有作者不可及矣。至於有周，其法益詳。今載之大司寇所掌，三典以刑邦國，五刑以糾萬民，若兩造、兩劑、嘉石、肺石，無非《舜典》之遺也。然而設參置輔，若小司寇之五聲求民情、八辟麗邦法、三刺斷訟獄，以施上服下服，固因時通變以多其法者，制也。然布象魏而浹日始斂，又慮民之偽而防之，後世所謂俗薄於唐虞者也。此先王之慎刑也。乃大司徒又有八刑糾萬民，是以鄕三物之敎而厲禁以弼成之，亦制刑中而敎祇德也。豈非協一之政耶？然成
translation_en:
…the presence of this supreme harmony throughout the world of Chengzhou was a rare recurrence of what had existed in the days of Tang and Yu.
I have also examined the Book of Changes. The Image commentary on the hexagram Lü, “The Traveler,” says: “The gentleman is discerning and cautious in applying punishments and does not allow cases to linger in prison.” This describes the fundamental principle of punishment and the utmost reverence in its use. In the Documents of Yu, Gao Yao was appointed Director of Justice. The prescribed punishments were represented in images; exile mitigated the five punishments; whipping and beating served disciplinary purposes. Compassion in punishment alone was the concern. This is the model for discerning punishment for all ages. When the five punishments each had their appropriate application and the five forms of exile their designated places, discernment alone secured fairness, and punishment aimed at making punishment unnecessary. This was truly like Heaven and Earth nurturing what stands upright and overturning what leans toward collapse. Thus Shun’s virtue cherished life; no later ruler who arose could equal him.
Under the Zhou, the laws became still more detailed. As now recorded among the responsibilities of the Minister of Justice, the three penal codes regulated the states, and the five punishments corrected the myriad people. Such provisions as requiring both litigants to appear, examining the two parties’ documents, and using the Fine Stone and the Lung Stone all continued the legacy of the Canon of Shun. Yet additional officials and assistants were established. The Vice Minister of Justice, for example, used the five modes of hearing to ascertain the people’s true circumstances, the eight grounds for special deliberation to apply the laws of the realm, and the three consultations to decide lawsuits and criminal cases, thereby imposing heavier or lighter penalties. These were indeed institutions that adapted to changing times by multiplying legal provisions. The penal statutes were displayed on the palace gateway towers and taken down only after ten days; precautions were also taken against deceit among the people. This was what later generations meant when they said that customs had become less generous than in the days of Tang and Yu. Such was the former kings’ caution in punishment.
The Minister of Education, moreover, had eight punishments with which to correct the myriad people. This meant reinforcing the three branches of instruction in the districts with strict prohibitions, helping that instruction achieve its purpose. This too was to make punishments fitting and teach reverence for virtue. Was this not a unified and coordinated government? Yet in the reign of King Cheng…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
康之世刑措不用又自唐虞以來一再見
也三代而下雅樂既隱新聲代變耀祥於
寶鼎較度於律尺無平心宣化之道而惟
以導欲長怨焉陵夷至於勝國胡部雜進
先王之樂亡矣德教既弛禁罔寖密緩深
故之罪急縱出之誅雖以隋唐之律疏稍
備而繁苛失當先王用刑之義湮矣洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝挺生南服驅除胡虜統一華夏功
===
成作樂悉屏前代諠譊之習
命尚書詹同陶凱製宴享九奏樂章曰本太初
曰仰大明曰民初生曰品物亨曰御六龍
曰泰階平曰君德成曰聖道成曰樂清寧
洋洋乎得和平廣大之義後以大成樂器
頒降學校又嘗
謂侍臣曰禮以道敬樂以宣和不和不敬何
以為治大哉
王言所以道中和而崇治體之極垂裕萬世無
punctuated:
康之世，刑措不用，又自唐虞以來一再見也。三代而下，雅樂既隱，新聲代變，耀祥於寶鼎，較度於律尺，無平心宣化之道，而惟以導欲長怨焉。陵夷至於勝國，胡部雜進，先王之樂亡矣。德教既弛，禁罔寖密，緩深故之罪，急縱出之誅，雖以隋唐之律疏稍備，而繁苛失當，先王用刑之義湮矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝挺生南服，驅除胡虜，統一華夏，功成作樂，悉屏前代諠譊之習。命尚書詹同、陶凱製宴享九奏樂章，曰《本太初》，曰《仰大明》，曰《民初生》，曰《品物亨》，曰《御六龍》，曰《泰階平》，曰《君德成》，曰《聖道成》，曰《樂清寧》，洋洋乎得和平廣大之義！後以大成樂器頒降學校，又嘗謂侍臣曰：「禮以道敬，樂以宣和，不和不敬，何以為治？」大哉王言！所以道中和而崇治體之極，垂裕萬世，無
translation_en:
…in the reign of King Kang, punishments were set aside and went unused: this was another occurrence of what had been seen in the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. After the Three Dynasties, classical music fell into obscurity, and new sounds changed with each succeeding age. Auspicious signs were displayed in precious tripods, and measurements were compared against pitch-standard rulers; yet there was no way of calming hearts and spreading moral transformation. These practices merely encouraged desires and fostered resentment. Decline continued until the preceding dynasty, when ensembles of non-Chinese music were introduced indiscriminately, and the music of the former kings disappeared. Moral instruction grew lax while the net of prohibitions became ever denser. Deliberately imposing unduly severe sentences was punished lightly [?], while letting offenders go free was punished harshly. Although the statutes and commentaries of the Sui and Tang were somewhat comprehensive, their provisions were excessively intricate, harsh, and inappropriate. The principles by which the former kings employed punishment were thus obscured.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao arose with outstanding gifts in the southern lands, expelled the northern invaders, and unified the Chinese realm. His achievements accomplished, he instituted music, entirely eliminating the clamorous practices of preceding dynasties. He ordered the ministers Zhan Tong and Tao Kai to compose musical texts for the nine performances at imperial banquets: Rooted in the Primordial Beginning; Looking Up to the Great Brightness; The People’s First Beginnings; The Myriad Things Flourish; Driving the Six Dragons; The Three Steps Are at Peace; The Ruler’s Virtue Is Perfected; The Sagely Way Is Perfected; and Rejoicing in Purity and Tranquillity. How richly these embodied the meaning of harmony, peace, breadth, and grandeur! Later, he distributed instruments for the Music of Great Completion to the schools. He also once told his attendant officials: “Ritual guides reverence; music gives expression to harmony. Without harmony and reverence, how can there be good government?” How great were these royal words! They guide people toward equilibrium and harmony, elevate the essential principles of government to their utmost perfection, and bequeath blessings to ten thousand generations, without …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
如見也是宜和氣薫蒸充塞宇宙湛恩濊
澤覃被海隅不戢之萌旋就底定五帝之
德三王之治千載一時矣愚生何幸躬逢
其盛
第三問
李伯廉
同考試官教諭易批命意鑄詞雅有渾噩氣象
同考試官教諭金批上下數千載文字之詳略
具見篇
===
考試官教諭何批論文而本之於道可謂知本
考試官教諭錢批深厚爾雅是宜式之
夫文辭之興也其因時而為之者乎然以
志闡以道章者也夫文非徒為也觀於時
則教化因之矣求之志則人品因之矣體
之道則情理因之矣是故文以載道而輪
轅是飾則虛車也言以觀人而論篤是與
則色莊也辭以敷化而實不中聲則畫象
也嗚呼文者心之精而道之寄也君子於
punctuated:
如見也。是宜和氣薫蒸，充塞宇宙；湛恩濊澤，覃被海隅。不戢之萌，旋就底定。五帝之德，三王之治，千載一時矣！愚生何幸，躬逢其盛！

第三問
李伯廉

同考試官教諭易批：命意鑄詞，雅有渾噩氣象。
同考試官教諭金批：上下數千載，文字之詳略，具見篇。
考試官教諭何批：論文而本之於道，可謂知本。
考試官教諭錢批：深厚爾雅，是宜式之。

夫文辭之興也，其因時而為之者乎？然以志闡，以道章者也。夫文非徒為也，觀於時，則教化因之矣；求之志，則人品因之矣；體之道，則情理因之矣。是故文以載道，而輪轅是飾，則虛車也；言以觀人，而論篤是與，則色莊也；辭以敷化，而實不中聲，則畫象也。嗚呼！文者，心之精而道之寄也。君子於
translation_en:
…as we see here. Thus it is fitting that harmonious influences should spread warmly throughout the universe, and that profound beneficence and abundant favor should reach the farthest shores. The unruly populace was soon brought to order. The virtue of the Five Emperors and the governance of the Three Kings have appeared together in this moment, encountered but once in a thousand years! How fortunate I, an unworthy student, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Third Question
Li Bolian

Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “In its conception and crafting of phrases, this essay possesses a distinctly simple and unadorned grandeur.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: “Spanning several thousand years, the fullness and brevity of literary expression are all displayed in this essay.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “In discussing literature, he grounds it in the Way: he may be said to understand the foundation.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “Profound, substantial, and refined: this deserves to serve as a model.”

Does not literary expression arise in response to its times? Yet through it aspiration is made clear and the Way is manifested. Writing is not undertaken without purpose. Viewed in relation to its times, it reveals moral instruction and transformation; examined for its aspirations, it reveals personal character; considered as an embodiment of the Way, it reveals human feelings and their underlying principles. Thus, writing serves to carry the Way, but if one merely embellishes the wheels and shafts, it is an empty carriage. Speech serves to assess a person, but if one approves only earnest-sounding discourse, it is mere outward solemnity. Literary expression serves to spread moral transformation, but if its substance does not match its sound, it is only a painted likeness. Ah! Writing is the essence of the heart and the lodging place of the Way. The gentleman, in this …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
是乎考德而徵教焉是豈可以易言哉嘗
聞之太上立德其次立功其次立言言也
者君子不得已而為之然由之不朽者固
道化之極也說者謂文章與時高下以易
詩書春秋屬之皇帝王伯焉是故虞夏之
書渾渾爾商書灝灝爾周書噩噩爾此時
代之變也泥焉者為之則犧尊而青黃之
以簿書而效羲軒之畫舛矣夫子之教曰
有德者必有言是故吉人之辭寡躁人之
===
辭多中心疑者其辭枝誣善之人其辭游
此志氣之別也矯焉者為之則繡其鞶帨
羊質而虎皮鑿矣或者謂文者貫道之器
無係於道非其至者也是故說天莫辨乎
易說事莫辨於書說志莫辨於詩說體莫
辨於禮說理莫辨於春秋此理道之殊致
也昧焉者為之則牛鬼蛇神施之廊廟而
駭矣嗟夫文若是也與哉粵自天地儲精
因文以示日月星辰之爛曜山川草木人
punctuated: 是乎考德而徵教焉，是豈可以易言哉？嘗聞之：太上立德，其次立功，其次立言。言也者，君子不得已而為之，然由之不朽者，固道化之極也。說者謂文章與時高下，以《易》《詩》《書》《春秋》屬之皇帝王伯焉。是故虞夏之書渾渾爾，商書灝灝爾，周書噩噩爾，此時代之變也。泥焉者為之，則犧尊而青黃之，以簿書而效羲軒之畫，舛矣！夫子之教曰：「有德者必有言。」是故吉人之辭寡，躁人之辭多，中心疑者其辭枝，誣善之人其辭游，此志氣之別也。矯焉者為之，則繡其鞶帨，羊質而虎皮，鑿矣！或者謂文者貫道之器，無係於道，非其至者也。是故說天莫辨乎《易》，說事莫辨於《書》，說志莫辨於《詩》，說體莫辨於《禮》，說理莫辨於《春秋》，此理道之殊致也。昧焉者為之，則牛鬼蛇神，施之廊廟而駭矣！嗟夫！文若是也與哉？粵自天地儲精，因文以示，日月星辰之爛曜，山川草木人
translation_en:
…herein examines virtue and seeks evidence of moral teaching. How could this be spoken of lightly? I have heard it said: highest is establishing virtue; next is establishing achievements; next is establishing words. Setting forth words is something the gentleman undertakes only when he cannot do otherwise. Yet to attain immortality through them is indeed the culmination of transformation through the Way. Commentators maintain that writing rises and falls with its age, assigning the Changes, Odes, Documents, and Spring and Autumn Annals respectively to the ages of sovereigns, emperors, kings, and hegemons. Thus the documents of Yu and Xia are profound and ample; the Shang documents are vast and flowing; the Zhou documents are grave and austere. These are changes arising from different ages. Those who write while clinging rigidly to such forms merely paint a sacrificial vessel blue and yellow: to imitate the diagrams of Fuxi and Xuanyuan through registers and documents is misguided!

The Master's teaching says: “Those who possess virtue invariably have something to say.” Thus the words of an auspicious person are few, while those of an impetuous person are many; those harboring doubts speak in branching circumlocutions, while those who slander the good speak evasively. These are differences in aspiration and temperament. Those who write by forcing an outward appearance merely embroider their belts and kerchiefs: sheep in substance but clad in tiger skins, they are contrived!

Some say that writing is a vessel through which the Way is conveyed, yet has no connection with the Way itself. This does not represent its highest attainment. Thus, for explaining Heaven, nothing is more discriminating than the Changes; for explaining affairs, nothing is more discriminating than the Documents; for explaining aspirations, nothing is more discriminating than the Odes; for explaining proper forms, nothing is more discriminating than the Rites; and for explaining principles, nothing is more discriminating than the Spring and Autumn Annals. These are distinct expressions of principle and the Way. Those who write in ignorance of this produce ox-headed ghosts and serpent spirits: brought into the court, such things cause consternation!

Alas! Is writing really like this? From the time Heaven and Earth stored up their essences, they manifested them through patterned forms: the brilliant radiance of sun, moon, and stars; mountains, rivers, grasses, trees, and human…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
物之森錯此天地之至文也及夫河洛肇
祥圖書著象而天地之文寄之人矣聖人
者因象以闡數因數以明理彌綸天下之
事著古昔之昬昬傳千里之忞忞莫非發
揮精蘊經緯人物無意於爲文而文莫尚
焉墳典以降六經繼作帝王之道可得而
睹矣秦漢而下言文者率稱漢魏之際多
文人才士焉今觀魏文典論其言七子之
失得詳矣然謂四科不同人有偏能引氣
===
不齊巧拙有素斯文林之攷鏡而達旨之
真詮也陸機文賦備極敷陳妙解情理至
稱謝朝華之已披啓夕秀於未振固百代
之上所獨得者又謂立片辭以居要乃一
篇之警策彬彬乎文質之至矣所謂弘博
君子者耶唐獨孤郁之爲文辨有言彩飾
其字慎所爲體斯易春秋之一畫一字極
而與天地準者乃所謂其心卓然而絶於
俗不求文而自至者故達論也李文饒忠
punctuated:
物之森錯，此天地之至文也。及夫河洛肇祥，圖書著象，而天地之文寄之人矣。聖人者，因象以闡數，因數以明理，彌綸天下之事，著古昔之昬昬，傳千里之忞忞，莫非發揮精蘊，經緯人物。無意於爲文，而文莫尚焉。墳典以降，六經繼作，帝王之道可得而睹矣。

秦漢而下，言文者率稱漢魏之際多文人才士焉。今觀魏文《典論》，其言七子之失得詳矣。然謂四科不同，人有偏能，引氣不齊，巧拙有素，斯文林之攷鏡，而達旨之真詮也。陸機《文賦》，備極敷陳，妙解情理。至稱「謝朝華之已披，啓夕秀於未振」，固百代之上所獨得者。又謂「立片辭以居要，乃一篇之警策」，彬彬乎文質之至矣！所謂弘博君子者耶？

唐獨孤郁之《爲文辨》有言：「彩飾其字，慎所爲體。」斯《易》《春秋》之一畫一字，極而與天地準者，乃所謂「其心卓然而絶於俗，不求文而自至」者，故達論也。李文饒忠
translation_en:
…and things in their dense, interwoven array: this is the supreme patterned beauty of Heaven and Earth. When auspicious signs first appeared in the Yellow and Luo Rivers, and the River Chart and Luo Writing displayed their images, the patterns of Heaven and Earth were entrusted to human beings. The sages used images to elucidate numbers, and numbers to illuminate principles. They comprehensively ordered the affairs of the world, made manifest the obscurities of antiquity, and transmitted what was obscure a thousand li away [?]. Everything they did brought forth profound meanings and ordered human beings and things. They had no intention of producing literary writing, yet no writing surpassed theirs. From the ancient Canons onward, the Six Classics appeared in succession, making the Way of emperors and kings visible.

From the Qin and Han onward, those who discuss literature generally praise the abundance of accomplished writers and talented scholars at the transition from Han to Wei. Looking now at Emperor Wen of Wei’s Authoritative Discourses (Dianlun), we find a detailed discussion of the merits and shortcomings of the Seven Masters. His statements that the four categories of writing differ, that individuals possess particular strengths, that their drawing upon vital energy is unequal [?], and that skill and awkwardness have inherent foundations provide a critical mirror for the literary world and a true exposition of its essential meaning. Lu Ji’s Rhapsody on Literature (Wen fu) offers an exceptionally full exposition and a subtle understanding of feelings and principles. His words, “Bid farewell to the morning blossoms already unfolded; open the evening blooms that have yet to emerge,” express an insight uniquely his across a hundred generations. He further says, “Set a brief phrase in a pivotal position: it becomes the arresting admonition of the entire composition.” How perfectly refinement and substance are harmonized here! Was he what is called a gentleman of broad and ample learning?

Dugu Yu of the Tang says in his Disquisition on Literary Composition (Weiwen bian): “Adorn the words with color, and take care over the form you employ.” A single line in the Changes or a single word in the Spring and Autumn Annals reaches the utmost and accords with Heaven and Earth. This is precisely what is meant by “His mind stands loftily apart from vulgar conventions; without seeking literary accomplishment, he attains it of himself.” This, therefore, is a penetrating judgment. Li Wenrao’s loyalty…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
貞世篤丹扆諸箴油然正君之大雅古之
遠不忘君者也然其文論謂氣不可不貫
故曹氏之遺旨也至於文箴謂文之為物
自然靈氣信乎迫於促節者音律之為病
矣知言哉由是以推代有述作然莫備於
有唐之朝史稱唐文三變故一代之極則
也攷之劉禹錫序柳子之集曰三代之文
至戰國而病涉秦漢復起漢之文至列國
而病唐興復起治亂之致文辭因之言時
===
代之變者莫當於此矣而非其至也尚衡
序文道元龜有曰君子之文其德全志士
之文其義全詞士之文其思全此自其人
三等之義也然辭士徇辭無取頹靡志士
氣高調苦有感激之道焉誠介然自立者
衡且自道也若夫飾行表德道天人之際
達性命之元非君子之行為之質焉曷以
文成而見情著事耶故言人品之差者莫
辨於此矣而非其宜也吕温秀含五行光
punctuated: 貞世篤，《丹扆》諸箴，油然正君之大雅，古之遠不忘君者也。然其《文論》謂「氣不可不貫」，故曹氏之遺旨也。至於《文箴》，謂「文之為物，自然靈氣」，信乎迫於促節者，音律之為病矣。知言哉！由是以推，代有述作，然莫備於有唐之朝。史稱唐文三變，故一代之極則也。攷之劉禹錫序柳子之集曰：「三代之文，至戰國而病，涉秦漢復起；漢之文，至列國而病，唐興復起。治亂之致，文辭因之。」言時代之變者，莫當於此矣，而非其至也。尚衡序《文道元龜》有曰：「君子之文，其德全；志士之文，其義全；詞士之文，其思全。」此自其人三等之義也。然辭士徇辭，無取頹靡；志士氣高調苦，有感激之道焉，誠介然自立者，衡且自道也。若夫飾行表德，道天人之際，達性命之元，非君子之行為之質焉，曷以文成而見情著事耶？故言人品之差者，莫辨於此矣，而非其宜也。吕温秀含五行，光
translation_en:
… steadfast loyalty was deeply rooted through generations [?]. Li Wenrao’s Admonitions for the Vermilion Screen and his other admonitions naturally possess the grand elegance of writings that set the ruler right: he was one of those men of old who, though far away, did not forget their sovereign. Yet his Discourse on Literature says, “Vital energy must run throughout”—an idea inherited from Master Cao. As for his Admonition on Literature, it says, “Literature, as a thing, is the numinous energy of nature.” Indeed, being constrained by hurried rhythms shows how tonal and metrical rules can become a malady. How well he understood!

Extending the inquiry from this point, every age had its writings, but none attained the comprehensiveness of the Tang dynasty. The histories speak of three transformations in Tang literature; these thus constitute the highest standards of that dynasty. Consider Liu Yuxi’s preface to Master Liu’s collected works: “The literature of the Three Dynasties fell into decline by the Warring States period, and revived through the Qin and Han. Han literature fell into decline by the period of the divided states [?], and revived with the rise of the Tang. Literary expression follows the conditions brought about by order and disorder.” No account of changes across the ages is more apt than this, yet it does not reach the ultimate principle.

Shang Heng’s preface to the Primal Tortoise Mirror of the Way of Literature says: “In the gentleman’s writing, virtue is complete; in the man of resolve’s writing, righteousness is complete; in the literary craftsman’s writing, thought is complete.” This distinguishes three grades according to the persons themselves. Yet literary craftsmen pursue diction, and their decadent softness offers nothing worth adopting. Men of resolve have lofty spirit and an anguished tone, with a capacity for impassioned feeling; they truly stand firmly on their own. Heng was also describing himself. But as for refining conduct and manifesting virtue, articulating the relationship between Heaven and humanity, and penetrating the source of human nature and destiny—unless a gentleman’s conduct supplies the substance, how can writing, once completed, reveal feelings and make affairs manifest? Thus no account distinguishes differences in human character more clearly than this, yet it does not establish the proper standard.

Lü Wen’s excellence embraced the Five Phases, and his radiance …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
掩一代其著人文化成論所稱夫以剛克
妻以柔立父慈而敎子孝而箴爲室家之
文君以仁使臣以義事違弼獻替爲朝廷
之文三公論道六卿分職百揆同歸爲官
司之文寬猛相濟爲刑政之文禮樂變通
爲敎化之文其意質而幾於理矣劉夢得
稱其以致君及物爲大欲考要帝王富疆
之際循理合心揭日月而行之韙矣其如
行不掩焉何哉雖然是數子之論文詳矣
===
然魏文父子狙詐相承情投七子而慙德
於七步之吟千載有餘慨焉徐蹤張蔡才
如積玉士衡亦一代之絕矣不免太息於
黑幔之夢劉呂之詞贍而豔矣乃身陷叔
文之黨此昔人重有感於言行相顧之難
也自唐而後宋德隆盛厥有歐曾蘇王稱
其名家而上擬唐漢不無濫觴餘波之誚
焉甚矣文之難言也故惟周子太極圖說
張子西銘程子易春秋傳序號著有宋四
punctuated:
掩一代。其著《人文化成論》，所稱「夫以剛克，妻以柔立，父慈而敎，子孝而箴」，爲室家之文；「君以仁使，臣以義事，違弼獻替」，爲朝廷之文；「三公論道，六卿分職，百揆同歸」，爲官司之文；「寬猛相濟」，爲刑政之文；「禮樂變通」，爲敎化之文。其意質而幾於理矣。劉夢得稱其以致君及物爲大，欲考要帝王富疆之際，循理合心，揭日月而行之，韙矣。其如行不掩焉何哉？雖然，是數子之論文詳矣。
然魏文父子狙詐相承，情投七子，而慙德於七步之吟，千載有餘慨焉。徐蹤張蔡，才如積玉；士衡亦一代之絕矣，不免太息於黑幔之夢。劉呂之詞贍而豔矣，乃身陷叔文之黨。此昔人重有感於言行相顧之難也。自唐而後，宋德隆盛，厥有歐曾蘇王，稱其名家，而上擬唐漢，不無濫觴餘波之誚焉。甚矣，文之難言也！故惟周子《太極圖說》、張子《西銘》、程子《易》《春秋》傳序，號著有宋四
translation_en:
… eclipsed his entire age. In his Discourse on Transformation through Human Culture, Lü Wen describes “the husband exercising firm self-mastery, the wife establishing herself through gentleness, the father teaching with kindness, and the son offering admonition with filial devotion” as the patterned order of the household; “the ruler employing his servants with benevolence, the servants serving with righteousness, correcting faults, offering good counsel, and rejecting what is wrong” as the patterned order of the court; “the Three Dukes discussing the Way, the Six Ministers dividing their duties, and the many officials working toward a common end” as the patterned order of government offices; “leniency and severity tempering one another” as the patterned order of punishment and administration; and “rites and music adapting to changing circumstances” as the patterned order of moral instruction. His meaning is substantial and approaches true principle. Liu Mengde praised him for making it his chief aim to guide his ruler to good government and benefit all things, seeking to investigate the essentials of how emperors and kings attained wealth and strength, following principle in accord with his heart, and holding aloft the sun and moon as he proceeded. This was admirable. Yet what are we to make of his conduct failing to measure up to it? Nevertheless, these writers discussed literary composition in detail.
