Yet Emperor Wen of Wei and his father inherited cunning and deceit from one another. He felt an affinity with the Seven Masters, but the poem composed in seven steps exposed his shameful lack of virtue, leaving cause for lament more than a thousand years later. Xu Zong [?], Zhang, and Cai possessed talents like heaps of jade; Shiheng, too, was unrivaled in his age, yet one cannot help sighing deeply over his dream of the black curtain. The writings of Liu and Lü were rich and ornate, yet they themselves became entangled in Shuwen’s faction. These cases made earlier generations keenly aware of the difficulty of making words and deeds accord with one another. After the Tang, the virtue of the Song flourished greatly. There were Ou, Zeng, Su, and Wang, acclaimed as masters; yet when compared with the Tang and Han writers before them, they were not free from the reproach of being mere derivative streams and lingering ripples. How very difficult it is to speak of literature! Thus only Master Zhou’s Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Master Zhang’s Western Inscription, and Master Cheng’s prefaces to the commentaries on the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals were renowned as the Song’s four …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
大作乃載道以為文斯百世不可易也繼
往聖之絕學開後儒之道統斯為聖賢之
徒而何以世代論哉然言文之體要者莫
過於宋真德秀氏其為文章正宗自六經
以下斷自左氏下及有唐而止分屬辭令
議論叙事詩賦四體擇取古文辭之雅馴
類輯標示來學總略旨要犁然當理足令
三代而下仰見古人之奥信乎修辭者之
矩矱百世可施行者也後之為文者有體
===
道之心若周程張子尤以六經為楨幹而
復參酌於真氏焉則於文道思過半矣
第四問
吳思學
同考試官教諭胡批意氣激昂議論切實竟非
空言者
同考試官教諭項批評品曲當詞采瀝目可敬可敬
考試官教諭何批知言之士取之
考試官教諭錢批是真有志尚友者
punctuated:
大作，乃載道以為文，斯百世不可易也。繼往聖之絕學，開後儒之道統，斯為聖賢之徒，而何以世代論哉？然言文之體要者，莫過於宋真德秀氏。其為《文章正宗》，自六經以下，斷自左氏，下及有唐而止，分屬辭令、議論、叙事、詩賦四體，擇取古文辭之雅馴，類輯標示來學，總略旨要，犁然當理，足令三代而下仰見古人之奥。信乎修辭者之矩矱，百世可施行者也。後之為文者，有體道之心若周程張子，尤以六經為楨幹，而復參酌於真氏焉，則於文道思過半矣。
第四問
吳思學
同考試官教諭胡批：意氣激昂，議論切實，竟非空言者。
同考試官教諭項批：評品曲當，詞采瀝目，可敬可敬。
考試官教諭何批：知言之士，取之。
考試官教諭錢批：是真有志尚友者。
translation_en:
…great works: these carry the Way through literary composition and cannot be superseded through a hundred generations. They carry forward the lost learning of the sages of old and open the orthodox transmission of the Way to later Confucian scholars. Their authors thus belong among the followers of the sages and worthies; how could they be judged by the age in which they lived? Yet in discussing the essential forms and principles of writing, none surpassed Zhen Dexiu of the Song. In compiling The Orthodox Tradition of Literature (Wenzhang zhengzong), he treated the writings after the Six Classics, beginning with Master Zuo and ending with the Tang. He divided them into four forms: diplomatic language, argumentation, narrative, and poetry and rhapsody. Selecting elegant and refined pieces of ancient writing, he arranged them by category to guide later students. His summaries of their main purport and essentials accord clearly with principle, enabling those living after the Three Dynasties to look up to and perceive the profundities of the ancients. Truly, this is a standard for those who cultivate literary expression, applicable through a hundred generations. If later writers have the resolve to embody the Way, like Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang, take the Six Classics above all as their structural foundation, and also consult and weigh Master Zhen’s judgments, they will have understood the greater part of the Way of writing.
Fourth Question
Wu Sixue
Associate Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: “His spirit is impassioned and his arguments address practical realities. These are certainly no empty words.”
Associate Examiner Xiang, an Instructor, comments: “His assessments are apt in every particular, and his literary brilliance is striking to the eye [?]. Admirable, admirable!”
Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: “A scholar who understands words. Select him.”
Examiner Qian, an Instructor, comments: “Here truly is someone resolved to seek friendship with the worthies of antiquity.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
君子之多識以畜德也而通於今者尤□
博古之助君子之論世以尚友也而求諸
近者尤為遠覽之資何則遠近一心也古
今一理也得其心與理則近猶遠也近篤
而遠益可舉矣今猶古也今準而古益可
酌矣不然即高極卷由逖窮綺里祇開喪
志之隙耳舍負郭而田甫田不以勞乎生
乎今之世反乎古之道不以倍乎故流水
之為物也不盈科不行君子之志於道也
===
不成章不達君子而欲斐然成章則吾黨
先進不可不論其世而尚友多識其前言
往行而畜德矣執事以江右雋傑言行表
見於我
朝者為問蓋以志尹學顏之業望諸生也愚
不敏往讀王子安滕王閣序其流連光景
模寫情狀吾無取焉獨於江藩形勢之盛
則攬結殆盡其曰星分翼軫翼軫鳥宿也
得文明之位矣曰地接衡廬衡岳宗廬山
punctuated:
君子之多識以畜德也，而通於今者尤□博古之助；君子之論世以尚友也，而求諸近者尤為遠覽之資。何則？遠近一心也，古今一理也。得其心與理，則近猶遠也，近篤而遠益可舉矣；今猶古也，今準而古益可酌矣。不然，即高極卷由，逖窮綺里，祇開喪志之隙耳。舍負郭而田甫田，不以勞乎？生乎今之世，反乎古之道，不以倍乎？故流水之為物也，不盈科不行；君子之志於道也，不成章不達。君子而欲斐然成章，則吾黨先進不可不論其世而尚友，多識其前言往行而畜德矣。
執事以江右雋傑言行表見於我朝者為問，蓋以志尹學顏之業望諸生也。愚不敏，往讀王子安《滕王閣序》，其流連光景、模寫情狀，吾無取焉。獨於江藩形勢之盛，則攬結殆盡。其曰「星分翼軫」，翼軫，鳥宿也，得文明之位矣；曰「地接衡廬」，衡，岳宗；廬山
translation_en:
The gentleman acquires broad knowledge to nurture his virtue, and understanding the present is especially □ an aid to comprehending antiquity. He considers the ages in which men lived so as to befriend the worthy of the past, and seeking among those nearer to him especially provides resources for surveying the distant past. Why? Those near and far share one mind; antiquity and the present share one principle. Once one grasps that mind and principle, the near is like the distant: with a firm grounding in the near, the distant becomes still easier to bring within reach. The present is like antiquity: with the present as a standard, antiquity becomes still easier to assess. Otherwise, even if one reaches upward as far as Juan and You [?], and searches into the remote past as far as Qili, one merely opens the way to losing one’s resolve. To abandon fields beside the city walls and cultivate vast fields afar—is this not to toil needlessly? To live in the present age yet revert to the ways of antiquity—is this not contrary to sound practice? Thus, flowing water does not advance until it has filled each hollow; the gentleman, setting his heart on the Way, does not attain further understanding until his learning has taken coherent form. If a gentleman wishes his learning to attain splendid, coherent form, he must consider the times of the predecessors of our own fellowship and befriend them, acquiring broad knowledge of their earlier words and deeds in order to nurture his virtue.
You, sir, have posed a question about outstanding men of Jiangyou whose words and deeds have distinguished them under our dynasty. Surely you expect us students to pursue the undertaking of aspiring to Yi Yin’s resolve and emulating Yan Hui’s learning. Slow-witted though I am, I once read Wang Zi’an’s Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng. I take nothing from its lingering over scenery and its depiction of feelings and circumstances. Yet it embraces almost completely the grandeur of the configuration and situation of Jiangxi. It says, “Its stellar divisions are Yi and Zhen.” Yi and Zhen are lunar lodges of the Vermilion Bird: thus it occupies a position of cultivated brilliance. It says, “Its lands adjoin Heng and Lu.” Heng is a chief among the sacred peaks; Mount Lu …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
鎮也神明和氣在焉曰襟三江而帶五湖
則馮夷陽侯所居實鍾靈秀曰控荆蠻而
引甌越則又見川原延袤寰宇寥廓而人
之生於其間者必皆疏暢洞達而非膚淺
狹小者矣故在晉則有若陶潛在漢則有
若徐穉在唐則有若李覯在宋元則有若
文天祥揭傒斯之數子者或以節義稱或
以文采著或以功業顯雖歷代之英不止
於此而此其最彰明者矣我
===
朝肇宇實汛胡元去穢德之氛復華夏之氣
文明之象也以
太祖之聖開混一之統煕洽之幾也則應五百
之運際風雲之會如元凱之於堯舜俊宅
之於文武寧無人耶矧吾江藩地靈人傑
素甲天下者耶嘗取列郡邑乗讀之每得
一人輒踊躍思奮恨未得與之遊而挹其
光霽又恨未得與之並立于朝而同寅協
恭也舉以語人則黨中一二長老猶歷歷
punctuated:
鎮也，神明和氣在焉。曰「襟三江而帶五湖」，則馮夷、陽侯所居，實鍾靈秀。曰「控荆蠻而引甌越」，則又見川原延袤，寰宇寥廓，而人之生於其間者，必皆疏暢洞達，而非膚淺狹小者矣。故在晉則有若陶潛，在漢則有若徐穉，在唐則有若李覯，在宋元則有若文天祥、揭傒斯之數子者，或以節義稱，或以文采著，或以功業顯。雖歷代之英不止於此，而此其最彰明者矣。
我朝肇宇，實汛胡元，去穢德之氛，復華夏之氣，文明之象也。以太祖之聖，開混一之統，煕洽之幾也。則應五百之運，際風雲之會，如元凱之於堯舜、俊宅之於文武，寧無人耶？矧吾江藩地靈人傑，素甲天下者耶？嘗取列郡邑乗讀之，每得一人，輒踊躍思奮，恨未得與之遊而挹其光霽，又恨未得與之並立于朝而同寅協恭也。舉以語人，則黨中一二長老猶歷歷
translation_en:
…is a guardian mountain; divine powers and harmonious energies reside there. When he says, “With the Three Rivers as its lapel and the Five Lakes as its girdle,” these are the dwelling places of Feng Yi and Yang Hou, the water deities, where numinous potency and natural excellence truly concentrate. When he says, “Commanding Jing and Man and drawing Ou and Yue toward it,” we see also the vast extent of its rivers and plains and the breadth of its horizons. Those born amid such surroundings must surely be open-minded and penetrating in understanding, rather than shallow and narrow. Thus, in the Jin there was Tao Qian; in the Han, Xu Zhi; in the Tang, Li Gou [?, who lived in the Song]; and in the Song and Yuan, men such as Wen Tianxiang and Jie Xisi. Some were renowned for integrity and righteousness, some distinguished by literary brilliance, and some eminent for their achievements. Although the outstanding men of successive ages were by no means limited to these, these are the most conspicuous examples.
When our dynasty established its dominion, it swept away [?] the alien Yuan, dispelled the foul atmosphere of corrupt virtue, and restored the vital spirit of Chinese civilization: this was a manifestation of cultural brilliance. Through the sagacity of Taizu, it inaugurated a unified imperial succession: this was the incipient promise of flourishing harmony. At such a conjunction of the five-hundred-year cycle and the auspicious meeting of wind and cloud, could there have been no men comparable to the Yuan and Kai under Yao and Shun, or the worthies in office [?] under Kings Wen and Wu? How much more must this be true of our Jiangxi, whose spiritually potent land and outstanding people have long ranked foremost in the realm! I have taken up and read the gazetteers of its prefectures and counties. Whenever I encountered one such man, I leapt with excitement and felt impelled to exert myself. I regretted that I had not been able to associate with him and imbibe the radiance of his character, like clear skies after rain; I regretted, too, that I had not been able to stand beside him at court, united in reverence and working together with respect. When I brought these men up in conversation, one or two elders in the community could still distinctly…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
道其事若目擊然無他居相近世不相遠
也故於泰和而得楊文貞士竒王文端直
焉於吉水而得周文襄忱於永新而得劉
文安定之焉於安福而得李文毅時勉劉
忠愍球劉南雄實焉於永豐而得鍾恭愍
同羅修撰倫焉於豐城於南昌於靖安崇
仁而得朱學士善胡祭酒儼况蘇州鍾吳
徵君與弼焉往秩宗楊文恪倣宋朝朱子
名臣言行錄為
===
皇明名臣言行錄自中山武寧王而下凡五十
有四人而文貞等十有三人與焉視彭司
寇所論賛更為詳悉今其書固在不可以
稽心術之微而驗行事之迹耶周禮大司
徒以建邦五典教萬民不啻足矣然必有
鄉師以掌其鄉之治教又有鄉大夫以攷
德行察道藝至於比閭族黨咸有師長胥
正焉無非欲其相觀而善相摩而成也故
曰吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易也張騫之
punctuated:
道其事，若目擊然。無他，居相近，世不相遠也。故於泰和而得楊文貞士竒、王文端直焉，於吉水而得周文襄忱，於永新而得劉文安定之焉，於安福而得李文毅時勉、劉忠愍球、劉南雄實焉，於永豐而得鍾恭愍同、羅修撰倫焉，於豐城、於南昌、於靖安、崇仁而得朱學士善、胡祭酒儼、况蘇州鍾、吳徵君與弼焉。往秩宗楊文恪倣宋朝朱子《名臣言行錄》，為《皇明名臣言行錄》，自中山武寧王而下，凡五十有四人，而文貞等十有三人與焉，視彭司寇所論賛更為詳悉。今其書固在，不可以稽心術之微而驗行事之迹耶？

《周禮》大司徒以建邦五典教萬民，不啻足矣，然必有鄉師以掌其鄉之治教，又有鄉大夫以攷德行、察道藝，至於比、閭、族、黨，咸有師、長、胥、正焉，無非欲其相觀而善，相摩而成也。故曰：「吾觀於鄉，而知王道之易易也。」張騫之
translation_en:
…recounted their deeds as though they had witnessed them themselves. The reason was simply that they lived near one another and were not far apart in time. Thus, in Taihe I found Yang Shiqi, posthumously titled Wenzhen, and Wang Zhi, posthumously titled Wenduan; in Jishui, Zhou Chen, posthumously titled Wenxiang; in Yongxin, Liu Dingzhi, posthumously titled Wen’an; in Anfu, Li Shimian, posthumously titled Wenyi, Liu Qiu, posthumously titled Zhongmin, and Liu Shi, Prefect of Nanxiong; and in Yongfeng, Zhong Tong, posthumously titled Gongmin, and Senior Compiler Luo Lun. In Fengcheng, Nanchang, Jing’an, and Chongren I found Academician Zhu Shan, Chancellor Hu Yan, Kuang Zhong, Prefect of Suzhou, and Wu Yubi, the scholar summoned to office. Formerly, Yang, posthumously titled Wenke, the Minister of Rites, modeled his Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers of the August Ming on Master Zhu’s Song-dynasty Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers. Beginning with the Prince of Zhongshan, posthumously titled Wuning, it included fifty-four men in all, among whom were Wenzhen and the other twelve men just named. It was still more detailed than the discussions and appraisals by Peng, the Minister of Justice. That book remains available today. Can we not use it to investigate the subtleties of their moral intentions and examine the traces of their conduct?

In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education teaches all the people through the five cardinal teachings by which the state is established. This is surely more than sufficient. Yet there must also be Township Preceptors to oversee government and instruction in their townships, and Township Grand Masters to assess virtuous conduct and examine understanding of the Way and mastery of the arts. Down through the neighborhood groupings—the bi, lü, zu, and dang—all have their preceptors, heads, assistants, and chiefs. The purpose throughout is that people should become good by observing one another and achieve maturity by mutually refining one another. Thus it is said: “When I observe the township, I understand how very easy the kingly Way is to practice.” As for Zhang Qian’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
窮河源也自豐水始未有不渡豐水而能
窮河源者也夸父之隨日而步也自嵎夷
始未有不由嵎夷而能隨日者也故遠有
所慕者必近有所遺明珠在懷而索之途
則亦左矣故凡鄉之賢士大夫不可不考
而知之則而象之也自今言之歷事
四朝卓然而弘輔相之業者文貞也巡撫三吳
淵然而裕
國計之大者文襄也胡李拜祭酒胡則身率
===
諸生成均翕然以從化李則教倣安定胄
子勃然而興起非辟雝之良範耶朱劉居
翰林朱則掌制校文不負乃祖令器之許
劉則三疏百首無忝八面受敵之才非瀛
洲之妙選耶文端首正奔競之習鳴朝陽
之鳳也彝正抗論起復之非攖龍鱗之雄
也恭愍作柱史而議揭三綱忠肝義膽貫
日月矣忠愍為侍講而條陳十事奇氣疎
節凌漢霄矣守蘇州而剛毅正直有張詠
punctuated:
窮河源也，自豐水始，未有不渡豐水而能窮河源者也。夸父之隨日而步也，自嵎夷始，未有不由嵎夷而能隨日者也。故遠有所慕者，必近有所遺。明珠在懷而索之途，則亦左矣。故凡鄉之賢士大夫，不可不考而知之，則而象之也。
自今言之，歷事四朝，卓然而弘輔相之業者，文貞也；巡撫三吳，淵然而裕國計之大者，文襄也。胡李拜祭酒，胡則身率諸生，成均翕然以從化；李則教倣安定，胄子勃然而興起，非辟雝之良範耶？朱劉居翰林，朱則掌制校文，不負乃祖令器之許；劉則三疏百首，無忝八面受敵之才，非瀛洲之妙選耶？文端首正奔競之習，鳴朝陽之鳳也；彝正抗論起復之非，攖龍鱗之雄也。恭愍作柱史，而議揭三綱，忠肝義膽貫日月矣；忠愍為侍講，而條陳十事，奇氣疎節凌漢霄矣。守蘇州而剛毅正直，有張詠
translation_en:
…in tracing the river to its source, began at the Feng River. No one has ever reached that source without crossing the Feng River. When Kuafu strode in pursuit of the sun, he began at Yuyi; no one has ever pursued the sun without passing through Yuyi. Thus, one who admires something distant is bound to overlook something nearby. To carry a bright pearl in one’s bosom yet search for it along the road is surely misguided. Therefore, we must investigate and learn about the worthy scholars and officials of our own locality, taking them as standards and emulating them.
Speaking of those relevant to us today: Wenzhen served through four reigns, outstandingly advancing the work of ministerial assistance to the throne; Wenxiang served as Grand Coordinator of the Three Wu region, with profound ability amply providing for the great needs of state finance. Hu and Li were appointed Libationers. Hu personally led the students, and the National University united in responding to his transforming influence; Li modeled his teaching on Anding, and the sons of the elite rose eagerly to their studies. Were these not excellent exemplars for the imperial college? Zhu and Liu served in the Hanlin Academy. Zhu drafted imperial pronouncements and evaluated compositions, living up to his grandfather’s appraisal of him as a man of outstanding promise; Liu, with his three memorials and hundred poems, proved worthy of his talent for meeting challenges from every direction. Were these not superb choices for Yingzhou, the isle of immortals—a figure for the Hanlin Academy? Wenduan took the lead in correcting the habit of scrambling for advancement: he was a phoenix singing toward the morning sun. Yizheng boldly argued against the impropriety of recalling officials to service during mourning: he was a hero who dared brush against the dragon’s scales. Gongmin served as a Censor, and his arguments upheld the Three Bonds; his loyal heart and righteous courage shone through the sun and moon. Zhongmin served as an Expositor-in-waiting and set forth ten matters in a memorial; his extraordinary spirit and lofty integrity soared above the Milky Way and the heavens. Governing Suzhou with firmness, resolve, uprightness, and integrity, possessing Zhang Yong’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之遺風非況伯律耶知南雄而耿介清貧
如范丹之寒素非劉嘉秀耶乃若厭舉子
之業鄙箋註之繁聘之以幣帛則應授之
以官職則辭則又吳子傅也玆惟十有三
人或嘉猷茂績足以尊主而庇民或行修
言道足以垂世而立教或危辭崇論足以
正君而善俗或清風高誼足以起懦而廉
頑譬之瑤琨球琳爲體不同均爲和氏之
需矣楩楠杞梓爲材不同均爲大匠之用
===
矣抑聞心者身之本也家者國之本也未
有幼不學而壯能行者也未有不修之于
家而能達之於天子之庭者也夷攷文貞
諸君子美質性成茂才夙稟蓋湖山江岳
之秀有以助天施地生之秀故迥然出類
磊落不羣有年方髫齔卽通舉業而爲子
弟師者有聰穎不弄十歲通經銳然自任
聖賢之學者有博極羣書旁通醫卜閒居
講求性命之理者有少年登科自陳願學
punctuated:
之遺風，非況伯律耶？知南雄而耿介清貧，如范丹之寒素，非劉嘉秀耶？乃若厭舉子之業，鄙箋註之繁，聘之以幣帛則應，授之以官職則辭，則又吳子傅也。玆惟十有三人，或嘉猷茂績，足以尊主而庇民；或行修言道，足以垂世而立教；或危辭崇論，足以正君而善俗；或清風高誼，足以起懦而廉頑。譬之瑤琨球琳，爲體不同，均爲和氏之需矣；楩楠杞梓，爲材不同，均爲大匠之用矣。

抑聞心者身之本也，家者國之本也。未有幼不學而壯能行者也，未有不修之于家而能達之於天子之庭者也。夷攷文貞諸君子，美質性成，茂才夙稟，蓋湖山江岳之秀，有以助天施地生之秀，故迥然出類，磊落不羣。有年方髫齔，卽通舉業而爲子弟師者；有聰穎不弄，十歲通經，銳然自任聖賢之學者；有博極羣書，旁通醫卜，閒居講求性命之理者；有少年登科，自陳願學
translation_en:
…the legacy of his exemplary conduct—was this not Kuang Bolü? Serving as prefect of Nanxiong, upright and incorruptible, living in honest poverty like Fan Dan—was this not Liu Jiaxiu? Then there was one who wearied of examination studies and disdained the profusion of textual annotations: when invited with gifts of silk, he responded; when offered official appointment, he declined. This was Wu Zifu. These thirteen men possessed, variously, excellent counsels and outstanding achievements sufficient to honor their sovereign and shelter the people; cultivated conduct and words expressing the Way sufficient to instruct posterity and establish moral teaching; fearless speech and lofty arguments sufficient to rectify their ruler and improve popular customs; or pure integrity and exalted righteousness sufficient to rouse the timid and make the avaricious honest. They may be compared to the precious jades yao, kun, qiu, and lin: different in substance, yet all sought by jade connoisseurs like Mr. He. Or to the timbers pian, nan, qi, and zi: different in their qualities, yet all useful to a master carpenter.

I have also heard that the heart is the foundation of the person, and the family the foundation of the state. Never has someone who failed to learn in youth been able to put learning into practice in maturity; never has someone who failed to cultivate himself within his family been able to extend that cultivation to the Son of Heaven’s court. Examining Wenzhen and these other gentlemen, we find that their fine qualities were inherent in their natures and their abundant talents endowed from early life. Surely the finest influences of lakes and mountains, rivers and peaks helped nurture the excellence bestowed by Heaven and brought forth by Earth. Thus they stood far above their peers, openhearted and exceptional. Some, while still children with hanging forelocks and shedding their milk teeth, already mastered examination studies and taught the younger members of their families. Some were intelligent and disinclined to play, understood the Classics at ten, and resolutely took the learning of the sages and worthies as their own responsibility. Some ranged widely through the whole body of literature, also understood medicine and divination, and in retirement investigated the principles of human nature and destiny. Some passed the examinations while young and personally declared their wish to study…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而來有志之許者有少負大志書無不讀
而窮道德之奥者有奉親盡懽居喪盡禮
而昆仲同居無間言者有自幼端重異於
常兒而家貧力學苦好學者有起家從事
而無異儒流者有計偕京師而不見達官
者有年方十九而一見聖學心竊慨慕者
有天資絕倫而過目輒誦不違父教者有
飽庭訓踐孝友而忠義有根基者有性慷
慨面斥人而遇事無回避者惟其幼而學
===
也心行足以自立故其壯而行也德業足
以成名修之于家也有隱居求志之功故
施之于國也有行義達道之效在當時為
一時之人望在後世為百世之師模雖不
敢謂夔龍臯益伊呂周召之復生而視蕭
曹丙魏房杜姚宋諸人則遠過矣今夫莫
為之前無以彰其美莫為之後無以續其
傳使楊劉諸君子而無足法焉諸君子之
罪也諸君子足法而人莫之法焉咎孰執
punctuated:
而來有志之許者；有少負大志，書無不讀，而窮道德之奥者；有奉親盡懽，居喪盡禮，而昆仲同居無間言者；有自幼端重，異於常兒，而家貧力學苦好學者；有起家從事，而無異儒流者；有計偕京師，而不見達官者；有年方十九，而一見聖學，心竊慨慕者；有天資絕倫，而過目輒誦，不違父教者；有飽庭訓，踐孝友，而忠義有根基者；有性慷慨，面斥人，而遇事無回避者。惟其幼而學也，心行足以自立，故其壯而行也，德業足以成名；修之于家也，有隱居求志之功，故施之于國也，有行義達道之效。在當時為一時之人望，在後世為百世之師模。雖不敢謂夔龍臯益伊呂周召之復生，而視蕭曹丙魏房杜姚宋諸人，則遠過矣。
今夫莫為之前，無以彰其美；莫為之後，無以續其傳。使楊劉諸君子而無足法焉，諸君子之罪也；諸君子足法，而人莫之法焉，咎孰執
translation_en:
…and thereby earned praise as a man of aspiration. Some cherished great ambitions from youth, read every kind of book, and plumbed the mysteries of the Way and virtue. Some brought their parents every happiness, observed the mourning rites fully, and lived together with their brothers without a word of discord. Some were upright and grave from childhood, unlike ordinary children, and, though their families were poor, applied themselves strenuously and devotedly to learning. Some entered official service from private life yet were no different from Confucian scholars. Some traveled to the capital as examination candidates but did not visit high officials. Some, at only nineteen, first encountered the learning of the sages and inwardly felt a profound admiration for it. Some possessed incomparable natural gifts, could recite whatever they had once read, and never disobeyed their fathers’ teachings. Some were steeped in paternal instruction and practiced filial piety and brotherly affection, laying firm foundations for loyalty and righteousness. Some were spirited and forthright, rebuked others to their faces, and never shirked when matters arose.
Because they learned in youth, their dispositions and conduct enabled them to stand on their own; thus, when they put their learning into practice in adulthood, their virtue and achievements sufficed to establish their reputations. In cultivating themselves at home, they accomplished the work of living in retirement to pursue their aspirations; thus, when they applied themselves to the service of the state, they achieved the results of practicing righteousness and giving effect to the Way. In their own time they commanded the esteem of their contemporaries; for later ages they became exemplary teachers for a hundred generations. Though we dare not call them Kui, Long, Gao Yao, Yi, Yi Yin, Lü Shang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao reborn, they far surpassed such men as Xiao He, Cao Shen, Bing Ji, Wei Xiang, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yao Chong, and Song Jing.
Now, without predecessors, there would be no means of bringing their excellence to light; without successors, there would be no means of carrying on their tradition. If Yang, Liu, and the other gentlemen offered nothing worthy of emulation, the fault would be theirs. But if these gentlemen are worthy of emulation and no one emulates them, who bears the blame…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
哉或曰周公思兼禹湯仲尼祖述堯舜拘
方徇俗者曲士之見也博諮遠訪者達人
之觀也故一鄉一國不足以盡友古人之
道必欲其與稽以宇宙内事莫非分内事
也愚則以為不然子賤之成德由魯國之
多賢孟子之學孔以鄒魯之甚近彼誠見
古今一理遠近一心學孔子即所以學堯
舜而師魯國之多賢即所以師文王惟其
人不惟其古今則師今者法古之漸也惟
===
其賢不惟其遠近則自邇者行遠之漸也
故愚於備萬而取其孝於若思而取其勤
於文貞而取其達於恂如而取其量於文
毅而取其正於求樂而取其直於行儉而
取其剛於蘇州而取其明於南雄而取其
廉於徵士而取其恬於主靜而取其敏於
世京而取其忠於彛正則又取其有仁者
之勇焉然方有志進取乃所願則學彛正
矣學彛正而文貞諸君子可學也學文貞
punctuated:
哉？或曰：「周公思兼禹湯，仲尼祖述堯舜。拘方徇俗者，曲士之見也；博諮遠訪者，達人之觀也。故一鄉一國不足以盡友古人之道，必欲其與稽，以宇宙内事莫非分内事也。」愚則以為不然。子賤之成德，由魯國之多賢；孟子之學孔，以鄒魯之甚近。彼誠見古今一理，遠近一心。學孔子，即所以學堯舜；而師魯國之多賢，即所以師文王。惟其人，不惟其古今，則師今者法古之漸也；惟其賢，不惟其遠近，則自邇者行遠之漸也。
故愚於備萬而取其孝，於若思而取其勤，於文貞而取其達，於恂如而取其量，於文毅而取其正，於求樂而取其直，於行儉而取其剛，於蘇州而取其明，於南雄而取其廉，於徵士而取其恬，於主靜而取其敏，於世京而取其忠，於彛正則又取其有仁者之勇焉。然方有志進取，乃所願則學彛正矣。學彛正而文貞諸君子可學也，學文貞
translation_en:
…indeed? Someone says: “The Duke of Zhou sought to unite the achievements of Yu and Tang; Zhongni followed and transmitted the ways of Yao and Shun. Confinement to one locality and compliance with its customs reflect the outlook of a narrow scholar; broad consultation and inquiries far afield reflect the vision of a person of wide understanding. Thus, one district or one state cannot exhaust the way of befriending the ancients. One must extend one’s inquiries [?], for nothing within the universe lies outside one’s own responsibilities.” I humbly disagree. Zijian perfected his virtue because the state of Lu had many worthy men; Mengzi learned from Kongzi because Zou and Lu were so close. They truly understood that past and present share one principle, and that people near and far share one heart. Learning from Kongzi is precisely how one learns from Yao and Shun; taking the many worthy men of Lu as teachers is precisely how one takes King Wen as a teacher. If we attend to the person, regardless of whether he belongs to antiquity or the present, taking contemporaries as teachers becomes a gradual approach to emulating the ancients. If we attend to his worthiness, regardless of whether he is far or near, beginning nearby becomes a gradual approach to journeying far.
Thus, I take Beiwan as my example in filial devotion; Ruosi, in diligence; Wenzhen, in discernment; Xunru, in magnanimity; Wenyi, in uprightness; Qiule, in frankness; Xingjian, in firmness; Suzhou, in clear judgment; Nanxiong, in incorruptibility; the Recruited Scholar, in tranquility; Zhujing, in quickness of action; and Shijing, in loyalty. From Yizheng, moreover, I take the courage of a benevolent man. Yet, as I now aspire to advance, my wish is to learn from Yizheng. By learning from Yizheng, I can learn from Wenzhen and the other gentlemen; by learning from Wenzhen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸君子而靖節孺子盱江文山可學也學
靖節孺子盱江文山而夔龍臯益伊傅周
孔可學也執事以爲然否
第五問
廖如春
同考試官教諭袁批人養食蓄盡之矣窮此策盡之
同考試官教授蔣批識時務者俊傑非子耶
考試官教諭何批自是不易之論
考試官教諭錢批指畫犁然佳士也
===
用兵無一定之法制馭者貴乎妙通變之
宜養兵有一定之規經略者貴乎得推行
之利何則兵有行於一時之權者不能以
無利也而非其所可恃也食有出於經常
之計者不容以易盈也而非其所可緩也
苟當其有事而不征調則無以備倉卒之
虞及其無事而不撙節則無以應供億之
費故善用兵者隨時以通其變使緩急有
頼不失夫先事之防善理財者酌古以準
punctuated:
諸君子，而靖節、孺子、盱江、文山可學也。學靖節、孺子、盱江、文山，而夔、龍、臯、益、伊、傅、周、孔可學也。執事以爲然否？

第五問
廖如春
同考試官教諭袁批：「人養食蓄，盡之矣。窮此策，盡之。」
同考試官教授蔣批：「識時務者俊傑，非子耶？」
考試官教諭何批：「自是不易之論。」
考試官教諭錢批：「指畫犁然，佳士也。」

用兵無一定之法，制馭者貴乎妙通變之宜；養兵有一定之規，經略者貴乎得推行之利。何則？兵有行於一時之權者，不能以無利也，而非其所可恃也；食有出於經常之計者，不容以易盈也，而非其所可緩也。苟當其有事而不征調，則無以備倉卒之虞；及其無事而不撙節，則無以應供億之費。故善用兵者，隨時以通其變，使緩急有頼，不失夫先事之防；善理財者，酌古以準
translation_en:
…these gentlemen, and one can learn to emulate Jingjie, Ruzi, Xujiang, and Wenshan. By learning to emulate Jingjie, Ruzi, Xujiang, and Wenshan, one can learn to emulate Kui, Long, Gao, Yi, Yi, Fu, Zhou, and Kong. Do you, honored sir, consider this so?

Fifth Question
Liao Ruchun
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “Men maintained and provisions stored: this covers everything. Pursue this policy essay to its limits, and all is covered [?].”
Associate Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “One who understands the affairs of the times is an outstanding man—is that not you?”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “This is indeed an argument that cannot be overturned.”
Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: “His proposals are lucidly laid out: a fine scholar indeed.”

There is no fixed method for employing troops; those who command them must prize a subtle grasp of how best to adapt to changing circumstances. There are fixed rules for maintaining troops; those who plan and administer military affairs must prize the benefits of putting these rules into practice. Why is this? Military operations involve expedients suited to a particular moment: these cannot be without benefit, yet they are not what one can rely upon. Provisions come from regular, continuing arrangements: they cannot be regarded as easily made abundant [?], nor can they be treated as a matter admitting delay. If troops are not levied and mobilized when trouble arises, there will be no means of preparing against sudden dangers. If expenditure is not restrained when there is no trouble, there will be no means of meeting the costs of supply. Thus, those skilled in employing troops adapt to changes as circumstances demand, ensuring that there is something to rely upon in ordinary times and emergencies alike, without neglecting advance precautions. Those skilled in managing finances weigh the practices of antiquity in order to establish a standard for…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
夫今使上下相安適得夫恒足之道知乎
此可與言兵食矣執事發策而以是下問
爲地方慮至深切也敢不悉心以對昔者
聖人之作易也觀象於坤上坎下之卦而
名之曰師孔子因而傳之曰地中有水師
君子以容民畜衆蓋古者寓兵於農伏至
險於大順藏不測於至靜之中民以養兵
兵以衛民斯二者相有而不可以相無相
資而非所以相病也考之周禮以鄉遂出
===
兵以九法治兵則兵出於賦而先王治兵
之法莫有善於此矣貢民以九式斂民以
九賦則賦出於田而先王理財之法莫有
要於此矣自夫兵甲之制作而期門羽林
府兵彍騎之名日益以多天下始困於兵
稅畝之法立而榷茶榷鹽筭緡筭車之數
日益以煩天下始困於食法之不競而治
之不古有由然也我
祖宗創制立法軍雖分隸於衛所復立萬戶府
punctuated: 夫今，使上下相安，適得夫恒足之道。知乎此，可與言兵食矣。執事發策而以是下問，爲地方慮至深切也，敢不悉心以對？昔者聖人之作《易》也，觀象於坤上坎下之卦，而名之曰「師」。孔子因而傳之曰：「地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。」蓋古者寓兵於農，伏至險於大順，藏不測於至靜之中，民以養兵，兵以衛民。斯二者相有而不可以相無，相資而非所以相病也。考之《周禮》，以鄉遂出兵，以九法治兵，則兵出於賦，而先王治兵之法莫有善於此矣。貢民以九式，斂民以九賦，則賦出於田，而先王理財之法莫有要於此矣。自夫兵甲之制作，而期門、羽林、府兵、彍騎之名日益以多，天下始困於兵；稅畝之法立，而榷茶、榷鹽、筭緡、筭車之數日益以煩，天下始困於食。法之不競而治之不古，有由然也。我祖宗創制立法，軍雖分隸於衛所，復立萬戶府
translation_en:
…present circumstances, enabling those above and below to live in mutual harmony and thereby attaining the way to enduring sufficiency. Whoever understands this may be consulted about troops and provisions. In setting this policy question and asking about these matters, you show the deepest concern for the region. How could I fail to devote my whole attention to answering?

When the sage composed the Book of Changes, he contemplated the image of the hexagram with Kun above and Kan below and named it “The Army.” Confucius accordingly commented upon it: “Within the earth there is water: The Army. Thus the noble man shelters the people and nurtures the multitude.” In antiquity, soldiers were embedded among the farmers: the utmost danger lay concealed within the utmost compliance, and the unfathomable was hidden within perfect stillness. The people supported the troops, and the troops protected the people. These two depended upon one another and could not exist apart; they sustained one another rather than causing one another distress.

Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that troops were supplied by the townships and outer districts and governed through nine methods. Thus troops came from the levies, and no method by which the former kings administered troops surpassed this. The people's contributions were regulated through nine expenditure formulas [?], and collections from the people through nine levies. Thus revenue came from the fields, and no method by which the former kings managed finances was more essential than this.

Once military institutions were established, however, formations bearing such names as the Qimen Guards, Yulin Guards, militia troops (fubing), and expanded cavalry (kuoqi) multiplied daily, and the realm began to suffer under the burden of troops. Once taxation by the mu of land was instituted, the exactions from tea and salt monopolies, taxes on merchants' capital, and taxes on vehicles became ever more complicated, and the realm began to suffer under the burden of provisioning. There were reasons why the laws lost their efficacy and government ceased to follow ancient practice.

Our imperial ancestors created institutions and established laws. Although troops were assigned to guards and battalions, they additionally established myriarchies…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以簡民兵田因則壤以起科復立丁田法
以徵工食以其所徵之食養其所簡之兵
隨操於無事之時效用於有事之日其法
十年一編悉取民間少壯以充其選是卽
寓兵於農之意也夫何法久弊滋民兵之
制猶昔也而審編不慎則老弱者得以參
雜其間况團操之法久矣不行聞金皷則
心悸見旌旗則目眩矣安在其爲足兵工
食之徵猶昔也而催科不嚴則攬泊者得
===
以漁獵其利况豪猾之徒閔不知畏追呼
之則卽逋拘係之則待斃矣安在其爲足
食惟民兵之不可恃故盜賊之起不免於
募兵惟軍餉之不易足故征調之際不免
於借辦此兵食之所以俱困也江右承平
日久民不知兵邇者吳楚閩粤之間山箐
溪峒之頑乘間竊發往歲流突臨吉諸郡
已不勝其荼毒賴我
皇上軫念東南特命撫臣出師勦滅
punctuated:
以簡民兵，田因則壤以起科，復立丁田法以徵工食，以其所徵之食養其所簡之兵，隨操於無事之時，效用於有事之日。其法十年一編，悉取民間少壯以充其選，是卽寓兵於農之意也。夫何法久弊滋！民兵之制猶昔也，而審編不慎，則老弱者得以參雜其間。况團操之法久矣不行，聞金皷則心悸，見旌旗則目眩矣，安在其爲足兵？工食之徵猶昔也，而催科不嚴，則攬泊者得以漁獵其利。况豪猾之徒閔不知畏，追呼之則卽逋，拘係之則待斃矣，安在其爲足食？惟民兵之不可恃，故盜賊之起不免於募兵；惟軍餉之不易足，故征調之際不免於借辦。此兵食之所以俱困也。
江右承平日久，民不知兵。邇者吳楚閩粤之間，山箐溪峒之頑乘間竊發，往歲流突臨吉諸郡，已不勝其荼毒。賴我皇上軫念東南，特命撫臣出師勦滅。
translation_en:
…to select militiamen. Taxes on fields were assessed according to the quality of the soil, and a further system of levies on adult males and land was established to collect funds for service rations. The provisions thus collected supported the men thus selected: they attended drills in peaceful times and rendered service when trouble arose. Under this system, enrollment was revised once every ten years, drawing on the young and able-bodied among the people to fill the ranks. This embodied the principle of lodging the soldiery within the farming population. Yet how abuses have multiplied as these arrangements have aged! The militia system remains as before, but careless scrutiny of the rolls allows the old and weak to mingle among its ranks. Moreover, organized drills have long fallen into disuse: the men’s hearts tremble at the sound of gongs and drums, and their eyes grow dizzy at the sight of banners. How can this provide sufficient troops? The levies for service rations remain as before, but lax enforcement of tax collection allows tax-collection intermediaries [?] to prey upon the proceeds. Moreover, powerful and cunning men know no fear [?]: when pursued and summoned, they promptly abscond; when detained, they merely await death. How can this provide sufficient provisions? Precisely because the militia cannot be relied upon, troops must be recruited whenever bandits rise; precisely because military funds are difficult to make sufficient, borrowing and makeshift financing become unavoidable whenever troops are mobilized. This is why both troops and provisions are in such straits.
Jiangyou has enjoyed peace for many years, and its people know nothing of warfare. Recently, malefactors from the mountain thickets and streamside valleys of Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue have seized opportunities to rise in revolt. In past years they swept into the prefectures of Linjiang, Ji’an, and elsewhere, inflicting unbearable suffering. Fortunately, our Emperor, mindful of the southeast, specially ordered the Grand Coordinator to dispatch troops and exterminate them…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
玄威神武汛掃廓清起瘡痍之民而置之衽席
之上固皆遊於熈皥之天矣然猶思患預
防隨事為制建中營於省會而以遊擊領
之以待東西之應援建東營於南豐而以
參將領之以固吳楚之門戶建西營於萬
安而以守備領之以控閩粤之襟喉設險
守固靡不悉至誠有不戰而屈人兵先聲
而褫虜魄者矣但各營召募類非土著以
之戍守則歲月之無期餽之糧餉恐供億
===
之難繼故愚以為禦寇而藉召募之兵則
寇未至而我益勞守望而資土著之民則
寇可待而我常逸昔人云屯兵十年五年
無益言靡濫之可惜也又曰養兵十萬五
萬可去言老弱之當汰也為今之計不必
易民而教之也特教之者無其素耳誠能
於精常二兵慎其揀選汰其老弱而後畀
之閫帥使之更番操練專委任以責成之
則人人皆壯勇也何患乎兵之不足也哉
punctuated:
玄威神武，汛掃廓清，起瘡痍之民而置之衽席之上，固皆遊於熈皥之天矣。然猶思患預防，隨事為制：建中營於省會，而以遊擊領之，以待東西之應援；建東營於南豐，而以參將領之，以固吳楚之門戶；建西營於萬安，而以守備領之，以控閩粤之襟喉。設險守固，靡不悉至，誠有不戰而屈人兵、先聲而褫虜魄者矣。但各營召募類非土著，以之戍守，則歲月之無期；餽之糧餉，恐供億之難繼。
故愚以為，禦寇而藉召募之兵，則寇未至而我益勞；守望而資土著之民，則寇可待而我常逸。昔人云：「屯兵十年，五年無益。」言靡濫之可惜也。又曰：「養兵十萬，五萬可去。」言老弱之當汰也。為今之計，不必易民而教之也，特教之者無其素耳。誠能於精常二兵慎其揀選，汰其老弱，而後畀之閫帥，使之更番操練，專委任以責成之，則人人皆壯勇也，何患乎兵之不足也哉！
translation_en:
…With august might and divine martial prowess, they swept away the disorder and restored peace, raising the afflicted people and settling them upon comfortable bedding. All indeed now live beneath a heaven of radiant harmony. Yet precautions against future troubles were still taken, and arrangements made as circumstances required: a central camp was established at the provincial capital under a Mobile Corps Commander, ready to provide support to east and west; an eastern camp was established at Nanfeng under a Regional Commander, to secure the gateway to Wu and Chu; and a western camp was established at Wan’an under a Commandant, to control the strategic approaches to Min and Yue. Every measure for establishing defenses at strategic points and holding them securely was thoroughly implemented. Truly, these dispositions could subdue an enemy’s troops without battle and rob the foe of courage through their reputation alone. Yet those recruited into the various camps are mostly not local inhabitants. If employed as garrison troops, their service has no foreseeable end; if supplied with provisions and pay, it is feared that these supplies will prove difficult to sustain.
Thus, in my humble judgment, if we rely on recruited troops to repel bandits, we become increasingly exhausted before the bandits even arrive; if we rely on local inhabitants to keep watch, we can await the bandits while remaining at ease. A man of old said: “Of ten years of maintaining troops in garrison, five yield no benefit.” This speaks of the regrettable waste and excess. He also said: “Of a hundred thousand troops maintained, fifty thousand could be discharged.” This means that the old and weak should be weeded out. For our present purposes, there is no need to replace the men in order to train them; it is simply that those responsible for their training have provided no regular preparation. If careful selection could be made among the elite and regular troops, removing the old and weak, and the remainder then entrusted to military commanders to drill in rotation, with those commanders given full responsibility and held accountable for results, every man would be strong and brave. Why then worry that the troops are insufficient?

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不必加賦而益之也特賦之者無其術耳
誠能於額編工食取之有時用之有節而
實惠於民兵毋令冒破虛耗督逋負而禁
絕之則時時有糗糒也何患乎食之不足
也哉夫如是而議銷兵則召募之衆可以
漸而遣也如是而議畜儲則汰兵之積可
以漸而盈也古之人深知兵食之不容已
而又不可以相離也趙充國賦田臨羌以
待先零之弊諸葛孔明雜耕渭濱以省成
===
都之運此役諸有籍之兵也今之田隸於
衞而屯屬於軍民兵雖欲屯其可得乎曹
瑋以閒田募弓弩手而為前鋒黃好謙以
田募民保甲而代強壯此役諸無業之民
也今之地無遺利而民無遺力募兵雖欲
耕其可得乎惟保甲之法歷世可行而團
練之制庶幾有合誠能考其故而見諸行
則民不改聚而少壯可使兵不出鄉而行
伍可成較藝於平日使之各精其能而後
punctuated:
不必加賦而益之也，特賦之者無其術耳。誠能於額編工食，取之有時，用之有節，而實惠於民兵，毋令冒破虛耗，督逋負而禁絕之，則時時有糗糒也，何患乎食之不足也哉？夫如是而議銷兵，則召募之衆可以漸而遣也；如是而議畜儲，則汰兵之積可以漸而盈也。
古之人深知兵食之不容已，而又不可以相離也。趙充國賦田臨羌，以待先零之弊；諸葛孔明雜耕渭濱，以省成都之運，此役諸有籍之兵也。今之田隸於衞，而屯屬於軍，民兵雖欲屯，其可得乎？曹瑋以閒田募弓弩手而為前鋒，黃好謙以田募民保甲而代強壯，此役諸無業之民也。今之地無遺利，而民無遺力，募兵雖欲耕，其可得乎？惟保甲之法，歷世可行，而團練之制，庶幾有合。誠能考其故而見諸行，則民不改聚而少壯可使，兵不出鄉而行伍可成。較藝於平日，使之各精其能，而後
translation_en:
There is no need to increase taxes to augment provisions; it is simply that those who levy them lack the proper methods. If the funds budgeted for wages and provisions were collected at appropriate times, spent with restraint, and actually used to benefit the militia, with fraudulent charges and waste prevented and arrears pursued and eliminated, there would always be dry rations. Why worry that provisions would be insufficient? Under these conditions, if we considered reducing the troops, the recruited forces could gradually be discharged; if we considered building reserves, the savings from reducing the troops could gradually fill the stores.
The ancients understood well that neither soldiers nor provisions could be dispensed with, and that the two could not be separated. Zhao Chongguo allotted fields at Linqiang to await the exhaustion of the Xianling Qiang; Zhuge Kongming had his soldiers cultivate land among the inhabitants along the Wei River to reduce transport from Chengdu. These measures employed soldiers enrolled on military registers. Today, the fields belong to the guards, and the military agricultural colonies belong to the regular troops. Even if the militia wished to farm such colonies, could they do so? Cao Wei used idle fields to recruit bowmen and crossbowmen as a vanguard; Huang Haoqian used fields to recruit commoners into the baojia communal security organization in place of the able-bodied militia. These measures employed commoners without a livelihood. Today, no productive capacity of the land remains untapped, and the people have no labor to spare. Even if recruited soldiers wished to cultivate land, could they do so? Only the baojia system is practicable across successive ages, and the system of organizing and training local militia comes close to matching it. If we could investigate its precedents and put them into practice, the young and able-bodied could be employed without moving people from their settlements, and military ranks could be formed without soldiers leaving their home districts. Let their skills be tested in ordinary times, so that each perfects his abilities, and then …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
試用於臨時使之各効其力養之者雖不
出於屯田而意師夫古賦之者雖不出於
九則而制宜於今則戰守皆精壯而不食
無用之人軍餉有常經而不給無名之費
養之精而士氣作強銳足以禦侮矣節其
財而民力裕富庶足以供輸矣通變之宜
推行之利不外乎此又何待於加賦以足
用加募以振威哉抑又有說焉軍餉之需
已有定法江右土瘠民貧他無可以裨益
===
者吾不得而議之矣但團操之法講求蓋
已有年而迄無成效何哉訓練者不得其
人故也必欲撤遣召募而資藉團練可不
擇官以任之乎蓋田野之民一旦驅而之
戰非其所便習者況力有強弱稟有知愚
善教者本之孝弟忠信以啓其良繼之坐
作進退以示其法與之弓矢甲胄以利其
器懸之號令賞罰以鼓其趨使之久而安
焉習而化焉如饑之欲食如寒之欲衣就
punctuated: 試用於臨時，使之各効其力。養之者雖不出於屯田，而意師夫古；賦之者雖不出於九則，而制宜於今。則戰守皆精壯，而不食無用之人；軍餉有常經，而不給無名之費。養之精而士氣作，強銳足以禦侮矣；節其財而民力裕，富庶足以供輸矣。通變之宜、推行之利，不外乎此，又何待於加賦以足用、加募以振威哉？抑又有說焉：軍餉之需，已有定法。江右土瘠民貧，他無可以裨益者，吾不得而議之矣。但團操之法，講求蓋已有年，而迄無成效，何哉？訓練者不得其人故也。必欲撤遣召募，而資藉團練，可不擇官以任之乎？蓋田野之民，一旦驅而之戰，非其所便習者；況力有強弱，稟有知愚。善教者，本之孝弟忠信以啓其良，繼之坐作進退以示其法，與之弓矢甲胄以利其器，懸之號令賞罰以鼓其趨，使之久而安焉，習而化焉，如饑之欲食，如寒之欲衣，就
translation_en:
…put them to the test when the occasion arises, so that each may exert his strength. Although their maintenance would not come from military agricultural colonies, its intent would follow antiquity; although the levies for their support would not derive from the Nine Principles of taxation, the arrangements would suit present circumstances. Those fighting and defending would thus all be fit and strong, and no useless men would be fed. Military provisioning would follow established rules, and no expenditure without a legitimate purpose would be funded. With proper maintenance, the soldiers’ spirit would rise, and their strength and resolve would suffice to repel aggression. With expenditure restrained, the people’s resources would be ample, and their prosperity would suffice to provide supplies. Appropriate adaptation to changing circumstances and the benefits of putting it into practice extend no further than this. Why should we need increased taxes to meet expenses or additional recruitment to enhance military might?

Yet there is another point to make. Established rules already govern the provision of military supplies. In Jiangyou, the soil is poor and the people impoverished; there are no other resources that could supplement these provisions, so I can propose nothing further on that matter. But methods of militia drill have been studied for years, yet have produced no results. Why? Because the right men have not been obtained to conduct the training. If we truly wish to discharge the recruited troops and rely on the militia, can we fail to select officials to take responsibility for it?

Country people, suddenly driven into battle, face something to which they are unaccustomed. Moreover, some are strong and others weak, some intelligent and others dull. A skilled instructor begins with filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness to awaken their goodness. He follows this with sitting and rising, advancing and withdrawing, to demonstrate the prescribed methods. He gives them bows and arrows, armor and helmets, to equip them effectively, and publicly establishes commands, rewards, and punishments to spur their efforts. Over time he makes them comfortable with these practices, transformed through familiarity, so that they take to them as the hungry desire food and the cold desire clothing, adapting to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
其資之所近而各成一藝之名則技能之
巧膂力之強將必有脫穎而出者由是以
一教十雖百千萬人皆可化而為兵彼將
遇敵而求以試之也又何患乎寇之至哉
愚故曰訓練者貴得其人此一得之見也
執事儻以為然則條理節目之詳尤有可
言者惟進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 其資之所近，而各成一藝之名，則技能之巧、膂力之強，將必有脫穎而出者。由是以一教十，雖百千萬人，皆可化而為兵。彼將遇敵而求以試之也，又何患乎寇之至哉？愚故曰：「訓練者貴得其人。」此一得之見也。執事儻以為然，則條理節目之詳，尤有可言者。惟進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …what accords with their natural abilities, so that each gains distinction in a particular skill; then men of exceptional technical skill and physical strength will surely stand out. In this way, with one man teaching ten, even hundreds, thousands, or tens of thousands can all be transformed into soldiers. When they encounter the enemy, they will seek to put their abilities to the test. Why, then, worry about the arrival of bandits? Thus I humbly say: “In training, the essential thing is to find the right men to conduct it.” This is my modest insight. If you, sir, consider it sound, there is still more to say about the detailed arrangements and procedures. I would be most grateful if you would permit me to come forward and receive your instruction.

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
今歲甲子江西省大比羣國
士舉其雋如
制得九十有五人將獻賢能之
書道瀾與匡之司役考試已
於事而竣故事宜有序言序
曰夫大江以西吳楚之交江
===
湖之奧區也是惟介在閩粤
南國之紀矣惟楚有才自昔
記之
明興以來貞亮翼輔之臣彬彬
輩出甲于諸藩省乃其舉士
制額自兩畿而下亦甲于諸藩
省誠爲多才賢也今多士舉
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

今歲甲子，江西省大比羣國士，舉其雋，如制得九十有五人。將獻賢能之書，道瀾與匡之司役考試，已於事而竣。故事宜有序言。序曰：夫大江以西，吳楚之交，江湖之奧區也。是惟介在閩粤，南國之紀矣。「惟楚有才」，自昔記之。

明興以來，貞亮翼輔之臣彬彬輩出，甲于諸藩省。乃其舉士制額，自兩畿而下，亦甲于諸藩省，誠爲多才賢也。今多士舉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

This year, the jiazi year, Jiangxi Province held its great triennial examination for the assembled scholars [?], selecting the most outstanding among them. In accordance with the regulations, ninety-five men were chosen. As the register of the worthy and capable was about to be submitted, Daolan and Kuangzhi, charged with conducting the examination, had completed their duties [?]. Established practice calls for a postface, which reads as follows:

The land west of the great Yangtze, where Wu and Chu meet, is a secluded heartland of rivers and lakes. Situated between Min and Yue, it forms a principal bond of the southern regions. “Chu indeed has men of talent”: this has been recorded since antiquity.

Since the rise of the Ming, upright and trustworthy ministers who support and assist the throne have emerged here in splendid succession, surpassing those of all the other provinces. Its statutory quota for selecting scholars likewise ranks first among the provinces, after the two metropolitan regions. Truly, this is a land rich in talented and worthy men. Now the many scholars have been selected…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
于鄉登名
天府將乘時顯庸矣亦繹思有
司者所以𢘆愼遴選意耶夫
有司者攄誠協恭期於以人
事君如治絲者然蠶繅紬繹
經之綸之以充筐篚衣裳黼
黻之需也然而經緯不同期
===
於為章也如治室者然掄求
山林度修絜鉅牽江輓陸以
輸將作宗廟明堂之具也然
而虞斵不同期於成材也又
如往大都者馳於阪飄於川
飭轅結靷周其帆檣以車以
舟引重致遠之資也然而遠
punctuated: 于鄉，登名天府，將乘時顯庸矣。亦繹思有司者所以𢘆愼遴選意耶？夫有司者攄誠協恭，期於以人事君。如治絲者然，蠶繅紬繹，經之綸之，以充筐篚衣裳黼黻之需也。然而經緯不同，期於為章也。如治室者然，掄求山林，度修絜鉅，牽江輓陸，以輸將作宗廟明堂之具也。然而虞斵不同，期於成材也。又如往大都者，馳於阪，飄於川，飭轅結靷，周其帆檣，以車以舟，引重致遠之資也。然而遠
translation_en: …in the Provincial Examination, and their names have been entered in the imperial registers; they will now seize their opportunity to distinguish themselves in service. Have they also pondered why the responsible officials are always so careful in making their selections? These officials give full expression to their sincerity and work together with reverence, seeking to serve their sovereign by providing him with worthy men. They are like those who prepare silk: raising silkworms, reeling silk, drawing out and unraveling its threads, arranging and twisting them, to supply the requirements of ceremonial baskets, robes, and embroidered axe-head and paired bow-shaped designs. Yet although warp and weft differ, their common purpose is to form a pattern. They are like those who build halls: selecting and seeking timber in mountains and forests, measuring its length and girth, towing it along rivers and hauling it overland, to deliver to the Directorate of Palace Buildings the materials for ancestral temples and the Hall of Enlightenment. Yet although foresters and woodworkers differ, their common purpose is to make usable timber. Again, they are like those traveling to a great metropolis: speeding over slopes and sailing along rivers, putting shafts in order and fastening traces, making sails and masts ready—using carts and boats as the means to convey heavy loads over great distances. Yet although the distant…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
近不同期於共致也是數者
爲道不同期於適用也有司
者之於士謹科條明敎化聯
之師儒以儲養於鄉國者非
一日矣今玆殫精竭智朝夕
匪懈披沙見寳觸目琳琅亦
至勤矣誠不異於前數者之
===
求於用哉仰惟
皇上道久化成四海厎治然乃加
惠元元登用賢哲廣厲風敎
嵗飭功令惓惓焉以共成雍
熈悠久之盛多士者亦又服
膺
德意潔齊快覩雲蒸虎變千載
punctuated:
近不同，期於共致也。是數者，爲道不同，期於適用也。有司者之於士，謹科條，明敎化，聯之師儒，以儲養於鄉國者，非一日矣。今玆殫精竭智，朝夕匪懈，披沙見寳，觸目琳琅，亦至勤矣。誠不異於前數者之求於用哉！
仰惟皇上道久化成，四海厎治，然乃加惠元元，登用賢哲，廣厲風敎，嵗飭功令，惓惓焉以共成雍熈悠久之盛。多士者亦又服膺德意，潔齊快覩，雲蒸虎變，千載
translation_en:
…near differ, yet they share the aim of bringing their burdens to their destination. In these several cases, the methods differ, but all aim at practical use. In their dealings with scholars, the responsible officials have carefully maintained examination regulations, made moral instruction clear, and brought scholars together under learned teachers, nurturing a reserve of talent in the localities and throughout the realm. This has been going on for far more than a single day. Now they have exhausted their energies and understanding, untiring morning and evening, sifting the sand to reveal treasures, with fine jade meeting their eyes everywhere. Their diligence has indeed been utmost. Surely their pursuit of useful talent is no different from the preceding examples!
Reverently considering His Majesty: his Way has long prevailed, his transforming influence has reached fulfillment, and all within the Four Seas has attained good government. Yet he further bestows kindness upon the common people, raises worthy and wise men to office, and broadly promotes moral instruction. Each year he orders the enforcement of the examination regulations, earnestly seeking, together with others, to bring about enduring prosperity in harmony and peace. The assembled scholars likewise take his gracious intentions to heart, purify and compose themselves, and joyfully behold talent rising like clouds and undergoing the tiger’s splendid transformation—an occasion in a thousand years …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
一時矣毋亦慎所趨以求不
負於用耳昔者墨子惜絲之
染非能無染也懼所以染之
者非也匠氏之不勝任以其
斵而小之然材或堅外而中
液也楊氏逢岐路而有感以
多岐則衆惑競趨也其於士
===
亦然是故五色宣炳文章之
華也染之而非則玄黃而紺
紫之矣隆棟藻梲大壯之觀
也眩於用而無實則棟梁而
榱桷之矣殊途同歸達道之
致一也以虛車弊舟而趨狹
邪沿汙潦焉則戾矣是故染
punctuated: 一時矣！毋亦慎所趨，以求不負於用耳。昔者墨子惜絲之染，非能無染也，懼所以染之者非也。匠氏之不勝任，以其斵而小之，然材或堅外而中液也。楊氏逢岐路而有感，以多岐則衆惑競趨也。其於士亦然。是故五色宣炳，文章之華也；染之而非，則玄黃而紺紫之矣。隆棟藻梲，大壯之觀也；眩於用而無實，則棟梁而榱桷之矣。殊途同歸，達道之致一也；以虛車弊舟而趨狹邪、沿汙潦焉，則戾矣。是故染
translation_en:
…a singular moment indeed! Should scholars not take care over the direction they pursue, seeking only not to fall short when put to service? In antiquity, Mozi lamented the dyeing of silk—not because it could remain undyed, but because he feared that what dyed it might be wrong. A craftsman’s failure to make timber fit its intended use may result from his hewing it down too small; yet the timber may also be hard outside and soft within. Master Yang was moved when he encountered a fork in the road, for numerous forks leave people confused, vying to take different paths. So it is with scholars.

Thus, the five colors shining brilliantly constitute the splendor of patterned ornament; but if the dyeing is done wrongly, black and yellow are turned into deep blue and purple. Lofty ridgepoles and decorated king-posts present a spectacle of grandeur; but if one is dazzled by usefulness where there is no substance, timber meant for great beams is reduced to rafters. Different paths leading to the same destination express the ultimate unity of the universally followed Way; but to take an empty carriage or a worn-out boat along crooked, narrow ways and through foul puddles is to go astray. Thus, dyeing…

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之而善則善人矣染之而惡
則惡人矣是在人也用之大
則成大用之小則爲小是在
人也騖於紛華舍大道而由
徑竇焉是速化同塵非遠器
也
國家何賴焉爾多士涵泳德教
===
誦法古昔明詩書以求適於
用所自期待非鮮淺也今顧
始進之也上之而篤棐寅亮
總壹方略賛承化理於無疆
次之而屏翰四方經營底績
稱其股肱下之因事宣猷和
衷靖共亦不失一方之寄固
punctuated:
之而善，則善人矣；染之而惡，則惡人矣。是在人也。用之大，則成大；用之小，則爲小。是在人也。騖於紛華，舍大道而由徑竇焉，是速化同塵，非遠器也。國家何賴焉？
爾多士涵泳德教，誦法古昔，明詩書以求適於用，所自期待非鮮淺也。今顧始進之也，上之而篤棐寅亮，總壹方略，賛承化理於無疆；次之而屏翰四方，經營底績，稱其股肱；下之因事宣猷，和衷靖共，亦不失一方之寄。固
translation_en:
…if the influence upon them is good, they become good people; if the influence upon them is evil, they become evil people. This depends upon the individual. Employed in great affairs, they achieve great things; employed in small affairs, they accomplish small things. This depends upon the individual. To chase dazzling splendor, abandon the great Way, and follow narrow paths and openings is to succumb readily to worldly influences and mingle with the dust, rather than possess the capacity for far-reaching achievement. How could the state rely upon such people?
You scholars have steeped yourselves in moral instruction, recited and taken as models the teachings of antiquity, and clarified the meaning of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents so as to make your learning fit for practical use. Your expectations of yourselves are neither meager nor shallow. Yet now you are only beginning your advancement [?]. At the highest level, you may offer steadfast assistance and reverent guidance, coordinate plans and policies, and aid the work of moral transformation and government without limit. At the next level, you may serve as protective bulwarks throughout the realm, manage affairs and bring undertakings to fruition, proving worthy to act as the sovereign’s limbs. At a lower level, you may carry out his plans as circumstances require, working harmoniously, diligently, and respectfully, and still fulfill the trust placed in you for a locality. Indeed …

title: 嘉靖四十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
多士分內事也藉令毋貳爾
心不見異物而遷焉卽所樹
勛揚休皦然較著將世世永
有令聞有司者不與有聲施
哉先正有言下不負所學上
不負
天子是適用之謂也敬爲多士誦
===
之勖之
河南開封府許州郾城縣儒
學教諭何道瀾謹序
punctuated:
多士分內事也。藉令毋貳爾心，不見異物而遷焉，卽所樹勛揚休，皦然較著，將世世永有令聞，有司者不與有聲施哉？先正有言：「下不負所學，上不負天子。」是適用之謂也。敬爲多士誦之，勖之。
河南開封府許州郾城縣儒學教諭何道瀾謹序。
translation_en:
…these are duties incumbent upon you scholars. If you keep your hearts undivided and do not let unfamiliar things deflect your resolve, the achievements you establish and the excellence you make manifest will shine forth clearly, and your good name will endure for generation after generation. Would not the officials responsible also share in that renown? A worthy predecessor said: “Below, do not betray what you have learned; above, do not fail the Son of Heaven.” This is what it means to put learning to practical use. I respectfully recite these words for you scholars, to exhort you.
Preface respectfully composed by He Daolan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yancheng County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.
